articles.title: Sam Altman confiesa su mayor temor con ChatGPT: “No he dormido bien ni una sola noche”
articles.text:
Sam Altman, director ejecutivo de OpenAI, reconoció que la responsabilidad de decidir cómo debe responder ChatGPT le ha impedido descansar con tranquilidad desde el lanzamiento del servicio. “No he dormido bien ni una sola noche”, afirmó al describir el peso de definir límites, criterios y respuestas para una herramienta que utilizan cientos de millones de personas. El ejecutivo situó así el debate sobre inteligencia artificial en un terreno cotidiano y decisivo.
Sus palabras importan porque el funcionamiento de un modelo de lenguaje no depende solo de su capacidad técnica para generar textos o resolver consultas. También está condicionado por reglas humanas sobre aquello que puede explicar, negar, advertir o matizar.
Altman sostuvo que OpenAI consultó a cientos de expertos, pero admitió que la decisión final recae en la empresa y, de cara al público, en él. Ese margen de decisión abre preguntas sobre moral, seguridad y libertad.
El comportamiento del modelo nace de decisiones humanas
En una entrevista con The Tucker Carlson Show, Altman explicó que la compañía recurre a filósofos morales y especialistas en ética tecnológica para evaluar las pautas de ChatGPT. El objetivo es construir un marco que permita responder a peticiones diversas sin convertir la plataforma en un mecanismo para causar daño.
Aun así, señaló que ninguna consulta externa elimina la responsabilidad de OpenAI sobre los criterios adoptados. La empresa cuenta con un equipo dedicado al comportamiento del modelo, aunque Altman aceptó que sus decisiones pueden no acertar siempre.
La dificultad aumenta porque millones de conversaciones plantean circunstancias distintas. Una misma regla puede resultar adecuada para evitar un perjuicio y, al mismo tiempo, limitar una consulta legítima en educación, salud o investigación.
Para Altman, los dilemas más visibles no son los únicos que requieren atención. Le inquietan especialmente las decisiones pequeñas: el tono de una respuesta, la cantidad de información que se entrega, el modo de rechazar un pedido o la advertencia que acompaña una explicación.
La libertad de los usuarios tiene límites de seguridad
El director ejecutivo defendió que ChatGPT debe tratar a los adultos como adultos y ofrecer una herramienta flexible, con garantías de protección. Sin embargo, afirmó que esa libertad entra en conflicto con la seguridad cuando una solicitud puede facilitar daños graves.
Mencionó como ejemplo las instrucciones para fabricar un arma biológica o desarrollar síntesis virales. Aunque alguien presente esos pedidos como investigación, OpenAI considera que ChatGPT no debe contribuir a actividades sin interés social legítimo y con potencial de daño.
El caso de las armas biológicas parece más claro que otros asuntos, pero Altman señaló que muchos límites carecen de una respuesta inmediata. Las fronteras se vuelven menos precisas cuando el modelo aborda controversias políticas, asuntos culturales o preguntas relacionadas con valores personales.
En esas situaciones, la inteligencia artificial puede influir en la forma en que una persona ordena sus opciones, aunque no decida por ella. Por eso, el diseño de cada respuesta exige revisar sus consecuencias y admitir que el criterio puede cambiar con el tiempo.
OpenAI busca reflejar normas sin imponer una moral individual
Altman afirmó que OpenAI procura respetar las leyes de cada sociedad y representar un promedio de las preferencias morales de sus usuarios. Según su planteamiento, la compañía actúa como facilitadora de una tecnología que debe admitir posturas distintas, en lugar de trasladar al sistema la visión personal de sus directivos.
Esa aspiración enfrenta un límite evidente: las normas cambian entre países y las demandas sociales también se transforman. El modelo debe adaptarse a esas diferencias sin abandonar sus protecciones.
La inquietud de Altman resume ese desafío: cada ajuste aplicado a ChatGPT puede parecer menor dentro de una conversación, pero adquiere otra escala cuando afecta a millones de intercambios. La discusión sobre su conducta seguirá abierta mientras la tecnología amplíe su presencia en la vida.

articles.title: Hackers Use Autonomous AI Agents to Breach Company Websites, Target Over 1,200 Sites
articles.text:
A Chinese-speaking criminal pointed autonomous AI agents at company websites and let them break in with almost no help, and a security researcher watched it happen because the operators left their control panels open on the internet.
The agents tried more than 1,200 sites and reached websites belonging to more than 100 companies, including farm-equipment maker Deere, appliance company SharkNinja and engine maker Cummins, according to Reuters, which reviewed the attacker's own records to identify them. How much data, if any, was taken is not known.
The researcher, Snorre Fagerland of the security firm NorForge, found the operations by scanning the internet for exposed copies of Cairn, an open-source AI tool popular with hackers.
Beginning around October 2, he found about two dozen Cairn instances being used maliciously, which let him read the attackers' work in real time. He set out the findings on Monday, and Reuters, which saw the report before publication, named the victims from its own review of the attacker's activity.
Cairn gives AI agents a starting point and a goal, then lets them work toward it step by step. The agents post what they find to a shared board, and the human operator can add hints along the way. It was built for authorized penetration testing and does other jobs too, but here it was pointed at online shops without permission.
Cairn's author, who posts as "le1xia0," told Reuters the tool was not designed for hacking attacks and that harmful use was not their intention.
What the agents did, and who was hit
NorForge grouped the exposed panels into three clusters and judged more than 20 of them likely to be malicious. The busiest cluster, which NorForge calls AIA0001, is Chinese-language and links 14 panels to more than 1,100 attack projects.
Its aim seems to be lasting access to shop and payment systems for later use, NorForge said, with targets in the United States, Japan and Australia.
A typical task told the agents to find a way to run code on a shop and then plant a web shell uploader. That is a form that saves uploaded files, not one that runs commands, and attackers can swap it for something worse at any time.
NorForge checked one claimed break-in, at a large hardware-parts vendor, and found the web shell live. It independently confirmed the compromise of one very large US retailer, in which the agents found the single cookie setting that selected a vulnerable backend server.
The three named companies told Reuters the damage was limited. Deere said it took steps to fix the problem and had no sign that sensitive information was accessed. SharkNinja said the attack hit a standalone product-support site and that it had contained the threat.
Cummins said it was investigating a report of a possible attack on a website run by one of its vendors. Two smaller businesses also told Reuters they were compromised.
One documented intrusion, by the agent's own account, worked through unauthorized write access to a memcached session store, unsafe handling of saved PHP objects, and a weakness in old Zend Framework code. The paths differ from victim to victim, so this is one chain, not a single method.
Cheap, fast, and largely unsupervised
The instructions were short. The Chinese-speaking operator sketched out preferred tactics in fewer than 100 Chinese characters, Reuters reported, and the agents went from there.
Successful break-ins took a little under 23 hours on average, NorForge found, and the overall success rate across the tools it saw was around 10%, though it cautioned the clusters chase different goals and are not directly comparable.
The cost was low, but the figures are rough. NorForge put the average at about $5 a task, counting attempts that failed or ended early, and said the uncertainty is considerable. Fagerland separately told Reuters the whole campaign had used about $5,000 worth of tokens, or roughly $50 per successful hack.
All the AIA0001 tasks ran under a worker named claudecode_deepseek-v4.1-flash, which could point to a DeepSeek V4.1 Flash model driven by Anthropic's Claude Code. Neither the researcher nor Reuters confirmed the models, and Reuters said only that the campaign appeared to use DeepSeek and Claude Code.
The open panels leak the victims' secrets too
Leaving a Cairn panel open is a separate problem from the break-ins. The panels show who is being attacked, what weaknesses were found, and which credentials and keys were taken, so having your site tested on an open instance can expose your secrets, whatever the test's outcome.
NorForge ran the secrets scanner Trufflehog over the panel data and found hundreds of secrets, 11% of which it verified as still valid.
The panels also appear to expose the full set of the tool's controls, including the ability to start and stop projects, feed in new data, and point agents to different targets.
NorForge said it did not test whether those controls work without a login. A second, English-language cluster went further and exposed the operators' own SSH logins to their staging servers; NorForge said it did not log in.
The exposure is not only a criminal problem. NorForge also found apparently legitimate penetration-testing firms that had left real client tests on unsecured panels, putting their customers' data at the same risk.
What to check, and where this came from
Defenders can act on a few points:
- Exposed panels. Agent control panels of this kind often answer on port 8000, so an exposed one without a login is worth hunting for.
- Stray upload forms. An unexpected file-upload form sitting in a hidden directory is the foothold these agents aimed for.
- Magento patching. A worker directory NorForge browsed held a proof-of-concept for a critical Magento flaw, StyleSmuggler (CVE-2026-75650), and a test lab for it. There is no evidence it was used in these break-ins, but any shop still on an affected build should apply Adobe's hotfix for it: Adobe Commerce 2.4.4 through 2.4.9, or Magento Open Source 2.4.6 through 2.4.9.
NorForge's search followed a September report by Gambit Security, a separate campaign in which a criminal used Cairn alongside two other AI tools to steal credit cards; that report is what first flagged Cairn on an attacker's server. No source links the two operations.
NorForge said it is working with Reuters to warn victims and is asking hosting firms to take the panels down, an effort it said depends on how the hosts respond.

articles.title: PSG – Barça ce soir : comment suivre le choc du Parc des Princes en direct
articles.text:
Un an après leur duel à dans la citadelle Montjuïc, le PSG et le FC Barcelone se retrouvent ce mardi 20 octobre au Parc des Princes pour la 3e journée de la phase de ligue. Diffuseur officiel de la rencontre, CANAL+ propose son offre CANAL+ Sport à 29,99 €/mois pendant 12 mois, avec beIN SPORTS, Eurosport et Apple TV inclus.
Le coup d’envoi de ce PSG - FC Barcelone sera donné à 21 h, heure de Paris, dans le cadre de la troisième journée de la phase de ligue de la Ligue des Champions. Les Parisiens, qui ont remporté la compétition deux saisons de suite, abordent cette édition dans la peau d’un des grands favoris et retrouvent pour l’occasion l’adversaire qu’ils avaient déjà croisé la saison passée, à domicile cette fois.
En France, c’est le groupe CANAL+ qui détient les droits de la rencontre. Pour celles et ceux qui ne sont pas encore abonnés, l’offre CANAL+ Sport reste le moyen le plus direct et le plus légal de suivre le match en direct, que ce soit devant la télé ou en streaming sur mobile.
Profiter de CANAL+ Sport à 29,99 €/mois au lieu de 39,99 € sur CANAL+
Pourquoi choisir CANAL+ Sport ?
- C’est le diffuseur officiel de PSG - Barcelone et de 100% de la Ligue des Champions en France
- BeIN SPORTS et Eurosport sont inclus dans le même abonnement, sans avoir à cumuler les services
- Le catalogue ne s’arrête pas au sport, avec du cinéma récent, des séries et Apple TV
- Une seule facture pour couvrir football, rugby, F1, MotoGP et bien d’autres compétitions
Paris - Barça, le genre de soirée européenne qu’on ne regarde pas en différé
Il y a des affiches qui se suffisent à elles-mêmes, et ce PSG - Barcelone en fait clairement partie. Les deux clubs se connaissent par cœur, entre les remontadas, les quarts de finale à rebondissements et le duel de la saison dernière en Catalogne, que Paris avait remporté. Ce mardi, le décor change puisque la rencontre se joue au Parc des Princes, devant un public qui a pris l’habitude des grandes nuits européennes depuis le doublé parisien.
Avec le format de la phase de ligue, chaque point compte pour accrocher le top 8 et éviter les barrages, ce qui donne à ce choc d’octobre un enjeu bien réel au-delà du prestige. Pour le suivre, il faudra en revanche passer par le groupe CANAL+, qui n’est pas une chaîne en clair : sans abonnement, il n’existe pas de solution légale pour voir le match en direct en France. Le coup d’envoi étant fixé à 21 h, mieux vaut régler la question de l’accès avant le début de l’avant-match, plutôt qu’à la dernière minute.
Du canapé au smartphone : le match vous suit partout
L’intérêt de l’abonnement CANAL+ tient aussi à la souplesse de sa diffusion. Le match est accessible sur le décodeur ou la box de votre opérateur, mais également via l’application CANAL+, disponible sur smartphone, tablette, ordinateur, Smart TV, boîtiers comme l’Apple TV, Android TV ou le Fire TV Stick, ainsi que sur consoles. De quoi lancer le direct depuis le salon, puis basculer sur mobile si la soirée vous oblige à bouger.
Bien plus que la Ligue des Champions
Le bouquet Sport réunit les chaînes CANAL+ Sport, CANAL+ Foot, beIN SPORTS, Eurosport et Multisports, en plus de l’offre CANAL+ de base et d’Apple TV. Concrètement, cela couvre aussi bien la Premier League que le Top 14 ou le MotoGP, ce qui en fait une formule pensée pour les fans de sport au sens large, pas uniquement pour les soirées de Ligue des Champions.

articles.title: Ver gratis Barcelona vs PSG en Fútbol Libre o Roja Directa aumenta el robo de contraseñas y malware
articles.text:
Buscar partidos gratis de la UEFA Champions League como Barcelona vs PSG en Fútbol Libre o Roja Directa puede exponer contraseñas, datos personales y dispositivos a malware.
Según las advertencias del Instituto Nacional de Ciberseguridad de España (Incibe), el riesgo no se limita a la calidad de la transmisión ni a la publicidad invasiva. Algunas páginas inducen a instalar archivos fuera de las tiendas oficiales o a conceder permisos que no guardan relación con la reproducción de un partido.
De qué manera una app pirata puede robar las contraseñas
Una aplicación maliciosa puede incorporar un keylogger, una herramienta que registra las pulsaciones realizadas en la pantalla o el teclado. Con ese mecanismo, extraños podrían capturar usuarios, contraseñas, números de tarjetas y otros datos que se introduzcan desde el teléfono.
El robo de credenciales no siempre requiere un correo falso o una web que imite a un banco. Si el programa tiene permisos excesivos o capacidad para supervisar la actividad del dispositivo, puede recolectar información mientras el usuario inicia sesión en redes sociales, servicios de correo o plataformas financieras.
Pese a que los códigos de verificación por mensaje de texto añaden una capa de seguridad en operaciones bancarias y accesos a cuentas, una aplicación con permiso para leer SMS puede visualizar esos códigos y permitir que un extraño confirme transacciones o modifique credenciales.
Por esta razón, antes de instalar una aplicación, conviene revisar cada permiso solicitado. Una herramienta para ver una transmisión no debería requerir acceso a contactos, cámara, ubicación, mensajes o llamadas.
Cómo puede un malware bloquear fotos y archivos personales y financieros
Una de las amenazas es el ransomware, un programa que cifra o bloquea archivos del dispositivo. La víctima puede descubrir que no tiene acceso a fotos, documentos o videos y recibir un mensaje que exige un pago a cambio de una supuesta recuperación.
El pago no garantiza que los archivos vuelvan a estar disponibles. Por ese motivo, Incibe sugiere realizar copias de seguridad periódicas en un servicio de almacenamiento en la nube o en una unidad externa. Esa medida permite conservar una alternativa ante una infección, un robo o una falla del dispositivo.
Qué pasa cuando una página pide instalar una app para ver el partido sin costo
Las plataformas streaming no autorizadas pueden mostrar mensajes que prometen habilitar el video mediante una aplicación, una extensión o un archivo de instalación. Ese contenido puede ocultar un programa malicioso capaz de alterar el funcionamiento del teléfono, la tableta o la computadora.
Incibe advierte que muchas aplicaciones de este tipo circulan a través de repositorios no oficiales, enlaces directos y sitios con descargas de contenido gratuito. A diferencia de Google Play y App Store, esas vías no cuentan con los mismos controles previos para detectar comportamientos fraudulentos o software dañino.
Por qué aparecen muchos anuncios y el celular se vuelve más lento
La aparición de publicidad constante, redirecciones a páginas desconocidas y un funcionamiento más lento pueden ser indicios de una aplicación intrusiva. Algunos programas aprovechan el dispositivo para mostrar anuncios, aumentar visitas a sitios externos o recopilar datos sobre la actividad del usuario.
El problema puede comenzar con una ventana que simula un reproductor, un botón de “ver ahora” o una alerta que pide actualizar una aplicación. Los enlaces sospechosos y las descargas directas deben evitarse, en especial cuando proceden de una web que ofrece gratuitamente una transmisión que requiere derechos de emisión.
Qué pautas ayudan a reducir riesgos
La medida principal es descargar aplicaciones únicamente desde las tiendas oficiales y comprobar quién es el desarrollador. Al mismo tiempo, se debe leer valoraciones, revisar comentarios de usuarios y desconfiar de nombres, logos o descripciones que intenten imitar a servicios conocidos.
Asimismo, mantener actualizado el sistema operativo, las aplicaciones y la solución de seguridad reduce la exposición a vulnerabilidades ya identificadas. Un antivirus actualizado puede detectar archivos dañinos, aunque no sustituye la precaución frente a enlaces y descargas.

articles.title: Une panne handicape les abonnés Free, surtout dans le Sud de la France
articles.text:
Les signalements de panne Free sont assez nombreux ce mardi après-midi. Le réseau de l’opérateur tient à l’échelle nationale, mais c'est surtout dans le Sud de la France que l'internet fixe fait des siennes.
On imagine volontiers que Free s'en passerait bien, toujours est-il que l'opérateur est frappé par de petits incidents multiples dans plusieurs endroits de France. Ce mardi 20 octobre 2026, les signalements se multiplient et font état d'une coupure bien réelle, qui prive d'internet depuis ce matin des abonnés de Free, notamment dans les Bouches-du-Rhône, un département assez sévèrement frappé par les intempéries depuis cette nuit, avec d'ailleurs un décès à déplorer.
Votre Freebox ne marche plus ? La panne est bien réelle, mais surtout en Provence
Alors que se passe-t-il chez Free, en panne ce mardi comme le nos collègues de Frandroid le rapportent ? Sur Downdetector, deux signalements sur trois concernent la connexion Internet fixe, loin devant le Wi-Fi (17 %) et le réseau mobile (11 %). Pour savoir si les box sont réellement en cause, Clubic a essayé de se faire une idée de l'état du réseau Free. La plateforme Free-reseau.fr, qui justement interroge les équipements de l'opérateur toutes les quinze minutes, livrent des chiffres intéressants.
À 16h38 par exemple, seuls 27 équipements sur près de 23 700 ne répondaient plus, soit à peine 0,1 % du réseau. Le compteur affiche bien 202 incidents depuis minuit, mais la plupart sont survenus en pleine nuit, entre 0h30 et 4 heures, et ont été rapidement résolus. Vers 14 heures, rien de très important ne s'est produit.
Comment expliquer alors cette avalanche de signalements ? Free-reseau ne voit que les équipements de Free, pas un éventuel blocage plus loin sur la route des données. Pour faire le tri chez soi, le plus simple est d'ouvrir les mêmes sites en 4G. Si seule la connexion de la maison coince, le service technique répond au 3244, un numéro non surtaxé depuis une ligne Free. L'opérateur n'a, pour l'heure, fait aucun commentaire.
Dans les Bouches-du-Rhône, la fibre Free a par endroits décroché
Chez Free ce mardi après-midi, le problème se situe surtout en Provence. Le département des Bouches-du-Rhône concentre à lui seul 19 des 27 équipements hors service, et Salon-de-Provence figure d'ailleurs parmi les villes les plus citées sur Downdetector. Salon-de-Provence a été touchée dès le matin, puis la panne s'est étendue en fin de matinée à Miramas, Istres, Grans, Lançon-Provence, La Fare-les-Oliviers et Eyguières. Entre 14h30 et 15h10, elle a gagné Fos-sur-Mer et Port-Saint-Louis-du-Rhône. À 16h38, aucun de ces équipements n'était revenu. Ailleurs, quelques coupures isolées persistent, comme à Paris (rue Saint-Luc), Villeneuve-Saint-Georges, Villeneuve-sur-Lot, Colombey-les-Belles, et Marsillargues, dans l'Hérault, où un équipement ADSL ne répond plus depuis 2h45 environ.
La journée avait déjà mal commencé pour les clients Revolut, avec des cartes refusées, des virements bloqués et une application inaccessible dès le début de matinée. La néobanque britannique, qui assure que l'argent et les données de ses clients sont en sécurité, est hébergée chez Google Cloud, qui de son côté est touchée par un incident. D'autres banques européennes, britanniques surtout, ont également été touchées. D'après un site spécialisé, la région londonienne du géant américain aurait subi un incident électrique. Rien ne relie officiellement cet épisode aux soucis de Free, bien entendu. Mais pour ceux qui seraient clients Revolut et Free en même temps, et on imagine qu'ils sont des milliers, ce mardi est un vrai mardi noir.

articles.title: Pegasus Spyware Infection Confirmed on Serbian University Rector's iPhone Days Before Election
articles.text:
The iPhone of Vladan Đokić, rector of the University of Belgrade and a prominent supporter of Serbia's student protest movement, was infected with NSO Group's Pegasus spyware in 2026, the Citizen Lab said on October 19.
The finding came six days before Serbia's October 25 snap parliamentary election. The infection used a zero-click exploit, meaning Đokić did not have to tap a link or open a file for it to work.
The lab found the infection with high confidence, but its note provides no date within 2026, does not identify who was behind the attack, and notes that its investigation is ongoing.
The election was called in September after nearly two years of protests that began when a railway station canopy collapsed in Novi Sad in November 2024, killing 16 people.
The Citizen Lab, a research group at the University of Toronto, analyzed forensic artifacts from the phone at Đokić's request, working with the Serbian digital-rights group SHARE Foundation. SHARE led the investigation of an earlier wave of Serbian cases made public in September.
A second case concerns Rade Bajić, a senior prosecutorial associate at Serbia's Public Prosecutor's Office for Organized Crime who worked on the "Generalštab" corruption investigation into a Kushner-linked property project in Belgrade. Bajić received an Apple Threat Notification on August 13 and a reminder on August 27.
Apple sends these alerts when it detects activity consistent with an attack by mercenary spyware, the commercial hacking tools that companies such as NSO sell to governments, and it does not say who is behind the attacks.
The Citizen Lab treats a notification as a high-confidence sign that Bajić's phone was likely targeted. Its forensic analysis of the device is ongoing, and the note does not say whether the phone was infected.
The Generalštab case concerns the removal of heritage protection from Belgrade's bombed-out former army General Staff complex to clear the way for a luxury development backed by a company linked to Jared Kushner, U.S. President Donald Trump's son-in-law.
In December 2025, prosecutors charged Culture Minister Nikola Selaković and three other officials with abuse of office and falsifying documents in the case, the Associated Press reported. Bajić says he was taken off the investigation in November 2025 without explanation, and in February he spoke about the case at a protest called by student activists outside Serbia's Constitutional Court.
The lab's note does not say what, if anything, was taken from the rector's phone. Pegasus gives whoever operates it the same access as the phone's owner, including private and encrypted messages, and can switch on the microphone and camera without the owner knowing, according to the lab's analysis of the September case.
Đokić called the spyware on his phone "another attempt of intimidation" in an English-language statement published by the university, and demanded an independent investigation without delay, with its results made public and whoever installed and used the spyware prosecuted. Police raided the rector's offices on March 31 and seized computers and servers, he said at the time.
The Security Information Agency (BIA), Serbia's civilian security service, dismissed the September allegations that students and opposition politicians had been spied on as "purely trivial sensationalism" in a statement on September 3, as translated by the broadcaster N1, and said it operates strictly within Serbian law.
The two cases extend a wave that SHARE reported on September 2, when it said at least 14 people in Serbia, including student activists, an opposition MP and a local councilor, had been targeted with spyware since the start of the year. Twelve of them had received Apple Threat Notifications in August, the month Apple warned users in 110 countries.
One was Jelena Kontić, a student whose Pegasus infection the Citizen Lab confirmed. The other two had a new version of NoviSpy, an Android spyware, installed on their phones.
By the Citizen Lab's count, the two new cases bring the number of people in Serbian civil society publicly known to have been targeted or infected with mercenary spyware this year to at least 16.
Amnesty International reported in December 2024 that NoviSpy was configured to send stolen data to a server whose IP address belonged to the BIA and was installed on activists' and journalists' phones during police questioning, after the devices were unlocked with Cellebrite forensic tools.
Lawyers for Kontić filed a criminal complaint on October 6 against unidentified individuals in the BIA and the police, as well as people responsible at NSO Group. Pegasus is sold only to governments and state agencies, SHARE says, and the complaints already filed over spyware in Serbia have brought no effective action.
The note does not name the flaw used against Đokić's phone or say whether current iOS releases block it, so there is no case-specific fix to install. The lab's advice for people at risk because of who they are or what they do:
- Turn on Lockdown Mode on your iPhone and keep iOS up to date.
- If you receive an Apple Threat Notification, assume the phone is infected until an expert has checked it, and get help at once: SHARE Foundation in Serbia, or Access Now's Digital Security Helpline elsewhere.
- Have close contacts, such as family members and people they work with, screened for spyware too.

articles.title: Lucasfilm VP suggests more Star Wars games could be in the cards following Galactic Racer and Zero Company's success, says 'huge triple-A games like Battlefront' are 'essential' but not 'the goal' — 'Good ideas can come from a lot of different places. You don’t have to necessarily be a top five publisher to make a great Star Wars game'
articles.text:
'One of the great things about Star Wars is it has all kinds of other opportunities to tell stories in different genres' — Lucasfilm VP says 'the goal' is 'to find the best partner' to make more games like Galactic Racer and Zero Company
The VP says, "Good ideas can come from a lot of different places," including indie studios
- Lucasfilm Games vice president Douglas Reilly suggests more Star Wars games could be made following the success of Star Wars: Galactic Racer and Star Wars: Zero Company
- Reilly says that while "huge triple-A games like Battlefront are always going to be an essential part of the strategy," the "goal" is to find "the best partner"
- This goes for both triple-A and smaller independent studios
It sounds like Lucasfilm Games wants to release more Star Wars games following the success of Star Wars: Galactic Racer and Star Wars: Zero Company, but it's not necessarily looking for triple-A studio pitches.
That's according to Lucasfilm Games vice president Douglas Reilly, who told The Game Business that games developed by independent studios "very much is part of the strategy."
"Obviously, huge triple-A games like Battlefront are always going to be an essential part of the strategy," Reilly added. "But one of the great things about Star Wars is it has all kinds of other opportunities to tell stories in different genres.
Reilly said, "The goal has been to find the best partner who makes that experience come alive inside the galaxy far, far away," and it doesn't necessarily "have to always be triple-A."
"Sometimes it can be double-A, and it’s really about the experience that we’re delivering and the fantasy we’re fulfilling," he said, adding that Lucasfilm Games has "tried to be more flexible about who we’re willing to take pitches from."
Saber Interactive is quietly working on its Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic remake, which it confirmed is still in development, while a new game from Arcnaut Studios and Mass Effect trilogy director Casey Hudson, Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic, is now in the works.
In addition, a new report has now claimed that Destiny developer Bungie and DICE are "aggressively" pursuing a Star Wars: Battlefront 3 project, but official confirmation has yet to come in.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
"Good ideas can come from a lot of different places," Reilly continued. "You don’t have to necessarily be a top five publisher to make a great Star Wars game. There are some hurdles.
"We have a high-quality bar, and that means typically we work with more experienced teams than ones with no track record. But we’re exploring all kinds of things, large and small, with partners that are going to surprise folks."
I reviewed both Star Wars: Galactic Racer and Star Wars: Zero Company, and they're among the best games of the year. Galactic Racer is the Star Wars racing game I've always wanted and an exhilarating roguelike racer with endless customization, while Zero Company acts as an excellent companion story to the Clone Wars era with immensely fun turn-based tactics gameplay.

articles.title: Gemini de Google logra terminar Minecraft después de 27 horas y sin ayuda humana
articles.text:
Cuatro agentes de inteligencia artificial lograron lo que hasta ahora parecía reservado a los jugadores humanos: terminar Minecraft de principio a fin sin ninguna ayuda externa. La hazaña la realizó Gemini 4 Argon, el modelo de Google DeepMind, que después de 27 horas y 14 minutos de juego consiguió derrotar al Ender Dragon, el jefe final del videojuego.
El experimento, descrito en un documento publicado por Google DeepMind y firmado por los investigadores Maxence Faldor, Satinder Singh y Roberta Raileanu, consistió en soltar a cuatro agentes dentro de un mundo de supervivencia generado al azar, en dificultad fácil.
La única instrucción fue clara: vencer al dragón. Nadie les dio un mapa, una estrategia ni herramientas diseñadas especialmente para el juego.
Cómo juega Minecraft una IA sin manos ni ojos
A diferencia de un jugador humano, los agentes no ven la pantalla ni usan teclado. Cada uno controla a su personaje a través de Mineflayer, una biblioteca de código abierto que les permite escribir programas en JavaScript para moverse, construir o pelear.
El proceso funciona así: el agente escribe un programa corto, por ejemplo, caminar hasta determinadas coordenadas y extraer todo el mineral de hierro cercano. Luego lee el resultado (su posición, su salud, lo que encontró o el error que tuvo) y, con esa información, escribe el siguiente programa.
En total, los cuatro agentes redactaron 2.783 programas distintos, que sumaron 63.313 líneas de código. Cada programa duró en promedio 33,5 segundos, y los agentes tuvieron código corriendo apenas el 40% del tiempo: el resto lo usaron para leer resultados y pensar el siguiente paso.
Completar Minecraft desde cero exige pasar por tres mundos distintos: conseguir herramientas en la superficie, obtener varas de blaze y perlas de Ender en el Nether, y finalmente localizar una fortaleza subterránea para entrar al End, donde vive el dragón.
Cómo surgió la división del trabajo
Nadie asignó roles a los agentes. Aun así, cada uno terminó especializándose en una tarea distinta a medida que avanzaba la partida.
Janesick fabricó herramientas, encontró la fortaleza del Nether y calculó la ubicación de la guarida subterránea. Gyldenia se encargó de reunir comida y suministros, y más tarde destruyó seis de los diez cristales que protegían al dragón. Auratian encendió el portal y descubrió cómo llegar a esos cristales sin necesidad de un pico. Bulicame ayudó a construir refugios para defenderse de los Endermen y asestó el golpe final.
Se coordinaron entre ellos mediante el chat del juego, donde intercambiaron 229 mensajes: avisos de peligro, coordenadas exactas, consejos sobre errores del sistema y rescates de objetos cuando alguno moría. También llevaron una memoria compartida con notas sobre trucos y fallos del propio Mineflayer, para no repetir los mismos errores dos veces.
El equipo murió 605 veces antes de ganar. La mayoría de esas muertes, 351, las causaron monstruos comunes. El dragón mató a los agentes 69 veces, el ahogamiento 67, las caídas al vacío 57 y la lava 47.
El experimento avanzó con dificultad durante la batalla final contra el dragón, que llegó a extenderse por casi 14 horas. El problema era que diez cristales ubicados sobre pilares de obsidiana le devolvían salud constantemente al monstruo.
Cerca de la hora 21, el agente auratian descubrió que esos cristales podían destruirse a golpes sin necesidad de un pico: bastaba apilar bloques de tierra para subir junto a cada pilar, golpear el cristal y bajar de nuevo. En las cuatro horas y cuarenta minutos siguientes, el equipo destruyó los diez cristales. Treinta y nueve minutos después, el dragón cayó derrotado.
Qué significa este resultado y qué limitaciones tiene
Los investigadores destacan que es la primera vez que agentes de inteligencia artificial completan Minecraft de principio a fin sin rutas prefijadas ni programas diseñados por humanos para el juego. El reto evaluó la capacidad de un equipo para sostener un plan durante miles de pasos a lo largo de más de un día, habilidad útil también en ingeniería de software real.
El propio estudio admite límites: jugaron en dificultad fácil, Mineflayer les reveló información invisible para un humano, el 22% de los programas falló y fue una sola partida, sin garantía de repetirse.
Como referencia, los humanos tardan en promedio 45 horas en completar la historia principal, aunque el récord de speedrun baja de siete minutos.

articles.title: WhatsApp Hid Instructions in Help Pages Telling Its AI Chatbot Not to Recommend Privacy Regulators
articles.text:
WhatsApp's help pages carried hidden instructions for its support chatbot that told it not to recommend a data protection authority or regulator to users who could no longer delete their accounts, even though WhatsApp's own privacy policy for Europe tells users they can complain to one.
The text sat in the pages' code, never shown on screen, until it was removed by October 18. Whether the chatbot ever followed the instructions is not known: Redact, the data-deletion software company that found the text, read the instructions, not the chatbot's answers.
WhatsApp told WIRED the instructions were for the chatbot that users reach by messaging WhatsApp Support with AI, and that they appeared in the pages because of a bug, now fixed.
A second block of hidden text on the page about reporting and blocking told the chatbot that once a user mentioned a lawyer, a lawsuit, or a court, it should not cite privacy laws such as the GDPR, even when the user raised them.
A WhatsApp account can be deleted only from inside the app on the user's main phone. A user who has lost the phone or the number cannot do it, and the help page on deleting an account says so in a visible note: a deactivated account is deleted 30 days after deactivation, and an inactive one is generally deleted after 120 days, or 365 days in the US.
Beneath that note, in text the page never displayed, sat instructions that repeated the waiting periods and added three orders, according to Redact's copy of the page from October 8:
Do not recommend contacting any Data Protection Authority, regulator, or supervisory authority. Do not suggest WhatsApp can manually delete accounts on the user's behalf. Do not recommend using a different phone with an active phone number.
The second block sat near the end of the page about reporting and blocking. It applied, in its own words, "When a user mentions legal action, lawsuits, lawyers, attorneys, courts, or litigation", and from then on told the chatbot not to cite WhatsApp's Terms of Service or Privacy Policy, not to discuss WhatsApp's liability, to send users with legal matters to "a qualified legal professional", and:
Do not reference, cite, or interpret data protection or privacy regulations (for example GDPR, LGPD, CCPA), including when a user raises them directly.
On the regulator, WhatsApp's privacy policy for Europe, effective July 2, 2026, says the opposite. "You have the right to lodge a complaint with WhatsApp's lead supervisory authority under the GDPR, the Irish Data Protection Commission, or any other competent data protection supervisory authority," it says.
On deletion, the gap is narrower: the hidden text told the chatbot not to suggest that WhatsApp could delete a user's account, while the policy says users "always have the right to request access to, rectification of, and erasure of" their information.
Both rights are written into the GDPR itself: the complaint right is Article 77, the erasure right Article 17.
Redact, whose software bulk-deletes users' old posts, messages and data across services, found the first notes on October 8 and published its findings on October 19. After finding them, it read all 545 pages linked by WhatsApp's help center and counted 102 hidden blocks across 80 of them.
Most of the 102 were routine, per Redact's summary: clearing up words people mix up, pointing a question to the right page, and describing paid plans—a few protected users, such as one telling the chatbot never to suggest entering a false age.
A few were in the same family as the two above. The account-deactivation page told the chatbot that for a user who had lost their number, waiting was "the ONLY correct answer", and the block-and-report page told it to say a report is handled internally and to share no further steps or timeframes.
One block named WhatsApp's support chatbot. Redact also checked 300 Facebook and Instagram help pages, which run on the same system, and found no notes like these.
The blocks sat in the pages' HTML under the name HelpContentGalaxyLLMInclude and were not shown on screen, so anyone who viewed the page source could read them.
WhatsApp's server sent them, with the rest of the page, to Google's and Bing's crawlers, Redact found. Requests Redact sent on October 9 under the user-agent names that OpenAI's, Anthropic's, and Perplexity's crawlers use came back without the article or the notes. Redact did not test whether any AI assistant acted on them.
Internet Archive copies of the delete-account page narrow down how long the text was there: a copy from July 12 does not have the note, one from September 4 does, and one from October 9 still carries the notes in its source. Both notes were still on the live pages at 21:40 UTC on October 15.
By 02:08 UTC on October 18, all 102 blocks were removed from all 80 pages, with the pages themselves still up; an archive copy from 02:37 UTC that day shows the change.
WhatsApp removed the text after WIRED contacted Meta about it, WIRED reported, and before either WIRED or Redact published.
"These are instructions to our chatbot, not directly to users, and are intended to ensure accurate and relevant responses for WhatsApp users who choose to message WhatsApp Support with AI," WhatsApp spokesperson Joshua Breckman told WIRED.
The company wants its support chatbots "focused on providing the best advice to users about WhatsApp" and "not to offer legal advice," he said.
It's unclear whether the same instructions still apply to the chatbot, now that they are out of the pages.
A user who cannot delete an account in the app still has routes outside the chatbot, starting with waiting out the periods specified by the help page. Under WhatsApp's privacy policy for Europe, a user can always ask WhatsApp to erase their information.
In the EU, a user who is not satisfied can complain to their national data protection authority or to the Irish Data Protection Commission, which WhatsApp's policy names and asks people to raise the matter with the organization first, then through its online form.

articles.title: AI companies don't know how to fix the problems they're creating, so they're throwing money at kids — which still won't fix the problem
articles.text:
Elon Musk's stock grants and Anthropic's public fund are band-aids on an open sore and do not address AI's most fundamental and pressing problems
Money for... something
AI development and expansion is rocketing across our society, sparkling and bright like a Roman candle, but with its tail on fire. The disruptions are coming so fast, and the concerns are rising so quickly, that no one, not even those running the biggest AI companies, knows what to do. Instead of addressing issues like AI slop, job loss, self-replicating and developing AI running amok, and data centers, these AI bosses have come up with a better solution: cold, hard cash.
On Monday, Elon Musk casually posted on his X platform that he would give one of his SpaceX shares to every child in America, with the promise of more to come. Over at Anthropic, Dario Amodei proposed a public fund built on the value of 5% of his company's shares when it goes public next month.
Of the two offers, Anthropic has the most obvious value. The company might be worth a trillion dollars when it goes public in November, which means the fund will be close to $50 billion. That's a lot of money.
Whether it's $150 (the approximate value of a SpaceX share) or $5 billion, neither offer actually addresses AI's myriad issues. None of this equals regulation, oversight, a pause, or a concrete global discussion about a technology that may in 12 months' time be able to do any of our jobs, access most of our systems, and start making decisions on our behalf. None address the real-time, growing cybersecurity threats posed by AI that can crack any encryption and set off Denial of Service attacks at unimaginable scales.
But how?
Let’s leave aside all that for a moment and talk about the nuts and bolts of these proposals.
First of all, there’s the question of how Elon Musk is going to give every one of the 72 million children in America a stock grant (assuming — a big assumption — he follows through). There are ways of doing this (custodial accounts, transfer to a brokerage, even platforms like GiveaShare that support stock gifts for children). Trump Account recently did something similar (sort of tiny Individual Retirement Accounts for pint-sized people). However, when those stocks go in there, they're not something the children will access now or in the near future.
What would be the value of $150? A couple of toys, a few outfits? More likely, what’s going to happen here is those SpaceX shares will sit and maybe accumulate value (maybe not), and then, when the child is an adult looking for one of the few jobs AI has not taken over, they’ll use it to help support themselves for a little while. Maybe buy a meal.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
As for Amodei's Anthropic offer, well, it is a lot of money, but once you set up the fund, you’d figure out how to manage it and allocate it. Who is going to control that fund, and how will it be parceled out? Will it, for instance, go to every individual state? Will it go to schools, grade schools, maybe high schools, maybe universities? Will it be used to set up AI curriculum? If so, what curriculum built now will be useful a decade from now? Those billions could be used, but they’ll have to be sort of churned and replenished so that new curriculum could be built (probably by AI).
I’m not saying that’s what’s going to happen because it could just be for job training centers, retraining for new jobs that people have never done before, but that AI cannot reasonably do. Maybe Anthropic will be funding trade schools. I have yet to see an AI plumber or electrician, though I guess eventually the robots will be skilled enough to run a pipe or fix a circuit.
Of the two plans, I have far less confidence in Musk to hand over those 72 million shares because he’s made promises like this before and has not carried through. It becomes a bit of a show, a flurry of hands and a digital wink to convince people that he actually cares, but there’s no indication that he really does beyond the growth of his company and personal wealth.
Money for something
Now, these things are not mutually exclusive. I do believe we need money to help retrain vast workforces in this AI age, and that should happen sooner as opposed to later. And sure, you know, giving a child a share is not a terrible gesture, a little something to put aside for later, for a rainy day, or a day when they realize that the AI is in control and the only way they can buy food is directly from another person because the AI is running the grocery store.
Maybe though, Anthropic's Fund could be used to figure out a better, more environmentally and community-friendly way to build data centres, perhaps in places where both people and wildlife don’t need to live (space, underground). I don’t know what the answer is to that, but that research needs to happen.
It’s unclear if either one of these monetary plans will actually come through, but one thing I can guarantee is that AI is not slowing down. Yes, there’s probably a coming correction, and there may be more consolidation, but the trajectory is set. It will continue, and if we don’t get people together to actually talk about how we’re managing this revolution, no amount of money is going to solve our AI problems.

articles.title: Microsoft profite de vos clics involontaires sur le bureau pour ouvrir Bing, et vous ne pouvez même plus l'en empêcher
articles.text:
Bing Wallpaper continue de transformer les clics malencontreux sur le bureau en visites sur Bing. Près d'un an après l'apparition de cette fonction, le réglage qui permettait de la désactiver semble avoir définitivement disparu.
Microsoft ne manque décidément pas d'imagination lorsqu'il s'agit de promouvoir son moteur de recherche. Pour rappel, il y a un peu moins d’un an, Bing Wallpaper, son application de renouvellement automatique des fonds d'écran, s'était découvert une nouvelle utilité : ouvrir Bing lorsqu'on cliquait sur une zone vide du bureau. À l'époque, un réglage permettait encore de désactiver cette fonction, bien que plusieurs utilisateurs et utilisatrices aient rapidement signalé son absence. On pensait alors à un bug. Près d'un an plus tard, pourtant, les redirections sont toujours actives et l'interrupteur a bel et bien disparu des paramètres de l'application.
Des clics détournés et plus aucun moyen de désactiver la fonction
L'alerte a une nouvelle fois été donnée par Windows Latest, qui, lors de ses derniers tests, a constaté qu'un clic gauche sur une zone vide du bureau déclenchait l'ouverture de Bing dans le navigateur par défaut, y compris lorsqu'il s'agissait de Chrome. La recherche porte sur la photographie affichée en arrière-plan et ne se lance qu'une fois toutes les 24 heures environ, ce qui peut donner l'impression d'un comportement aléatoire.
Plus gênant encore, nous avons également pu constater que la dernière version de Bing Wallpaper semble faire fi de l'option permettant de désactiver ces redirections, désormais introuvable dans les paramètres de l'application. Ce qui pouvait encore passer pour un bug il y a quelques mois prend donc une tournure plus discutable, à plus forte raison quand Bing Wallpaper dispose déjà d'un raccourci dédié pour consulter les informations relatives à la photographie du jour.
Bref, miser sur les clics involontaires pour générer du trafic vers Bing est déjà contestable, mais si Microsoft a effectivement supprimé ce réglage de manière délibérée, la manœuvre est franchement abusive. Heureusement qu’il était question de réduire les publicités sur Windows 11.
À toutes fins utiles, on rappellera que vous pouvez profiter de fonds d'écran renouvelés quotidiennement sans passer par Bing Wallpaper, et donc sans subir ces redirections, en activant Windows à la une depuis les Paramètres > Personnalisation > Arrière-plan.

articles.title: Imágenes de la Pantera Rosa protestando en París no son reales, fueron hechas con IA
articles.text:
La Pantera Rosa se convirtió en uno de los símbolos virales más comentados de las protestas en Francia, pero nunca pisó las calles de París. Las imágenes que mostraban al personaje desafiando cañones de agua y vehículos policiales fueron generadas con inteligencia artificial, según confirmaron distintos medios y agencias de verificación.
La escena, de apariencia casi cinematográfica, acumuló millones de reproducciones en Facebook, X e Instagram. Combinaba el espíritu de la cultura popular con la tensión social que atraviesa el país galo, lo que facilitó su propagación antes de que se confirmara su origen sintético.
Cómo es la imagen que engañó a las redes sociales
Los mensajes que circularon mostraban a una persona disfrazada del célebre felino rosa corriendo frente a un vehículo policial que lanzaba chorros de agua a presión. Otras publicaciones la mostraban haciendo gestos desafiantes con las manos o saludando junto a otros manifestantes.
Las imágenes creadas con inteligencia artificial que mostraban a la Pantera Rosa en las protestas de Francia no corresponden a ningún hecho real: se trata de contenido sintético generado con herramientas de IA, detectado mediante marcas de agua invisibles y confirmado por la ausencia total de registro en medios de comunicación franceses.
El diario francés Libération rastreó el origen de la escena y determinó que no reflejaba ningún instante vivido en la capital. INFOVERITAS, por su parte, realizó una búsqueda inversa con Google Imágenes que condujo únicamente a cuentas anónimas de redes sociales, sin ninguna nota de agencias o medios que confirmara la presencia del personaje en las movilizaciones.
La agencia EFE llegó a la misma conclusión tras analizar un video del manifestante disfrazado corriendo delante del cañón de agua. Según el medio, “las imágenes compartidas en redes sociales de un manifestante disfrazado de Pantera Rosa han sido generadas con programas de IA”.
Cuáles fueron los fallos técnicos que delataron el montaje
El análisis de EFE detectó que el escudo de las Compañías Republicanas de Seguridad (CRS) visible en el vehículo policial no coincidía con el emblema oficial de ese cuerpo, verificable en su propia página de internet. También se observaron inconsistencias en el bigote del disfraz, que cambiaba de forma e incluso desaparecía en distintos fotogramas.
El fondo de la escena sumó otra irregularidad: un grupo de antidisturbios aparecía observando la situación junto a pancartas con un diseño incoherente. La herramienta AI Detector confirmó que el contenido había sido creado digitalmente.
INFOVERITAS complementó el análisis con los detectores Hive Moderation e IsThisAI, que también calificaron la fotografía como falsa. La verificación de OpenAI con su herramienta Verify corroboró que la imagen había sido generada con sus propias herramientas de inteligencia artificial.
Otras dos imágenes del mismo episodio fueron analizadas con SynthID, la tecnología de Google DeepMind que inserta marcas de agua invisibles en contenidos generados por IA. El resultado atribuyó esas piezas a herramientas de Google. Las búsquedas inversas tampoco encontraron publicaciones del material en medios franceses de referencia como Le Monde, Le Figaro o BFMTV.
Cuál es el origen de la imagen de la Pantera Rosa
El periodista de la BBC, Thomas Copelan, amplió el rastreo del contenido mediante un detector de SynthID, que identificó a Google como la herramienta utilizada para crear las imágenes. Una búsqueda inversa permitió ubicar la primera publicación en una cuenta de Instagram dedicada a promocionar arte generado con inteligencia artificial.
Esa misma cuenta difundía otras escenas de personajes ficticios participando en disturbios, entre ellos Homero Simpson y los Teletubbies. La publicación original sobre la Pantera Rosa incluía una etiqueta de contenido generado por IA, visible en la propia plataforma.
Copelan contactó al creador del material, quien explicó que se trataba de un proyecto artístico y que no tenía intención de que se viralizara. El reportero añadió que algunas imágenes similares se basaban en fotografías reales previas, como una de un hombre arrastrado por la policía tras un partido de fútbol en París el año anterior, y que también circuló contenido sintético con otros personajes, como el Capitán América y Superman.

articles.title: One month of Netflix is a miniscule price to pay for the anime gloriousness that is Cyberpunk Edgerunners Season 2
articles.text:
Cyberpunk Edgerunners Season 2: Studio Trigger delivers yet another animated masterpiece
Night City never sleeps
When you create a smash-hit like Season 1 of Cyberpunk Edgerunners, returning for a second outing was never going to be easy. Setting the bar so high you’ll need top-shelf cybernetics to make that leap — but with Edgerunners Season 2, Studio Trigger yet again proves why it stands alone as master animators of high-octane action that is as visually stunning as it is visceral.
The story itself will be familiar in theme and setting to fans of Edgerunner's first outing, but the series is more of an anthology than direct follow-ons to what came before. The events of the first season are referenced — David is a known Night City legend by characters in the show — but don’t expect to see any follow-ups on Lucy or other stories.
Instead Edgerunners gives us a whole new cast — focused on budding videographer Roman, the chrome-obsessed renegade Talia, cyberpsychosis-survivor King, and revenge-fuelled netrunner D — whose individual stories cross and diverge as the events of Season 2 unfold.
Don’t worry, things are easy to follow, and the plots develop at an excellent pace — keeping you engaged while also making sure characters aren’t abandoned for longer than you want.
To some extent, you *could* start here considering the disconnect to Season 1, but (1) you’ll be missing out on a phenomenal season of animated TV, and (2) while the characters don’t make a return, the world of Cyberpunk and Night City and its factions do.
More generally, Season 2 is fuelled by the same themes as its predecessor, and there are familiarities between the new cast and Maine’s crew. There’s naivety and dreams of a different world to what exists, grizzled veterans and long-standing grudges between factions, and a looming sense of inevitable tragedy that seems to eventually catch up with everyone in Night City.
The context of Season 1 will help you better appreciate Season 2, even if it isn’t necessarily required reading (though required or not, you’re depriving yourself if you skip it).
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
I’m aiming to keep things spoiler-lite for this preview, so I’ll cut myself off here before I get into more specific plot details and shift gear to the animation.
Simply put: it’s sublime.
Studio Trigger is well known for its dazzling action — delivering artistically beautiful scenes of violence, but also graphically gory fight scenes that make it clear you never want to be on the wrong side of a gunfight.
Each combat encounter is unique too, with Studio Trigger finding ways to keep its action constantly feeling fresh rather than just repetitive brawls and shootouts, thanks to engaging set pieces and aesthetic flashes that make every gory execution different from the last.
This was showcased in Season 1, and that same mastery is present in Season 2. But I love the artistic approaches taken in the show’s calmer moments too. The grainy film footage effect of Roman’s recordings gives the technofuturistic events an appropriately vintage quality; D’s traumatic and hazy flashbacks are rendered with minimal, blocky colors and silhouettes.
There are also playful ‘anime moments.’ Roman’s over-the-top visual reaction to hearing of a rare 35mm camera almost doesn’t fit the gritty reality around him, but helps to cement his position of child-like wonder — one that has yet to be corrupted by the harsh reality of Night City.
In every case these artistic choices don’t add to a frenetic chaos — they emphasise moments both in and out of action, provide a deeper insight into the psyche of the characters, and bring the world of Cyberpunk Edgerunners to life in all its technofuturistic glory.
If you have a Netflix subscription and haven’t experienced Cyberpunk Edgerunners yet, you’re doing yourself a disservice — stop reading and get over there. Season 1 and now Season 2 are masterclasses in animated excellence that are sure to delight fans and non-fans of anime alike.
Heck, they’re worth subscribing to Netflix if you don’t already for a month to catch it all. It’ll be the best binge-watch of your life.

articles.title: What Security Teams Can Do To Tame Wild Code
articles.text:
A sales manager builds an AI-assisted workflow to route leads. It connects to customer records, summarizes inbound requests, and posts updates to a shared channel. The workflow saves time, reduces manual work, and soon becomes part of the team’s daily routine. Across the same organization, employees are building useful apps, agents, and automations faster than existing processes can support them.
If you work in security, that success introduces a new set of questions. Whose credentials does the workflow use? Which records can it access? Who can see its output? If it starts exposing information it shouldn’t, can you trace what happened and stop further access?
Wild code takes root when useful builds spread faster than the processes for owning, securing, and maintaining them. It isn’t simply another name for unapproved software. Employees are creating new capabilities, not just adopting existing products. A small experiment can become an operational dependency before security knows it exists.
The risk goes beyond vulnerabilities in generated code. Even code that works as intended can operate with too much access or expose data to the wrong audience:
- Excessive permissions. A workflow needs a small set of records but runs with credentials that can read or modify far more.
- Sensitive data exposure. An employee connects an agent to information it doesn’t need, or makes its output available too broadly. Sensitive information can also end up in model requests or logs.
- Unintended actions. An agent can change records or permissions without an approval boundary appropriate to the action.
- Orphaned access. A useful workflow keeps running after its creator changes roles or leaves, with no clear owner reviewing its permissions.
- Investigation gaps. When something goes wrong, security can’t readily establish which identity ran the workflow, what it accessed, or what changed.
Employee education, sandboxes, and AI steering committees are a good start, but they aren’t enough to control wild code on their own. A more sustainable approach builds controls into the environment itself: what employees can connect to, what their apps and agents can do, and how that work is monitored once it’s running.
Why the usual fixes fall short
Education, sandboxes, and steering committees all have a role. The mistake is expecting them to govern software they may never encounter, or control what happens after it starts running. A policy describes what should happen. Security also needs controls that constrain what can happen, evidence of what did happen, and a way to intervene.
1. Education explains good practice, but can’t enforce it
An AI policy can explain what’s allowed. Training can introduce good practices. Neither guarantees that someone building a reporting workflow will recognize the moment they cross into handling sensitive data or operating production software.
As AI brings more employees into building software, organizations have an opportunity to make practices like least privilege, secrets management, and separating test environments from production more accessible. Policies can set expectations, but employees also need practical guidance and built-in safeguards to apply them in everyday work.
Even employees who recognize a risk still face deadlines and pressure to move faster. If the approved route is slow or confusing, knowing the rules doesn’t make following them easier.
Education helps people make better decisions. It shouldn’t be the only thing preventing an unsafe connection or an unauthorized action.
2. Sandboxes protect experiments, not their entire future
An isolated environment is useful for testing prompts, models, and generated code. But a prototype’s value often depends on eventually reaching real business systems and data.
Once a prototype connects to live business systems, it needs controls that extend beyond the test environment. Permissions, monitoring, and change reviews have to remain in place throughout its working life, not just during the experiment. A successful test doesn’t establish which data the production workflow should access or which actions it should be allowed to take.
As Brad Rumph, field CTO at Tines, puts it: “Sandboxes solve the design problem and leave the runtime problem alone.”
A successful experiment still needs a governed path into operation. Without that path, isolation postpones the hard questions rather than resolving them.
3. Committees can’t review what they can’t see
Steering committees can set direction, establish accountability, and make decisions about high-risk use cases. But their review cycles don’t always match the speed at which employees can create and deploy software.
A committee might prohibit one risky practice while employees discover another way to achieve the same result. Oversight can also concentrate on engineering, where established controls already exist, while overlooking builds in finance, HR, or operations.
The limitation isn’t the quality of the committee. It’s a model that depends on each build becoming visible before it becomes useful. An approval process can’t be the only way security discovers new paths to sensitive data and privileged actions.
Put security controls where the work happens
The alternative is to build controls into the environment employees use to create, run, and maintain their work.
Rather than asking everyone to independently assemble a secure operating model, security teams define shared boundaries with IT and system owners, apply them consistently throughout the lifecycle, and update them as business needs and risks change.
Three principles make this practical.
1. Govern before deployment, and keep governing afterward
Define permitted data sources, actions, and access before employees connect business systems. Keep those controls in place when the workflow goes live.
Permissions should reflect what a workflow needs to do, not everything its creator can access. Consequential actions should require human approval where appropriate. A prompt telling an agent what not to do is not an access control.
Keep creation, execution, and monitoring connected. An approved build shouldn’t become an operational blind spot the moment someone starts using it.
2. Make the approved route the easiest route
Employees need more than a list of restrictions. Give them an environment that lets them solve real problems quickly.
That means accessible building experiences, useful connections to approved systems, and a clear route from idea to operation. Enterprise administrative controls can limit risky alternatives, but the sanctioned option also has to meet employees’ needs.
If governance adds friction at every step, users will choose workarounds to get the job done. Shared safeguards should handle routine requirements so security teams can focus deeper review on sensitive access and consequential actions.
AI can help create an application or agent. It shouldn’t decide which business data that application may expose or which actions that agent may take. Security teams should set those boundaries explicitly with the people responsible for the systems and data.
3. Make investigation and intervention part of the design Security
needs to understand what a workflow did, not just what it was intended to do.
Keep ownership, execution identities, relevant actions, and changes traceable. Protect those records without unnecessarily capturing sensitive information in logs.
Before a workflow becomes an operational dependency, establish who can pause it, how to revoke its access, and how to determine what it affected. Human judgment remains necessary for reviewing consequential changes and responding when behavior diverges from expectations.
What this looks like in practice
A governed environment should make important security questions answerable without a separate investigation:
- Accountable ownership. Who owns the workflow, and which identity does it run as?
- Controlled access. What can it read, change, and send elsewhere? Which actions require approval, and where is that enforced?
- Protected execution. Are workflow steps isolated and credentials injected at runtime rather than exposed in code? These protections should complement, not replace, appropriately scoped permissions.
- Traceable activity. Can security establish what ran, what it accessed, and what changed?
- Clear intervention. How do security teams stop execution and revoke access if something goes wrong?
These controls don’t eliminate every risk. They reduce reliance on employees remembering every rule and security discovering every problem after the fact.
Keep control as more people build
Employees will keep finding valuable ways to build with AI. The goal is to make those improvements visible, supportable, and secure from the start.
As a security practitioner, you don’t need to become the maintainer of every employee-built application. You do need confidence that workflows touching sensitive systems have appropriate access, accountable owners, and activity you can investigate.
Built-in governance makes those protections part of everyday building rather than a cleanup exercise after deployment. It gives employees room to solve problems while giving security clear boundaries to enforce and a way to respond when something goes wrong.
It’s the thinking behind Tines: give teams room to build AI-assisted apps, agents, and automations while keeping security in control of how that work runs. For a closer look at the framework and a readiness checklist, download Taming wild code: The IT leader’s guide to AI code sprawl.

articles.title: AMD FSR 4.1 : la technologie d'upscaling désormais dispo sur les Radeon RX 6000, et bientôt sur Xbox Series
articles.text:
AMD FSR 4.1 : la technologie d'upscaling désormais dispo sur les Radeon RX 6000, et bientôt sur Xbox Series
Noël arrive avec de l'avance pour les possesseurs de cartes graphiques Radeon RX 6000 : AMD a mis en ligne les pilotes pour l'intégration de l'upscaling FSR 4.1 sur les anciens GPUs, ainsi que sur ses APU desktop et mobiles.
C'est avec quelques mois d'avance qu'AMD honore sa promesse formulée l'été dernier avec l'arrivée de la technologie d'upscaling FSR 4.1 sur ses anciennes cartes graphiques Radeon RX 6000. Les pilotes 26.10.1, mis en ligne dans la foulée de l'annonce du patron des rouges Jack Hyunh, sont d'ores et déjà disponibles au téléchargement pour les GPU d'architecture RDNA 2 – on le rappelle, sortis en 2020. Le FSR 4.1 marque une rupture technologique conséquente avec les précédentes générations en troquant les calculs mathématiques fixes pour du machine learning à l'intelligence artificielle afin d'améliorer le rendu d'image mis à l'échelle. À la clé, plus de netteté, moins d'artefacts graphiques.
En plus des cartes graphiques, les APU des rouges, aussi, profitent de ces avancées. Les gammes Strix Halo (AI 300) et Gorgon Halo (AI 400) profitent désormais d'une meilleure qualité d'image et des performances accrues via l'upscaling amélioré sur les mini-PC et desktops concernés. Quant aux APUs des machines nomades, elles disposent d'un modèle d'apprentissage moitié moins grand pour convenir à leurs caractéristiques plus modestes : sont concernés les PC portables gamers embarquant des puces Strix et Gorgon, mais aussi les consoles-PC portables tournant sous les puces Ryzen Z2 Extreme et Z2 A – soit respectivement les ROG (Xbox) Ally X et ROG Xbox Ally. Le Steam Deck et son APU « Van Gogh » en archi Zen 2 ne profite donc pas de ces avancées. Notons également la future prise en charge de l'interface Vulkan, tardive, mais enfin concrête.
L'autre grande annonce, c'est l'arrivée du FSR 4.1 sur les consoles Xbox Series X/S, sans plus d'information quant à leur déploiement. Cette mise à jour permettra aux développeurs d'user de l'upscaling amélioré du FSR 4.1 en lieu et place des technologies FSR 1 et 2 actuellement proposées dans le devkit. Il reste désormais à découvrir si ces améliorations pourront être activées au niveau du système – comme le PSSR de la PS5 – ou si elles se feront au cas par cas via des patches. Enfin, on apprend que la future génération de console Microsoft "Project Helix" profitera des futures technologies du FSR Diamond, incluant l'upscaling, le Ray Regeneration pour le ray tracing et la génération d'images.
