articles.title: Guía de Dragon Ball Super Beerus: cuántos episodios tendrá y dónde verlos completos
articles.text:
Dragon Ball Super Beerus tendrá 19 episodios que se estrenan uno por semana. La serie llegó a Crunchyroll el 11 de octubre de 2026, tanto en Latinoamérica como en España, aunque las opciones de streaming cambian según la región.
En América Latina, el anime también está disponible en Disney+, HBO Max y Netflix, con estrenos escalonados. Disney+ comenzó el 14 de octubre, HBO Max el 16 y Netflix el 17.
En España, además de Crunchyroll, se sumaron AnimeBox, Disney+ y Netflix; Prime Video ofrece la serie a través de un canal de Crunchyroll. Los catálogos y las fechas pueden variar entre países, por lo que conviene comprobar la disponibilidad en cada servicio.
Cuántos episodios tiene Dragon Ball Super Beerus
La nueva entrega está formada por 19 capítulos, publicados semanalmente. No se trata de una temporada completa disponible de una sola vez: cada plataforma sigue un día de estreno propio, así que la cantidad de episodios que se puede ver depende del servicio y del país.
En Latinoamérica, el calendario publicado fija los estrenos de Crunchyroll para los domingos, los de Disney+ para los miércoles, los de HBO Max para los viernes y los de Netflix para los sábados. Si se mantienen esas fechas semanales, el episodio final llegará primero a Crunchyroll, el 14 de febrero de 2027, y después a Disney+, HBO Max y Netflix, entre el 17 y el 20 de febrero.
Quienes quieran ponerse al día pueden revisar cuántos capítulos hay cargados en su plataforma. Si prefieren esperar a que termine la emisión para ver la temporada seguida, tendrán que aguardar hasta que cada servicio publique el episodio 19.
Dónde ver el anime en Latinoamérica
Crunchyroll fue la primera plataforma en estrenar la serie en América Latina, con lanzamiento simultáneo con Japón el 11 de octubre. Después se incorporaron Disney+, el 14; HBO Max, el 16, y Netflix, el 17. Los capítulos llegan semanalmente y con varios días de diferencia entre servicios.
La disponibilidad puede depender del territorio. Por eso, aunque la serie figure en el catálogo regional de una plataforma, el usuario debería buscarla en la aplicación de su país para confirmar que puede reproducirla y conocer las opciones de audio y subtítulos. La ficha de Prime Video, por ejemplo, muestra subtítulos en español latinoamericano, pero no confirma que esa plataforma distribuya la serie en todos los países de la región.
Dónde ver Dragon Ball Super Beerus en España
En España, Crunchyroll y AnimeBox estrenaron el anime el 11 de octubre. Disney+ lo incorporó el 14 y Netflix el 18. Prime Video también presenta la serie mediante la suscripción del canal de Crunchyroll. La oferta, por tanto, es distinta a la de Latinoamérica: allí HBO Max forma parte de las opciones citadas, mientras que AnimeBox corresponde a España.
De qué trata la historia
La trama comienza años después de la derrota de Majin Buu, cuando la Tierra atraviesa una etapa de paz. Esa tranquilidad cambia con el despertar de Beerus, el Dios de la Destrucción, quien oye hablar del Saiyan que venció a Freezer y viaja para buscar a Goku.
El encuentro amenaza con desatar una batalla de escala cósmica. Goku y sus aliados tendrán que encontrar la manera de detener a Beerus, un adversario capaz de destruir planetas. La historia retoma personajes conocidos y presenta el conflicto de forma accesible para quienes se acercan por primera vez a la franquicia.
Dragon Ball Super Beerus ofrece una versión renovada del anime, con escenas nuevas y redibujadas, mejoras visuales y una narración reconstruida, según Disney+. Con 19 episodios y estrenos semanales, los espectadores de Latinoamérica y España pueden seguir el regreso de Goku, aunque deberán elegir la plataforma según su país y el calendario que prefieran.

articles.title: Revolut, Lloyds, HSBC… les banques britanniques dans la tourmente, un incident Google Cloud ?
articles.text:
Outre Revolut, d’autres banques britanniques comme Lloyds, HSBC ou NatWest enregistrent ce mardi une vague de signalements. Au même moment, Google Cloud reconnaît un incident d’ampleur sur ses serveurs de Londres, sans en préciser l’origine.
La panne de Revolut, qui bloque depuis ce mardi 20 octobre 2026 les cartes et application de nombreux clients jusqu'en France, pourrait bien n'être que la partie visible de l'immense iceberg qui cache les banques… britanniques. Oui, Outre-Manche, les signalements grimpent aussi chez Lloyds, HSBC, NatWest ou Santander, pour une matinée du 20 octobre 2026 franchement agitée. En coulisses, un nom revient avec insistance, celui de Google Cloud, qui admet de sérieux déboires dans ses installations londoniennes.
Après Revolut, plusieurs grandes banques britanniques en panne
Chez Revolut, la journée a mal débuté. Dès 8 heures, l'application affichait un message d'erreur, la carte était refusée au supermarché ou dans un taxi, et les virements impossibles. Les plaintes ont afflué du Royaume-Uni, son pays d'origine, mais aussi de France où la banque compte plus de 8 millions de clients, d'Espagne, d'Allemagne ou de Grèce, et l'offre Revolut Business n'est pas épargnée. L'entreprise a reconnu une interruption touchant plusieurs fonctionnalités, sans avancer ni cause ni horaire. Sa page de statut, restée au vert une bonne partie de la matinée, affichait au dernier relevé ses 31 services comme indisponibles, même si certains clients arrivent encore à payer en magasin.
Sur Downdetector, le site qui agrège les signalements d'internautes, la version britannique affiche en tête de sa page d'accueil un trio éloquent avec Revolut, Lloyds Bank, HSBC et, un peu plus loin, Google et Google Cloud. Bank of Scotland est aussi passée au rouge, tout comme Halifax, Scottish Widows, MBNA, NatWest et Santander UK, qui présentaient encore tout à l'heure des pics suspects. Or Lloyds, Halifax, Bank of Scotland, Scottish Widows et MBNA appartiennent toutes au même groupe bancaire.
Les opérateurs télécoms (BT, EE, Vodafone, O2) ne présentent aucune anomalie. Ce ne serait donc pas l'internet britannique qui cale, mais plutôt des services hébergés quelque part. Le désordre dépasse d'ailleurs le cadre bancaire, avec des signalements chez Royal Mail, Rightmove ou sur le portail gouvernemental GOV.UK.
Le cloud de Google sous les projecteurs
Ce « quelque part » pourrait bien s'appeler europe-west2, la région londonienne de Google Cloud, autrement dit un ensemble de centres de données où les entreprises louent serveurs et stockage. Google y signale un incident depuis 8h08, heure de Paris, et liste une trentaine de produits touchés, avec les machines virtuelles, bases de données, stockage et réseau. La seule consigne concrète, ajoutée à 11h24, est destinée aux entreprises clientes : déplacer, si elles le peuvent, leurs applications vers une autre zone ou une autre région. Une région se découpe en effet en plusieurs « zones », des compartiments isolés les uns des autres pour limiter la casse en cas d'incident, et Google ne précise pas lesquelles sont touchées. Sur Reddit, un administrateur système affirme que les problèmes se concentrent sur l'une d'elles, europe-west2-b, les autres restant accessibles.
Or ces briques forment les fondations de n'importe quelle application. Une banque dont les serveurs tournent à cet endroit peut perdre d'un coup l'accès à ses données et la capacité de valider un paiement, ce qui expliquerait une carte refusée en caisse. Le calendrier coïncide à peu de chose près avec les premiers déboires de Revolut, et une panne cantonnée à une seule zone éclairerait aussi pourquoi tous les clients ne sont pas logés à la même enseigne.
Attention toutefois, car ni Google ni les banques concernées n'ont officiellement établi de lien, et rien ne garantit qu'elles soient toutes hébergées chez le même fournisseur. Downdetector a aussi ses biais, comme en témoignent les pics affichés par AWS ou Azure, parfois signalés par simple réflexe un jour de grosse panne. Google, qui n'a toujours livré ni cause ni horaire de rétablissement, promet un nouveau point vers 13 heures. Sa région londonienne avait déjà vacillé en 2020 puis en 2024, rappel assez cru qu'une seule région cloud peut suffire à gripper une partie du système bancaire, surtout quand le plan B consiste à déménager en pleine tempête.

articles.title: This Dell workstation costs less than the Nvidia Blackwell GPU inside it
articles.text:
Dell’s Pro Max Tower T2 workstation costs less than the Nvidia Blackwell GPU inside it
Impossibly good value for the Nvidia RTX Pro Blackwell 6000 GPU alone
This is an odd one - and I don't know how long it'll last, but right now you can get the Dell Pro Max Tower T2 workstation with Blackwell GPU for $15,149 at Dell.
Now, it's an excellent desktop - we scored it 4.5 stars in our review and found it ideal for pure, uncompromising performance in intensive workflows. But the reason it's so strange to me is because the Nvidia RTX Pro Blackwell 6000 graphics card alone is priced at $16,400 at EmpoweredPC (and $26,900 at Newegg).
So you're effectively buying the card cheaper than anywhere I can find, and getting a free desktop PC on top.
• Best for: Enterprise professionals, AI researchers, and creative studio engineers.
• What we like: I still can't get over the cost of this machine relative to the price of a standalone Blackwell 6000 GPU. As ever with Dell machines we've tested, it's hugely upgradeable and configurable for just about any demanding workload.
• What to know: Most business professionals won't need Blackwell graphics - this is best for those who want to run complex tasks direct from the desktop.
Today's best Dell PC deal
Like most Dell PCs, the Pro Max T2 is available in a range of configurations. This is the cheapest one with the Nvidia RTX Pro Blackwell 6000 GPU, running Windows 11 Pro on an Intel Core Ultra 5 235 CPU, 8GB DDR5, and 256GB SSD. But you can spec the machine to fit any workload.
Why we recommend it
Scoring 4.5 stars in our review, and awarded a TechRadar Pro Highly Recommended badge, the Dell Pro Max T2 impressed us as we ran it alongside engineers working with large data warehouses, AI, 3D modeling, 4K and 6K video editing, and large-scale visual events. The workstation never missed a beat. We called it "a beast of a machine for professionals who need uncompromising power in engineering, AI, and all-around business performance, and who want a machine that is capable today and upgradable for the future."
For more top-performing PCs, we've tested out the best business computers.
Price context & historical value
The price for the workstation with this GPU is about what I'd expect in today's market. The real value is getting that Blackwell 6000 graphics card for less than you can buy it on its own.
I've listed the cheapest Blackwell config here. However, for truly demanding tasks, I'd recommend bumping up the memory to 32GB - although you can go as high as 128GB, and potentially increasing storage from the base 256GB (Dell sells configurations up to 4TB).
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the Dell Pro Max T2 if...
You want a high-performance workstation desktop for complicated workloads, AI, or production-grade creative projects.
❌ Skip the Dell Pro Max T2 if...
You need a business PC for largely administrative or general content creation tasks. You could spec out the Pro Max T2 for that, but personally, I rate the highly configurable Dell Tower Plus (EBT2250).

articles.title: Hay disturbios y saqueos en Francia, así que Vinted se ha llenado de anuncios muy sospechosos de Sephora, Louis Vuitton y Burberry
articles.text:
Francia vive unos días convulsos marcados por las protestas por el precio de la vida que han acabado con la capital envuelta por el humo de las barricadas en llamas. Entre cargas policiales y disturbios, los escaparates de las tiendas de lujo de Paris saltaron en pedazos y más de 50 comercios se vieron afectadas en solo una noche de disturbios.
Tras unas horas, parte del botín obtenido en esos saqueos busca salida. El lugar elegido es la app en la que media Francia compra vaqueros usados: Vinted.
Una noche que se fue de las manos. Según recogía Euronews con datos del Ministerio de Interior francés, las protestas del 17 de octubre contra el coste de la vida terminaron con saqueos en París, Lyon y otras ciudades. Casi 2.400 personas fueron detenidas y cerca de 1.000 agentes resultaron heridos. El primer ministro, Sébastien Lecornu, habló de una "violencia de extrema intensidad".
Lyon amaneció entre escombros y escaparates rotos. Más de 3.000 comercios sufrieron daños, contaba el loca L'Avenir. Catherine Spindler, presidenta de Sephora en Europa, admitió que varios de sus locales fueron saqueados por los manifestantes.
Un llamamiento a las plataformas de venta. Desde el domingo circulan capturas de anuncios con mercancía que parece robada durante esos saqueos. Anne Le Hénanff, ministra francesa de Asuntos Digitales hacía un llamamiento inmediato a las plataformas de venta de segunda mano como Vinted, Amazon, eBay, Leboncoin, Meta y TikTok.
"Esperamos de estas plataformas que retiren sin demora los anuncios en cuestión", pedía la ministra, al tiempo que advertía a los asaltantes: "Tales comportamientos no quedarán impunes. No dejaremos pasar esto".
Las plataformas han tomado cartas en el asunto. Le Hénanff y su homólogo de Comercio, Serge Papin, y representantes de Justicia e Interior se reunieron de inmediato con las plataformas de venta para bloquear las ventas y llevar a los vendedores ante la justicia.
Varios usuarios denunciaron perfiles de vendedores que vendían bolsas enteras con productos de cosmética de Sephora con etiqueta, zapatillas deportivas, prendas de Louis Vuitton en cuyos anuncios se reconocía explícitamente que habían sido robadas en Paris. En un comunicado enviado al francés Le Monde, Vinted asegura que ha "tomado medidas inmediatas para identificar y eliminar los anuncios vinculados a los saqueos".
La plataforma asegura que aplica una política de "tolerancia cero" hacia la venta de artículos robados y que coopera "activamente" con las autoridades: "Desde este fin de semana, nuestros equipos han actuado de inmediato para identificar y eliminar anuncios que probablemente involucren artículos robados, y hemos reforzado la vigilancia de anuncios sospechosos.
Vinted ya tiene experiencia. En 2023, los disturbios por la muerte de Nahel Merzouk dejaron un escenario de protestas y disturbios muy parecido. Los productos robados en aquellos saqueos también llegaron a las plataformas de venta de segunda mano. Vinted respondió entonces endureciendo sus normas del catálogo y se prohíbe explícitamente vender artículos robados. También dejan fuera los testers y las muestras promocionales no destinados a la venta, algo común en cosmética, para evitar dejar una grieta por la que puedan colarse estos productos.
El Código Penal francés castiga la compra o aceptación de mercancía robada con hasta cinco años de cárcel y 375.000 euros de multa. En este caso, algunos de los anuncios reconocen que se trata de mercancía expoliada de las tiendas, por lo que los compradores de estos productos también están sujetos a sanción porque Vinted lleva el registro de operaciones en su plataforma.

articles.title: Chris Lattner: AI Code Generation Doesn't Solve Software Engineering - EE Times
articles.text:
For AI chip companies, the promise of AI-based coding agents is compelling: generate the low-level kernels needed to get a model running on new hardware, optimize them for performance, and do it without the software engineering resources traditionally required.
But according to Chris Lattner, CEO of AI software startup Modular (recently acquired by Qualcomm, where he now serves as executive VP of software engineering), chip companies should be wary of the limits of AI code generation. Making a kernel run fast is a very different problem from building software infrastructure we can depend on, he told EE Times in an exclusive interview.
“Agents are good, but they’re like anything else; it’s a tool, and you have to use it the right way,” Lattner said. “What I’ve seen with agents is they make tons of throwaway code. So, if you’re building a product, you don’t want to agent-generate everything.”
Agentic code generation makes sense for projects that are well-defined and limited in scope (e.g., “make this kernel go fast”), which can be quantified, measured, and validated, Lattner said, but bigger projects require product design and software engineering and can’t be delegated to agents.
“If you’re a startup and you only care about getting one model working, or getting it to go fast, [then go ahead,] use AI tools to prove it’s possible,” he said. “But that’s not going to be great for when you want to sell your chip to someone else, and they want to run a model you don’t have access to.”
Lattner said that despite some high-profile companies’ performance claims for their AI-generated low-level software, there are still many unanswered questions, including the dollar cost to generate large amounts of code and its applicability to large, open-ended problems.
“I have heard of hardware companies that say they don’t believe in software anymore; they just want to use agents to generate everything,” Lattner said. “I think that’s interesting because they’re definitely using LLVM and still investing in compilers, but saying they’re not. So there’s a divergence between the party line and what’s actually happening.”
Writing performant low-level code for new and novel hardware has long been a difficult task for chip companies, and some are now relying on agents for this.
“Various people use [agentic code generation] as a talking point, particularly when their software is known to be problematic,” Lattner said. “So, I don’t really know what to believe in all these cases… great claims need great proof.”
Porting code
While AI is useful in some use cases, it can’t be used for everything, Lattner said. AI might help get a demo up and running, but this isn’t the same as writing a usable software stack with determinism and adaptability.
“The hard part about building a company or building a product or building something meaningful in the world is understanding the product requirements,” he said. “What is the marketing story? What is the product-market fit that you have to get for your product? I think that remains quite hard.”
At Modular, teams use agentic code generation for tasks such as porting PyTorch code into the company’s Max AI framework and for porting CUDA code to its programming language Mojo. Lattner said that porting code is a great use case for AI, along with specializing existing software (for example, specializing a matmul kernel for a specific size of matrix), since the agent can do this quickly and efficiently.
People will always need to know how to code, he said, since prompting in English isn’t precise enough to get a good result.
“It’s true things are changing very rapidly—I use AI to write code, and I wouldn’t go back, personally—but that doesn’t mean that writing code was the job,” he said. “If you go back five years, more code was read than written.”
Open source under pressure
The downsides to AI code generation are still making themselves apparent in the world of software. Lattner identified open-source projects, the backbone of much of modern software, as being particularly under threat.
“Open-source projects like LLVM are under assault,” he said.
Before generative AI, people who wanted to contribute to open-source projects were motivated by the satisfaction of identifying and fixing problems, most often because they were using the software themselves and wanted to contribute. Making changes meant they had to invest a certain amount of time. Maintainers, people who had been working on the project for a long time, reviewed contributions for quality and worked with the community to teach them the nuances of the codebase. Lattner said the investment in teaching contributors improved the code.
“Today, that model is broken, because people are just vibe coding tons of patches and sending them to tons of projects, and the maintainers are getting completely overwhelmed with AI crap,” he said.
The deluge of AI-generated code is increasing the workload for maintainers, who have to review and iterate code before accepting it, Lattner said.
“And then the submitter doesn’t actually care, so the investment back into the human doesn’t lead to a future maintainer; it leads to someone who walks away, or just sets up their agents to spam a bunch of different projects to try to get GitHub badges,” he said. “This is a huge issue, so a lot of projects have stopped accepting contributions.”
The response from open-source projects such as LLVM has been to consider working only with established contributors, a move Lattner described as “terrifying.”
“The value of open-source projects is the humans, it’s the relationships, it’s the tribal knowledge,” he said. “If you destroy that, there’s going to be a huge problem… Running an open-source project and making it successful has always been super hard, so this is another pretty big threat.”
This is a huge challenge for all open-source projects today.
Modular’s programming language, Mojo, was recently open-sourced, but contributions aren’t yet being accepted. Lattner said the company intends to open to submissions gradually.
“It’s not just about the lines of code; it’s about the social side of things—if you have an employee that’s investing their effort into someone else, traditionally the thought would be, we’re investing in you, and if you’re good we’ll hire you, or [something might come out of it],” he said.
Things will stabilize, Lattner said. AI code review tools will improve, easing some of the burden, but ultimately, code review is difficult to automate completely because it requires judgement.
“What you’re building doesn’t just need to pass a test; it needs to be able to support the architecture we need for tomorrow and the future,” he said. “Models tomorrow will be better and faster, but I think these are inherent structural problems.”
Max alliance
For startups without the resources to build a state-of-the-art software stack, Lattner is planning on opening up Max, Modular’s AI framework, by starting an alliance for hardware makers. The alliance is planned to kick off around the end of the year, he said.
“This will be a big deal,” Lattner said. “We’re saying to everyone who has chips: You now have software. A lot of startups have been asking for help, but we always had to say no; we couldn’t scale to support them. Now we’ll be able to say yes, you can do it for yourself.”
Coding agents can solve for a specific kernel for a specific chip, but today’s complex, disaggregated, heterogeneous data center needs orchestration, scaling, and management, all of which must be handled by software, Lattner said.
“We’ve been building this for four and a half years—now you’ll be able to use it and scale it for yourself,” he said.
This is part of Qualcomm’s plan for Modular, Lattner said.
“[Qualcomm] wants it to be an open ecosystem so [its data center chip] can compete on its own merits,” he said. “Qualcomm is modest enough to understand it can’t [overtake Nvidia]. There will be a lot of different players with great contributions in different parts of the value chain, but it needs to be an open ecosystem.”
The Max alliance will enable edge chip companies and markets such as China, which Lattner is looking forward to.
“This is going to be very, very fun and exciting,” he said.

articles.title: Scaled Cognition targets customer service with low-cost voice model - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Scaled Cognition targets customer service with low-cost voice model
Scaled Cognition Inc., an artificial intelligence lab building models for enterprise customer service agents, is introducing a text-to-speech model today that it says provides more accurate pronunciation of account numbers, addresses and other details at a lower cost than competing services.
The product, called Voice, is available through an application programming interface or for self-hosted deployment. It supports more than 25 languages, voice cloning and can work with existing artificial intelligence agents, contact center platforms and older telephone systems. Voice cloning creates a digital replica of a given person’s voice.
The launch targets a gap between natural-sounding speech and AI that reliably communicates information customers need to complete transactions.
“Modern generative TTS models can sound fantastic, but they often stumble over the details that matter most in customer service, like reading back an alphanumeric confirmation code, a dollar amount or a street address,” Akshay Kannan, vice president of product management at Scaled Cognition, said in e-mailed comments.
Those difficulties become more pronounced in languages other than English, Kannan said. Scaled Cognition said Voice enables enterprises to get natural-sounding speech and accurate readings without paying premium prices.
Voice costs $9 per million characters through the hosted API or $1 per million characters for self-hosting. The latter figure excludes the infrastructure needed to operate it.
Kannan explained how the math works out to lower costs than competing providers. One graphics processing unit can handle about 32 simultaneous conversations using Voice. A redundant setup using two GPUs on standard cloud hardware costs roughly $6,000 a month and supports about 500 million characters, he said.
Including infrastructure, Kannan estimated costs at about $13 per million characters at that 500 million-character rate and less than $7 at 1.5 billion. He compared that to between $35 and $100 per million characters charged by other hosted voices, which he declined to name.
“Self-hosting gets economical faster than people expect,” he said.
Cloud option
At low usage, the self-hosting cost can exceed Scaled Cognition’s hosted API price. “Most of the enterprises we work with already run their own infrastructure, so Voice just drops in,” Kannan said. “For teams that don’t want to manage it, we host it for them.”
The company also claims 70 milliseconds of speech-generation latency, the time from receiving text to starting speech, rather than the total time an AI system takes to understand a caller and formulate an answer.
“Even with 16 live conversations sharing a single GPU slice, typical response time stays around 80 milliseconds,” he said. “The biggest factor customers control is distance.” Running Voice in the same cloud region as the rest of a call stack adds only a millisecond or two of latency. “That’s a big reason we let enterprises self-host it right next to their agents and telephony,” Kannan said.
One of the distinctive features of Voice is its ability to interpret meaning before generating audio, the company said. For example, its Smart Pronunciation capability determines whether abbreviations refer to titles, street names or other information and how numbers should be spoken. For example, it reads “Pay 1/2 by 1/2” as “pay half by January second.”
“Voice doesn’t just read text left to right,” Kannan said. “Before it says a word, Smart Pronunciation works out what the sentence actually means, powered by the same customer-experience-tuned intelligence behind our APT model.”
APT is the company’s model for customer-service conversations and actions in enterprise systems. When the products are paired, APT supplies conversation context that can help Voice resolve ambiguities beyond an individual sentence.
Voice doesn’t require APT or another large language model to operate. “It streams audio through a standard API and is tuned for phone audio, so anything that can send text and play back speech can use it, from modern AI agents and contact center platforms to legacy [interactive voice response systems],” Kannan said.
That compatibility could give enterprises a way to update interactive voice response systems without replacing the underlying applications.
Scaled Cognition is also offering a blind listening test that compares Voice with other models across price ranges. Kannan said early feedback favored Voice, although the supplied materials did not provide sample sizes or detailed results.
The company, which raised $100 million in Series A funding led by Khosla Ventures LLC, is positioning speech as another component of its enterprise AI platform.

articles.title: Rumor: NVIDIA RTX 6060 May Be Years Away, and Possibly Slower Than the PS6
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
Rumor: NVIDIA RTX 6060 May Be Years Away, and Possibly Slower Than the PS6
Anyone holding out for an affordable next-gen NVIDIA card might have a long wait. Hardware leaker Kepler_L2 claims on NeoGAF that the GeForce RTX 6060 will "launch much later," adding that, based on recent trends, he doubts it will even match the PlayStation 6. He was replying to a forum member who argued the PS6 would compete with the RTX 6060, in the same thread where he claimed the console's RAM and storage alone cost over $680. Kepler didn't give an actual date, and the 2029 figure going around seems to be an extrapolation. Both Kepler and kopite7kimi have placed NVIDIA's Rubin-based RTX 60 series in 2028, and the x60 cards usually trail the flagship by a few months. The RTX 5060 arrived under four months after the RTX 5090, while the RTX 4060 took over eight months to follow the RTX 4090. 
With a flagship launch around mid-2028 or later, that could push the RTX 6060 into 2029. That said, the "much later" comment seems to be relative to the PS6, which is reportedly targeting late 2027, so the exact timing is still anyone's guess. Kepler didn't say why, but the ongoing memory shortage looks like the obvious suspect. NVIDIA reportedly postponed its RTX 50 SUPER refresh earlier this year to prioritize AI products that use the same GDDR7 memory, and the company recently admitted that RTX 5090 supply is tight. Of course, NVIDIA hasn't announced the RTX 60 series officially yet, so treat this as a rumor. Anyone looking to buy a new NVIDIA GPU should probably expect the current RTX 50 lineup to stick around for quite a while.

articles.title: Marshall Heston 120 : la finition Cream s'invite sur la barre de son haut de gamme
articles.text:
Marshall Heston 120 : la finition Cream s'invite sur la barre de son haut de gamme
Plus claire et résolument désirable, la finition Cream arrive le 20 octobre sur la Heston 120, la barre de son Dolby Atmos la plus ambitieuse de Marshall. De quoi transformer le modèle en véritable objet de design pour le salon, et l'occasion de revenir sur un produit qui revendique son esthétique autant que ses performances home cinéma.
Marshall a toujours puisé dans l'esthétique de ses amplis pour dessiner ses enceintes. La Heston 120 ne fait pas exception. Chez Marshall, une barre de son n'est jamais un simple accessoire de téléviseur : c'est un objet que l'on expose, au même titre qu'une guitare accrochée au mur ou qu'un ampli posé dans un coin du salon. Jusqu'ici réservée à une livrée noire, la barre de son s'offre une déclinaison Cream. Plus lumineuse, cette nouvelle finition ouvre la Heston 120 à des univers déco plus clairs et contemporains. Le reste de l'appareil, lui, ne change pas d'un hertz.
Une couleur qui modifie le statut de l'objet
La finition Cream fait plus que rafraîchir une fiche produit. Associée aux commandes physiques crantées et aux cadrans inspirés des amplificateurs maison, elle déplace la Heston 120 du côté du meuble assumé plutôt que de l'électronique que l'on cherche à masquer. Les habitués de la marque y retrouveront la grammaire visuelle des Stanmore et autres Woburn, transposée cette fois sous le téléviseur. Un parti pris esthétique qui vaut autant que ses arguments techniques, et que Marshall place désormais au centre de sa promesse.
Home cinéma : Dolby Atmos et configuration 5.1.2
Sous le capot, la Heston 120 aligne onze amplificateurs de classe D pour 150 watts, répartis sur une configuration 5.1.2 compatible Dolby Atmos et DTS:X. L'enjeu est clair : restituer une scène sonore en hauteur sans multiplier les enceintes dans la pièce. Deux subwoofers orientés vers l'arrière et quatre radiateurs passifs se chargent des basses, ce qui permet à la barre de se passer d'un caisson dédié dans la plupart des salons. Les plus exigeants pourront tout de même brancher un subwoofer actif via la sortie prévue à cet effet. Quatre modes d'écoute, dont un mode nuit et un mode voix, ajustent le rendu selon le contenu.
De l'écran éteint à la playlist
Marshall n'oublie pas que sa clientèle est d’abord composée de mélomanes intransigeants. Une fois le téléviseur en veille, la Heston 120 redevient une enceinte musicale à part entière, connectée en Wi-Fi 6 comme en Bluetooth 5.3 avec prise en charge d'Auracast. Spotify, TIDAL et le service de radios « airable » sont intégrés directement, AirPlay 2 et Google Cast complétant l'éventail fonctionnel. L'application Marshall autorise par ailleurs un réglage fin de l'égaliseur et un calibrage acoustique de la pièce. De quoi justifier une présence au salon toute la journée, et pas seulement pour les séances cinéma…
La finition Cream s'inscrit dans une gamme home cinéma désormais étoffée, aux côtés de la Heston 60, du caisson Sub 200 et de la Heston 120 noire. Plus compacte, la Heston 60 reprend le même ADN (configuration 5.1 Dolby Atmos, design signature Marshall et finition Cream) pour les salons plus modestes. Pour la découvrir en détail, rendez-vous sur la page produit officielle de la Heston 120.

articles.title: Online retail market to cross $90b in 2026 with grocery overtaking mobiles: Redseer
articles.text:
Online retail market to cross $90b in 2026 with grocery overtaking mobiles: Redseer
The gross merchandise value of India’s ecommerce market expanded roughly 25% on a year-on-year basis to about $38 billion in the first half of 2026, marking its strongest H1 performance in four years.
India's online retail market is projected to cross $90 billion in 2026, registering an annual growth of 22-24%, its fastest expansion in five years, driven by everyday consumption categories such as grocery rather than mobile phones, Redseer Strategy Consultants said in a report.
According to the analysis, ecommerce gross merchandise value (GMV) expanded roughly 25% year-on-year to about $38 billion in the first half (H1) of 2026, marking its strongest H1 performance in four years.
While online retail accelerated, mobile sales remained flat at 0% growth during the first half and are projected to grow by just 2-3% across the full year due to sharp price increases curbing sales volumes.
Consequently, the grocery segment is poised to overtake mobile phones as the second-largest category in Indian ecommerce, behind fashion.
"This year, India's online retail is growing fastest where demand is steadiest," said Kushal Bhatnagar, Partner at Redseer.
The report noted that grocery, beauty and personal care (BPC), and home and furniture will account for about 40% of overall online retail GMV in 2026 and roughly three-fifths of the incremental GMV added during the year.
Grocery alone is projected to account for nearly a third of the added GMV, expanding 50-53% for the full year and lifting its market share from 16% in 2025 to 19% in 2026. Mobiles, which accounted for around 19% of total sales last year, are expected to see their market share drop to roughly 16%.
BPC is projected to rise 36-39%, while home and furniture is estimated to expand 31-34% in 2026.
In contrast, electronics experienced a 22% rebound in H1 2026 after contracting 5% in the corresponding period of 2025. Redseer attributed this spike to "pre-loaded" demand, spurred by the reduction of goods and services tax (GST) on large appliances from 28% to 18% in September 2025, heavy discounting on air conditioners due to changes in Bureau of Energy Efficiency star ratings, an LPG shortage driving a 200–300% surge in induction cooktops, and early laptop purchases ahead of expected component price increases.

articles.title: Criptomonedas: cuál es su precio en el mercado este martes 20 de octubre
articles.text:
Las criptomonedas son un activo digital innovador que han experimentado un crecimiento monumental en los últimos tiempos debido a varios elementos que contribuyen a ello, entre ellos que algunos gobiernos hayan decidido darles una oportunidad como moneda de curso legal; no obstante, también han sufrido descalabros que han puesto en duda su viabilidad, como el más reciente episodio conocido como el "criptoinvierno".
Pese a este panorama, cada vez más personas han empezado a adquirir criptomonedas para poder invertir en algo "seguro" y "fiable" tanto a corto como a largo plazo, a pesar de los niveles extremos de inestabilidad que sufre constantemente.
Sin embargo, invertir o comprar en criptodivisas es más fácil de lo que parece. Hay que recordar que se trata de monedas virtuales, por lo que serán controladas en carteras o monederos que comparten esa particularidad, pues a diferencia del dinero corriente, no tienen un soporte físico.
El precio de las criptomonedas hoy
Esta es la cotización de las criptodivisas más destacadas en este momento.
El Bitcoin, cotiza a 81.569,17 dólares, lo que implicó un cambio de -0,347% en las últimas horas.
La segunda criptomoneda más popular del mercado, Ethereum, ha mostrado un movimiento de -0,501% en las últimas 24 horas, por lo que su valor se ubica en 2.392,77 dólares.
En el caso de TetherUs, su precio es de 1 dólares, por lo que en el último día tuvo un movimiento de -0,01%.
Por su parte, BNB, tiene un valor de 729,16 dólares, con un cambio de 0,96%, en cambio el Litecoin cotizó a 59.407 dólares, tras una variación de 0.5668745.
Finalmente, el Dogecoin, una de las monedas virtuales que fue impulsada por Elon Musk, tiene un valor de 0,08 dólares tras presentar un cambio de -0,04% en las últimas 24 horas.
Qué pasa con las criptodivisas
Luego de que en las primeras semanas de mayo del 2022 se viviera el "criptocrash" o "criptoinvierno" que dejaron al descubierto la enorme volatilidad de estas monedas digitales, ha llegado un nuevo periodo de relativa estabilidad.
Bitcoin, ethereum y BNB han mostrado variaciones "controladas", puesto que no se han disparado los precios como en semanas previas. Por ejemplo, a inicios de agosto, las mencionadas anteriormente tuvieron un cambio menor del 2%.
Por otra parte, algo que esta llamando la atención en el mundo de las criptomonedas es que China está ablandando sus restricciones y podría comenzar a permitir su uso. Específicamente sería Hong Kong en donde este cambio se haría presente.
Sumado a ello, la plataforma de transacciones digitales PayPal anunció su propia stablecoin llamada PayPal USD (PYUSD), que cuenta por el respaldo de depósitos en dólares, bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos a corto plazo y activos equivalentes.
La compañía ha afirmado en su declaración que permitirá la transferencia de fondos a monederos digitales de terceros y proporcionará detalles sobre cómo integrar su servicio en exchanges centralizados y descentralizados, con el objetivo de ser utilizado en Finanzas Descentralizadas (DeFi, por sus siglas en inglés). Por lo tanto, es muy probable que se utilice ampliamente en la industria Web3.
Criptomonedas en Latinoamérica
Criptomonedas en México: el Banco de México (Banxico) ha determinado que ninguna de las instituciones que participan en el sistema financiero nacional podrá hacer uso o deberá permitir operaciones de ninguna clase a través de este medio de pago.
En territorio mexicano el empresario Ricardo Salinas Pliego, uno de los más ricos del país, ha mostrado interés en las criptomonedas y ha asegurado que varios de sus negocios aceptarán bitcoin en el futuro, incluido su banco; hasta el momento una de sus tiendas más populares ya lo hace.
Criptomonedas en Perú: el Banco Central de Reserva del Perú (BCR) ha dejado en claro que su misión no es ser el primero ni el segundo banco central que regule el uso de las criptomonedas, ello debido a la inestabilidad que las caracteriza. Sin embargo, hace días el presidente del (BCR) aseguró que el BCR trabajaba en un proyecto de moneda digital propia.
Criptomonedas en Colombia: en la nación sudamericana hay más de 500 sitios donde es permitido pagar con criptodivisas. Colombia ocupa el puesto 14 entre 26 países de adopción de criptomonedas, según el informe de Finder.
Criptomonedas en Centroamérica: en el gobierno de El Salvador, el bitcoin, que en septiembre de 2021 se convirtió en moneda de curso legal, ha perdido oficialmente este estatus en este enero del 2025 tras una reforma aprobada por la Asamblea Legislativa del país. Según informó la prensa local, la modificación de la Ley Bitcoin fue impulsada por el gobierno del presidente Nayib Bukele y respaldada por la mayoría oficialista en el órgano legislativo. Este cambio marca el fin de una política que había colocado al país centroamericano en el centro del debate global sobre las criptomonedas.
¿Cómo crear una criptomoneda?
Al momento de crear una criptomoneda es importante primero determinar qué se desea tener: una moneda o un token. La primera usa su propia blockchain, mientras que la segunda se basa en una red preexistente.
De acuerdo con el sitio de Binance, para crear una criptomoneda se necesita de un gran equipo de desarrolladores y expertos; mientras que para el token sí se requieren conocimientos técnicos pero es posible crearlo en minutos a través del uso de otras blockchains como Ethereum o BNB, que son las más populares.
Los costos de creación, el tiempo requerido y el uso de fuerza de trabajo dependerá de si se opta por hacer una moneda virtual o un token. En éste último caso también se puede usar un código establecido para crear tokens o pagar para usar un servicio de creación de monedas.
Es importante saber que antes de crear una criptomoneda se debe considerar su utilidad y estado legal.
En el caso de elegir crear una criptomoneda, entonces se debe elegir una blockchain, posteriormente se debe hacer un plan acorde al funcionamiento y la funcionalidad de la blockchain para diseñar los nodos y la interfaz.

articles.title: Clicked on your desktop and got a Bing search out of nowhere? Windows 11 users with Bing Wallpaper are having to suffer Microsoft's promotional nonsense (again)
articles.text:
Microsoft has gone too far promoting Bing search, as Windows 11 users are again having to suffer a confusing and weird 'feature' in the Bing Wallpaper app
And this time you can't turn off these spontaneous Bing searches
- The Bing Wallpaper app has seen an annoying feature reintroduced
- This means those clicking on a blank space of the Windows 11 desktop will get a Bing search fired up in their default browser
- Unlike the last time Microsoft tried this stunt, there's no way to disable the ability this time around
Microsoft is up to its old tricks again, except even worse this time — with a scheme whereby Windows 11 users with the Bing Wallpaper app installed are sent to its search engine with a mere stray click on the desktop.
Windows Latest reports that an old, potentially off-putting shortcut has been reintroduced to the Bing Wallpaper app, whereby if you click anywhere on the Windows 11 desktop, a search in the (separate) Bing engine is fired up (in your default web browser).
If you recall, this actually happened a year ago, but Microsoft reversed course, although now appears to be trying to reintroduce this feature. The difference is that this time around, Windows Latest notes that there's no option to turn off the functionality (which was present last year, in the app's settings).
However, there are some points to note here: firstly that you must choose to install the Bing Wallpaper app (which cycles Bing images daily for your desktop background). It's not a default Windows 11 app, so this isn't something Microsoft is piping directly to Windows users.
Secondly, the Bing search doesn't trigger every time you click on a blank piece of desktop (a space without a file, folder or icon). It does this once, and then the Bing search won't be triggered for another 24 hours. You'll only experience this once per day, in other words.
Analysis: Microsoft must do better
Just because this app isn't part of Windows 11 by default doesn't give Microsoft the excuse to push functionality like this. It's just going to annoy or even confuse people if they accidentally click the desktop and end up with a Bing search being loaded.
The search relates to the wallpaper image, in case you're curious, and fair enough – maybe some folks might be inquisitive and actually want to know more about the picture by clicking on it.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
However, this should be an ability that's optional and can be turned on, not something that's enabled by default. What's worse still is that in this new incarnation of the click-to-Bing farce, you can't even turn it off if you want to do so.
Why is Microsoft engaging with this kind of nonsense to promote its own services? I really can't begin to guess given that 2026 is the year of fixing Windows 11 and curing all the ills around the OS, and while this app may not be part of the operating system, it's still a piece of official Microsoft software – and there shouldn't be any place for this cynical Bing traffic grab or any other remotely anti-consumer practices.
Whether it's a part of Windows by default, or not – or whether you have to be 'foolish' to install the Bing Wallpaper app, as some online commenters argue – is besides the point. Microsoft is supposed to be better than this now, but another episode with a recent Harry Potter advert in this Bing app – one that provoked a considerable rebellion – suggests that it very much needs to try harder.

articles.title: Der Mond zieht sich weiter zusammen – warum die schrumpfende Kruste künftige Missionen gefährden könnte
articles.text:
45 Meter kleinerer Radius: Warum der schrumpfende Mond die Raumfahrt vor Probleme stellt
Tatsächlich zieht sich der Mond immer weiter zusammen: In seiner jüngsten geologischen Phase, den vergangenen 400 bis 800 Millionen Jahren, hat sich sein Radius um 42 bis 46 Meter verringert, wie in einer im Fachjournal The Planetary Science Journal veröffentlichten Studie zu lesen ist. Ein Forschungsteam um den Geologen Thomas R. Watters vom National Air and Space Museum in Washington, D.C. hat dafür erstmals die jungen Brüche in den gebirgigen Hochländern und in den dunklen Tiefebenen des Mondes gemeinsam ausgewertet.
Auf Bildern der Kamera an Bord der Mondsonde Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LROC) zählten Watters und sein Team insgesamt mehr als 11.500 junge Verwerfungen, an denen die Gesteinskruste gerissen ist. „Die Anzahl dieser jungen Verwerfungen, die auf den LROC-Bildern sichtbar wurden, ist weitaus größer, als ich es mir jemals vorgestellt habe“, erklärt der Studienleiter, wie das Museum in einer Mitteilung schreibt.
Kameradaten des Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter belegen doppelten Krustendruck
Ursache für die Risse ist, dass der Mond seit seiner Entstehung vor rund 4,5 Milliarden Jahren im Inneren langsam auskühlt und sich dabei zusammenzieht. Sichtbar wurden die Brüche auf Aufnahmen der Sonde Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LROC), die den Mond seit Juni 2009 umkreist und vom Goddard Space Flight Center der US-Raumfahrtbehörde Nasa in Greenbelt im US-Bundesstaat Maryland gesteuert wird.
Mit einer Auflösung von bis zu einem halben Meter pro Pixel machte die Bordkamera in den gebirgigen Hochländern über 8.900 bogenförmige Geländestufen sichtbar. An diesen bis zu 164 Meter hohen Klippen hat sich die schrumpfende Kruste an schrägen Brüchen übereinandergeschoben. Hinzu kommen 2.634 flachere Gesteinsfalten in den dunklen Tiefebenen, die Nypaver und seine Kolleg:innen bereits Ende 2025 in einer Voruntersuchung zu den Basaltebenen des Mondes erfasst hatten.
Im Schnitt verkleinert sich der Radius des Mondes dadurch um sechs bis elf Zentimeter pro einer Million Jahre. Das entspricht einem Zehntausendstel Millimeter pro Jahr. Weil die Forscher:innen nun aber deutlich mehr Brüche kennen als noch im Jahr 2015, fällt der berechnete Druck in der äußeren Gesteinsschale mit vier statt zuvor zwei Megapascal doppelt so hoch aus. Das entspricht einem Druck von 40 Bar, vergleichbar mit etwa dem 16-fachen eines gewöhnlichen Autoreifens.
Einplattenkörper Mond: Wo die Kruste unter Spannung bricht
Dieser Druckwert deckt sich mit dem Spannungsabfall jener flachen Mondbeben, die zwischen 1969 und 1977 von den Seismometern der Apollo-Missionen aufgezeichnet wurden, und deutet darauf hin, dass Gesteinsbrüche auch in größeren Tiefen auftreten können. Anders als die Erde, deren äußere Hülle in mehr als 15 bewegliche Platten unterteilt ist, besitzt der Mond als sogenannter Einplattenkörper eine einzige, geschlossene Gesteinsschale.
Kühlt das Innere ab, bricht die Oberfläche deshalb nicht an festen Plattenrändern auf, sondern gibt dem Druck über den gesamten Mond verteilt nach. Besonders oft reißt die Gesteinsschale dort, wo sie eine mittlere Dicke von 30 bis 40 Kilometern hat, wie Messungen der Nasa-Mission Grail belegen. An ihren dicksten Stellen, wie rund um das Orientale-Becken, hält die Kruste den Spannungen hingegen stand und weist nur wenige Brüche auf.
Wärmedämmung aus Gestein: Warum der Mond viel weniger schrumpft als berechnet
Eigentlich hätte der Mond seit seiner Entstehung noch deutlich stärker schrumpfen müssen, denn gängige Computermodelle sagen einen Radiusverlust von 750 Metern bis zu über einem Kilometer voraus. Lange vermuteten Wissenschaftler:innen deshalb, dass der lockere Trümmerboden an der Oberfläche wie ein Schwamm wirkt und die fehlende Schrumpfung ohne sichtbare Risse ausgleicht, indem lose Gesteinsschichten einfach dichter zusammengedrückt werden.
Die Berechnungen des Forschungsteams zeigen jedoch, dass schon die Schwerkraft des Mondes diesen Gesteinsschutt in wenigen Hundert Metern Tiefe so fest zusammenpresst, dass dort kaum noch Hohlräume übrig bleiben. Stattdessen wirkte die mehrere Kilometer dicke Trümmerschicht über Milliarden Jahre wie eine Wärmedämmung, die die Hitze im Inneren einschloss und den Mond erst in den vergangenen 800 Millionen Jahren stärker auskühlen und schrumpfen ließ.
Mondbeben und Hangrutsche als Risiko für das Artemis-Programm der Nasa
Weil im Zentrum des Mondes noch immer ein flüssiger Kern steckt, ist dieser Abkühlungsprozess längst nicht vorbei. „Da das Innere des Mondes weiter abkühlt und sich zusammenzieht, ist davon auszugehen, dass das Wachstum bestehender und die Bildung neuer Verwerfungen auch heute noch andauert“, sagt Watters.
Mithilfe der lichtempfindlichen Spezialkamera Shadowcam entdeckte das Team solche über 100 Meter hohen Klippen selbst im ewigen Schatten tiefer Krater an den Mondpolen, wie die auf der Wissenschaftsplattform Figshare veröffentlichten Kartendaten zeigen. Genau diese dunklen Krater am Südpol sind wegen ihrer Wassereis-Vorkommen das Ziel des Artemis-Programms der Nasa sowie geplanter Mondstationen Chinas und Russlands.
Rutscht das Gestein an einer dieser Bruchstellen ruckartig ab, reicht wegen der geringen Schwerkraft auf dem Mond schon ein leichtes Beben aus, um an steilen Kraterhängen Gerölllawinen auszulösen. Anders als auf der Erde klingen solche Erschütterungen nicht nach wenigen Sekunden ab, sondern hallen im trockenen Mondgestein über Stunden nach und können Landefähren oder Wohnmodule gefährden.
Obwohl diese Gefahr bekannt ist, planen Raumfahrtbehörden und private Unternehmen ihre Landeplätze bislang ohne aktuelle Messdaten von der Oberfläche, weil die vier Bebenmessgeräte der Apollo-Missionen bereits im Jahr 1977 abgeschaltet wurden. Watters und sein Team fordern deshalb ein neues Netz aus Messstationen rund um den Mond, damit Astronaut:innen ihre Quartiere nicht direkt neben aktiven Bruchzonen errichten.

articles.title: Adiós al blooming: así evoluciona el MiniLED con la novena generación de TCL y su tecnología SQD-MiniLED
articles.text:
El mercado de los televisores lleva unos años girando alrededor de una idea clara: el MiniLED se ha consolidado como la alternativa más sólida para quienes buscan un gran brillo y negros profundos sin dar el salto directo a los paneles OLED. Sin embargo, la carrera por presumir de cifras cada vez más altas en las especificaciones técnicas ha chocado a menudo con un problema en entornos reales: la gestión del color y los molestos halos de luz (blooming).
Con la presentación de su novena generación de tecnología de pantalla, bautizada como SQD-MinLED (Super Quantum Dot), TCL busca precisamente equilibrar esa ecuación. Tras años impulsando esta tecnología desde que lanzó el primer MiniLED en el mercado en 2019, la marca traslada su desarrollo de paneles (a través de su filial TCL CSOT) a una nueva familia de televisores.
TCL 55Q7D Pro 55 Pulgadas SQD-Mini LED 4K HDR10+ Smart TV
TCL 75X11L 75 Pulgadas SQD-Mini LED 4K HDR10+ Smart TV
¿En qué consiste el SQD-MiniLED?
Hasta ahora, la combinación de MiniLED y puntos cuánticos (Quantum Dots) se centraba en utilizar miles de diodos diminutos tras el panel para controlar la luz por zonas. La evolución hacia el SQD-MiniLED ataca a dos problemas para mejorar la experiencia visual en el día a día:
- Tratamiento cromático más preciso: introduce un nuevo material de puntos cuánticos (Super QLED) combinado con un filtro de color de alta precisión (Ultra Color Filter), diseñado para mantener la fidelidad y la intensidad de los colores según el estándar cinematográfico BT.2020, incluso en las escenas más luminosas.
- Control drástico del blooming: mediante una arquitectura óptica perfeccionada, se busca minimizar los halos de luz que suelen aparecer alrededor de los objetos brillantes sobre fondos oscuros, uno de los talones de Aquiles tradicionales de esta tecnología.
Los nuevos modelos: así queda el catálogo
Esta novena generación no se queda en simple teoría, sino que se despliega en varias gamas diseñadas para diferentes perfiles de usuarios:
- TCL X11L: el buque insignia de la marca. Está enfocado directamente a los entusiastas de la tecnología y del cine en casa que buscan el máximo rendimiento visual sin concesiones.
TCL 75X11L 75 Pulgadas SQD-Mini LED 4K HDR10+ Smart TV
- TCL C8L: se posiciona como una opción de corte prémium orientada a quienes buscan montar una experiencia de gran formato en salones amplios.
TCL 85C8L 85 Pulgadas SQD-Mini LED 4K HDR10+ Smart TV, 6.000 Nits
- TCL C7L y Q7D Pro: los modelos pensados para llevar esta tecnología a un público más amplio. El C7L actúa como un televisor todoterreno para el uso diario (series, deportes o consolas), mientras que el Q7D Pro se plantea como la puerta de entrada más accesible a las ventajas del SQD-MiniLED.
TCL 85C7L 85 Pulgadas SQD-Mini LED 4K HDR10+ Smart TV
TCL 55Q7D Pro 55 Pulgadas SQD-Mini LED 4K HDR10+ Smart TV
En el apartado acústico, la marca ha apostado por alianzas de peso: los modelos X11L, C8L y C7L integran un sistema de sonido avanzado firmado por Bang & Olufsen, mientras que el modelo Q7D Pro confía en un sistema Onkyo 2.1.
También pueden interesarte
TCL S55HE Barra de Sonido 2.1, 220W
TCL A65K Barra de Sonido 3.1.2ch

articles.title: AI startup Firefly secures $20M to make the physical world a safer place - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
AI startup Firefly secures $20M to make the physical world a safer place
The digital world has already become much smarter thanks to the rise of artificial intelligence, and now a startup called Firefly Technology Inc. wants to do the same for the physical world, beginning with workplace safety.
It has just raised $20 million in funding via a Series A round to make that happen. Today’s round was led by Definition Capital, which previously funded Ramp Business Corp. and Cognition Inc., developer of the AI coding assistant Devin. It was joined by BoxGroup, making its third investment in Firefly, and Susa Ventures, which led the startup’s seed round earlier this year.
Firefly’s goal is to make the world a safer place, and it believes it can do that by extending AI into the physical world to make safety systems more intelligent. Though devices such as security cameras, radios and sensors have helped make locations such as schools, hospitals and other venues safer than they used to be, there’s still a lot of disconnect between these systems. Cameras can see what’s happening, radios can facilitate communication between security personnel and sensors can trigger alarms, but these devices all work in isolation.
What this means is that when something happens, humans still need to waste valuable time understanding the situation before they can put together a response.
Firefly co-founder and Chief Executive James Batt Buckley believes AI can help to close this gap. He says the next frontier for AI is the physical world, which he wants to become as intelligent, connected and programmable as the digital one already is. His idea is to build a single, intelligent system that spans security cameras, sensors and communications, so that AI will immediately understand what’s happening and coordinate a response the moment the alarm registers within the brains of the humans tasked with executing that response.
The startup has developed a combination of purpose-built safety hardware and emergency response management software that’s designed to plug into existing hardware such as cameras and radios. The Ember Safety Management platform works by extracting intelligence from those devices and sensors to build up a clear picture of what the situation is, so it can immediately detect an incident, provide the right context and then organize the response. Firefly has also developed specialized hardware such as wearable panic buttons and AI beacons that enable panic button triangulation and detect gunshots, as well as a network gateway to ensure those systems are always connected.
Buckley said the safety technology industry has seemingly accepted a very strange contradiction. “The more important the job, the more complicated the tools seem to become,” he said. “But we now have the technology to build something fundamentally different. We’re starting with safety because it’s a problem we know deeply, but what we’re building has the potential to transform how people interact with the physical world.”
Constellation Research analyst Holger Mueller said startups such as Firefly are a reminder that AI is going to impact a lot more than just our digital experiences. “Ultimately, AI is going to have a dramatic impact on the physical world too, with one of the first being to improve physical safety in places like schools, hospitals and other large venues,” he said.
The analyst believes AI has obvious advantages over humans when it comes to monitoring a physical area for signs of danger, because it’s always on, always focused and therefore much more vigilant than any human security guard could be. “It will provide more timely and reliable alerts to any malfeasance,” Mueller said. “As with any AI innovation, a degree of cautiousness is still needed to make sure Firefly’s systems work as intended, but any teething problems can probably be ironed out. It’s good to see the innovation helping to keep schools and the kids inside them safe.”
Firefly’s platform has already been deployed by Colorado’s largest community college, Front Range Community College, where it provides unified intelligence across three expansive campuses, helping safety teams to quickly understand emergencies and take action. The startup now wants to expand its deployments, targeting educational centers, hospitals, enterprise campuses and other locations.
Definition Capital’s Teddy Citrin said the intersection of AI and hardware means organizations now have better ways to protect their people. “Firefly is building the central nervous system for physical safety, bringing together specialized hardware, existing data and coordinated action into a single platform,” he said.

articles.title: Pool of Radiance: Ruins of Myth Drannor Comes to Steam and GOG.com on November 6th
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
Pool of Radiance: Ruins of Myth Drannor Comes to Steam and GOG.com on November 6th
Boutique publisher SNEG, in collaboration with Wizards of the Coast, a subsidiary of Hasbro, Inc., are proud to announce the restoration of heritage Dungeons & Dragons title Pool of Radiance: Ruins of Myth Drannor will be available for the first time digitally on November 6th. You won't have to wait that long to play it, however, as a demo is available today through October 26th for Steam Next Fest - and your progress will transfer over into the full game!
Originally released in 2001 by Ubisoft and developed by Stormfront Studios, Pool of Radiance: Ruins of Myth Drannor is a turn-based party RPG set in the Forgotten Realms. It returns to the legendary Pool of Radiance, one of the most storied legacies in CRPG history - now updated to run smoothly on modern systems!Featuring the Dungeons & Dragons game rules with different species, classes and spells, Pool of Radiance: Ruins of Myth Drannor offers over 100 hours of gameplay. After a Pool of Radiance has been discovered in the Forgotten Realms, emanating a wave of pure evil cursing all it touches, the legendary wizard Elminster sends your party on a quest to find out what is behind this vile resurgence - and put a stop to it. 
Build a band of heroes, descend into the haunted elven ruins of Myth Drannor, and use tactical positioning, spellcraft and steel to stop an ancient evil from spreading across Faerûn. Players may choose between the genuine turn-based style of role-playing or focus on action with a timed-turn style of play.
This re-release features plenty of modern bells and whistles, including widescreen support up to 4K, upscaled background assets for sharper visuals, full controller support, and a reworked camera. The UI has also been improved with upscaling, a new action bar, and additional tooltips, while adjustable combat animation speeds let players fine-tune the pace of battles. For those who prefer the original experience, an optional "Legacy" mode preserves the classic gameplay and visuals. Steam Achievements, Cloud Saves, Steam Deck support, numerous bug fixes, and other quality-of-life improvements round out the package, giving players more ways than ever to enjoy this lost classic.
Features
- Features official Dungeons & Dragons rules
- Return to the legendary Pool of Radiance - back to where the legacy began
- Answer Elminster's call and face a new threat to Faerûn in the ruins of Myth Drannor
- Build a party of six: create up to four heroes and recruit two companions along the way
- Develop characters up to level 16, with powerful spells reaching 8th level
- Explore sprawling dungeons and battle through tactical turn-based encounters
- Use the optional turn timer to add extra pressure and a faster pace to combat
- Play comfortably on modern systems with widescreen support up to 4K, full controller support, and reworked camera controls
- Enjoy sharper visuals, an improved UI, adjustable combat animation speeds, and numerous bug fixes and quality-of-life improvements
- Choose how much you want to modernize the experience with granular settings and an optional "Legacy" mode that preserves the original gameplay and visuals
Artem Shchuiko, Director at SNEG"Pool of Radiance: Ruins of Myth Drannor was an ambitious game for 2001. It has its own place in Dungeons & Dragons gaming history, but for years it has been challenging to experience on modern systems. Our goal with this re-release is simple: preserve what made the original special, fix what needs fixing, and make it accessible again to both longtime fans and a new generation of CRPG players."
