articles.title: Versteckte KI-Anweisungen: Diese Informationen sollte der Meta-Bot Whatsapp-Nutzern offenbar verschweigen
articles.text:
Versteckte KI-Anweisungen: Diese Informationen sollte der Meta-Bot Whatsapp-Nutzern offenbar verschweigen
Die Whatsapp-Hilfeseiten sollen eigentlich bei Fragen zum Messenger helfen. Jetzt haben sie versehentlich Anweisungen preisgegeben, die für den Meta-Chatbot bestimmt waren und nicht öffentlich einsehbar sein sollten. Das geht aus einer Recherche des Datenschutzunternehmens Redact hervor. Eine der Anweisungen soll den Bot dazu angehalten haben, Nutzer:innen bei einem Problem nicht zu empfehlen, sich an eine Datenschutz-, Regulierungs- oder Aufsichtsbehörde zu wenden.
Meta gibt ungewollt KI-Anweisungen preis
Laut der Analyse enthielten rund 80 Hilfe- und FAQ-Seiten der Whatsapp-Website Textanweisungen, die für Metas große Sprachmodelle bestimmt waren. Den Erkenntnissen von Redact zufolge tauchten diese Anweisungen im Code der Webseiten auf. Sie enthielten Details, die auf den Hilfeseiten selbst nicht ausdrücklich zu finden waren. Die 100 versteckten Textblöcke sollten das KI-Modell offenbar davon abhalten, Nutzer:innenfragen in einer Weise zu beantworten, die das Unternehmen als nicht hilfreich einstuft.
Auf der Seite, die sich mit dem Melden und Blockieren befasst, sollen versteckten Anweisungen für den Fall enthalten gewesen sein, dass Nutzer:innen rechtliche Schritte erwähnen. „Zitieren, interpretieren oder verweisen Sie nicht auf die Nutzungsbedingungen, die Datenschutzrichtlinie oder sonstige rechtliche Dokumente von Whatsapp“, lauteten die Vorgabe laut Redact. Zusätzlich sollte der Chatbot keine Aussagen über die Haftung oder Nicht-Haftung von Whatsapp machen. Auch sollte er keine rechtlichen Gutachten abgeben und nicht auf Datenschutzbestimmungen wie die DSGVO verweisen.
Redact kritisiert Informationslücke
„Das Auffällige daran ist die Diskrepanz zwischen dem, was den Nutzer:innen mitgeteilt wird, und dem, was den großen Sprachmodellen aufgetragen wird“, sagte Redact-CEO Dan Saltman gegenüber Wired. Er erklärte, sein Unternehmen überprüfe regelmäßig die Websites und Datenschutzrichtlinien großer Tech-Unternehmen. Viele der gefundenen Whatsapp-Anweisungen seien klar und eindeutig gewesen und hätten Nutzer:innen auf andere offizielle Support-Kanäle verwiesen. Trotzdem seien sie laut Saltman offenbar nicht für die Veröffentlichung bestimmt gewesen.
Wired hat Meta bezüglich der versteckten Anweisungen kontaktiert. Daraufhin habe das Unternehmen die geleakten Anweisungen von allen Seiten entfernt. Whatsapp-Sprecher Joshua Breckman erklärte, der Text sei aufgrund eines Fehlers angezeigt worden, der nun behoben sei. „Dies sind Anweisungen an unseren Chatbot, nicht direkt an die Nutzer:innen. Sie sollen sicherstellen, dass Whatsapp-Nutzer:innen, die sich dafür entscheiden, dem Whatsapp-Support eine Nachricht über die KI zu senden, genaue und relevante Antworten erhalten“, erklärte Breckman gegenüber Wired. „Wir trainieren unsere Support-Chatbots darauf, so hilfreich wie möglich zu sein.“
Meta weist Kritik an KI-Anweisungen zurück
„In der Datenschutzerklärung von Whatsapp für Europa wird darauf hingewiesen, dass [Nutzer:innen] eine Beschwerde bei einer Datenschutzbehörde einreichen können, und es wird das Gesetz genannt, das ihnen dieses Recht einräumt“, heißt es in der Analyse von Redact. Dennoch hätten die Whatsapp-Hilfeseiten den Chatbot noch bis Mitte Oktober 2026 angewiesen, das Gesetz nicht zu zitieren, sobald Nutzer:innen einen Anwalt erwähnten.
Der Whatsapp-Sprecher widersprach gegenüber Wired. Er betonte, das Unternehmen informiere Nutzer:innen transparent über ihre Datenrechte und darüber, wie sie im Streitfall Maßnahmen ergreifen können. „Wir möchten, dass sich unsere Chatbots im Produkt-Support darauf konzentrieren, den Nutzer:innen die bestmögliche Hilfe zu Whatsapp zu bieten – und keine Rechtsberatung“, so Breckman.

articles.title: AuxoAI raises over $20M to bring AI expertise to the enterprise and redesign how work gets done - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
AuxoAI raises over $20M to bring AI expertise to the enterprise and redesign how work gets done
AuxoAI Inc., an enterprise engineering and consulting company that helps large businesses build and deploy artificial intelligence systems, today announced it has raised $20.7 million in a Series A funding to accelerate growth and scale its enterprise AI consulting model.
The company said it has spent over three years working with Global 2000 enterprises and strategic partners, bringing AI into the core of their operations. It focuses on combining business-process expertise, data engineering and AI agents – autonomous systems that use artificial intelligence to work with little or no human oversight, with deep insight into company data to complete long-term tasks.
AuxoAI builds AI solutions by sending on-site engineers and strategy teams to understand enterprise culture, data, workflow automation and customer engagement to tailor experiences to business and employee needs.
At the core of the company’s platform is Damia, which the company describes as an FDE Workbench, or “forward-deployed engineer” toolkit that also transforms data into applications and licenses for customers. It combines reusable agent capacities with tools for capturing a company’s business knowledge and processes.
The company said that over the years, it has learned how to work with customers to encode relevant knowledge and relationships and use that to create AI agents around the company’s processes. This preserves what the team learns in software and structured knowledge, rather than only interviews or paper documents, but in living software that can work alongside employees.
The company calls this effect “intelligence embedded in the work itself,” where consulting treats AI as a lever or tool for the customer rather than an end product.
AuxoAI partners with companies that businesses already know and trust, including Google LLC, Amazon Web Services Inc., Snowflake Inc., Databricks Inc. and Microsoft Corp., allowing the company to provide enterprise-ready AI, cloud, data and productivity via these platforms.
NTT Venture Capital, a Silicon Valley venture capital firm backed by Japanese technology conglomerate NTT Inc., led the funding round. The round also included participation from prominent industry executives and strategic investors, such as George Still Jr., partner emeritus at Norwest Venture Partners; Amit Zavery, president, chief product officer and chief operating officer at ServiceNow Inc.; and Giacomo Sonnino, managing director at Charlesbank Capital Partners and former chief operating officer of Quantum Black North America.
NTTVC’s portfolio includes Anthropic PBC, which will bring on another major artificial intelligence leader to extend AuxoAI’s capabilities.
The company said the new funding will serve to accelerate the next phase of its journey to expand its global reach. It aims to provide onsite consulting talent for enterprise AI transformation, invest in proprietary technology and AI-native delivery capabilities, and scale up its presence and strategic ecosystem.

articles.title: Espressif Debuts ESP-Mosaico Modular Development Platform
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
Espressif Debuts ESP-Mosaico Modular Development Platform
Espressif Systems (688018.SH) today announced ESP-Mosaico, a modular development platform designed for AI-assisted hardware creation. ESP-Mosaico allows creators to combine functional modules and multiple devices while enabling Coding Agents to understand the current hardware configuration and participate directly in application development.
ESP-Mosaico supports two complementary development approaches. Chat Coding lets creators start from a natural-language request and quickly build working hardware prototypes without setting up a local development environment. Vibe Coding brings AI Agents deeper into the engineering workflow, including implementation, deployment, testing on physical hardware, and continuous iteration.Software can now be generated and modified rapidly with AI, but hardware is still often constrained by fixed boards, interfaces, and product forms. ESP-Mosaico is designed to make hardware equally extensible: capabilities can be added as ideas evolve, without requiring creators to define the final form of a device from the outset.
The name Mosaico, meaning "mosaic," reflects this concept—individual hardware building blocks can be combined to create something larger and continuously evolving.
Modular Hardware That Grows with the Application
At the center of ESP-Mosaico is a compact standalone host featuring a 480 × 480 OLED touchscreen, haptic feedback, a built-in battery, USB Type-C connectivity, and expansion I/O.
The host is powered by Espressif's ESP32-S31, a RISC-V SoC running at up to 320 MHz, with 512 KB SRAM and support for up to 32 MB of high-speed DDR PSRAM. ESP32-S31 also integrates Wi-Fi 6, dual-mode Bluetooth 5.4, and 802.15.4, and supports interfaces including 1 Gbps Ethernet, USB 2.0 High-Speed OTG, hardware JPEG encoding and decoding, and DVP camera input.ESP-Mosaico extends these capabilities through modular hardware for functions such as cameras, sensors, buttons, lighting, and motors. Supported modules can be automatically identified and integrated by the system, reducing the need to repeatedly handle wiring and low-level driver adaptation.
Composability also extends across devices. Multiple ESP-Mosaico hosts can recognize their relative position and orientation and synchronize application state wirelessly, allowing devices to be joined, separated, or rearranged as part of the application itself. This enables experiences ranging from cross-screen games to modular information displays and other multi-screen applications.
Bringing AI Agents into Real-World Development
Chat Coding: From an Idea to a Working Prototype
For creators new to programming or AI-assisted development, ESP-Mosaico provides Chat Coding through ESP-Claw, the Coding Agent built into the platform.
Creators simply describe what they want to build. ESP-Claw uses the capabilities of the connected ESP-Mosaico hardware to generate, build, and deploy the application. Development does not require a locally configured toolchain, while application interfaces, logic, and peripheral control that do not depend on online services run locally on the device after deployment.
Creators can then continue refining the application conversationally—for example, adding functionality, changing behavior, or improving the user interface—turning an initial idea into an interactive hardware prototype through successive iterations.
ESP-Mosaico also connects to Skills Lab, where device applications can be packaged as reusable Skills containing Lua scripts, assets, and peripheral dependencies. Creators can install existing Skills, customize supported applications, or publish their own Skills for others to use.
Vibe Coding: Iterating Directly on Real Hardware
ESP-Mosaico is supported on ESP ZeroCode AI platform including its complete board and peripheral simulation. You can find various ESP-Mosaico community projects here.
For more advanced development, ESP-Mosaico is designed to bring other coding agents into the complete build-test-debug loop.
The platform provides:
- Specification-driven UI development, giving Agents defined design rules, components, resources, and constraints.
- ESP-GSP, an AI-oriented UI framework, where interfaces can be represented using structured JSON, validated during build, simulated on a PC, and then deployed to ESP32 hardware.
- Closed-loop device debugging, exposing flashing, device control, inputs, UI state, performance data, and fault information through unified interfaces so Agents can analyze results and iterate.
- Agent-ready development resources, including BSPs, SDKs, schematics, reference projects, documentation, and Agent References.
- Together, these capabilities allow an Agent to repeatedly modify code, build and deploy, test on real hardware, analyze feedback, and refine the application, while developers define the goals, constraints, and acceptance criteria.
Built on the Open ESP Development Ecosystem
AI-generated code still depends on a strong engineering foundation to run reliably on physical hardware. ESP-Mosaico builds on Espressif's established development ecosystem, including ESP-IDF, drivers and components, technical documentation, development and debugging tools, ESP Component Registry, and community projects. 
More than 200,000 projects related to ESP32 and ESP8266 are available on GitHub, along with more than 300 books published in over 10 languages. These resources can provide Coding Agents with engineering context, reference implementations, and proven development practices.
By connecting these open engineering resources with direct feedback from physical devices, ESP-Mosaico provides a foundation for AI-assisted hardware development that Agents can not only reference, but also build against and validate on real hardware.
Bring Ideas Beyond the Screen
Whether starting with Chat Coding or using Vibe Coding for deeper product development, ESP-Mosaico enables creators to move from an idea to a working physical device—and continue evolving it through software, hardware, and AI-assisted iteration.
Developers can visit the ESP-Mosaico website to learn more about the product and access development resources, or share applications with other users through Skills Lab.
The ESP-Mosaico development kit is now available for purchase. For additional product information, please contact the Espressif customer support team.
From natural-language creation to Agent-driven development, and from modular hardware to multi-device applications, ESP-Mosaico brings AI coding beyond the screen and into the physical world.

articles.title: Polestar tries to quantify what it’s like to drive a performance car
articles.text:
The human desire to go fast is old, dating back at least as far as the first time some adventurous Yamnaya saw a horse on the Pontic-Caspian steppe and thought, “I bet if I jumped on that thing’s back, it would be faster than walking.”
A thousand years later, someone else invented the wheel—and the chariot—and humanity was ready to roll. Now, about five millennia since that first horseback ride, equestrianism is mostly a leisure activity, and we drive cars, propelled by motors with more power than an entire herd of beasts could muster.
Acceleration, top speed, and lap times are the usual ways we quantify that performance, and performance electric vehicles are currently in an arms race to see which one can hit 60 mph in the least amount of time. But measuring a car’s performance is easy—all you need is a stopwatch and a track. How about measuring the effect of car performance on the driver? That’s a question Polestar is trying to answer with researchers at the University of Oxford.
“As electric cars redefine what performance can be, we wanted to understand something that can’t be captured by a specification sheet alone: the human experience behind the wheel,” said Christian Samson, Polestar’s head of product attributes. “Working with University of Oxford allows us to look at performance through a different lens—connecting the engineering of the car with the experience of the person driving it.”
The pilot study involved 12 drivers who track-tested both rear- and all-wheel-drive versions of the Polestar 4 at a track in Sweden. The Polestar 4 is the OEM’s midsize crossover, a compelling Porsche Macan alternative that you can sadly no longer buy here in the US. The drivers were instrumented with heart rate monitors and skullcaps studded with electrodes, plus the cars’ gaze-tracking driver monitoring system to gather physiological data, which was combined with telemetry from the cars and subjective interview assessments after the fact. While being measured, drivers lapped the Gotland Ring circuit gently, then dynamically.

articles.title: OYO-parent PRISM to nearly halve IPO fresh issue size to up to Rs 3,350 cr: Sources
articles.text:
OYO-parent PRISM to nearly halve IPO fresh issue size to up to Rs 3,350 cr: Sources
People familiar with the matter said the reduction in the issue size follows continued strong cash generation and an improving balance-sheet position, which has lowered the amount of capital the company needs to raise compared with what was originally envisaged.
OYO parent PRISM is planning to nearly halve the size of the fresh issue in its proposed initial public offering (IPO) to up to Rs 3,350 crore from almost Rs 6,650 crore, sources said.
People familiar with the matter told PTI the reduction in the issue size follows continued strong cash generation and an improving balance-sheet position, which has lowered the amount of capital the company needs to raise compared with what was originally envisaged.
"The original issue was sized before the company's more recent financial performance came through. With cash generation remaining strong and the balance sheet improving, the funding requirement has come down, allowing the company to reduce the amount of primary capital it raises.
"The objective is to raise what the business needs while keeping the capital structure efficient. The plan is to repay the residual debt over the next two to three years through cash flows generated by the business," a person familiar with the matter said.
Earlier, OYO had planned to raise up to Rs 6,650 crore through an IPO, of which around Rs 5,000 crore was intended for debt repayment.
The revised issue size comes with PRISM continuing to focus on reducing its outstanding debt.
Under the revised structure, most of the issue proceeds are proposed to be used towards repayment or prepayment, in part or full, of certain borrowings.
The revised issue comes as PRISM moves towards the next stage of its proposed IPO following its earlier filing of the uUpdated draft herring prospectus.
Moody's Ratings has revised the outlook on PRISM to 'positive' from 'stable', while reaffirming the travel tech unicorn's B2 corporate family rating.
Explaining the rationale behind ratings, Moody's said, "We expect OYO's EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation) to grow to around Rs 3,000 crore ($315 million) over the next 12-18 months as the company continues to scale and add new storefronts to its platform.
For FY26, OYO's EBITDA more than doubled to Rs 2,630 crore from Rs 1,080 crore in FY25.
OYO was founded in 2013 by Ritesh Agarwal, who currently holds a 30.52 per cent stake in the company. SVF India Holdings (Cayman) Ltd, a subsidiary of SoftBank Group Corp is the largest shareholder in the company, with a 40.04% stake.

articles.title: IA y ciencia ciudadana: un estudio muestra cómo millones de observaciones en línea alimentan la investigación ecológica
articles.text:
Millones de personas en todo el mundo salen a observar aves, fotografiar mariposas o registrar plantas silvestres. Lo hacen por placer, casi siempre sin sospechar que cada comentario que dejan en plataformas gratuitas como eBird o iNaturalist podría contener información valiosa para la ciencia. El problema era que esos datos quedaban sepultados bajo millones de anotaciones que ningún equipo de investigación podía revisar de forma manual.
¿Cómo acceder a registros sobre la forma en que distintas especies se relacionan entre sí, ya sea al polinizar una flor, competir por alimento o depredar a otro animal? Documentar esas dinámicas en el campo exige vigilancia continua, algo que ningún grupo de científicos puede sostener las 24 horas del día en cada rincón de un ecosistema. Sin embargo, cientos de millones de aficionados a la naturaleza ya lo hacían sin saberlo cada vez que anotaban lo observado en una plataforma digital.
Un equipo liderado por la Universidad de Míchigan demostró que la inteligencia artificial puede extraer y clasificar datos ecológicos ocultos en esos comentarios. Los resultados, divulgados en la revista Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, revelaron además indicios de especies vegetales foráneas en ecosistemas de la costa oeste de Estados Unidos, un tipo de alerta temprana que, sin este método, habría pasado inadvertida.
Cómo la inteligencia artificial lee lo que los humanos no alcanzan a revisar
Para probar la viabilidad de este enfoque, el equipo diseñó dos estudios de caso. El primero se centró en la relación entre una mariposa polinizadora que habita la costa oeste de Estados Unidos y México, y las plantas que visita, con datos tomados de iNaturalist. El segundo analizó vínculos diversos entre aves de Míchigan documentados en los comentarios de eBird, desde conductas cooperativas como el vuelo en bandada hasta disputas por un lugar en un comedero.
En ambas plataformas, cada avistamiento se sube acompañado de metadatos esenciales, es decir, información sobre el momento y el lugar exacto de la observación. El desafío consistía en determinar cuáles de esas entradas incluían, además, un comentario con datos útiles sobre vínculos entre organismos. Cualquier persona puede reconocer esas descripciones sin necesidad de vocabulario científico, pero la escala del problema lo volvía inabordable: había millones de anotaciones por filtrar.
El equipo recurrió entonces a modelos de lenguaje extenso, sistemas de inteligencia artificial diseñados para procesar texto del mismo modo en que lo haría un lector humano. Herramientas como Claude y ChatGPT fueron entrenadas con instrucciones específicas, elaboradas junto con estudiantes de grado en ecología e informática, que les permitieron extraer y clasificar las relaciones detectadas con buena precisión.
Así lo indicó Hengxing Zou, autor principal del estudio, quien realizó el trabajo como investigador posdoctoral en el Instituto de Biología del Cambio Global de la Universidad de Míchigan, según la comunicación institucional.
Seis minutos frente a ocho horas
Para medir el ahorro de tiempo que ofrece esta herramienta, el equipo llevó a cabo una comparación directa. Primero, ChatGPT aisló de los datos de eBird aquellos comentarios que contenían relaciones entre organismos. Luego, Olivia Stein, asistente de investigación de grado, tomó una muestra aleatoria de casi 500 de esos comentarios para clasificar manualmente qué tipo de vínculo describían. Después, Claude realizó la misma tarea. Lo que a Stein le demandó ocho horas, Claude lo completó en seis minutos.
“El enfoque es realmente versátil y tenemos una enorme cantidad de datos esperando a ser analizados”, afirmó Zou según la comunicación institucional. El investigador reconoció que existen controversias en torno al uso de inteligencia artificial en el ámbito científico, pero señaló que este proyecto demuestra cómo la tecnología amplía el esfuerzo humano en lugar de reemplazarlo.
“Sería casi imposible para los humanos revisar los millones de comentarios que existen. Usamos los modelos de lenguaje para generar conjuntos de datos, no para analizarlos ni para sustituir el trabajo creativo de los científicos”, agregó.
Un método que va más allá de aves y mariposas
“Este enfoque nos da algo que los ecólogos han necesitado durante mucho tiempo: una forma de examinar las relaciones entre especies a gran escala espacial y temporal”, afirmó Kai Zhu, autor sénior del estudio y profesor asociado en la Escuela de Medio Ambiente y Sostenibilidad de la Universidad de Míchigan, según el comunicado de prensa. La inteligencia artificial, añadió, puede convertir registros dispersos en conjuntos de datos capaces de revelar cómo las comunidades biológicas responden al cambio global.
El propio Zou subrayó que, más allá de la tecnología, el enfoque conecta con una tradición fundacional de la ecología: salir a observar la naturaleza y anotar lo que resulta llamativo. Ese hábito, multiplicado por cientos de millones de usuarios en plataformas digitales, abre la puerta a detectar fenómenos como la infiltración de especies foráneas en ecosistemas nativos. En un contexto de cambio climático y pérdida de biodiversidad, ese tipo de vigilancia adquiere un valor difícil de reemplazar. “Creo que hay mucha más información por recuperar de este tipo de comentarios, además de las relaciones entre especies”, concluyó según el comunicado.

articles.title: UK schools caught in a 'learning technology balance gap' as kids demand more tech in the classroom
articles.text:
UK schools caught in a 'learning technology balance gap' as kids demand more tech in the classroom
Digital classrooms aren't doing what they need to
- Epson study finds IT managers agree that most investments have covered buying new tech but not use cases
- Teachers are seeing declines in student attention, critical thinking and knowledge retention
- Schools need to focus on determining real-world use cases
New research from Epson claims UK teachers feel their classroom is falling behind when it comes to successful tech integration, with nearly two-thirds (64%) worried that tech adoption may have accelerated faster than its actual effective use.
In other words, they worry that many tech implementations have been done for the sake of it, but they're not getting the most out of it.
This comes as nine in 10 (91%) UK students report to use technology in almost every aspect of their lives – as many as half (48%) even expect to have extensive technology use during lessons nowadays.
Students want more digital classrooms, it turns out
Three in four (72%) school IT managers say their schools have introduced more tech over the past year, however 84% of them agree that those investments have mostly covered acquiring new devices and not determining how they should actually be used.
Teachers generally agree that there's too much tech without enough purpose, too, with three in five saying there are too many individual screens and a further three in five believing there's too much emphasis on AI.
"Education systems must move beyond simply adopting technology and instead focus on how it is used," Epson Europe Education Lead Dr Sarah Henkelmann-Hillebrand explained, noting the need to design around learning outcomes and strike a better balance between digital and physical tools.
However, teachers are also worried that tech in the classroom so far hasn't been all that positive – 83% note a reduction in student attention, 77% saw a decrease in critical thinking, 76% have seen knowledge retention decline and 68% even believe teaching fundamental literacy and numeracy skills has become harder.

articles.title: Le patron de Rivian en est convaincu : la conduite autonome va transformer radicalement le design des voitures
articles.text:
Et si la conduite autonome changeait la forme même de nos voitures ? RJ Scaringe, le patron de Rivian, assure que l’automobile va subir une profonde mutation.
Le constructeur américain, connu pour ses pick-up et SUV pensés pour l’aventure, a lancé en juin le R2, une voiture plus compacte et plus abordable. Et son modèle commence à porter ses fruits après des années de pertes : Rivian a livré 19 248 véhicules au troisième trimestre, un record, soit environ 46 % de plus qu’un an plus tôt.
RJ Scaringe, son fondateur et P.-D.G de Rivian, s’est justement exprimé il y a quelques jours lors du TechCrunch Disrupt, grande conférence américaine consacrée aux nouvelles technologies. Ses prédictions sont fascinantes.
Des « expériences radicalement différentes »
Il a en effet expliqué à TechCrunch que l’autonomie permettrait à son entreprise de construire des « expériences radicalement différentes ». Le dirigeant se dit « follement enthousiaste « à l’idée de ce que les dix prochaines années vont rendre possible dans le secteur, et il est même prêt à repousser la rentabilité de Rivian pour y parvenir.
L’enjeu dépasse le simple confort de conduite. Si la voiture n’a plus besoin d’être pilotée, ses concepteurs n’ont plus à respecter les codes actuels de l’automobile, « on imagine les formats que l’on veut construire pour un véhicule autonome », étaye-t-il. Selon lui, cela « ouvre toutes sortes d’opportunités de design ».
Et Scaringe s’oppose directement à Tesla : il ne croit pas à un monde où tout le monde laisserait sa voiture au garage pour appeler un robotaxi. Même si les voitures savent un jour conduire seules sur certains trajets, il estime peu probable que les habitudes changent radicalement. Reste à voir à quoi ressembleront ces voitures personnelles et autonomes.
Des concepts, mais c’est tout
Mais ce concept n’est pas nouveau. Il y a dix ans, constructeurs automobiles et spécialistes de la conduite autonome annonçaient que les voitures sans conducteur, associées aux moteurs électriques plus simples et moins encombrants que les moteurs thermiques, feraient naître des formes de véhicules inédites.
Quand Mercedes présentait une cabine en forme de bulle, Toyota imaginait des « salons sur roues » tandis que Hyundai dévoilait une voiture dotée de pattes. Aucun de ces projets n’a dépassé le stade du prototype : l’autonomie a demandé bien plus de temps que prévu, et lancer une toute nouvelle catégorie de véhicule s’est révélé bien plus compliqué. Les robotaxis, eux, sont bien là, même s’ils doivent encore faire face à des défis.
De son côté, le système de conduite autonome de Rivian permet aujourd’hui de lâcher le volant, à condition de continuer à surveiller la route. D’ici à la fin de l’année, il doit être capable de mener une voiture d’un point de départ à une destination sans intervention, toujours sous le contrôle du conducteur. La véritable autonomie devrait arriver en 2028, avec la version robotaxi de la R2.

articles.title: Les Anneaux de pouvoir : la saison 3 dévoile les serviteurs de Sauron dans des nouvelles affiches
articles.text:
Les Anneaux de pouvoir : la saison 3 dévoile les serviteurs de Sauron dans des nouvelles affiches
Attendue le 11 novembre prochain sur Prime Video, la saison 3 de la série Le Seigneur des anneaux : les anneaux de pouvoir vient de révéler de nouvelles affiches mettant en avant les forces de Sauron.
Fans du Seigneur des anneaux, courage : plus que trois grosses semaines à patienter avant de retourner se balader en Terre du Milieu avec la sortie de la saison 3 de la série Les Anneaux de pouvoir sur la plateforme de streaming Prime Video.
Et comme pour remercier la persévérance de ses fidèles, le show d'Amazon vient d'ailleurs de dévoiler deux affiches particulièrement guerrières et prometteuses, avant l'arrivée imminente d'une nouvelle bande-annonce.
Les Nazgnagôl à l'honneur
La première affiche nous montre ainsi Sauron (Charlie Vickers) tout en armure vêtu, arborant sa couronne de métal sombre (aussi appelée couronne de Morgoth) devant quatre de ses nouveaux serviteurs, les fameux Nazgnagôl qui font leur apparition dans cette troisième saison.
Ces personnages inédits de l'univers de J. R. R. Tolkien, créés par les créateurs du show J.D. Payne et Patrick McKay, sont des sortes de "proto-Nazgûl" : des Nazgûl qui ont encore forme humaine, avant d'être consumés par les anneaux de pouvoir et qu'ils ne deviennent des spectres de l'anneau.
Ce terme a été inventé par les showrunners à partir du “parler noir” (la langue du Mordor), mélange de nazg (anneau) et nagôl (serviteur) et signifiant “serviteur de l'anneau”. Si l'identité de tous les Nazgûl n'a pas été révélée par Tolkien, on sait que l'un d'entre eux sera Khamül l'Oriental.
Ce seigneur de guerre apparaîtra dans la saison 3 sous les traits de Zubin Varla (Andor), et l'acteur a même précisé dans une interview que son personnage suivra “le même chemin que Gollum” : “Le mal engendre le mal, et la violence engendre la violence. Leurs âmes et leurs corps sont corrompus jusqu'à être littéralement évidés, presque dépourvus de toute forme physique”.
Moins impressionnante, la seconde affiche nous montre l'un de ces Nazgnagôl sur son cheval cabré dans les plaines du Mordor, avec la Montagne du destin en arrière-plan. C'est peu, mais cela a de quoi nous faire patienter jusqu'à la sortie imminente d'un nouveau trailer, alors que la dernière bande-annonce date de juillet dernier.
Cette nouvelle saison ne sera d'ailleurs pas uniquement celle des ennemis de la Terre du milieu, et verra aussi l'apparition de l'elfe Celeborn, mari de Galadriel, incarné par Jamie Campbell Bower (Vecna dans Stranger Things). L'acteur rejoint au casting Morfydd Clark, Robert Aramayo, Charlie Vickers, Owain Arthur ou encore Benjamin Walker.
Pour rappel, la troisième saison se déroule cinq ans après les événements de la saison 2, alors que la guerre entre les Elfes et Sauron bat son plein. Le seigneur des ténèbres cherche à forger l'anneau unique, l'arme qui lui donnera l'avantage décisif pour remporter la guerre, asservir tous les peuples à sa volonté et régner enfin sur la Terre du milieu tout entière.

articles.title: Nach Rekordsommer: Was deutsche Städte beim Hitzeschutz tun könnten – und woran es hapert
articles.text:
Nach Rekordsommer: Was deutsche Städte beim Hitzeschutz tun könnten – und woran es hapert
Bereits 2008 hat die damalige Bundesregierung eine Klimaanpassungsstrategie entwickelt. Seit zwei Jahren hat sie Gesetzescharakter. Sie schreibt unter anderem Ländern und Kommunen vor, den Klimawandel bei allen Planungen zu berücksichtigen. Was hat das Gesetz bisher bewirkt und wie ließe sich die Anpassung verbessern? Anja Bierwirth beschäftigt diese Frage schon lange. Sie hat Umweltwissenschaften und Architektur studiert und arbeitet seit 2008 am Wuppertal Institut für Klima, Umwelt, Energie – einem renommierten Thinktank für Nachhaltigkeitsforschung. Dort leitet sie den Forschungsbereich Stadtwandel. Ihre Arbeitsschwerpunkte sind kommunale Energie- und Klimaschutzpolitik, Gebäudeenergieeffizienz sowie nachhaltige Stadtentwicklung. Im Interview spricht sie über verpasste Chancen und Möglichkeiten bei der Klimaanpassung.

articles.title: La psicología sabe por qué algunas personas aman los días de lluvia mientras el resto del mundo se queja
articles.text:
Hay gente que adora esos días en los que la lluvia cae en la calle y el mejor plan que tienen en mente es quedarse en casa mientras escuchan el agua caer. Para muchos, esto puede asociarse a una personalidad melancólica, pero la psicología nos sugiere que disfrutar de la lluvia tiene mucho que ver con la forma en la que nuestro cerebro procesa los estímulos de baja intensidad y busca el alivio del estrés.
Odiar el verano. Antes de entrar en el porqué ocurre esto a los amantes de la lluvia, hay que desmentir el hecho de que a todo el mundo le afecte el clima de la misma manera. Aquí tenemos de referencia un estudio de 2008 que analizó a más de 1.200 personas y concluyó que el efecto medio del tiempo sobre el estado de ánimo es pequeño, pero con una gran variación individual. Aunque curiosamente, se desmitifica la idea de la "relajación profunda" bajo la lluvia, puesto que la falta de luz solar se asociaba directamente con un mayor cansancio.
Fue tres años más tarde cuando un nuevo estudio nos reveló mucho más al analizar a casi 500 adolescentes y a sus madres junto a sus perfiles climáticos. Uno de ellos fue bautizado como 'Summer Haters', el cual estaba representado por el 27% de los adolescentes y el 12% de las madres, que se sentían más felices y satisfechos con más lluvia, menos sol y temperaturas más bajas.
La teoría. Para entender el atractivo de la lluvia, la psicología recurre a la Teoría de la Restauración de la Atención (ART), formulada originalmente por Stephen Kaplan en 1955. Aquí Kaplan propuso que nuestro entorno agota nuestra capacidad de concentración a través de lo que llamó "fascinación dura", que son estímulos intensos que absorben la atención por completo, como una pantalla o el tráfico.
Como antídoto, la naturaleza ofrece una "fascinación suave" que no es más que una atención que no requiere esfuerzo, provocada por estímulos tenues como mirar el movimiento de las nubes, el susurro de las hojas o el fluir del agua.
La lluvia encaja aquí perfectamente en esta fascinación suave, puesto que es un estímulo constante, predecible y de baja intensidad que ocupa una pequeña fracción de la atención, permitiendo que el resto del cerebro divague, reflexione y se restaure. Además, se sabe perfectamente que los sonidos de la naturaleza nos relajan bastante, siendo el sonido del agua caer uno de los que mayores efectos que tiene para impulsar las emociones positivas.
Lo que ocurre en el cerebro. Para entender este efecto, un estudio publicado en 2017 combinó resonancia magnética funcional y la variabilidad de la frecuencia cardiaca. Aquí descubrieron que los sonidos naturales, frente a los artificiales, aumentan la actividad del sistema nervioso parasimpático encargado del modo 'descanso' y mejoran el rendimiento en tareas de atención externa.
A nivel fisiológico, el efecto es sutil, pero medible, puesto que ya en 2010 se sometió a 40 participantes a una estresante tarea matemática y luego les hicieron escuchar sonidos naturales o ruido. Y aunque la variabilidad cardiaca no mostró grandes cambios, la conductancia de la piel (un indicador clásico de estrés y sudoración) se recuperó ligeramente más rápido con el sonido de la naturaleza.
El ruido blanco. Es común decir que el sonido de la lluvia puede reducir al momento el estrés y el nivel de cortisol, y por eso se usa para poder dormir como ruido blanco. Sin embargo, la evidencia que tenemos encima de la mesa nos dice algo diferente, puesto que tras medir el cortisol ante entornos naturales se vio que se activaba la parte parasimpática de nuestro sistema nervioso, pero no bajaba el nivel de hormona de estrés.
Imágenes | Leonardo Pavão
En Xataka | Así es la rutina ideal para manejar el estrés desde la mañana, sin meditaciones ni mindfulness

articles.title: Reino Unido propõe abrir NFC do iPhone a rivais do Apple Pay • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Reino Unido propõe abrir NFC do iPhone a rivais do Apple Pay
Proposta da autoridade britânica prevê acesso mais barato à tecnologia para bancos e carteiras digitais concorrentes.
A Autoridade de Concorrência e Mercados do Reino Unido (CMA) propôs, nesta terça-feira (20/10), novas regras para ampla a concorrência nos pagamentos por aproximação no iPhone. O órgão quer reduzir as taxas cobradas pela Apple e facilitar o acesso de bancos, fintechs e outras carteiras digitais ao chip NFC dos aparelhos.
As medidas incluem taxas de acesso mais baixas e a possibilidade de uso de tecnologias alternativas ao sistema atualmente oferecido pela Apple para pagamentos por aproximação, diz a Reuters. A proposta ficará em consulta pública até 17 de novembro.
Assim como na União Europeia, que regulou as carteiras digitais nos aparelhos da Apple em 2024, um dos mecanismos previstos é o Host Card Emulation (HCE). A tecnologia permite que os apps processem pagamentos sem depender do componente físico, conhecido como Secure Element. A Apple já permite atualmente integrações de terceiros ao NFC no iPhone através de APIs.
Apesar de seguir um caminho parecido, a proposta do Reino Unido é menos restritiva para a Apple do que as regras implementadas no bloco europeu. Por lá, a empresa se comprometeu a permitir o acesso gratuito de terceiros ao NFC do iPhone para pagamentos por aproximação.
A CMA britãnica, por outro lado, não propõe essa gratuidade. O órgão quer reduzir os valores cobrados e ampliar as formas de acesso ao NFC. A autoridade ganhou poder para intervir nesse tipo de prática após classificar Apple e Google como empresas com status de mercado estratégico no setor de plataformas móveis.
Segundo dados citados pela CMA, transações por aproximações representam atualmente 39% de todos os pagamentos realizados no Reino Unido, ante 3% há uma década. Mais de 60% dos adultos no país utilizam alguma carteira digital, segundo a autoridade, e o Apple Wallet é o mais usado entre os britânicos.
“Ouvimos que taxas altas, termos rígidos e restrições relacionadas à tecnologia sem contato da Apple tornam difícil demais para os concorrentes inovarem e competiram”, afirmou a diretora-executiva da CMA, Sarah Cardell.
O NFC faz parte de uma série de tecnologias e serviços presentes em aparelhos da Apple que estão na mira de análises regulatórias, especialmente na Europa. Recentemente, a empresa teve de abrir mão da exclusividade de ferramentas proprietárias em alguns casos, como:
A empresa entrou em acordo com o Conselho Administrativo de Defesa Econômica (Cade) para implementar parte dessas mudanças, incluindo a abertura da Apple Store e pagamentos externos, no Brasil.
A possível medida recebeu apoio de empresas do setor financeiro na região, mas desagradou a Apple. A empresa argumenta que desenvolvedores já dispõem de mecanismos para oferecer pagamentos por aproximação no iPhone por meio do NFC e do Secure Element e ampliar o uso de outras tecnologias pode reduzir as proteções do sistema atual.
“Não acreditamos que a CMA deva exigir que a Apple adote uma abordagem com menores proteções de privacidade e segurança”, afirmou um porta-voz da empresa. A CMA deve avaliar as contribuições recebidas na consulta pública antes de decidir se transforma as propostas em exigências formais.

articles.title: Meta Muse exposes users' personal and business secrets when they share conversations
articles.text:
Muse, the new general-purpose AI agent from Meta, can expose sensitive information when users share conversations through web links, researchers reported Monday. In response to questions from Ars about the behavior, Meta said it’s suspending the sharing feature while the company reviews it and considers making changes.
Like many online services, Muse has allowed users to share searches, conversations, images, and similar content with other people. Such share features usually involve clicking an option to create a unique URL that anyone can use to load a page hosting the content. To keep potentially sensitive information from being accessible to unintended people, the URLs typically contain a long sequence of text that can’t be easily guessed.
A single query is all that’s required
Muse, which Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said last month was “built from the ground up for privacy and security,” seems to take the same precautions. But a central design decision for constructing URLs has made the links easy to discover. As a result, researchers from security firm Claroc said they were able to enumerate 6,800 links Muse users created for sharing conversations with others. After opening a few hundred of them, the researchers found information that was clearly not intended to be publicly available, including:
- a candidate’s notes preparing for a confidential executive-search call with a frontier AI lab, naming the lab’s internal contact and the meeting time
- a national marketing company’s internal revenue review, marked for its CEO
- a small-business owner’s loan application, with the amount requested
- a to-do list that included a bank fraud alert, with a partial account number and a transaction amount and time
- a real-estate investor’s internal performance report, with two property addresses and exact return, income, and mortgage figures
- a workplace’s full-year staff vacation calendar, listing dozens of employees against the week each one would be away
“If you had asked us beforehand, we would have guessed that gathering these would take real effort,” the researchers wrote. “It took one query.”
In an emailed statement responding to questions from Ars, Meta said:
We opened the Muse bug bounty program so researchers could raise different scenarios and help us continue improving the product. People have the ability to share specific Muse artifacts, which creates a page that can be accessed by those with the link. However, we’ve paused this functionality while we review this report and consider changes to how these links can be discovered.
Asaf Aprozper, the co-founder and CTO of Claroc, said he reported the findings through Meta’s bug bounty program on October 8 and also tried reaching people at Meta on LinkedIn, but got no reply either way.
The easiest way to discover the URLs is to perform a passive DNS search through one of many available commercial services. Passive DNS records store the historical resolution of domain names to IP addresses, as well as nameserver, and mail-server records over time. Passive DNS systems typically collect DNS responses from sensors positioned at recursive DNS resolvers or other infrastructure. A passive DNS record is generally created when a monitoring system observes a DNS response. In the case here, once the intended party clicks on the share link, the DNS information is recorded in a searchable database.
And look! They call it superintelligence on that page, just like Trump.
Oh boy…

articles.title: TP-Link proposes $1 billion US Wi-Fi router manufacturing alliance with Key Tronic — potential deal seeks to end ongoing saga blocking its Wi-Fi 8 products from American homes
articles.text:
TP-Link proposes $1 billion US Wi-Fi router manufacturing alliance with Key Tronic — potential deal seeks to end ongoing saga blocking its Wi-Fi 8 products from American homes
You scratch my back, I’ll scratch yours
TP-Link is fully determined to get in the good graces of the U.S. government to break free from a total ban on newly developed routers manufactured outside of the country. Although TP-Link is incorporated in the U.S. with a headquarters in Irvine, California, the company has been under pressure from the full weight of the U.S. government because of its historical Chinese roots. However, in an effort to appeal to the Trump administration’s zeal for creating jobs and touting American manufacturing, TP-Link this week announced that it has signed a letter of intent to assemble routers in the U.S. through a crucial partnership with Key Tronic.
How did we get here?
The ongoing saga started back in late 2024, when the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party requested that the Department of Commerce investigate TP-Link. At the time, the committee warned that “TP-Link products are also found on U.S. military bases, with the Army and Air Force Exchange and the Navy Exchange selling these devices to members of the military and their families,” and claimed TP-Link routers were sending user data back to China.
The select committee implored the Department of Commerce to use its broad powers to investigate TP-Link and take any necessary action to mitigate threats to national security. The campaign against TP-Link ramped up in mid-2025, with 17 members of Congress petitioning the Commerce Department to ban the sale of the company’s hardware in the U.S. due to alleged deep ties to the CCP. In late 2025, 23 U.S. House members and Senators again asked the Commerce Department to investigate TP-Link’s actions, including adding the company to the Covered List, investigating any threats to national security, and informing the public about potential risks associated with using the company’s devices.
The situation reached a boiling point in March 2026, when TP-Link and other router manufacturers were added to the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) Covered List, forbidding the sale of foreign-made routers in the U.S. that hadn’t already been approved. At the time, the FCC noted, “Recently, malicious state and non-state sponsored cyber attackers have increasingly leveraged the vulnerabilities in small and home office routers produced abroad to carry out direct attacks against American civilians in their homes. From disrupting network connectivity to enabling local networking espionage and intellectual property theft, foreign-produced routers present unacceptable risks to Americans.”
Since that time, several things have changed, with none of them being positive developments for TP-Link. Over the past six months, Amazon, Asus, and Netgear have all gained conditional approvals from the FCC to sell new wireless products in the U.S., while TP-Link has been stonewalled (conditional approvals are valid for 18 months from the date of issuance). Considering that TP-Link has been the world’s largest provider of Wi-Fi routers and associated devices for over a decade, losing access to the U.S. market for its new line of Wi-Fi 8 devices is a significant blow. This was readily apparent in late September when TP-Link opened preorders for its Archer 8 Ultra Wi-Fi 8 router. The company announced that the router would be available in the United Kingdom, Germany, and Australia. However, the U.S. was conspicuously absent from that list because of the ongoing ban.
Adding insult to injury, earlier this month, multiple states (including Florida, Montana, Iowa, and Nebraska) sued TP-Link Systems, alleging that the company has made false and misleading claims about the security capabilities of its products and continued ties to China.
“TP-Link’s conduct has placed Montana consumers at risk of harm by making their home and small-office networks vulnerable to exploitation and intrusion by foreign actors with a proven track record of nefarious conduct. That risk is ongoing: many consumers keep their routers for years, and many of the compromised TP-Link models in Montana homes do not support automatic firmware updates and no longer receive security support at all,” stated Montana Attorney General Austin Knudsen.
Knudsen further claimed that while TP-Link touts that it employs 300 people in the U.S., the bulk of its workforce (numbering over 11,000 employees) conducts development and manufacturing operations in China. “Further, TP-Link claims to manufacture its U.S.-market products in Vietnam, but less than one percent of the components by value are sourced in Vietnam, and the rest are imported from or through China,” Knudsen added.
“Iowans’ sensitive data and our national security is at risk because of TP-Link and their connection to the communist Chinese government,” stated Iowa Attorney General Bird. “TP-Link tells Iowans its routers are safe, our personal data is secure, and that they have no ties to China. They are not telling the truth. It’s time to hold China and China-backed companies accountable.”
TP-Link barks back
Up until this point, TP-Link has vehemently denied any ties to the Chinese government and has refuted similar allegations from one of its primary competitors, Netgear. However, on October 13, the company issued its sharpest rebuttal yet in a letter to the FCC. TP-Link touted its “America-first” strategy and chastised the state lawsuits brought earlier this month.
“A group of 21 state-level officials recently raised a scattershot barrage of baseless and previously debunked allegations relating to TP-Link’s confidential, non-public application,” TP-Link exclaimed. Rather than seeking to advance legitimate public policy objectives, the letter appears aimed primarily at encouraging federal officials to apply a heightened standard to TP-Link’s pending application that would be unattainable to TP-Link or any other router manufacturer in the world.”
TP-Link stated that its innovation in the router space earned its position as the market leader in the U.S., and that the constant barrage of legal fights and war of words is undermining fair competition and is an actual threat to national security and critical infrastructure given the broad proliferation of its products.
To that end, TP-Link reiterated that it has officially filed for conditional approval from the FCC, so that it can specifically sell two next-generation Wi-Fi 8 routers in the U.S. The company noted, “As the United States positions itself as a leader in wireless technology, a Conditional Approval would guarantee American consumers access to the same cutting-edge wireless equipment that will soon be available in other parts of the world."
TP-Link proposes $1 billion investment in the U.S.
With its back against the ropes, TP-Link is appealing to the U.S. government in the best way it knows how: with money and jobs. If there’s anything that the U.S. government likes, it’s investment in manufacturing on its own soil and high-paying jobs to bolster local economies. To help push the U.S. government along in approving a conditional approval to sell Wi-Fi 8 hardware, TP-Link has signed a letter of intent with Key Tronic to manufacture routers in the U.S. instead of importing them from Vietnam. More specifically, the routers would be assembled in Corinth, Mississippi.
“This LOI with Key Tronic demonstrates our firm commitment to expanding domestic advanced manufacturing, and establishing America as our base for delivering secure, reliable connectivity solutions to households and businesses around the world,” said TP-Link Systems Inc. CEO Jeffrey Chao. “By choosing to assemble cutting-edge products here at home, we are thrilled to support U.S. high-tech job growth and empower a new generation of American innovation and innovators.”
TP-Link hopes that the investment will cut through most of the red tape that is currently preventing it from selling its latest products stateside. However, it remains to be seen if these latest sweeteners will be enough to sway President Trump and the agencies under his purview. As the company notes, it was the first to deliver Wi-Fi 7 routers in the U.S., and it wants to continue that leadership position by offering the first Wi-Fi 8 routers. The hardware is ready to go, as evidenced by the opening of preorders; it’s just currently being held up by roadblocks at the federal level, along with added pressure from state governments.
Until that time, Wi-Fi 8 products like the Archer 8 Ultra and Deco 8 Ultra will remain off-limits to Americans, which have given TP-Link a reported 65 percent share of the U.S. consumer router market.
Brandon Hill is a senior editor at Tom's Hardware. He has written about PC and Mac tech since the late 1990s with bylines at AnandTech, DailyTech, and Hot Hardware. When he is not consuming copious amounts of tech news, he can be found enjoying the NC mountains or the beach with his wife and two sons.

articles.title: Ils confient leur Android TV à une IA pour supprimer les pubs, et ça marche (presque) toujours
articles.text:
Allumer sa télévision et devoir passer devant une bande-annonce, une rangée de « recommandations » et une application jamais installée avant d’atteindre Netflix : le scénario est devenu banal pour de nombreux utilisateurs. Certains propriétaires ont décidé de régler le problème en confiant leur télé à un agent d’intelligence artificielle comme Claude Code, l’outil de programmation d’Anthropic. Nous l’évoquions déjà fin août, mais le phénomène a pris une tout autre ampleur ces derniers jours, au point que nos confrères de TechCrunch parlent de gens qui rendent leur TV « bête » à nouveau.
 Vibe coded my parents’ TV this afternoon!
It was showing a sponsored ad before you could even get to Netflix.
Gave Claude Code the model number, it found the TV on wifi, removed 25 Xiaomi packages and wrote a new launcher.
Looks like an Apple TV now lol https://t.co/E5Q4A1b0yI
— Gathin (Ø,G) (@gathint) October 17, 2026
Tout est reparti d’un développeur, Gathin T., agacé par les publicités qui s’affichaient sur le téléviseur Xiaomi de ses parents avant même d’accéder à Netflix. Il a laissé Claude Code nettoyer la télé et construire un écran d’accueil simple, puis a publié son prompt sur GitHub. « Quelques milliers de personnes ont fait la même chose sur leur télé dans les deux jours suivants », raconte-t-il. Son projet, CleanYourTV, dépasse aujourd’hui les 7 000 étoiles sur GitHub, et d’autres ont suivi, comme dumbtv.
« Votre télé devrait faire ce pour quoi vous avez payé : vos applications, vos entrées HDMI, et rien d’autre. Pas de pubs de la télé elle-même, pas de suivi de ce que vous regardez, pas de mise à jour que vous n’avez pas demandée. », le projet dumbtv, sur GitHub
Depuis, les avant-après et les retours d’expérience se multiplient sur X. Un utilisateur, Ryan Doyle, raconte avoir simplement envoyé à Claude Code la fiche produit de son téléviseur en lui demandant « peux-tu hacker ça ? », avant d’être guidé pas à pas pour supprimer pubs et logiciels inutiles et retrouver une interface réactive. Un autre utilisateur affirme avoir fait le ménage en un après-midi, avec des fonds d’écran qui défilent en prime.
 This is how fast the TV moves now that Claude deleted all the BS laggy bloatware it comes with https://t.co/g07CEgC1GJ
— Ryan Doyle (@doooyle) October 17, 2026
Certains ne s’arrêtent pas au ménage : l’un s’est offert un économiseur d’écran affichant météo, agenda et notifications de paiements, un autre a ajouté une bascule entre l’hindi et l’anglais pour ses parents, et un troisième affiche désormais en direct les cotes de paris sportifs de Polymarket sur sa télé. « On peut vraiment faire n’importe quoi de nos jours », s’amuse-t-il.
« Un après-midi avec Claude Code : 25 applications inutiles désactivées, le lanceur d’origine de 192 Mo remplacé par un lanceur maison de 83 Mo, et des fonds d’écran qui défilent. », Mihir Gupta, sur X
Comment ça marche ?
L’architecture ouverte et la flexibilité d’Android rendent possible l’accès à ADB (Android Debug Bridge), l’outil de débogage d’Android qui permet de piloter un appareil depuis un ordinateur. Pour en profiter, il faut activer les options développeur du téléviseur, généralement en appuyant sept fois sur la mention « Build » dans les informations système, puis le débogage USB ou réseau. On colle ensuite le prompt dans un agent capable d’exécuter des commandes sur l’ordinateur, comme Claude Code, et l’IA se connecte à la télé par le Wi-Fi après une autorisation à valider à l’écran.
L’IA se charge alors de sauvegarder la liste des applications, de désactiver la télémétrie, les services publicitaires et les logiciels préinstallés. Les applications ne sont pas supprimées, seulement mises en sommeil, et un script permet de tout restaurer. Une fois le ménage terminé, l’IA remplace l’écran d’accueil d’origine par un lanceur maison très léger, pensé pour les téléviseurs d’entrée de gamme. Le tout s’effectue sans root, ce qui rend la manipulation accessible au plus grand nombre. Comptez de dix minutes à un après-midi si l’on en croit les témoignages qui pullulent sur les réseaux sociaux, pour un coût nul en dehors de l’abonnement à l’outil d’IA.
Quels téléviseurs sont concernés ?
La méthode concerne surtout les téléviseurs et box sous Android TV ou Google TV, de Xiaomi à Sony en passant par TCL. Les Fire TV d’Amazon n’ont droit qu’au nettoyage, car la surcouche Fire OS refuse les lanceurs tiers.
Quant aux modèles de chez Samsung et LG, qui tournent sous Tizen OS et webOS, ils sont nettement plus difficiles à débrider : aucun équivalent d’ADB ne permet d’y désactiver les applications du fabricant. Du côté de Samsung, au terme d’un long parcours de développeur, on peut tout au plus installer un écran d’accueil qui se lance par-dessus l’interface d’origine, comme le propose le projet CleanFrame. Chez LG, remplacer l’accueil impose de rooter le téléviseur via une faille, puis de renoncer aux mises à jour pour conserver ses modifications.
Quels sont les risques ?
La plupart des listes de nettoyage coupent le service de mise à jour du fabricant, celui par lequel reviennent les publicités, mais aussi les correctifs de sécurité. Il faudra penser à le réactiver de temps en temps. Notez aussi qu’ADB par Wi-Fi passe en clair sur le réseau local, et doit être refermé une fois le travail terminé. Des botnets comme ADB.Miner ont en effet déjà infecté des milliers de box et de téléviseurs Android par ce biais.
L’IA peut aussi se tromper et certains utilisateurs se sont retrouvés bloqués à mi-parcours, l’un d’eux affirmant même avoir rendu son téléviseur inutilisable. S’il est le plus souvent possible de repartir de zéro en cas de problème majeur, ces étapes peuvent vite devenir fastidieuses, surtout si l’on n’a pas l’âme d’un bidouilleur. Enfin, toutes les recettes ne se valent pas : dumbtv désinstalle par exemple certaines applications de streaming, que son script de restauration ne fait pas revenir. Mieux vaut donc relire chaque changement proposé avant de l’accepter.
Pour ceux qui préfèrent éviter ces risques, il reste possible d’installer soi-même un lanceur alternatif tel que Projectivy Launcher ou FLauncher, que nous évoquions déjà cet été. Quant aux fabricants, l’intérêt pour ces outils dopés à l’IA leur envoie un message clair : si leurs clients sont prêts à passer un après-midi avec une IA pour retrouver une télé simple, une option dans les réglages éviterait bien des bricolages.

articles.title: SmartBear’s BearQ adds Sources to find coverage gaps and Workflows to automate test runs - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
SmartBear’s BearQ adds Sources to find coverage gaps and Workflows to automate test runs
Software testing company SmartBear Software Inc. is pushing its BearQ agentic quality assurance system beyond test automation with two new capabilities released today.
Both additions target the part of quality assurance that artificial intelligence has made more difficult by speeding up coding. SmartBear calls them Sources and Workflows.
Automating individual tests is no longer the bottleneck, in the company’s telling. The tougher job now is working out what still needs testing across sprawling systems, much of it already covered by tests sitting in other tools.
Sources widens BearQ’s view past the application itself. Requirements and bug reports now flow in from Atlassian Corp.’s Jira so the agent knows what ought to be tested. SmartBear’s own Reflect and Zephyr testing tools show what existing tests already cover. BearQ draws on that context to find gaps in coverage before it writes anything new, so teams end up with fewer duplicate tests.
Workflows picks up from there, letting a team chain jobs together behind a single trigger. Once a build lands in the continuous integration and delivery pipeline, for example, BearQ can spin up a test environment and run regression tests against it. Whatever the run turns up goes back into the team’s connected systems, and anyone who would rather not tie testing to builds can put the same sequence on a schedule. How much of a workflow runs without human review is up to the team.
Progressive autonomy is SmartBear’s name for that arrangement. Teams begin with people signing off on what BearQ does, then hand over more of the process as their confidence grows. Trust was the top barrier to adopting or scaling autonomous testing, named by 23% of the 1,436 U.S. and U.K. respondents in a survey SmartBear released Sept. 30.
Bridges Smith, vice president of product management for AI at SmartBear, called autonomous testing “the first step.” By Smith’s account, the bigger opportunity is connecting how an application actually behaves with what a team intends it to do and the test suite it has built up. People would still set the guardrails, Smith said, describing the shift as a move “beyond autonomous testing toward autonomous quality.”
SmartBear has been building BearQ out since it first appeared in March, when the company opened early access for web applications built by midmarket software-as-a-service providers. A September update made it an assignable agent inside Jira. SmartBear’s older lineup includes the Swagger tools for designing application programming interfaces, and about 32,000 organizations use its software, by the company’s count.
More Sources connections are due before the quarter ends. Both features get a public demonstration Thursday in a livestream with “Project Hail Mary” author Andy Weir.

articles.title: Axiomtek Launches MANO330 Compact Thin Mini-ITX Industrial Motherboard
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
Axiomtek Launches MANO330 Compact Thin Mini-ITX Industrial Motherboard
Axiomtek, a world-renowned leader relentlessly devoted to the research, development, and manufacture of innovative, highly efficient, and reliable industrial computer products, proudly introduces the MANO330, a compact Thin Mini-ITX motherboard powered by the Intel Processor N97 or N150 and DDR5 memory. Designed for space-constrained systems that require flexible connectivity and expansion, the MANO330 combines multi-display capability, dual LAN connectivity, versatile M.2 expansion, and industrial I/O in a compact platform. With a wide 12-24 VDC power input, the MANO330 provides system developers with a flexible foundation for smart manufacturing and industrial automation, digital signage, smart retail, and POS applications.
Compact Performance for Space-Constrained Systems
The MANO330 combines a compact Thin Mini-ITX design with Intel Processor N97 or N150 and DDR5-4800 memory support. The N97 supports up to 32 GB of memory, while the N150 supports up to 16 GB. Measuring just 170 x 170 mm, the MANO330 provides the essential computing performance and I/O capabilities needed for embedded systems, helping developers build space-efficient solutions for a wide range of industrial and commercial applications.Rich Visuals and Reliable Network Connectivity
Designed for information-rich applications, the MANO330 supports multiple independent display outputs through HDMI, VGA, LVDS/eDP interface, and USB Type-C with DisplayPort support. This display flexibility allows system developers to configure multiple screens for applications such as digital signage, retail displays, and industrial monitoring. The board also integrates 2.5GbE and GbE LAN, providing reliable network connectivity for connected systems and industrial applications.
Flexible Expansion to Fit Different Applications
The MANO330 provides flexible expansion options for storage and wireless connectivity. Its M.2 Key M 2280 slot supports SATA/NVMe storage, while M.2 Key E 2230 supports wireless connectivity. The M.2 Key B 3042/3052 interface provides an additional expansion option and is paired with a Nano SIM slot for wireless applications. These options allow customers to configure storage and connectivity according to their application requirements, helping simplify system development and integration.
Built-In I/O for Easier System Integration
The MANO330 integrates commonly used industrial interfaces directly on the board, including RS-232, RS-422/485, USB, SATA, and GPIO, helping reduce the need for additional interface hardware. Two RS-232 ports support jumper-selectable RS-422 or RS-485, while four additional RS-232 ports provide further serial connectivity for industrial devices. Combined with the board's 12-24 VDC power input, these built-in interfaces provide system developers with greater flexibility and help simplify system integration.
Tina Tu, Product Manager at Axiomtek"Today's embedded systems need to balance compact design with flexibility for different application requirements. With versatile display, connectivity, expansion, and industrial I/O options, the MANO330 gives system developers greater freedom to configure and integrate solutions for a wide range of industrial and commercial applications"
Advanced Features of MANO330
- Intel Processor N97/N150
- DDR5-4800 SO-DIMM, up to 32 GB with N97 and 16 GB with N150
- Dual LAN ports
- M.2 Key B 3042/3052
- M.2 Key E 2230
- M.2 Key M 2280
The MANO330 is now available.

articles.title: Eric Schmidt reportedly owns about half as much of Anthropic as CEO Dario Amodei | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Eric Schmidt’s fortune is about to get even bigger. The former Google CEO is reported to own about 1% of Anthropic after investing tens of millions of dollars in the leading AI lab’s Series A round in 2021, according to Bloomberg. The startup was valued at $461 million at the time, according to PitchBook data.
If Bloomberg’s estimate is accurate, Schmidt’s stake is remarkably large compared with the 2% of the company that co-founder and CEO Dario Amodei holds. Anthropic is widely expected to go public before the end of the year, with top-end market estimates valuing the company at as much as $2 trillion. At that valuation, Schmidt would add as much as $20 billion to his net worth, which Bloomberg currently puts at $57.5 billion.
Schmidt has been an active tech investor since stepping down as Google CEO in 2011. He deploys capital through multiple entities, including Tomorrow Ventures, Innovation Endeavors Management, and his family office, Hillspire. His other AI bets include Mistral, General Intuition, and Reflection AI.
Schmidt and Anthropic didn’t immediately respond to our request for comment.

articles.title: India-New Zealand trade pact kicks in
articles.text:
India-New Zealand trade pact kicks in
The agreement provides duty-free access to a range of Indian goods, including products from labour-intensive sectors such as textiles and leather.
The India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement (FTA), signed on April 27, came into effect on Tuesday, providing duty-free access to a range of Indian goods, including products from labour-intensive sectors such as textiles and leather.
It is the seventh trade pact to come into force in the last five years. The others are agreements with the UAE, Mauritius, the European Free Trade Association (EFTA) bloc, the UK, Oman and Australia.
Signed on April 27, 2026, the agreement follows negotiations launched in 2010, stalled in 2015 and revived in March 2025. The pact becomes India's 17th operational FTA.
According to experts, the sectors benefiting from the FTA are textiles and apparel, leather and footwear, engineering goods and auto components, gems and jewellery, agriculture and processed foods, pharmaceuticals, and other manufacturing industries.
Gulzar Didwania, Partner, Deloitte India, said the deal is expected to support higher FDI inflows into India, but the scale of any increase remains uncertain and will depend on private-sector investment decisions.
New Zealand has committed FDI worth USD 20 billion in over 15 years.
"The FTA's provisions on duty-free access for certain inputs, bilateral cumulation, customs facilitation, and investment-promotion mechanisms may encourage deeper value-chain integration and improve investment conditions," he said.
He added that the pact has significance beyond trade, strengthening India's strategic position in the Indo-Pacific, expanding its network of FTAs with developed economies.
At a time of growing global trade uncertainty, the India-New Zealand FTA is a strong endorsement of open markets and predictable trade rules. Its target of doubling bilateral trade by 2030 sets an ambitious agenda for both countries.
What makes this FTA particularly valuable is that it goes beyond goods to cover services, investment, skills and mobility, creating fresh opportunities for Indian professionals and businesses.
With 100 per cent of Indian exports gaining duty-free access to New Zealand from day one, the agreement gives Indian exporters a significant competitive advantage. MSMEs in textiles, leather, footwear and engineering goods are particularly well placed to benefit.
Economic think tank Chintan Research Foundation (CRF India) President Shishir Priyadarshi said that at a time of growing global trade uncertainty, the India-New Zealand FTA is a strong endorsement of open markets and predictable trade rules.
"What makes this FTA particularly valuable is that it goes beyond goods to cover services, investment, skills and mobility, creating fresh opportunities for Indian professionals and businesses," he said.
Trade expert and Hi-Tech Gears Chairman Deep Kapuria said the FTA operationalisation with New Zealand completes India's preferential market access in all major countries of the Asia-Pacific region.
"New Zealand is a very open economy; India has very well crafted this trade deal by securing market access for new services such as Ayush, yoga instructors and student mobility, including post-study work visa," he said.
Bilateral trade declined by about 11 per cent to USD 1.15 billion in 2025-26 from USD 1.3 billion in the previous fiscal year. India's exports stood at USD 566.51 million, while imports were USD 589.1 million, resulting in a meagre trade deficit of USD 22.59 million for India.
Rani Singh, Indian-origin New Zealander, said the deal is an important step forward for both countries as it is not just about trade; it is about bringing the two countries closer, creating opportunities for businesses and people, and building a stronger relationship for the future.
"India now has an opportunity to build its own strong partnership with New Zealand. With duty-free access to New Zealand for all Indian export tariff lines from day one, Indian businesses can become more competitive in this market," she said.
Singh added that the benefits are not limited to goods as there is also scope for greater cooperation in education, tourism, technology, professional services and investment.
Greater opportunities for eligible skilled professionals and young people can further strengthen these connections, she said.

articles.title: 50 morts : Anthropic veut réglementer l’IA, mais fixe des seuils qui font froid dans le dos
articles.text:
Selon les informations du média Politico, des représentants d’Anthropic, l’entreprise derrière Claude, se sont rendus au Capitole afin de présenter un projet de loi à des élus, visant à réglementer le développement de l’intelligence artificielle. Aussi surprenant que cela puisse paraître, les seuils fixés par Anthropic pour permettre aux autorités de faire suspendre un modèle d’IA sont particulièrement élevés : une menace pouvant provoquer plus de 50 morts ou blessés graves, ou plus d’un milliard de dollars de dommages.
50 morts ou un milliard de dollars de dommages : les seuils surprenants fixés par Anthropic
Ce projet de loi élaboré par Anthropic établit trois cas où une IA de pointe pourrait être bloquée : le développement d’une arme biologique, une cyberattaque et un modèle échappant au contrôle de son concepteur. Il s’agit donc de cas souvent évoqués et particulièrement redoutés. Mais nous arrivons au point le plus surprenant : le blocage d’une IA ne pourrait être déclenché par le gouvernement américain que si l’un de ces deux seuils risque d’être atteint. Le premier seuil serait atteint si une IA pouvait provoquer plus de 50 morts ou blessés graves. Le second seuil est quant à lui atteint lorsque plus d’un milliard de dollars de dommages sont enregistrés. Ce faisant, Anthropic fixe donc un prix à une vie humaine. en deors de toute question éthique posée par ce genre de calculs une autre question s’impose : pourquoi attendre de tels dégâts avant de stopper une IA ?
Précisons aussi que la surveillance des modèles d’IA serait confiée à des évaluateurs indépendants, enregistrés auprès du département américain du Commerce. Les laboratoires pourraient les rémunérer, à condition que leur paiement ne dépende pas des conclusions de leurs évaluations. Si un risque imminent est identifié, les évaluateurs devront le signaler au département du Commerce dans les 72 heures suivant la fin de leur évaluation. Un juge fédéral du district de Columbia serait par ailleurs le seul habilité à ordonner la suspension d’un modèle d’IA, à la demande du département américain du Commerce.
Pourquoi des seuils aussi élevés ?
Si l’on résume l’actualité récente : Anthropic appelle à ralentir le développement de l’IA et annonce la création d’un fonds destiné au bien public, tout en proposant de limiter le blocage d’un modèle d’IA aux cas où il risque de provoquer plus de 50 morts ou blessés graves, ou plus d’un milliard de dollars de dommages. À première vue, il est difficile d’y voir une logique.
En réalité, Anthropic devrait continuer à encadrer en interne le développement de ses IA, sans attendre que l’une d’entre elles risque de provoquer plus de 50 morts ou blessés graves. Avec ce projet de loi, l’entreprise cherche surtout à définir les conditions dans lesquelles le gouvernement américain pourrait bloquer un modèle d’IA, tout en limitant les possibilités d’intervention des autorités.

articles.title: Marie Curie y Einstein se escribieron cartas durante más de 20 años. 100 años después podemos leer lo que se decían
articles.text:
El 7 de julio de 1922, Marie Curie le escribió a Albert Einstein para echarle la bronca. Con buenas formas, sí; pero bronca al fin y al cabo: Curie le llegaba a decir que le había causado una 'gran decepción'.
Durante 21 años, dos de los científicos más importantes de la historia se escribieron cartas en las que apenas se hablaba de física. Lo que hicieron fue cubrirse las espaldas. Y ahora, un siglo después, podemos leer la historia completa.
¿"Una gran decepción"? Tres días antes de aquella carta del 7 de julio, Einstein le había contado a Curie que iba a dimitir de la comisión de cooperación intelectual de la Sociedad de Naciones. Le confesó las razones, pero le pidió que no se las contara a nadie.
El 24 de junio habían asesinado en Berlín al ministro de Exteriores de la República de Weimar, Walther Rathenau, un viejo amigo de Einstein. Aquello había acabado por desmoralizarle. Y, precisamente por eso, Curie le cantaba las cuarenta. Claro que había corrientes de opinión extremadamente dañinas, pero a su juicio había que combatirlas y, de hecho, estaba convencida de que el mismo Rathenau estaría de acuerdo con ella. ¿No había alguna posibilidad de que cambiara de idea?
Un libro para la historia de la ciencia. No ha sido fácil recopilar la correspondencia entre ambos. Durante años, se han rastreado archivos en Jerusalén, París, Zúrich, Princeton, Düsseldorf o Varsovia y apenas se han encontrado 32 cartas. Algunas eran muy conocidas (como aquella en la que Einstein le decía a Curie que ignorara a los haters), otras se habían llegado a publicar. Algunas, en cambio, conservaban polvo radioactivo y hubo que limpiarlas.
Sin embargo, juntas cuentan alguna de las historias más interesantes de la ciencia del siglo XX.
Todo empezó con un linchamiento. Aunque se había conocido antes, su amistad surgió después del primer Consejo Solvay en 1911. Ella era la única mujer y él era el invitado más joven. En plena conferencia, la prensa desveló el romance que Curie supuestamente mantenía con Paul Langevin, casado y separado de hecho. Fue un escándalo mayúsculo para la sociedad el momento.
Al llegar a París, según cuentan, había una muchedumbre rodeando la casa. La polémica fue tan grande que Svante Arrhenius, del comité Nobel, le sugirió que no fuera a recoger su segundo premio.
Una semana antes, Einstein desde Praga le escribió diciéndole que estaba furioso con cómo el público se metía en su vida, que admiraba su trabajo, su energía y su honestidad y que no leyera lo que escribía "la chusma". Finalmente, Marie Curie fue a recoger el premio contra viento y marea.
¿Y colaboraron juntos? La verdad es que no. Es verdad que en esa 'primera' carta, Einstein añadió algunos comentarios científicos; pero sus campos apenas se tocaban. Eran "amigos sociales": en 1913 se fueron de excursión a pie por la Engadina con los niños. Días después, Einstein confesaría a su futura esposa que Curie era muy inteligente, pero "fría como un pez" (aunque los expertos no se ponen de acuerdo en si era verdad o una estrategia para que Löwenthal no se pusiera celosa).
¿Pero dimitió finalmente? En ese momento no. El apoyo de Curie y el de otros amigos hizo que la retirara. En 1923 dimitió finamente y en el 24 volvió al comité. Aquellos años fueron complicados. No hace falta ni decirlo. Por eso sorprende tanto leerlo contado en primera persona.
