articles.title: XUPER TV Conecta y deportes En Vivo: por qué se busca en Google y no es recomendado
articles.text:
“XUPER TV Conecta” y “deportes En Vivo” son algunas de las búsquedas que más crecen entre quienes quieren ver series, películas y eventos deportivos sin pagar suscripciones. La aplicación, antes conocida como Magis TV, circula fuera de las tiendas oficiales y se instala de forma manual en televisores, TV Box y celulares con Android.
Según un análisis de ESET, ese método de distribución puede comprometer el funcionamiento del dispositivo y exponer datos personales de los usuarios.
El interés por “XUPER TV Conecta” y “deportes En Vivo” no se limita a la calidad de la transmisión. El verdadero riesgo aparece en los permisos que estas plataformas solicitan para funcionar, muchos de los cuales exceden lo necesario para reproducir contenido. Esos accesos pueden facilitar la lectura de archivos privados, la instalación de otros programas sin aviso y el envío de notificaciones engañosas.
Por qué buscar “XUPER TV Conecta” y “deportes En Vivo” implica un riesgo
Quienes buscan “XUPER TV Conecta” y “deportes En Vivo” suelen llegar a páginas web, enlaces compartidos en redes sociales o grupos de mensajería. Ese circuito evita los procesos de revisión que aplican Google Play Store, App Store y otros catálogos oficiales antes de habilitar una descarga.
La ausencia de esos controles permite que el archivo descargado incluya funciones no informadas al usuario. Es posible que el enlace lleve a una versión modificada de la aplicación, con malware incorporado desde el origen.
En ese escenario, el televisor o el dispositivo conectado a la pantalla queda expuesto desde el momento mismo de la instalación. No existe forma de verificar, antes de instalar, qué contiene realmente el archivo descargado.
Qué datos personales quedan expuestos al instalar la aplicación
ESET advirtió que el archivo de Magis TV, asociado ahora a la búsqueda de XUPER TV, pide autorizaciones que permiten revisar el contenido guardado en el dispositivo. Esto puede abarcar fotos, videos, documentos, grabaciones de audio y otros archivos disponibles en el almacenamiento interno o externo.
En un televisor, el riesgo puede alcanzar a los dispositivos vinculados. Si una memoria USB, un teléfono o una cuenta personal se conectan al equipo, una aplicación con permisos amplios puede obtener información que no guarda relación alguna con la reproducción de contenidos.
¿Por qué es peligroso instalar XUPER TV en el televisor? Porque la aplicación circula fuera de las tiendas oficiales y puede solicitar permisos excesivos que permiten acceder a archivos privados, instalar otros programas sin autorización explícita y enviar notificaciones fraudulentas que buscan robar datos personales.
Cómo una app pirata puede instalar programas sin control del usuario
Uno de los accesos detectados permite que la aplicación solicite la descarga e instalación de otros paquetes de software. En apariencia, esa función puede presentarse como una actualización, un complemento para ver un canal o una mejora del reproductor.
Sin embargo, ese mismo mecanismo puede utilizarse para introducir programas espía, troyanos o herramientas destinadas a capturar información del usuario. La persona puede aceptar la acción sin advertir que instaló una aplicación adicional ajena al servicio original.
Una supuesta actualización, entonces, puede convertirse en una vía directa para agregar software malicioso al dispositivo sin que exista un control real por parte de quien lo utiliza.
El riesgo se extiende a toda la red doméstica
Las autorizaciones analizadas por ESET incluyen capacidades para revisar procesos activos, modificar archivos y gestionar unidades de almacenamiento. En manos de una aplicación no confiable, esas funciones pueden alterar documentos, borrar contenido o afectar la operación normal del dispositivo.
El alcance tampoco queda limitado a la pantalla del televisor. Un equipo conectado al mismo router que computadoras, celulares, cámaras o asistentes domésticos forma parte de una red compartida.
Si el dispositivo principal se infecta, puede convertirse en una puerta de entrada para ataques contra otros aparatos conectados a esa misma red. El riesgo puede extenderse desde el televisor hacia toda la red WiFi doméstica.
Notificaciones falsas: la puerta de entrada al robo de datos
Las aplicaciones de este tipo pueden pedir autorización para mostrar avisos en pantalla. Una función pensada para informar novedades puede usarse para distribuir publicidad invasiva, mensajes fraudulentos o alertas que imiten comunicaciones legítimas de servicios conocidos.
A través de esas notificaciones, un atacante puede intentar que la persona ingrese credenciales, descargue una nueva aplicación o entregue información personal sin notarlo. El riesgo aumenta cuando el aviso recurre a mensajes urgentes, como advertencias sobre una suspensión de cuenta, fallas técnicas o supuestas verificaciones de seguridad.

articles.title: IBM-backed llm-d framework adds controls for running AI models in-house - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
IBM-backed llm-d framework adds controls for running AI models in-house
IBM Corp. and several other contributors to the open-source llm-d project are releasing version 1.0 of their distributed artificial intelligence inference framework, adding operational controls intended to help enterprises run large models reliably on their own infrastructure.
The release, announced ahead of the PyTorch Conference North America in San Jose today and tomorrow, focuses on managing competing workloads, maintaining service during upgrades and improving hardware efficiency as AI agents generate growing volumes of model requests.
Built for Kubernetes, llm-d coordinates model serving across computing infrastructure. IBM, its Red Hat subsidiary and Google LLC are its lead maintainers. They co-founded the project last year with CoreWeave Inc. and Nvidia Corp. Other contributors include Advanced Micro Devices Inc., Cisco Systems Inc., Hugging Face Inc., Intel Corp. and Mistral AI SAS.
The project offers organizations seeking more control over inference costs and infrastructure choices a way to reduce dependence on a single model provider, cloud or hardware platform.
“At IBM Research, we are seeing that open large language models and llm-d can greatly lower the costs of inference in computationally demanding problems such as designing hardware for quantum error correction, helping achieve a 11.8X efficiency advantage,” Ruchir Puri, IBM Research’s chief scientist, vice president of IBM’s Technology & Technical Community and IBM Fellow, wrote in e-mailed comments. “Llm-d 1.0 extends these savings by delivering the operational readiness needed for enterprises to extract more out of their computational capacity.”
The project is focused on what happens after deployment. A production inference service must handle changing traffic, hardware failures, software updates and users competing for resources while maintaining acceptable response times.
Version 1.0 adds support for quality of service across multiple tenants, zero-downtime operations and serving patterns tailored to AI agents. Flow controls and prioritization are designed to keep bursts of agent activity from overwhelming services that require fast responses, such as coding assistants used by people.
The release “adds the maturity to run it like any other critical service: a stable [application programming interface], multiple tenants with competing priorities sharing the same infrastructure and upgrades that don’t interrupt operations,” said Carlos Costa, distinguished engineer at IBM Research and a project co-founder and lead maintainer.
Workloads can behave differently even when they reach models through the same endpoint. An agent may issue many requests, pause to use an external tool and return for additional model calls.
The framework can keep requests directed to appropriate infrastructure across multiple turns, increasing opportunities to reuse previously processed context. That matters because agents repeatedly consult the same code, documents, instructions and conversation history while completing assignments.
A routing system directs requests toward replicas that already hold relevant cached context. Another capability moves cached information among graphics processing unit memory, CPU memory and storage, preserving reusable information when GPU capacity becomes constrained.
These techniques were previously available, but version 1.0 integrates them with operational controls, along with methods that separate prompt processing from response generation, optimize work batches and distribute large mixture-of-experts models across accelerators. IBM cited a recent agentic coding test in which the framework’s router captured 97% of available cache reuse.
In a separate demonstration, IBM and Red Hat said they ran 3,000 software-engineering agents concurrently on self-hosted infrastructure at a cost five to 10 times lower than serving the same open model through a hosted service.
The economics become more significant as agents perform multiple rounds of reasoning, tool use and revision for a single assignment, IBM said. Reprocessing identical material at each step consumes additional computing resources.
Llm-d works with inference engines including vLLM and SGLang, supplying distributed routing and operational capabilities around model servers. It is currently hosted as a sandbox project by the Cloud Native Computing Foundation.
“It delivers high-performance, distributed inference with the reliability and scale enterprises need within an operational model they already know,” said Stephen Watt, vice president in Red Hat’s chief technology officer’s office.

articles.title: The transformation trap: Why organizations are trying to change too much, too fast
articles.text:
The transformation trap: Why organizations are trying to change too much, too fast
Organizations can be under huge pressure to make changes to their IT estates. In particular, there are two drivers of this change.
Firstly, there’s the pressure to innovate. The rapid advancement of technology and AI coupled with shifting business priorities can put organizations under pressure to adopt the latest tools, with vendor messaging advocating for the speed of adoption. Simultaneously, ongoing inflation and slower economic growth can mean there is a need to find more cost-effective solutions.
Technical Manager at Cloudhouse.
Secondly, there’s the change that is forced. Operating systems might be reaching their end of life and need upgrading, or there are outages and cyber threats to defend against. There have also been several recent examples of software vendor prices rising significantly due to ownership changes, like with VMware, and companies therefore needing to find new solutions for their budget and reduce vendor dependency.
However, in dealing with these pressures, the trap companies can fall into is trying to deliver all of this change at once and within a small timeframe. Yet in doing so, this change becomes harder to manage and the risk of outages and system failures increases. So, how can they deliver any change that is needed safely?
The dangers of too much change at once
The main challenge in changing too much too quickly is visibility. Companies have to oversee complex IT estates – on-prem systems, the cloud, servers, end-user computing, networks – where change is constant and security updates are largely automated. As this change happens, there are more interactions between older and newer systems, different operating systems, different products, and this means the risk of failure can increase.
Configuration drift, for example, occurs when changes, which haven’t been recorded or authorized, cause a system to drift away from its intended baseline (of how it should perform). Without the right monitoring software, this drift can remain invisible, creating added risk to every subsequent change – and that’s when an outage or cyber incident happens.
In May, for example, Google Cloud suspended Railway’s production account without warning because Railway couldn’t see that the platform had a technical dependency on GCP that caused it to fail, leading to an eight hour outage.

What’s more, as we’ve seen with the adoption of AI tools, change can happen faster than training and processes can keep up with, further increasing the risk of disjointed workflows, security vulnerabilities and data breaches. But even when teams can see the changes that need to take place, they can also be faced with the challenge of deciding how to modernize their existing applications.
Finding alternatives to the buy-or-rebuild dilemma
Of course, trying to slow down change isn’t always possible. A company might have been priced out of its VM software or needs to upgrade its applications for security purposes. In this position, traditionally, IT teams have had to either buy new software or rebuild existing apps, which can both be expensive and time-consuming.
This can lead to vendor lock-in, as IT doesn’t see a viable alternative and doesn’t have the engineering capacity to rewrite applications tied to their original operating systems.
To overcome this dependency, as agentic coding matures, organizations may increasingly opt for a third option: using AI agents to build their own replacements for SaaS tools. But while this can appear to remove vendor lock-in and license costs, it also transfers responsibility for maintenance, security, configuration and ongoing support in-house, making it even harder to oversee change without additional resources or capacity.
However, there is another route. Packaging and migrating existing applications can allow teams to modernize without taking on the burden of building from scratch. By packaging an app’s or virtual machine’s existing operating system dependencies, teams can move them into containers and modern desktop infrastructure without needing to rewrite the app.
The app maintains its existing behavior, but can now work on the latest operating systems and in workspaces like AWS.
Delivering change at scale
With a modernization strategy formed, how do teams gain ongoing visibility across their entire estate and know when apps need to be packaged?
With so much change taking place, manual monitoring and reconciliation processes will struggle to keep up with the demands of infrastructure modernization. Instead, teams should consider using configuration monitoring software to gain continuous visibility into change across their entire estate.
Drift detection tools, for example, can automatically measure change across an estate against established configuration baselines and alert IT teams whenever a change triggers a system to move away from its baseline. This means that an automated patch by an external provider or a manual intervention by a user gets detected and flagged to IT, changes that might otherwise go unnoticed and trigger an outage further down the line.
Imperatively, this estate-wide visibility means teams can see and understand the impact of any unauthorized changes taking place and intervene before they lead to failure.
It also gives them the information they need to understand how a transformation project might interact with the systems currently running in their estate, helping to inform the feasibility and implementation of the proposed changes and deliver more targeted, impactful and safer change.
Alongside configuration visibility, it’s also possible for teams to automate the packaging and delivery of apps, saving them a large amount of time and cost in manually performing a typically laborious task. This subsequently creates a repeatable and scalable process that enables apps to be regularly deployed and made available to users.
Escaping the trap
With so much pressure to change, above all, escaping the transformation trap requires a mindset shift. It involves, one, seeing change as an ongoing problem to manage, and two, not attempting to carry out too many innovation projects at once.
Small, incremental changes can deliver more meaningful impact and ensure systems are properly deployed or integrated, while this targeted approach also provides more capacity for IT teams to deal with any forced change that might surface.
Yet by prioritizing change visibility, IT teams can mitigate forced change by addressing risks earlier and seeing when upgrades are needed in good time. And by automating processes like packaging apps, they gain more capacity to prioritize innovation projects as routine changes take place faster and more securely.
When these processes are joined together, instead of grappling with an overwhelming and uncontrolled level of change that increases risk, teams can ensure change remains a driver of security, resilience and innovation.

articles.title: Mysterious AMD Zen 6 APU with 24GB of LPDDR5 memory appears in benchmarks — chip may be for next-gen Steam Deck or gaming handhelds
articles.text:
Mysterious AMD Zen 6 APU with 24GB of LPDDR5 memory appears in benchmarks — chip may be for next-gen Steam Deck or gaming handhelds
A mysterious AMD chip points to a possible Steam Deck successor.
An AMD engineering sample has made an appearance in a listing on OpenBenchmarking. According to a report by TechPowerUp, the chip could potentially be a part of AMD’s upcoming Gainsborough family and a possible candidate for the next-generation Steam Deck handheld console. As per the OpenBenchmarking listing, the chip comes with a six-core, 12-thread processor paired with 24GB of high-speed LPDDR5 memory.
The engineering sample with part number 100-000001930-12_Y was tested on an AMD GBR-FF6-SKT validation board, with the CPU running at clock speeds of 2.4 GHz. The system also features four 6GB SK Hynix memory packages, resulting in 24GB of LPDDR5 memory running at 9,600 MT/s. That’s a big jump when compared to the current Steam Deck, which comes with 16GB of LPDDR5 memory running at 6,400 MT/s, alongside a four-core, eight-thread AMD Zen 2 processor.
The benchmark listing also provides some clues about the processor’s underlying architecture. As per Notebookcheck, the sample’s CPU microcode revision corresponds to AMD’s Family 1Ah, model DCh. Linux kernel changes indicate that this model falls within the range reserved for newer Zen 6 processors, suggesting that Gainsborough could use AMD’s next-generation CPU architecture. However, there is no clarity or any confirmation whether it will use standard Zen 6 cores or the denser Zen 6C variant.
The integrated GPU is listed with a clock speed of 2,400 MHz, although its architecture and compute unit count remain unknown. The sample was tested using the GpuTest benchmark suite on Ubuntu 24.04 at 1024 x 768 resolution, resulting in scores of 3,871 in GiMark, 3,508 in FurMark, and 9,319 in TessMark. While the FurMark score is comparable to the original Stam Deck, we can’t really come to any conclusions at this point, as the tests were conducted on an engineering platform using development software rather than a finished handheld. For now, the results do not establish how the chip would perform in games, as power limits, cooling, driver maturity, and the final GPU configuration all contribute to the performance in a compact gaming device.
If these specifications carry over to a future Steam Deck, the additional CPU cores along with the larger and faster memory would provide a meaningful hardware upgrade. That being said, neither AMD nor Valve have confirmed a connection between the Gainsborough family and a future Steam Deck. Thus, it is best to take this with a grain of salt and wait until there is more concrete information in the future.

articles.title: Ils détournent une PS5 pour faire tourner une IA locale et les résultats sont surprenants
articles.text:
Une PlayStation 5 capable de faire tourner des modèles d'intelligence artificielle à plus de 100 tokens par seconde ? C'est ce que démontre PS5LM Plus, un projet open source qui exploite le processeur graphique de la console pour exécuter des IA localement. Une prouesse technique, mais réservée aux PS5 modifiées.
Faire tourner une IA locale exige généralement un ordinateur doté de suffisamment de mémoire et de puissance de calcul. Pourtant, des développeurs ont trouvé un moyen d'exploiter un matériel déjà présent dans des millions de foyers : la PlayStation 5.
Tout commence avec PS5LM, un projet de Mert Cobanov qui adapte le moteur llama.cpp à la console de Sony. En quelques jours, un dérivé baptisé PS5LM Plus, développé par abhi245y, est allé beaucoup plus loin en permettant aux modèles d'utiliser directement le GPU AMD de la machine.
Du processeur au GPU, les performances changent d'échelle
La première approche utilisait uniquement le processeur de la PS5, avec environ 6 Gio de mémoire accessibles au programme. Sur un modèle volumineux, Qwen 3.8 27B, le résultat était extrêmement lent : environ un token généré par minute, les données devant être lues depuis le stockage.
PS5LM Plus contourne ces limitations grâce à une application native exploitant Vulkan et le processeur graphique de la console. Elle peut ainsi utiliser environ 12 Gio de mémoire partagée pour exécuter les modèles.
Le changement est spectaculaire : Qwen 3.8 27B atteint désormais une vingtaine de tokens par seconde, contre un seul par minute auparavant. Le développeur annonce également 61 tokens/s avec Gemma 4 E4B et jusqu'à 124 tokens/s avec Llama 3.2 3B.
Le projet rapporte même une réponse de 7 775 tokens produite à une moyenne de 19,7 tokens/s avec Qwen, signe que le débit peut se maintenir sur une génération relativement longue. Ces résultats restent toutefois ceux du développeur, et non de tests indépendants.
Pour tenir dans la mémoire disponible, le modèle de 27 milliards de paramètres utilise une quantification très poussée : ses paramètres sont compressés avec une précision d'environ 2 bits chacun. Cette méthode réduit considérablement les besoins en mémoire, mais peut dégrader la qualité des réponses.
Un serveur d'IA dans le salon, mais réservé aux bidouilleurs
Alors non, l'intérêt ne se limite pas à discuter avec une IA depuis son téléviseur ! PS5LM Plus propose une interface utilisable à la manette, une bibliothèque de modèles téléchargeables depuis Hugging Face et un serveur accessible aux autres appareils du réseau local.
Un ordinateur ou un smartphone peut ainsi envoyer des requêtes à la console, qui exécute les modèles sans passer par un service d'IA distant. Le serveur propose des interfaces compatibles avec les API OpenAI et Anthropic, permettant notamment à Claude Code, Codex ou OpenCode d'utiliser la PS5 comme moteur d'IA local, sous réserve des capacités du modèle installé.
Mais cette expérimentation exige une PS5 jailbreakée, avec un firmware compatible et plusieurs outils communautaires, notamment kstuff-lite, etaHEN et ShadowMountPlus. L'installation implique des manipulations techniques, avec des risques d'instabilité, de sécurité et d'éventuelles restrictions d'accès aux services Sony.
Il ne s'agit donc pas d'une solution prête à l'emploi, ni d'une raison suffisante pour acheter une PS5 afin d'exécuter des modèles d'IA. Les résultats dépendent aussi du modèle choisi, de sa compression et des ressources disponibles. L'expérience reste révélatrice : en exploitant le GPU d'une console conçue avant tout pour les jeux vidéo, les développeurs montrent qu'un appareil de salon peut aussi devenir un serveur d'intelligence artificielle.
Les projets PS5LM et PS5LM Plus sont disponibles sur GitHub.

articles.title: BetaCreator: TIM oficializa plano com 50 GB e acesso exclusivo por convite • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
BetaCreator: TIM oficializa plano com 50 GB e acesso exclusivo por convite
Reformulação do TIM Beta mantém os R$ 60 por mês, mas agora permite acumular a internet para os meses seguintes.
A TIM oficializou nesta terça-feira (20/10) a reformulação do TIM Beta, antecipada pelo Tecnoblog no mês passado. O plano do agora BetaCreator custará R$ 60 por mês e será exclusivamente por convites. Ele oferece 50 GB de internet, além de redes sociais, TIM Mais e Deezer inclusos.
Durante a apresentação acompanhada pelo Tecnoblog, a executiva Julia Martins, diretora de marketing do pré-pago da TIM Brasil, explicou que o plano não poderá ser contratado espontaneamente por nenhum canal da operadora. Nesta primeira fase, o acesso será feito por meio de convites distribuídos a influenciadores e criadores de conteúdo.
Quem já é cliente TIM Beta também terá acesso à novidade. Segundo Martins, os usuários do plano antigo serão os primeiros a receber convites, sob a categoria Beta Founder. Após o recebimento, eles ficarão disponíveis para ativação em até 48 horas.
O TIM Beta atual custa o mesmo valor, mas oferece uma franquia menor de internet. Além disso, no BetaCreator, os dados que sobrarem passam para os meses seguintes e não expiram enquanto a linha permanecer ativa no plano. Por exemplo, se o cliente usar 30 GB da franquia de 50 GB, os 20 GB restantes não expiram.
Lançado em 2010, o TIM Beta nasceu como um produto voltado ao público jovem, com foco em comunidade e engajamento. Segundo a operadora de origem italiana, a marca agora é renovada com benefícios pedidos pelos clientes.
A experiência ficará concentrada no aplicativo Meu TIM, enquanto o app exclusivo do TIM Beta deve ser encerrado. De acordo com a operadora, a mudança busca reunir os serviços em um só lugar. A TIM ainda não detalhou quantos convites serão distribuídos nem quantos clientes poderão aderir ao Creator.

articles.title: Sicherheitslücke in Routern entdeckt: Wie ein 16 Jahre alter Fehler erneut zum Problem wird
articles.text:
Sicherheitslücke in Routern entdeckt: Wie ein 16 Jahre alter Fehler erneut zum Problem wird
Router vernetzen zahlreiche Haushalte mit dem Internet. Sie können aber schnell zum Einfallstor für Cyberkriminelle werden, wenn du nicht die richtigen Einstellungen am Router vornimmst. Gleiches gilt, wenn es eine Lücke im System der Router gibt, die lange Zeit unerkannt bleibt. So soll es laut einem Sicherheitsforscher schon seit 2010 der Fall sein. Laut ihm sind von der Lücke potenziell Millionen Geräte betroffen.
Neue Router-Sicherheitslücke: Welche Gefahr droht
Die Warnung stammt vom belgischen Sicherheitsforscher Quentin Kaiser, der die Sicherheitslücke „WPSplinter“ getauft hat. Im Grunde handelt es sich dabei um zwei Fehler, die in der Software von Broadcom zu finden sind. Broadcoms Wi-Fi-Implementierung wird laut Kaiser von dutzenden Routerherstellern genutzt. Dadurch finden sich die Fehler in hunderten Produkten und potenziell in „Millionen von Broadcom-basierten Access-Points weltweit“.
Die Fehler sorgen dafür, dass sich Unbefugte über WPS (Wi-Fi Protected Setup) Zugriff auf die Router verschaffen können. Über das Feature können Endgeräte und Router ohne Passworteingabe miteinander verknüpft werden, indem eine WPS-Taste auf dem Router gedrückt wird, während das Endgerät ebenfalls einen WPS-Prozess startet. Laut Kaiser kann eine manipulierte WPS-Nachricht eingeschleust werden, um den Speicher der Router zu verändern.
Dadurch können Angreifer:innen, falls sie sich in Reichweite des WLAN-Signals des Routers befinden, eigenen Code ausführen. In seinen Tests war Kaiser so etwa in der Lage, auf dem Gerät ein Wi-Fi-Passwort aus dem Speicher zu extrahieren und es anschließend zu benutzen, um sich in das Netzwerk einzuklinken. Die User:innen würden davon nichts mitbekommen, wenn sie nicht regelmäßig auf die Liste verbundener Geräte schauen.
Kaiser hat Broadcom mit seinen Funden konfrontiert. Laut dem Unternehmen war das Problem schon seit 2010 bekannt und wurde mit einem Fix 2018 ohne öffentliche Meldung behoben. Doch offenbar war die Lösung damals nicht ausreichend. Die neue Lücke adressierte Broadcom bislang nicht und verwies auf die einzelnen Hersteller. Kaiser wandte sich deshalb auch an eine Reihe von Herstellern in Belgien sowie belgische Behörden für Cybersecurity. Bis zu seiner Veröffentlichung hatte er von keiner der Parteien eine Reaktion erhalten.
Der Sicherheitsforscher sieht trotz der ausbleibenden Reaktionen ein enormes Risiko für Anwender:innen. Bei betroffenen Routern müssten sich die Angreifer nur vor der Wohnung oder dem Haus befinden, um in Reichweite des Netzwerkes zu gelangen. Auf der GitHub-Seite zu seinem Fund aktualisiert er regelmäßig eine Liste mit Routern, die von dem Bug betroffen sind. So können User:innen selbst nachschauen, ob potenziell Gefahr besteht.

articles.title: Samsung Galaxy S27 : lancement précoce, RAM limitée et nouvel écran, les dernières fuites peignent un tableau contrasté
articles.text:
Samsung Galaxy S27 : lancement précoce, RAM limitée et nouvel écran, les dernières fuites peignent un tableau contrasté
Entre calendrier de sortie incertain, compromis sur la quantité de mémoire vive et nouvelle technologie d’affichage, les trois dernières rumeurs autour des Samsung Galaxy S27 soufflent le chaud et le froid.
À quelques mois du renouvellement de sa gamme phare, Samsung arbitrerait encore entre des éléments clés de la fiche technique de ses futurs Galaxy S27. Alors qu’un nouvel écran devrait faire son apparition pour soulager les yeux sensibles, la pénurie de composants pourrait limiter la quantité de mémoire vive de cette génération. Une situation qui n’impacterait pas le lancement des terminaux avec une date de sortie bien plus précoce, aux alentours de février 2027.
Galaxy S27 : une sortie précoce, mais un retour en arrière sur la mémoire vive ?
La première rumeur de ce début de semaine concerne effectivement le calendrier de lancement. Selon le divulgâcheur Lanzuk, Samsung tablerait sur une sortie en février 2027 au plus tard, sans écarter le mois de janvier. Une arrivée précoce sachant que les Galaxy S26 avaient été annoncés le 25 février pour une commercialisation le 11 mars 2026.
On apprend au passage que même si les Galaxy S27 et S27+ sont quasiment finalisés, la liste des composants des versions Pro et Ultra fait encore débat en interne. La faute aux prix élevés de la RAM LPDDR6 et du stockage UFS 5.0, liés à la pénurie de mémoire, forçant la firme sud-coréenne à faire les bons choix pour ne pas trop faire grimper la facture. L’informateur @kro_roe affirme sur X que Samsung envisagerait de commercialiser des versions dotées de seulement 8 Go de RAM aux côtés des modèles 12 Go, histoire de maintenir un prix de départ attractif.
En parallèle, la marque mixerait différentes générations de stockage UFS selon les variantes, augmenterait le prix du modèle Ultra de 1 To et réduirait ses traditionnelles promotions de précommande.
Fin du scintillement : l'écran du Galaxy S27 va enfin soulager vos yeux
La bonne nouvelle proviendrait finalement de l’écran, à en croire une seconde rumeur issue du réseau social d’Elon Musk. D’après @WalleGalaxy, Samsung intégrerait une option DC dimming sur les dalles des Galaxy S27. Cette technologie régule mieux la luminosité en ajustant directement la tension électrique de l’affichage au lieu de reposer sur un scintillement rapide. Ce changement matériel mettrait fin à un calvaire pour les utilisateurs de smartphones Samsung, victimes de maux de tête, de douleurs oculaires et de nausées depuis plusieurs générations.

articles.title: Meta's Muse hits 10M U.S. downloads in 40 days, a milestone reached by only 11 other apps | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Meta’s AI companion, Muse, is now one of only a dozen mobile apps to have reached 10 million U.S. downloads in its first 40 days on the market. According to new data from market intelligence provider Sensor Tower, Muse has seen 10.9 million downloads since its September debut, 10.2 million of which were in the United States.
Only 11 other apps to date have reached this type of post-launch milestone, said Sensor Tower’s Senior Insights Analyst Kara Lee. The most recent of these was Meta’s Threads, back in July 2023.
Other apps that saw this kind of scale were largely mobile games, Lee noted, like Fortnite, PUBG Mobile, Pokémon GO, and others. Besides Threads, Disney+ was the only other non-game app to make it into the exclusive club.
Meta’s success is tied to the company’s ability to scale its new apps by marketing them across its other services, which it has done with both Threads and Muse. Threads was built on top of Instagram’s social graph, and its content has been integrated into both Facebook and Instagram. However, Muse isn’t only benefiting from Meta’s ability to market the AI agent across its family of apps, which today includes 3.6 billion daily active users; the company is also heavily investing in advertising to drive new users to Muse.
Per Sensor Tower’s data, Meta has allocated 39% of its total advertising spend to market Muse in October, up from 23% last month. In addition, Muse now ranks as the 21st largest brand in the U.S. by advertising impressions this month, up from 73rd in September.
Still, marketing an app and retaining users after the initial shine wears off are two different things. In this case, Muse is seeing better retention rates than its AI competitors like ChatGPT, Claude, and Grok.
In the U.S., the app had a 30% retention rate after 7 days and a 23% retention rate after 14 days. By comparison, its rivals saw an average of a 19% 7-day retention rate and a 16% 14-day retention rate, according to the firm’s data.
Muse also hit another milestone that demonstrates active engagement with the AI app. Its daily active users reached 2.5 million for the first time on October 16, a 15% week-over-week increase.
Meta’s latest AI app, which can handle various tasks on users’ behalf, has seen breakout success since its debut. It shot up to No. 1 on the App Store, and, at one point, even outpaced some of the metrics ChatGPT saw following its launch. Its latest milestone sees it topping its rivals again, as ChatGPT saw 3.7 million U.S. downloads in its first 40 days on the market. Grok and Claude saw only 500,000 and 200,000 U.S. downloads, respectively, in their first 40 days.
Globally, ChatGPT beat out Muse, having scaled to around 15 million global downloads in its first 40 days. But this isn’t a fair comparison, as ChatGPT benefited from a wider reach. Muse is only available in the U.S. and Canada for now, while ChatGPT’s app attracted attention from markets like Japan, Brazil, and Germany, too. (Japan, for instance, accounted for 25% of its global installs during its first 40 days.)
Since launching, Muse has retained its No. 1 rank on the U.S. App Store for all days except October 19, when streaming app Kick briefly beat it out. It has since reclaimed the top spot as of Tuesday. Muse has also been No. 1 on Google Play over the past 30 days.

articles.title: Visiting Slate’s first showroom as its $25,000 electric truck nears production
articles.text:
As I sat in the cab of the pickup truck and manually rolled down the windows, I closed my eyes and, for the briefest moment, flashed back to opening the windows on a cold, winter day in my dad’s 1975 Ford Ranger to let more cigarette smoke escape. I opened my eyes and looked through the windshield at a wall in the Slate Customer Experience Center studded with bright color chips.
Last week, in a former Tesla store staffed by some former Tesla employees, Slate opened its first showroom. Located in the Fulton Market District just northwest of the Chicago Loop, the Slate Experience Center is a place for would-be buyers to poke around a prototype, check out customization options, buy some Slate merch, and even preorder a new Slate Truck with a $300 deposit.
Designed for the American obsession with pickup trucks, the Slate Truck is a bare-bones electric pickup truck retailing for $24,950. It sports plastic panels, a minimalist interior design sensibility, actual window winders, and a projected range of 205 miles. Ars went for a ride in a Slate Truck over the summer, but we haven’t had a chance to shop for one. So I stopped by the Slate Experience Center so I could, er, experience the Slate.
The Slate Customer Experience Center in Chicago on a bright autumn day.
Eric Bangeman/Ars Technica
The Slate Customer Experience Center in Chicago on a bright autumn day.
Eric Bangeman/Ars Technica
Customers can wrap their Slate Truck with all the colors of the spectrum.
Eric Bangeman/Ars Technica
Customers can wrap their Slate Truck with all the colors of the spectrum.
Eric Bangeman/Ars Technica
The Slate Customer Experience Center in Chicago on a bright autumn day.
Eric Bangeman/Ars Technica
Customers can wrap their Slate Truck with all the colors of the spectrum.
Eric Bangeman/Ars Technica
Upon walking into the showroom on a Monday morning, the first thing I noticed was a marquee-style sign on the wall boldly and brightly serving as a price tag for the black truck parked in the middle of the showroom. The vibe was industrial-barn-chic-meets-SoHo-loft. Three other people were there, and another shopper entered as I left. One man alternated between sitting in the cab, peering at the truck as he walked around it, and peppering Manager of Customer Experience Steve Purdy with questions.
The showroom has been open since October 15, launching with a three-day event that offered ridealongs. Interest has been strong, Purdy told me, and while he couldn’t provide sales numbers, he said the response has been “incredible.”
“We’re really happy with the number of [$300] deposits we’ve gotten since we opened,” Purdy said.
I was hoping there would be at least two Slate Trucks on site so I could compare build quality between trucks and check things like panel gaps, window operation, and chassis creaks. But only one truck was on display. And it wasn’t close to a production model; rather, the black Slate Truck was a hand-built older prototype with a black wrap (the Slate Truck base color is gray). The bed and passenger sides were cordoned off, but the driver-side door was open so shoppers could hop in and check out the interior.
It was bigger than I expected—to my eye, roughly the size of a Hyundai Santa Cruz. The tailgate was down, and it felt reassuringly sturdy when I pressed down on it. The 5-foot-long (152.4 cm) bed floor looked and felt durable, not much different from any other pickup on the market.
I really wanted to jump up and down on the tailgate. But I couldn’t even sit on it.
Eric Bangeman/Ars Technica
I really wanted to jump up and down on the tailgate. But I couldn’t even sit on it.
Eric Bangeman/Ars Technica
You roll down the windows the old way.
Eric Bangeman/Ars Technica
You roll down the windows the old way.
Eric Bangeman/Ars Technica
The early prototype on display in the showroom.
Eric Bangeman/Ars Technica
The early prototype on display in the showroom.
Eric Bangeman/Ars Technica
You roll down the windows the old way.
Eric Bangeman/Ars Technica
The early prototype on display in the showroom.
Eric Bangeman/Ars Technica
The exterior passed the eye test, with the panels appearing well-fitted. The doors sat flush with the surrounding body panels when closed. Of course, I was looking at a prototype carefully built to be poked and prodded by automotive reporters and the general public, so the level of fit and finish was no surprise. The challenge for Slate will be getting consistent build quality with minimal panel gaps, watertight seals, consistent door-to-fender transitions, and hood/frunk alignment. The Slate assembly line in Warsaw, Indiana, is still making prototyping runs at this point, Purdy told me, and the company is hoping to start on production models “soon.”
I hopped inside the cab once I got the opportunity, and the door closed with a solid-sounding “thunk.” It’s spartan inside, with a small screen for the instrument panel, a phone holder, physical climate controls, and window winders. The seats were both supportive and comfortable, and, after moving my seat, I had ample legroom. While the seat slid back and forth smoothly, the seatback recline lever on the side didn’t work.
The shopping experience
Beyond the default Blank Slate body style, Slate offers two SUV options—the Squareback SUV and Fastback SUV—and an open-air kit. I asked Purdy if they were selling any of the SUVs. “Most customers are going with the truck configuration,” he said. “And then they’re customizing their trucks in the Slate Garage.”
Being able to order online and have the truck delivered is a major attraction for those who can’t stand “the kabuki dance of f***ery at a dealership,” as one of my colleagues put it. But if you want to do all that at the Slate Experience Center, staffers will sit down and help you configure your customized Slate. There is a wall with removable dashboard panels across the color spectrum and a couple of miniature models of the cab with tiny, colored panels to help customers decide on the details.
All the headlight and taillight options for the Slate Truck are on display.
Eric Bangeman/Ars Technica
All the headlight and taillight options for the Slate Truck are on display.
Eric Bangeman/Ars Technica
Miniature interior models help customers visualize what their Slate Truck will look like.
Eric Bangeman/Ars Technica
Miniature interior models help customers visualize what their Slate Truck will look like.
Eric Bangeman/Ars Technica
All the headlight and taillight options for the Slate Truck are on display.
Eric Bangeman/Ars Technica
Miniature interior models help customers visualize what their Slate Truck will look like.
Eric Bangeman/Ars Technica
Purdy told me that Slate is staying the course with the $24,950 sticker price. But will customers actually get their Slate Trucks this year as the company promised? “We will ship some trucks by the end of the year,” Purdy said. “Those will go to investors and employees, with early orderers receiving their Slate Trucks in early 2027.
For service, Slate will be using RepairPal. Owners will be able to choose from 4,000 shops, some of which can service the high-voltage electrical systems and others limited to body damage, Purdy said. For scratches or minor dings from fender benders, owners can replace the exterior body panels themselves. Pricing for replacement parts has yet to be finalized. And Slate is confident the plastic body panels will weather climate extremes without a hitch. “We’re a Michigan company,” Purdy reminded me.
Monday morning is not exactly prime time for dealership traffic, but a handful of prospective customers were in the showroom, which is a promising sign. While there is no shortage of electrified pickup trucks on the market, there is a shortage of affordable ones. At $25,000, the Slate Truck costs far less than a Rivian R1T, Tesla Cybertruck, Chevy Silverado EV, or any currently shipping battery-electric truck. It could be a breakout hit—especially if Slate can beat Ford’s sub-$30,000 Fathom pickup to market.
But the sleek-looking showroom and an attractive prototype still face a production reality check. Tesla had significant quality-control problems with early Model Ys, with customers receiving cars with loose seats and broken seatbelts, and some Cybertrucks have shipped with misaligned panel gaps. A new player is entering the game, but production is still on the (near) horizon, and no one knows if the Slate Trucks delivered to customers will live up to the promise of the carefully hand-built prototypes. People are definitely very interested in Slate. Now it’s time to deliver.
Eric Bangeman is the Managing Editor of Ars Technica. He lives in the northwest suburbs of Chicago, where he enjoys road cycling and plays bass in a band.

articles.title: Philips Monitors Introduces the 27E3C2500 and 32E3C2500
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
Philips Monitors Introduces the 27E3C2500 and 32E3C2500
The Philips Monitor line-up expands with the 27E3C2500 and 32E3C2500, two curved monitors designed for home and office users and casual gamers. Both feature a QHD resolution and 1500R curved VA panel, combining detailed visuals for everyday tasks with smooth motion for gaming. They are designed for people who use the same monitor for work and entertainment, from reviewing documents to watching a movie or playing a game.
With a QHD resolution of 2560 × 1440, both monitors provide more detail than Full HD and sufficient space to view documents and applications side by side. The curved screen adds a sense of immersion when watching movies or exploring game environments. The Philips 27E3C2500 offers a 27-inch (68.6 cm) screen for users who prefer a smaller display. The Philips 32E3C2500 provides a larger 31.5-inch (80 cm) viewing area, with the same QHD resolution and refresh rate. The choice allows users to select a size that suits their desk and viewing preferences.Both models support HDR10 for compatible HDR content. Philips SmartContrast analyses the displayed content and adjusts the backlight to enhance contrast.
Smooth motion for everyday tasks and casual gaming
A 144 Hz refresh rate makes scrolling and on-screen movement look smoother than on a conventional 60 Hz display. During gaming, Adaptive-Sync matches the display's refresh rate to the output of a compatible graphics source, helping reduce screen tearing and stuttering.
Both monitors also offer 0.5 ms MPRT for reduced perceived motion blur during gaming. This helps keep moving images clearer during fast-paced scenes.
Features for the home desk
SoftBlue technology reduces blue light emissions, while Flicker-free technology reduces screen flicker during everyday use. Both monitors also include an EasyRead mode for on-screen reading.
HDMI and DisplayPort inputs provide connections for compatible sources. Two built-in 2 W speakers let users listen to videos and games without adding separate speakers to the desk, while an audio output offers an additional listening option.
The stand allows users to tilt the screen to suit their viewing position. Both monitors support 100 × 100 mm VESA mounting for use with a compatible monitor arm or wall mount.
Full HD options in the same range
The range also includes the Philips 27E3C2200 and 32E3C2200, with 27-inch and 31.5-inch screens respectively. Both offer a Full HD 1920 × 1080 resolution with a 1500R curved VA panel, 144 Hz refresh rate, and Adaptive-Sync. 
Prices and availability
The Philips 27E3C2500 and 32E3C2500 combine curved QHD viewing with features for home working and casual gaming. Two screen sizes and built-in audio give users a choice of display for a desk shared between work and downtime.
The Philips 27E3C2500 will be available for purchase in November, at an MSRP of £129.99. 
The Philips 32E3C2500 will be available for purchase in November as well, at an MSRP of £169.99.

articles.title: Anneaux de pouvoir saison 3 : une nouvelle affiche montre un détail notable sur Sauron et l'Anneau unique
articles.text:
C’est une information qui ne surprendra personne, en tout cas pas celles et ceux qui suivent assidûment la série Les Anneaux de pouvoir sur Amazon Prime Video. La saison 3, attendue le 11 novembre, tourne autour de la fabrication de l’Anneau unique. Son synopsis officiel montre Sauron qui cherche à forger l’anneau qui lui donnera l’avantage dans sa guerre contre les Elfes.
La production communique beaucoup autour de cet artefact, que ce soit dans la bande-annonce, dans des clips promotionnels ou dans des affiches mises en ligne courant octobre. On y voit une forge, puis Sauron, incarné par Charlie Vickers, dans les entrailles de la Montagne du Destin, marteau en main face à la lave.
Une nouvelle affiche sur Les Anneaux de pouvoir
L’Anneau unique apparaît par moments, par exemple tenu par une pince, avec la silhouette de Sauron en arrière-plan. Sur la première affiche de la saison, publiée en juillet avant le Comic-Con de San Diego, Sauron tenait l’anneau dans sa main. Jusqu’ici, aucun visuel ne le montrait au doigt du seigneur des ténèbres. Une nouvelle affiche officielle montre désormais Sauron avec la bague au doigt.
Un éclat très vif apparaît en effet sur l’index de sa main droite. Peter Jackson avait fait le même choix dans La Communauté de l’anneau (2001) : dans le prologue du film, Sauron porte l’Anneau unique à l’index de la main droite. La série reprend donc un code visuel des films. J.R.R. Tolkien, lui, n’a jamais précisé à quel doigt Sauron le portait.
Ce Sauron bagué donne un indice sur la saison 3. L’Anneau unique pourrait être achevé bien avant le dernier épisode, ce qui laisserait le temps de montrer le seigneur des ténèbres en train de s’en servir.
Les huit épisodes de cette saison 3 arrivent en trois fois sur Prime Video : les quatre premiers le mercredi 11 novembre, les épisodes 5 et 6 le 18 novembre, puis les deux derniers le 25 novembre. Toute la saison sera donc disponible avant la fin du mois, alors que la saison 2 avait été diffusée chaque semaine.

articles.title: Eloelo's Saurabh Pandey bets that Dolphin AI can break the gatekeepers of Indian storytelling
articles.text:
Eloelo's Saurabh Pandey bets that Dolphin AI can break the gatekeepers of Indian storytelling
The Eloelo Group founder says AI-led production could turn India's storytellers into a global export force.
When James Cameron's epic sci-fi movie Avatar hit cinemas in late 2000s, plenty of Indians watched it and wondered why we weren't making films like that. According to Saurabh Pandey, Founder and CEO of Eloelo Group, that question is about to lose its force.
Eloelo is an Indian live social entertainment and social gaming platform headquartered in Bengaluru. It was launched in 2020 by former Flipkart executives Pandey and Akshay Dubey. The platform bridges video/audio livestreaming with interactive gaming tailored specifically for India's youth and vernacular markets.
At the 17th edition of TechSparks, YourStory's flagship event, Pandey showed off Dolphin AI, Eloelo's AI video creation tool, in a session titled 'Can AI turn India into a global content export hub?', moderated by Shradha Sharma, Founder and CEO of YourStory and The Bharat Project.
Dolphin AI currently has a waitlist, with the platform releasing invite codes in batches.
For now, Dolphin AI is free as Eloelo is giving away generous early credits so creators can make their first few videos and get a feel for the solution. However, a credit-based pricing model will arrive eventually. Pandey said the team mainly wants to see how people use Dolphin AI, and early signs are promising: roughly 15,000 videos were built in about eight days, mostly through organic discovery.
The end of the budget bottleneck
Pandey's pitch centres on who gets to tell big stories. In the VFX era, he said, movie making belonged to whoever had the money. A good storyteller with a period drama in mind simply could not afford the visuals it demanded, and that made budgets the real gatekeeper of content.
AI is a total game-changer, he argued. Production usually eats up 50 to 60% of revenue in this category, squeezing distribution budgets and destroying unit economics. By slashing those production costs, creator imagination finally gets the breathing room it needs to thrive.
Distribution, meanwhile, has become largely algorithmic. A creator in India now competes for attention in the US or Europe on the same footing as anyone else.
Why this time might be different
The conversation then moved to another area of content that is seeing traction: micro-drama and short-form content. These have attracted plenty of Indian startups, yet few have become popular.
In India, he said, the top four or five micro-drama players together are running at more than Rs 5,000 crore, a level they reached in just 18 months.
He also pointed to South Korea, a country of 52 million people that has built a $15-billion content export economy. India has 1.4 billion people and no shortage of creative talent, he said. What it has lacked is intent, technology, ambition and capital. Too many Indian creators, in his view, still focus only on local audience. Nobody asks whether a new LLM is launching for India, he noted; it just launches for the world. Why shouldn't Indian stories do the same?
Platforms will consolidate, but supply is wide open
Pandey doesn't expect micro-drama to escape the pattern seen elsewhere. Food delivery, quick commerce, ecommerce and ride-hailing all ended up with two or three heavily funded players holding 70 to 75% of the market, and he expects the same for content.
The real opportunity, he said, lies on the supply side.
Eloelo launched about 200 new micro-dramas last month, roughly five or six a night, and works with around 90 production houses. His advice to would-be founders is to skip the platform race and build lean AI studios instead: a handful of writers, editors, promo producers and a line producer who could feed micro-dramas, OTT content and exportable IP to the big platforms.
He also had a message for writers and producers wary of AI. Use it as a brainstorming partner, he said, and ship more. As an example, he floated an idea close to his heart. An AI Ramayana already exists, but nobody has yet made a spectacular AI Mahabharata.
Eloelo has grown from one platform to five within the same group, Pandey said, and an IPO is not on the cards anytime soon. The focus is on growing profitably and sustainably.

articles.title: El Fire TV se vuelve mucho más útil en España: ahora también permite jugar a Amazon Luna a través de Prime Video
articles.text:
Poco a poco, Amazon va integrando más funciones útiles a sus dispositivos Fire TV Stick, sobre todo a los de las generaciones más actuales. Más allá de ser un reproductor de contenido de cine y series, ahora también lo es para gaming gracias al paso que ha dado: integrar Amazon Luna en sus Fire TV Stick a través de Prime Video.
Fire TV Stick 4K Plus
Todo desde una sola app
Amazon Luna es el servicio de videojuegos de Amazon, similar a Game Pass, aunque salvando las grandes distancias. Lo que ofrece Amazon es un catálogo de títulos en la nube a los que ahora podemos acceder a través de la plataforma Prime Video, uniendo así este catálogo al de películas, series y documentales a través de su correspondiente sección de "juegos".
Esto ofrece una utilidad mucho más grande a estos pequeños dispositivos, permitiendo que podamos acceder a ellos a través de Internet, sin necesidad de tener a mano una consola o un PC gaming. Y lo bueno es que Amazon suele renovar los títulos con frecuencia.
Ahora mismo, por ejemplo, hay bastantes títulos como 'Star Wars Outlaws', el videojuego de la saga desarrollado por Ubisoft. También podemos encontrar 'Hogwarts Legacy', 'Marvel's Guardianes de la Galaxia', 'Indiana Jones y el Gran Círculo', 'Death Stranding Director's Cut' o 'Alan Wake II' y 'Assassin's Creed Valhalla'. También hay títulos para los más peques como 'Bluey'.
La diferencia con lo que teníamos antes es que, hasta ahora, teníamos que abrir la app de Luna para poder acceder al catálogo de videojuegos. Ahora lo tenemos todo mucho más unificado a través de Prime Video.
Amazon Luna ya está disponible a través de Prime Video. Para poder acceder a los videojuegos, hay que utilizar un smartphone o directamente un mando compatible, no necesariamente el de Luna (yo utilizo el 8Bitdo Pro 3). Además, es necesario tener una suscripción activa a Amazon Prime, que actualmente tiene un precio de 4,99 euros al mes o 49,90 euros al año.
También te puede interesar
Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K (última generación): streaming 4K sencillo con nuevo mando Fire TV; ten todas tus apps en un solo lugar, TV gratuita y en directo, y encuentra series más rápido con Alexa+
Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K Select: comienza a reproducir contenido 4K en streaming, ve cientos de miles de películas y episodios de series, encuentra series más rápido con Alexa+

articles.title: AI startup Vectorial lands $3M in funding to simulate human behavior for consumer research - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
AI startup Vectorial lands $3M in funding to simulate human behavior for consumer research
Consumer research is a slow and cumbersome challenge that few companies do well, but if Vectorial AI Inc. is successful, they’ll never have to worry about doing it again.
The startup today said it has raised $3 million in seed funding to propel the launch of its new artificial intelligence-driven platform that simulates human behavior to generate valuable feedback for product development and marketing teams. Today’s round was jointly led by Smilegate and SenseAI Ventures, with additional funding coming from the ecosystem funds of the University of California at Berkeley and Stanford University. Angel investors from Meta Platforms Inc., Mastercard Inc. and Shopify Inc. also contributed to the round.
Vectorial believes it has identified a critical bottleneck in technology development. These days, virtually every company is using AI tools to generate massive amounts of code, accelerating the development of new software products and applications.
But consumer research is still stuck in the dark ages. Most firms still rely on outdated surveys of real audiences, which can take weeks to compile and complete, and are usually very limited in scale, with perhaps only 50 to 100 participants.
According to Vectorial co-founder and Chief Executive Taranveer Singh, many smaller startups simply avoid doing user research altogether, and just assume or hope they know what consumers actually want. But that’s hit-and-miss at best, and it leads to hours of wasted time and money spent on products no one needs.
“We believe AI is creating two distinct frontiers,” Singh told SiliconANGLE. “One focuses on reasoning and solving complex problems, while the other focuses on simulations and decoding human behavior.”
Rather than gather up real humans to test new products, Vectorial has built a platform that uses AI to simulate thousands of users within specified target demographics. It’s based on the concept of a “living model” of target customers that continuously updates itself to take into account emerging trends and behavioral shifts.
Singh says the feedback generated from these simulated audiences is extremely accurate, and he’s convinced that this method will become the standard for all new consumer products within the next four years or so. “Two pieces are missing,” he said. “The ability to simulate many scenarios, and the ability to bring your users into the same room as you build.”
Several other startups have tried to use AI to solve the consumer research conundrum before, but Singh believes that all of them have fallen short, because none of them actually models human behavior. One solution that’s been tried repeatedly is AI-moderated interviews, but these still take multiple days to organize because they’re still reliant on real humans, and they usually involve small sample sizes. Another popular approach is to use synthetic agents, but Singh says these lack grounding in real consumer behavior, which means their outputs can’t be trusted.
So how does Vectorial improve on these methods? Its solution is to embed its simulated audiences directly into companies’ development workflows, so developers receive a continuous flow of feedback that informs all of their decisions. Vectorial’s platform is powered by a behavior model called SAPIENS, which is continuously being trained on latent socio-demographic, psychographic and behavioral traits across a mammoth database of more than 2.5 million real consumers.
This makes SAPIENS 30% more accurate than general-purpose models when it comes to predicting consumer behavior, said Chief Product Officer Rahul Garg. It should get better too, for Vectorial will use the funds from today’s round to expand its behavioral dataset and build a more advanced model called SAPIENS 2.0.
“We continue to invest in our behavior model, but a model alone doesn’t solve the problem,” Garg said. “That’s why we put behavior models to work inside the product development loop. We believe this fundamentally changes how products are designed and built, because it puts users in the room where you build.”
The early results have been pretty good. Vectorial’s platform has already been put to use by e-commerce, gaming and healthcare firms such as GoodRx Inc., Boat, Everkind Inc. and Concrete Software Inc. Those customers run an average of 600 simulations per month, meaning they’re constantly getting feedback on every design change, feature implementation and so on. Vectorial has compared the findings of its simulated audiences with real user studies, and it typically achieves accuracy of around 86%.
This level of accuracy is one of the reasons why Rahul Agarwalla of SenseAI Ventures decided he had to back the startup. He said most companies struggle to understand their user’s needs, which means they’re hardly benefiting from the accelerated development times AI enables.
“Vectorial replaces the slow theater of surveys with millions of simulated humans using the product and providing insights,” he said. “This is a new class of AI designed to predict human behavior, and not just the next work like LLMs do.”

articles.title: De nombreux HomePod victimes d'un bug fantôme : Apple corrige enfin le tir, mais n'assume pas
articles.text:
Il y a quelques années, certains HomePod se sont mis à dérailler. Sur les réseaux sociaux et sur les forums d’Apple, on trouve des milliers de témoignages de personnes dont l’enceinte s’est tout à coup mise à faire n’importe quoi. Concrètement, la musique démarre seule en pleine nuit, Siri s’active sans raison, le volume grimpe d’un coup. Le phénomène a été baptisé « ghost touch », ou toucher fantôme, par les victimes. Celui-ci survient lorsque la surface tactile située sur le dessus de l’enceinte enregistre des pressions qui n’existent pas, comme si un fantôme appuyait dessus pour vous tourmenter.
Un bug récalcitrant sur de nombreux HomePod
On a rencontré le problème il y a un peu plus d’un an sur notre HomePod mini, acheté dans le sillage de la sortie en 2020. L’enceinte a plusieurs fois lancé des playlists sur Apple Music au beau milieu de la nuit et s’est mise à répondre à des demandes qui n’existent pas. Dans les cas les plus graves, le HomePod est persuadé qu’on appuie en permanence sur la surface tactile. De facto, il finit par entrer dans une boucle de redémarrage. Le voyant rouge est impossible à éteindre. L’enceinte devient alors inutilisable. La défaillance touche surtout le HomePod mini et le HomePod 2. Il s’agit d’un problème au niveau du matériel.
Pendant des années, Apple n’a jamais reconnu officiellement le problème, pourtant massivement épinglé par ses clients. Les utilisateurs devaient se débrouiller tout seuls pour trouver une solution. Sur Reddit, on a trouvé plusieurs témoignages qui recommandent de modifier les réglages d’accessibilité de l’enceinte. L’un des réglages d’accessibilité impose en effet d’appuyer plusieurs secondes pour valider une commande sur la zone tactile. L’opération doit théoriquement empêcher le bug fantôme de se produire. Sans succès de notre côté. Parfois, il s’écoulait néanmoins plusieurs heures ou plusieurs jours avant que le HomePod ne recommence à devenir fou. Pour tenter de corriger le tir, on a aussi plusieurs fois réinitialisé l’enceinte. Là encore, cela n’a servi à rien.
Une deuxième option, bien plus radicale, est aussi apparue sur la toile. Elle consiste à ouvrir l’enceinte pour débrancher physiquement les connecteurs de la surface tactile. De facto, la zone n’est plus utilisable. Il faut impérativement passer par Siri pour la moindre commande. Ayant deux mains gauches, et aucune patience, nous avons renoncé. On a fini par débrancher l’accessoire et à le glisser dans un tiroir, dans l’espoir qu’Apple trouve un beau jour une solution.
À lire aussi : Apple dévoile le HomePod mini 2 : voici ce qui change
Un correctif qui ne s’assume pas
Bonne nouvelle, Apple s’est enfin penché sur le problème. Le géant de Cupertino vient en effet de déployer la mise à jour iOS 27.2 sur tous les HomePod, y compris les premiers modèles commercialisés il y a huit ans et sur le tout nouveau HomePod mini 2. Attention, il s’agit de la version release candidate, soit une itération presque définitive de la mise à jour. La version finale ne devrait pas tarder. Elle est attendue avant la fin du mois.
La mise à jour ajoute une fonctionnalité intitulée « Verrouiller les commandes » dans l’application Maison. Disponible sur tous les HomePod, ce réglage va tout simplement désactiver tout le pavé tactile du HomePod mini. Le toucher, le toucher prolongé qui appelle Siri et le réglage du volume seront totalement hors service. Évidemment, le capteur restera défectueux, mais il ne déclenche plus rien tout seul, ce qui permet de se servir à nouveau de l’enceinte. Toutes les autres fonctionnalités continuent de fonctionner normalement.
Officiellement, Apple ne présente pas cette option comme un correctif du bug des touches fantômes. Pour le moment, Apple ne reconnaît pas de défaut matériel sur ses enceintes. La mise à jour ne signifie pas que la marque reconnaît une défaillance massive. Apple présente plutôt le réglage comme une nouvelle option pour les parents de jeunes enfants ou les propriétaires de chats. Elle vise à éviter que les bambins ou les chats appuient sur la surface tactile du HomePod. De notre point de vue, elle rend surtout la vie à un appareil qui prenait la poussière, et qu’on avait presque condamné.

articles.title: Galaxy S26 Ultra com câmera de 200 MP sai mais barato no Mercado Livre • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Galaxy S26 Ultra com câmera de 200 MP sai mais barato no Mercado Livre
Galaxy S26 Ultra (256 GB) tem tela à prova de curiosos e câmera wide de 200 MP; topo de linha da Samsung recebe desconto competitivo frente às ofertas pré-reajuste
O Galaxy S26 Ultra de 256 GB está saindo por R$ 6.546 no Pix no Mercado Livre. O atual celular de ponta da Samsung, equipado com câmera principal de 200 MP e tela AMOLED de 120 Hz com recurso exclusivo de privacidade, recebe desconto de 45% sobre o preço oficial de R$ 11.999.
Este mês, os celulares da linha Galaxy S26 sofreram reajuste de preços, e o S26 Ultra ficou mais caro (antes era R$ 11.499 oficialmente). Contudo, a oferta de hoje ainda compete facilmente com os menores preços mais recentes. Mas fique atento: esta oferta é válida apenas para o modelo na cor Branca.
O Galaxy S26 Ultra traz um versátil kit traseiro de câmeras que filma em 8K. Ele inclui wide de 200 MP exclusiva, ultrawide de 50 MP, telefoto de 10 MP com zoom óptico de 3x e periscópica de 50 MP e 5x, que fazem capturas em nível profissional. A frontal de 12 MP tira ótimas selfies e filma em 4K a 60 fps.
Seu chip Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy e os 12 GB de RAM nem suam ao rodar apps pesados em multitarefa e soluções do Galaxy AI localmente. Nos nossos testes, o gadget tirou de letra tarefas como edição de imagens, games pesados e gravação de vídeo prolongada, sem engasgar.
A tela LTPO AMOLED Dinâmico 2X de 6,9″ conta com uma exclusiva tecnologia de privacidade, que bloqueia “espiadinhas” de curiosos posicionados nos lados do usuário. A taxa de 120 Hz e o brilho de até 2.600 nits entregam cores vibrantes, alta fluidez e visibilidade garantida em qualquer lugar.
O corpo de alumínio do S26 Ultra é revestido pelos vidros Gorilla Glass Armor 2 (tela) e Victus 2 (traseira), resistentes contra acidentes diversos. A certificação IP68 adiciona proteção contra poeira intensa e mergulhos acidentais.
Sua bateria de 5.000 mAh resiste a até 31 horas de vídeo, segundo a Samsung. O carregamento rápido de 60 W via USB-C e sem fio de 25 W permite usar o celular por um dia inteiro, um recurso ideal para usuários sem tempo a perder com tomadas e powerbanks.
O Galaxy S26 Ultra de 256 GB (R$ 6.546 no Pix) será atualizado até o Android 23 e possui conectividade 5G, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6.0 e NFC.
