articles.title: Super Mario Galaxy, cuántas horas dura y cómo usarlo en Android: hasta 1440p a 60 FPS
articles.text:
Super Mario Galaxy ya puede ejecutarse de forma nativa en teléfonos Android sin recurrir a un emulador. El responsable es Galaxy Android, un port no oficial que aprovecha la reciente decompilación completa del código fuente del juego de Wii para funcionar mediante Vulkan y AAudio, con la posibilidad de alcanzar hasta 120 cuadros por segundo en dispositivos móviles.
En paralelo, para quienes busquen la máxima calidad visual, el emulador Dolphin en computadora sigue siendo una vía para jugarlo a 1440p y 60 FPS estables.
Cuánto dura Super Mario Galaxy según el estilo de juego
La extensión de la aventura depende de qué tan a fondo se quiera explorar. Completar la historia principal y derrotar a Bowser toma entre 13 y 15 horas. Quienes además busquen estrellas adicionales y recorran la mayoría de las galaxias pueden extender la experiencia a entre 20 y 25 horas.
Para quienes apuntan al 100%, el desafío es mayor: reunir las 120 estrellas con Mario, desbloquear a Luigi y repetir la hazaña con el segundo personaje (240 estrellas en total) demanda entre 35 y 42 horas de juego.
Cómo correr Super Mario Galaxy en Android sin emulador
El desarrollo de Galaxy Android fue posible después de que, a finales de septiembre, Super Mario Galaxy se convirtiera en el primer título de Nintendo Wii en ser decompilado por completo. Ese proceso permitió a la comunidad de desarrolladores reconstruir el código fuente original y generar, a partir de él, versiones alternativas del juego para otras plataformas.
A diferencia de los ports clásicos que dependen de la emulación, esta aplicación traduce el código directamente al entorno de Android, lo que explica su funcionamiento fluido. Según detallan sus creadores, el título corre a 60 cuadros por segundo con un consumo de batería reducido.
Galaxy Android no incluye el juego en sí, sino que opera como un lanzador. Esto quiere decir que cada usuario debe conseguir por su cuenta la ROM original de Super Mario Galaxy antes de poder iniciar cualquier partida. Una vez cargado ese archivo, el sistema permite abrir el juego de manera directa en las sesiones posteriores, sin repetir la configuración inicial.
En paralelo a esta versión para Android, la misma decompilación del código fuente está siendo utilizada por otro grupo de desarrolladores para preparar un port de Super Mario Galaxy orientado a computadoras personales.
Requisitos y opciones gráficas del port para móviles
De acuerdo con capturas de pantalla compartidas por Android Authority, Galaxy Android ofrece la posibilidad de omitir las escenas cinemáticas del juego, una función pensada para ahorrar espacio de almacenamiento, ya que esas secuencias ocupan más de 2 gigabytes.
El port también incluye ajustes para la interfaz táctil, como la opacidad, el tamaño y la ubicación de los controles en pantalla, pensados para adaptar la experiencia a distintos tamaños de dispositivo.
En materia de rendimiento, la aplicación permite seleccionar una tasa de cuadros objetivo entre 30, 60, 90 o 120 FPS, además de elegir entre dos backends gráficos disponibles: Vulkan u OpenGL ES.
Para ejecutar Super Mario Galaxy en un teléfono se requiere, como mínimo, Android 11, 3 gigabytes de memoria RAM y 2,5 gigabytes de espacio libre. Si se desea conservar las cinemáticas originales, ese requisito de almacenamiento se duplica.
Super Mario Galaxy a 1440p y 60 FPS mediante Dolphin
La única forma de jugar Super Mario Galaxy a 1440p y 60 FPS, o incluso a resoluciones superiores como 4K, es utilizando el emulador Dolphin en un ordenador.
Mediante emulación es posible aumentar la resolución interna a 1440p (2560x1440) de forma nativa y mantener los 60 FPS estables que incluye el motor del juego.
A eso se suma la posibilidad de aplicar paquetes de texturas en alta definición y filtros como anti-aliasing o filtrado anisotrópico, opciones que no están disponibles en la versión original de Wii ni en el port para Android.
Riesgos legales y estado de desarrollo de Galaxy Android
Pese al logro técnico que representa, Galaxy Android se mantiene al margen de cualquier autorización por parte de Nintendo. La compañía japonesa tiene un historial de rechazo hacia los proyectos de terceros que manipulan su código o su propiedad intelectual.
Esa postura abre la puerta a que el port no logre mantenerse disponible a largo plazo, o que al menos quede restringido a canales de distribución no oficiales. Por el momento, la aplicación solo se puede conseguir a través de un repositorio alojado en GitHub.
El proyecto continúa, además, en una etapa temprana de desarrollo. Quienes ya lo han probado coinciden en que todavía necesita trabajo de ajuste antes de ofrecer una experiencia estable, y mencionan diversos errores que afectan el funcionamiento del juego durante las partidas. Quienes decidan instalarlo deben estar preparados para encontrarse con fallos técnicos durante su uso.

articles.title: Google Cloud went down after 'power event' causes major outage across Europe
articles.text:
Google Cloud went down after 'power event' causes major outage across Europe
Google Cloud suffered issues across Europe
Google Cloud is back up and running after suffering a major outage across most of Europe.
The company confirmed "Multiple services are experiencing issues in the europe-west2 region" with user reports spiking on outage tracker site DownDetector.
It later updated to reveal a 'power event' had caused the issue, with mitigation following soon after - but you can follow our live coverage as it happened below.
Good morning - well, maybe not so good for Google Cloud, which has confirmed it is suffering issues across Europe.
On its status page, the company confirmed it was seeing that "Multiple services are experiencing issues in the europe-west2 region."
The problems were confirmed at 10.24am BST/02.24am PST, so it could be a busy day for Google workers...
DownDetector is showing a big spike in user reports that something is not well at Google Cloud, although numbers do appear to have fallen slightly.
As the technological backbone for many other companies, the Google Cloud issue may well be affecting a range of customers.
DownDetector is showing a few spikes for other companies that seem to mirror its own pattern - with several major banking apps including the likes of Revolut and Lloyds Bank in the UK apparently affected.
You can follow TechRadar's coverage of that outage in our seperate live blog here.
Google Cloud's own status page doesn't make for pretty viewing either, with lots of orange alerts showing that multiple systems are down, and many regions across Europe affected.
The affected services include hugely important business tools such as BigQuery, App Engine, Looker, SQL and many many more...
After a slight fall in DownDetector reports, things have surged up slightly again.
On its status page, Google Cloud has promised an update soon, noting:
"We are experiencing an issue with multiple services in europe-west2 beginning on Monday, 2026-10-19 23:08 PDT.
Our engineering team continues to investigate the issue.
We will provide an update by Tuesday, 2026-10-20 04:00 PDT with current details.
We apologize to all who are affected by the disruption."
Here's that spike - bad news for Google Cloud customers, but hopefully we should be getting an update soon.
Looking at DownDetector, it seems some of the initial surges at other companies seems to be dying down, with Revolut, Lloyds, Rightmove and DpD all recovering.
It's too early to debate what might have caused the outage, but the limited reach of the damage (across European regions) could mean any number of things.
It's unlikely to have been a cyberattack, as user outage numbers are too low, so it could be an internal software or hardware issue, or even a power surge across the network.
Google Cloud is still set to give us an update soon, so we'll stay tuned for what they say.
The outage may have severe knock-on effects for some businesses, showing the need for effective backup systems.
“When a cloud outage leaves people unable to make payments or access everyday services, it exposes how much we depend on infrastructure we never see," Marijus Briedis, Chief Technology Officer at NordVPN, tells us.
“As Google is one of the world’s biggest technology companies, disruption to its cloud services can also affect businesses whose customers may have no idea they depend on Google at all.
“For everyday Google users, this dependence can mean several services they rely on suddenly being unavailable at the same time. Someone unable to pay through one banking app may find their alternative is affected too. Keeping a second payment option can help, although using a different bank does not guarantee it relies on different technology.
“Banks, retailers and delivery companies may look like separate businesses, but behind the scenes many rely on the same handful of technology providers. A problem at one supplier can quickly spread beyond its own customers.
“For businesses, the lesson is not that the cloud is unreliable, but that using a major provider does not remove the responsibility to prepare for disruption. Critical services need tested arrangements to switch to another system when something goes wrong.
“A backup is only useful if it can operate independently of whatever has failed. Businesses need to check whether their main service and their fallback rely on the same underlying systems, and test how quickly they can switch between them. Having copies of your data does not, on its own, mean customers can carry on making payments or accessing their accounts.”
A big update - Google has confirmed the cause of the issue - and it's one of the ideas we anticipated.
"We are experiencing an issue with multiple services in europe-west2 beginning on Monday, 2026-10-19 23:08 PDT," the company wrote.
"Due to a power event we had suffered an outage within europe-west2-b zone. The power event is mitigated. Partial mitigation to infrastructure services will be observed within the next 30 minutes and the remaining services will be mitigated there after."
Feeling concerned about the effect of the outage? It should be sorted soon, but here's some words of comfort from Dr. Pete Membrey, Chief Research Officer at ExpressVPN.
"Right now, a problem in Google Cloud’s London region is having a knock-on effect across banks, government services and retailers, because so many of them run on the same infrastructure underneath. When one part of that goes wrong, a lot of familiar apps and websites stop working at once."
"It’s too early to say what’s caused it, and people shouldn’t assume it’s a cyberattack. Most outages like this turn out to be technical faults rather than anything malicious."
"The main thing is not to panic. If your banking app isn’t working, it’s very likely the outage, not a problem with your account. There’s no need to reset passwords or reinstall anything. Be wary of any texts or emails claiming to be from your bank and asking you to confirm your details because of today’s disruption. Services should come back once the issue is fixed, so check official updates and give it time.”
Google's latest update also provides some hope for mitigation - noting that while, "Google Cloud services are unavailable in europe-west2-b zone; some services in europe-west2 region may experience elevated errors and intermittent network issues."
"If feasible, the impacted customer may try to migrate their workload impacted to another available location (zone or region)."
The good news seems to be that most customers aren't suffering any adverse effects, as DownDetector graphs for other companies does appear to be on the slide.
Let's hope this is the beginning of the end now...
The end may very well be in sight - Google Cloud's latest update notes that things may be completely fixed within the hour.
"Full recovery of existing workloads should be completed, tentatively by Tuesday, 2026-10-20 06:00," the update page says.
And that's a wrap - Google Cloud says the issue has now been fixed, and customers should see their services returning to normal.
"The issue with impacted GCP products has been mitigated for most of the customers and it is believed to be affecting currently a very small number of customers and our Engineering Team is working on it," the official update page says.
"If you have questions or are impacted, please open a case with the Support Team and we will work with you until this issue is resolved."
The company says it will also be opening a full investigation into the incident, and will publish its findings soon.

articles.title: US Army reportedly developing program that would deploy AI agents to autonomously seek and destroy targets in enemy digital infrastructures — experts warn ECHOTRIBBLE program could have disastrous consequences
articles.text:
US Army reportedly developing program that would deploy AI agents to autonomously seek and destroy targets in enemy digital infrastructures — experts warn ECHOTRIBBLE program could have disastrous consequences
Agents will self-destruct upon completing their mission
The U.S. Army is allegedly developing a program to deploy autonomous AI agents that can navigate digital and network infrastructures, identify targets, and “neutralize” them. According to an Oct. 19 report by The Intercept, citing leaked official documents from the Army Cyber Command (ARCYBER), the nascent program, codenamed “ECHOTRIBBLE,” is primarily focused on offensive missions with the goal of neutralizing targets by “disabling the threat completely or temporarily, deleting the threat from the target.”
The program purportedly seeks to develop modular, autonomous AI agents that would function like computer worms, stealthily navigating adversary networks, moving between devices, and self-replicating across different operating systems. The agents would operate lightly in contested cloud environments and air-gapped systems alike, keeping reports minimal and concealing any required transmissions. Once an agent identifies and neutralizes a target, it would self-destruct, ideally without alerting the target or leaving any traces of its existence.
Cybersecurity experts have raised safety concerns about the project. A recent string of events has seen AI agents escape their environments and autonomously execute unassigned tasks. The document says the army will implement “predefined triggers” to help agents precisely distinguish targets. However, experts worry that if agents designed for benign tasks could execute unplanned, sometimes dangerous, actions to achieve those tasks, what should be expected of self-replicating agents designed specifically for offensive missions? Anthropic’s experiments showed AI agents can set up inference on different hardware and replicate across a network.
The Army also wants the agents to be capable of “Self-Directed Behavior,” acting with as little human oversight as possible, as this is necessary to achieve the desired level of autonomy. Conversely, this level of autonomy has seen AI agents bypass guardrails to complete their tasks. Government intelligence agencies have also been known to penetrate target networks through civilian infrastructure. “The target may well be hit. But what path will it take?” asked Hyrum Anderson, co-founder and CEO of the AI security firm Abundant, as quoted by The Intercept. “Will it go through a U.S. water utility on its way, because that’s where the adversary has staged its command and control, and take that down too?”
Another angle of concern is how the agents would make judgment calls. While AI agents are excellent at overcoming obstacles in their path, there's no predicting with 100% accuracy what they would consider obstacles or what path they would take to overcome them. “One of the reasons that we trust 19-year-old Marine corporals in Ramadi with live rounds and a weapon is because they have both the compute substrate — the brain and the eyes — but the deep world knowledge to understand, ‘Yeah, I probably shouldn’t do that,’” said William Marcellino, a senior behavioral scientist at the RAND Corporation researching military AI applications. “That is not something that current public AI technology has.”
The ECHOTRIBBLE program is in the early prototyping and industry assessment phase and is led by ARCYBER, the Army Cyber Technology and Innovation Center (ArCTIC), and the Cyber Fusion Innovation Center (CFIC), with private vendors and academic researchers proposing and designing the software. ARCYBER and ArCTIC dictate the operational requirements and rules of engagement, while CFIC, a defense non-profit organization, acts as an intermediary between the Army and commercial tech companies. The Army recently held a virtual Assessment Event from October 6 to October 8, 2026, where it evaluated 65 technical whitepapers submitted by private vendors proposing solutions for the agentic framework and narrowed them to five. The final candidate(s) will be issued funding and formal prototype contracts.

articles.title: Revolut and Lloyds Bank are down for millions — here's all the latest on the outages
articles.text:
Revolut and Lloyds Bank are down for millions — here's all the latest on the outages
Is Google Cloud to blame?
The online banking services for Revolut and Lloyds Bank are down for many users right now, with Revolut confirming it's been hit by an outage that's affecting "multiple services".
The issues for both Revolut and Lloyds Bank started at the same time at about 6.46am BST / 1.46am ET, with both showing large spikes on Downdetector. At their peak, there were almost 1,500 reports from Revolut customers on Downdetector and arounds 500 for Lloyds Bank.
While the reports have since dropped slightly, the outage appears to be ongoing for many — here's all the latest news, including whether it could potentially be related to confirmed Google Cloud problems...
The latest news
- Revolut and Lloyds Bank have been hit by outages in the UK this morning
- Revolut has confirmed it's experiencing a "service disruption" hitting "multiple services"
- The issues could be related to a Google Cloud outage that's also hitting UK other services, although this hasn't been confirmed
Revolut says Google Cloud is to blame
We've long suspected it was the case, but a Revolut spokesperson has just confirmed to us that Google Cloud is the cause of its banking issues today.
"We are currently experiencing a service disruption affecting multiple services due to a recent outage with Google Cloud. We can confirm that all our customers’ money and data are safe. We’ve been working to fix the issue since it was identified this morning and apologise to anyone affected and for any inconvenience caused," the spokesperson said.
On the plus side, the number of reports from Revolut customers on Downdetector has now dropped significantly to only around 200 — so it seems the end could finally be in sight for an outage that's lasted over ten hours.
An update from Lloyds
If you've been struggling with your Lloyds Bank services today, we have some positive news.
A spokesperson just told me: "We understand the root issues have been resolved, so we expect to all our services to be back to normal soon."
It's not looking quite as positive for Revolut customers though — it still hasn't posted any updates since its first one at 8.54am, which understandably hasn't gone down very well with those affected. I've asked Revolut if it has any more updates and will post them here as soon as I hear anything.
A 'power event' to blame?
The Google Cloud status page now says that "a power event caused an outage" in its europe-west2 region, which is based in London.
We still don't know for sure that it was the cause of today's Revolut and Lloyds Bank issues, but given the timing it certainly seems possible — and the good news is that the event has been "mitigated", with Google Cloud saying it's "seeing the recovery of services".
Google Cloud has "tentatively" promised that "full recovery of existing workloads" should be complete by 2pm BST — so if you're still struggling with your banking apps today, there is hope on the horizon.
Revolut reports remain high
While the likes of Lloyds Bank and HSBC have seen their number of reported issues on Downdetector drop significantly in the last two hours, Revolut has stayed pretty steady — which suggests that it continues to be the worst hit by today's cloud issues.
At 12.49pm BST, there were still almost 600 reports for Revolut — and its warning-splattered status page remains unchanged. Its engineers seemingly haven't yet been able to find a migration fix to get things working.
However, Google Cloud's status page has now "tentatively" promised that "full recovery of existing workloads should be completed" by 2pm BST, which could be promising news — assuming the two are related.
Revolut apologises
The Revolut Support account on X is working overtime to try and placate its many frustrated customers — but there's still no update on a fix for today's problems.
The latest updates from the account say "our team is working to restore service as soon as possible" and points people towards its system status page for more updates.
Right now, that page still looks identical to earlier, with a "partially unavailable" header and warning flags across most of its features, from card payments to ATM withdrawals.
Revolut appears to be the worst hit by today's issues — that could potentially be related to its deep "strategic partnership" with Google Cloud.
Another app bites the dust
The financial budgeting app, Emma, is also reporting being down today — and interestingly it directly blames the Google Cloud issues for the issues.
As far as I'm aware, none of the other banking services experiencing problems today have directly blamed Google Cloud, but Emma just has — and it's confirmed that "this is a technical outage, not a security issue".
We've hit the five-hour mark
Frustration is growing with many Revolut and Lloyds Bank customers, who have now been without important banking services for several hours — and have, in some cases, been left stranded.
Some of the anecdotal reports include people who are stuck at petrol stations being unable to pay, someone who can't pay for their taxi en route to an airport, and another poor soul who seemingly can't exit their train station in Japan.
The first reports started at 6.55am BST, so we're now approaching five hours with no fix in sight. And the frustration is partly stemming from the scale of outage, which is still hitting most parts of Revolut's services from the app to payments and transfers.
Revolut's latest statement continues to be the one it sent to us earlier and also posted on X at 8.54am.
HSBC and Rightmove also hit
While Revolut and Lloyds Bank have the highest number of reported issues this morning on Downdetector, they're far from alone — with HSBC and Rightmove also showing significant spikes.
Just over 400 users are reporting issues with the Rightmove app and also the paid Rightmove Plus service, while HSBC reports have dropped to just over 100 from an earlier high of 266 at 10.16am BST — but seem to be on the rise again.
While we still can't directly confirm all of this to today's Google Cloud incident or the problems affecting Revolut and Lloyds Bank, the simultaneous problems all point to a shared cloud infrastructure outage — and the only major one right now is with Google Cloud.
The case for Google Cloud grows
It's looking increasingly likely that Google Cloud is to blame for this morning's banking app issues.
The incident reported on Google Cloud's service health page is still ongoing, and we're reporting live on that outage separately.
While neither Revolut or Lloyds Bank have directly blamed Google Cloud for their issues today, their report graphs on Downdetector closely match those for Google's cloud infrastructure today (above).
This means both banking services could be somewhat reliant on Google Cloud fixing its issues in the "europe-west2 region" (which is based in London). Google's latest update at 10.24am BST says "our engineering team continues to investigate the issue", and that it'll provide another update at 12pm BST.
A statement from Lloyds Bank
A Lloyds Bank spokesperson has just sent me a statement on the issues it's experiencing this morning.
"Our app is online and customers can log in normally, though we understand some are having issues with certain online services this morning. We are aware of similar issues affecting other organisations and are monitoring the situation closely," they said.
That tallies with our experiences — my colleague Matthew Bolton, for example, says the Lloyds app is working for him, but is very slow. It's also telling that Lloyds says it's aware of "similar issues affecting other organisations", which could again point to that major Google Cloud outage being a potential cause.
Revolut confirms your money is safe
I've reached out to Revolut and Lloyds Bank this morning for their latest statements on this morning's banking problems. But if you're worried about your money in either bank, Revolut did post the message above earlier today at 8.54am BST.
It confirms the service disruption and says "we can confirm that all our customers’ money and data are safe". However, that's scant consolation to those who need to spend their money today – for example, the person who's reported being stuck in Japan train as they can't pay to get out.
Hopefully the "fix" that Revolut is working on will come soon, but reports on Downdetector are continuing to climb...
Is Google Cloud to blame?
While this is just speculation for now, the simultaneous issues affecting both Revolut and Lloyds Bank today point to a shared cloud infrastructure issue — and one of those is also hitting Google Cloud right now.
The Google Cloud status page reports that "Multiple services are experiencing issues in the europe-west2 region", which is located in London.
We don't yet know if there's a connection to the Revolut and Lloyds Bank issues, but that would explain why multiple UK services are experiencing issues right now. We've also seen spikes in reports for the likes of Royal Mail this morning, too.
Reports are on the rise
Reports on Downdetector peaked for Revolut at around 8.10am BST, but they seem to be on the rise again — and that's also the case for Lloyds Bank customers.
Most of the reports for Lloyds Bank are around 'login' issues, while for Revolut it's 'app' and 'funds transfer'.
I'm asking Revolut and Lloyds for an update on the issues, but Revolut's system status page says it's "currently experiencing an incident" that's affecting everything from sign-ins, card payments and topping up via bank card to ATM withdrawals.

articles.title: Amazon Canada to hire 9,000 seasonal workers for the holidays
articles.text:
Amazon has announced plans to hire 9,000 seasonal employees in Canada this holiday season.
The e-commerce giant is looking to fill roles across 55 Canadian sites, including fulfillment centres, sortation centres, and delivery stations. It adds that the average hourly base wage for seasonal roles is nearly $24, with roles including select benefits on day one, including mental health and wellbeing support and a new 10 per cent discount on grocery and daily essentials purchases.
Amazon says available roles will be posted on hiring.amazon.ca, with more positions posted on a “rolling basis” throughout the holiday season. The company says this comes amid a $78 million increase in pay increases in Canada this year, including raising the average hourly base wage by $1 to more than $26 per hour. In the U.S., Amazon says it will also hire over 300,000 workers for the holiday season.
Of course, the holidays will be an especially busy period for Amazon, although it remains to be seen whether demand will be more muted than usual given the continued rise in the cost of living.

❌ Les limites

- L'ergonomie trop basique
- La luminosité de 250 cd/m² interdit le vrai HDR
- Une connectique d’ancienne génération

L’Acer Nitro KG272Gbmipfx, de son petit nom complet, reste une proposition cohérente pour les joueurs avec un budget limité et une carte graphique modeste. Si vous cherchez un écran bureautique, par contre, ce n’est pas le meilleur candidat, puisque les textes ne sont pas d’une grande netteté. articles.title: Google DeepMind presume de haber batido a Minecraft con agentes controlados por Gemini 4 Argon en apenas 27 horas
articles.text:
'Minecraft' no es sólo uno de los juegos más exitosos de la historia y una base genial tanto para divertirse como para aprender. El título de Mojang lleva años usándose para medir de qué son capaces los modelos de inteligencia artificial y Google Deepmind acaba de anotarse un tanto: su Gemini 4 Argon ha completado 'Minecraft' de principio a fin in intervención humana.
Y parece que esta IA lo ha hecho sin trampas.
En corto. Cuatro agentes basados en Gemini 4 Argon derrotaron al Ender Dragon en 27 horas y 14 minutos. Se trata del jefe final del juego y los resultados se publicaron en un paper en arXiv en el que los autores son algunos de los responsables de Google Deepmind.
Se trata de uno de los últimos modelos de la compañía, uno que lleva semanas en un circuito cerrado para que expertos en ciberseguridad lo pusieran a prueba, pero que se liberó a suscriptores de pago el pasado 13 de octubre. Ahora bien, tiene cierto truco.
A ciegas. La prueba se realizó en un mundo generado al azar, en dificultad fácil y con los comandos de trampa desactivados. A los agentes sólo se les dio el objetivo de matar a la dragona, sin otras instrucciones, herramientas específicas para Minecraft o estrategias para acelerar el progreso. Cada uno de los agentes controlaban a un jugador mediante Mineflayer, una bibloteca de código abierto para crear bots del juego y, para actuar, vibecodeaban un programa corto en Java que era el que emitía las órdenes.
Por ejemplo, ir a un sitio, minar ciertos materiales y ese tipo de cosas. Entre los cuatro agentes escribieron 2.783 programas, intercambiaron 229 mensajes y murieron 605 veces. Y hay un par de cosas curiosas: la primera es que, de todas esas muertes, sólo 69 de ellas fue a manos del jefe. La segunda es que se repartieron el trabajo por su cuenta.
Uno fabricaba herramientas, otro reunía suministros, otro encendió el portal y otro localizó la fortaleza. Cuando lo tuvieron todo, fueron a por la dragona y se embarcaron en una batalla de 14 horas en la que también idearon diferentes estrategias para minimizar las opciones del rival, como romper los cristales de regeneración.
El truco. Ya hemos contado que la dificultad estaba en 'fácil', pero hay otros detalles interesantes que ilustran un poco mejor esta victoria. Según los investigadores, el 22% de todos los programas que escribieron terminaron en error y había una app que informaba a los agentes de qué recursos y criaturas tenían a su alrededor, incluso aquellos que estaban fuera de su vista.
Un plugin también les planificaba las mejores rutas y partían con ventaja porque en el proceso de entrenamiento del modelo ya estaba 'Minecraft', así que aunque no hubiera un mundo preparado o humanos haciendo cosas, es evidente que los agentes no se enfrentaron al juego de nuevas.
Y, sobre el precio, hasta la victoria los agentes necesitaron unos 1.350 tokens de entrada y, aparte de los cuatro agentes jugadores, había un quinto que se encargaba de supervisar la sesión para que ninguno hiciera trampas. La sesión completa salió por unos 810 dólares.
Por qué Minecraft. Algo interesante es que, de entre todos los juegos que hay, sólo unos pocos son aptos para pruebas así. 'Minecraft' es uno de los elegidos para varios experimentos y, en el de DeepMind, lo que se busca poner a prueba es la constancia a lo largo de miles de pasos dependientes durante más de un día. Antes, la Universidad de Michigan ya había hablado de las bondades del juego debido a que era un entorno 3D flexible ideal para tareas de aprendizaje por refuerzo con observación parcial y recompensas diferidas.
Otras IAs se han entrenado con 'Minecraft' y esto no es sólo algo exclusivo de la IA, ya que en entornos educativos es un juego extremadamente interesante porque se pueden poner en práctica ejercicios colaborativos, deductivos, pensamiento lateral, entrenar esa paciencia, desplegar la imaginación, la creatividad y porque enseña pensamiento computacional casi sin querer.
El sistema del juego funciona con una lógica similar a la electónica y, además, hay herramientas de programación por bloques que hacen que sea una buena puerta de entrada a la programación. Es lo mismo que lo hace interesante para entrenar la IA, en definitiva, y ese mundo abierto con reglas claras, pero objetivos abiertos en los que hay que planificar a largo plazo y coordinarse es justo lo que DeepMind quería evaluar en su modelo.
La IA tramposa. Pero si 'Minecraft' es un buen patio de juego para la IA, otro juego que se usa mucho es 'StarCraft'. De hecho, antes de que la IA fuera el monstruo que es hoy, ya se usaba StarCraft como uno de los exámenes finales de la IA junto al juego chino Go. Recientemente, en una competición de bots en 'StarCraft: Brood War donde los modelos tenían una hora para programar un bot que controlara a una de las facciones del juego, GPT-6 Astra optó por la vía rápida.
GPT-6, que acumulaba varias derrotas, en lugar de mejorar su propio programa se descargó Stardust, un bot escritop por humanos que es una auténtica bestia en el competitivo. Esto es, evidentemente, una trampa, pero también algo conocido como 'reward hacking' o lo que es lo mismo: cumplir el objetivo usando atajos, como aprobar un examen con chuletas.
No era la primera vez y ya hubo una IA de DeepmMind que se pasó 'Sonic The Hedgehog' usando fallos en el código del juego y, precisamente, para eso estaba ese quinto agente en el nuevo experimento de DeepMind controlando a los otros cuatro de 'Minecraft': para que no usaran esa vía rápida de las trampas.

articles.title: Un SUV chinois éligible à l’aide de 6 000 euros : un tour de magie qui fait mal à l’industrie européenne
articles.text:
Affiché à 31 400 €, le Leapmotor B10 est un SUV chinois relativement classique. Il n’est pas mémorable à conduire, ni même à regarder. Son équipement est en contrepartie plutôt riche mais ses possibilités de personnalisation bien limitées. Il se montre en revanche assez confortable et tout à fait pratique. Bref, assez quelconque en somme… Sauf qu’il revient aujourd’hui sur le devant de la scène en brandissant une nouvelle fois l’argument prix.
En étant désormais produit à l’usine Stellantis de Saragosse, en Espagne, le B10 s’affranchit des droits de douane imposés par l’Union Européenne sur les véhicules électriques importés de Chine. Surtout, il pourrait être éligible à la Prime Coup de Pouce récompensant les modèles à batterie fabriqués en Europe. Un avantage indéniable qui lui permettra d’abaisser significativement son tarif pour aller chercher à coup sûr de nouveaux clients.
Pourquoi produire en Europe devient indispensable pour les marques chinoises
Pour établir ce plan d’attaque, l’usine de Saragosse n’a pas été choisie au hasard. Le site possède en effet une forte capacité de production pouvant accueillir la fabrication d’un nouveau modèle. Le B10 sera ainsi assemblé aux côtés des Peugeot 208, Opel Corsa et Lancia Ypsilon. Cette initiative s’inscrit dans la stratégie FaSTLAne 2030 du géant automobile, qui souhaite renforcer fortement sa compétitivité industrielle.
C’est ainsi que la politique européenne peut se transformer en opportunité selon Silvia Vernetti, porte-parole de Stellantis : « la transition électrique doit aussi être une transition industrielle. Si notre partenariat constitue notre stratégie, Saragosse est la preuve que nous pouvons conjuguer technologie mondiale, compétitivité et capacités industrielles européennes ». Cela fait bien les affaires de Leapmotor, qui espère se développer en Europe.
Que change ce virage industriel pour les clients français ?
C’est ce que confirme Jiangming Zhu, PDG de la marque chinoise : « nos racines sont en Chine et notre ambition est mondiale. L’Europe est un élément stratégique de cette ambition, et la production à Saragosse nous permet de rapprocher notre technologie des marchés et des clients européens ». Faire les yeux doux à l’Europe est aussi synonyme d’une avance cruciale sur les autres constructeurs chinois.
La taxe de 30,7 % s’appliquant habituellement aux modèles électriques chinois importés dans l’Union Européenne devrait logiquement sauter. Mieux, la Prime Coup de Pouce, dont le montant oscille entre 3 600 et 6 100 €, pourrait tomber pour le SUV électrique. S’il valide tous les prérequis exigés par l’Union Européenne, le B10 verrait son prix de départ tomber potentiellement à 25 300 €. Imbattable pour un modèle familial offrant 361 km d’autonomie !

articles.title: Prime Video tient sa série ultime pour Halloween avec Carrie, un raz-de-marée mondial
articles.text:
Prime Video a sorti la série un peu plus de trois semaines avant Halloween, en pleine saison des programmes d’horreur. Ce mardi 20 octobre, Carrie est toujours la série la plus regardée de Prime Video dans le monde, selon le classement de FlixPatrol, et elle est en tête aux États-Unis, au Royaume-Uni comme en France.
Prime Video frappe fort avec Carrie
Amazon a confié le premier roman de Stephen King à Mike Flanagan (The Haunting of Hill House, Midnight Mass), qui avait déjà adapté l’écrivain au cinéma avec Jessie en 2017 et Doctor Sleep en 2019. Il pilote la série, en signe le scénario et réalise quatre des huit épisodes. Stephen King en est producteur exécutif.
Pour le scénario, on retrouve Summer H. Howell qui joue Carrie White, la lycéenne harcelée, et Samantha Sloyan sa mère Margaret, une fanatique religieuse. Amber Midthunder et Matthew Lillard, qui joue le proviseur du lycée, font partie de la distribution principale. Nous avons détaillé ce que vaut cette relecture, entre harcèlement scolaire, fanatisme religieux et télékinésie, dans notre critique complète de la série.
Huit épisodes à voir avant Halloween
Carrie sort dans un mois chargé en films et séries d’horreur, et mêle scènes sanglantes et drame psychologique. Côté critique, la série obtient 86 % d’avis positifs sur Rotten Tomatoes (126 critiques recensées), même si ses libertés avec le roman divisent.
Les huit épisodes, de 48 à 59 minutes chacun, sont tous en ligne depuis le 7 octobre, soit environ sept heures à caser avant le soir du 31 octobre.
Alors que la période est traditionnellement saturée de productions horrifiques au rabais, Carrie s’impose comme la seule (du moins la rare) proposition majeure capable de conjuguer horreur viscérale et drame psychologique d’une justesse assez terrifiante. Les réseaux sociaux étouffent sous les réactions, propulsant le show au rang de phénomène pop-culturel incontournable de cet automne. Clairement.

articles.title: Exclusive: Kantata's Expertise Insights answers services firms' business questions in plain English - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Exclusive: Kantata’s Expertise Insights answers services firms’ business questions in plain English
Professional services automation software company Kantata Inc. today added generative business intelligence to its Expertise Engine platform with the launch of Expertise Insights.
Users ask about the business in plain English, as in where margin pressure is showing up, and the software answers with an interactive chart, a calculation or an executive summary.
Kantata’s pitch rests on how long it takes services firms to get answers out of their own data. The company says a request often has to go through a business intelligence analyst or a services engagement, and the wait can run to a week.
Sarah Edwards, Kantata’s chief product and strategy officer, said the value of an insight in professional services “depends on how quickly you can act on it.” Reports often show up after the moment has passed, she said.
Expertise Insights runs on Amazon Web Services Inc.’s Amazon Quick. On top of it Kantata has added a semantic layer that translates database field names into the vocabulary staff at a particular firm use every day. Firm-specific terms are covered, down to distinctions such as “chargeable utilization” versus “billable utilization.”
Kantata ships the product with four ready-made dashboards. Finance teams get margin, revenue per head and cost leakage trends in one of them, and the rest are given over to delivery, time and resourcing. On the delivery dashboard, project health is broken out by schedule, scope, budget and client health.
Users who need something the stock dashboards don’t show can turn to Ask Insights for new analysis on demand. Kantata says a complete board deck can be assembled in minutes. Saved work goes into Bookmarks and Pinboards, so a filtered view or a one-off analysis can be kept without spawning another copy of a master dashboard. Kantata is pitching that as a cure for dashboard sprawl.
The software can also link capacity, margin, delivery risk and financial performance. Piecing those relationships together might otherwise take several reports, or a seasoned operator who knows where to look.
Vikas Nehru, Kantata’s chief technology officer, said artificial intelligence in professional services should make a firm’s “collective expertise available at the moment a decision needs to be made.” That requires clean data and context, he said, plus AI that understands how a business works.
Life sciences consultancy Lumanity Inc. is among the customers already running the product. Andy Newbill, its senior manager of professional services automation, recently put together a complex report using calculated fields in an hour, and by his estimate the job would have taken hours before. Most striking to him was the chance to describe what he needs “in natural language and have the system help me build it.”
Kantata announced Expertise Insights at the Technology & Services World conference in Las Vegas, and it is available now. The company’s previous launch, Agent Studio, came a month ago and lets firms build custom AI agents by describing them in plain language.

Galaxy Watch 9 com Snapdragon atinge menor preço desde lançamento
Galaxy Watch 9 BT (40 mm) tem chip Snapdragon e novos recursos de saúde; smartwatch da Samsung recebe desconto histórico de 37% no Pix com cupom no Mercado Livre
O Galaxy Watch 9 Bluetooth de 40 mm está saindo por R$ 1.889 no Pix com cupom OFFSOHJ no Mercado Livre. O novo smartwatch da Samsung, que traz chip Snapdragon e novos recursos para monitorar a saúde do usuário, atinge o menor preço desde o lançamento com desconto de 37% sobre o original de R$ 2.999.
O novo Galaxy Watch 9 é o 1º smartwatch da Samsung equipado com um chip Snapdragon, o Wear Elite SW6100, substituindo os Exynos. Aliado a 2 GB de RAM e 32 GB de armazenamento interno, ele permite a instalação e execução local de aplicativos com alto desempenho.
Seus sensores avançados suportam várias atividades esportivas e trazem novos recursos de qualidade de vida ausentes no Galaxy Watch 8, como o Sinais Vitais, que cruza dados de frequência cardíaca, oxigenação, temperatura da pele e frequência respiratória, e a Pontuação de Saúde do Coração.
A tela Super AMOLED de 1,34″ do Galaxy Watch 9 possui brilho de até 3.000 nits e reproduz imagens com cores realistas, além de garantir a visibilidade em qualquer ambiente. O vidro Cristal de Safira protege o display contra pancadas e arranhões.
O corpo de alumínio Armor de 40 mm recebe as certificações IP68 e militar MIL-STD810H, e resiste a até 5 atmosferas de pressão (5 ATM+), podendo ser usado também em esportes aquáticos em águas rasas. A pulseira redesenhada é 25% mais leve e flexível do que a da geração anterior.
Este wearable ainda pode salvar a vida do usuário em uma situação crítica: no caso de uma emergência médica, ele pode ligar para contatos específicos e números como 190 (polícia) e 192 (ambulância), desde que pareado a um celular.
O Galaxy Watch 9 Bluetooth de 40 mm (R$ 1.889 no Pix com cupom OFFSOHJ) roda Wear OS 7 e sua bateria de 390 mAh garante até 40 horas de autonomia, segundo a Samsung. O smartwatch possui conectividade Wi-Fi 5, Bluetooth 6, NFC e GPS multibanda, que determina a posição do usuário em tempo real.

articles.title: Mysteriöse Nachricht in Super Mario 64: Wurde sie nach 30 Jahren endlich entschlüsselt?
articles.text:
Super Mario 64: Ist ein 30 Jahre altes Rätsel endlich gelöst?
Schon 1996 haben Zocker:innen auf der ganzen Welt in Super Mario 64 auf ein seltsames Detail geschaut. In einem Hinterhof des Schlosses steht die Statue eines Sterns. Darunter ist eine Plakette mit einer Inschrift angebracht. Die Auflösung von 32 x 32 Pixeln hatte es bisher aber unmöglich gemacht, die genauen Wörter zu entziffern. Doch das hat Gamer:innen nicht aufgehalten, Theorien aufzustellen.
Super Mario 64: Theorien zur Plakette
Seit Jahrzehnten hält sich hartnäckig die Theorie, dass die obere Zeile der zweizeiligen Inschrift „L is real 2401“ zeigen würde. Die kryptische Nachricht soll laut einigen Gamer:innen ein versteckter Hinweis der Entwickler:innen sein, dass Luigi (also „L“) sich doch im Spiel befindet. Die Zahl 2401 soll indes ein Hinweis sein, wie er freischaltbar ist.
Im Laufe der Jahre hatte Nintendo diese Theorie aber schon zerstört. Damals hieß es in einem Schreiben an einen Fan, dass die Nachricht bewusst unleserlich ist und niemand genau wüsste, was da überhaupt steht. Doch jetzt will ein Fan endlich Licht ins Dunkel gebracht haben. Unter dem Nicknamen „Supermochi64“ hat er auf GitHub eine ausführliche technische Analyse der mysteriösen Plakette veröffentlicht.
Was sagt die Inschrift wirklich?
Um das herauszufinden, hat der Mario-Fan nicht einfach KI genutzt, um die niedrigaufgelöste Plakette hochzurechnen. Er hat den umgekehrten Ansatz gewählt und eigene Plaketten erstellt, die er dann auf die Größe von 32 × 32 Pixeln geschrumpft hat. So konnte er Font und die geschriebenen Wörter mit dem Original vergleichen und die Phrasen mit der höchsten Wahrscheinlichkeit finden. Das ist möglich, weil die Buchstaben trotz der geschrumpften Größe ein Muster hinterlassen. Die Plakette benutzt insgesamt 32 verschiedene Grautöne.
Am Ende bekam „Supermochi64“ für eine Reihe von Phrasen einen Mismatch-Score. Je niedriger dieser ist, desto besser stimmen die Ergebnisse mit dem Original aus Super Mario 64 überein. Allein für das erste Wort ließ der Mario-Fan mehr als 1,2 Millionen Optionen vom System analysieren. Dabei kristallisierte sich „Eternal“ als klarer Sieger heraus. Andere Wörter dahinter waren lediglich Varianten von „Eternal“ mit Schreibfehlern. Erst auf dem 13.217. Platz landete das nächste fehlerfreie englische Wort „Sternal“.
Denselben Vorgang wiederholte er auch für die anderen Wörter und Phrasen. Am wahrscheinlichsten steht auf der Plakette in Super Mario 64 demnach „Eternal Star / We hope so“. Bei der zweiten Zeile gibt es noch andere Kandidaten mit ähnlichen Resultaten wie „We hope he“ oder „We hope as“. Da sie mit dem Rest aber keinen Satz ergeben, geht „Supermochi64“ davon aus, dass sich lediglich das Schriftbild ähnelt.
Um sein System zu überprüfen, versteckte der Mario-Fan anschließend noch 50 andere Wörter in der Plakette und ließ sie analysieren. Bei 38 von ihnen befand das System aus über 1,2 Millionen Kandidaten das korrekte Wort als bestmögliches Ergebnis. Bei den anderen zwölf Wörtern schnitten Varianten mit Schreibfehlern (wie „Dnration“ bei „Duration“) nur geringfügig besser ab.
Zu guter Letzt prüfte „Supermochi64“ auch noch andere Theorien, die sich im Laufe der Jahre angesammelt hatten. Seine Phrase erreichte einen Gesamt-Mismatch-Score von 1.129 über beide Zeilen. „L is real 2401“ hat einen deutlich höheren Mismatch-Score von 2.031, der auch nur die erste Zeile umfasst. Denn die Theorie hat nie eine Phrase für die zweite Zeile geliefert. Und auch der Satz „A Secret Star / lie here“, der seit Jahren in der Community kursiert, kommt auf einen hohen Mismatch-Score von 4.304.

articles.title: Ex-Nvidia-turned-VC Amulya Vishwanath: 'Physical AI is in it's LEGO era' | TechCrunch
articles.text:
It’s the moment everyone is waiting for — the ChatGPT moment for robotics, Amulya Vishwanath explained to TechCrunch’s Equity.
She is the founder and managing partner of Techable Ventures, a VC firm focused on physical AI, which she started after spending nearly seven years as a product marketer at Nvidia. Before that, she held the same role at a company that was later bought by Intel and was a digital signal processing engineer at Interconnect Systems, which was later bought by the electronics manufacturer Molex.
She stopped by Equity to talk about the future of physical AI — one of the industry’s latest buzzwords. “
A lot of companies and experts have been talking about the ChatGPT moment for robotics,” she said, adding that right now the industry was more in a “LEGO era.”
“There are a lot of foundational software and building blocks for robotics that are being rethought right now as we speak, and it’s super important in order for innovation to scale,” she continued.
Right now, people are building the basics — the robotic hands or the actuators — that can one day come together and build that big-ticket-item, like a bunch of LEGOs coming together. There’s general- and special-purpose robots being built right now too, and eventually, as people continue building them, they will get better and more advanced.
“We’ve done this during the internet era,” she said. “We’ve done this long, long time ago with the Industrial Revolution. I think it’s just a matter of time before things fall into place.”
“Talent is also going to be very critical,” she continued, adding elsewhere in the convo that talent is still a key definer of the U.S. market. This is one of the “moats” of her firm, she said, helping connect founders to top talent so they can stay competitive right now, as so much talent is going to big companies like Anthropic and Nvidia. She pointed out that she’s built up a strong network to help founders from her years of working in this space.
“This just make sit a lot more easier for me to be the strength or the first call for founders,” she said.

articles.title: "Lamentablemente, los modelos más avanzados no son confiables", Microsoft reconoce el riesgo con sus propios agentes de IA
articles.text:
Microsoft anunció nuevas herramientas de seguridad para proteger a las empresas de sus propios agentes de inteligencia artificial, porque, según la compañía, ni siquiera sus modelos más avanzados son del todo confiables.
La pieza central del anuncio es Guardian Agents, un conjunto de agentes de IA (programas que ejecutan tareas por su cuenta) diseñados para supervisar cada acción de los demás agentes que una empresa usa, antes de que ocurra y durante las 24 horas del día.
“Lamentablemente, los modelos más avanzados, sin importar su origen, no pueden ser confiables”, escribió Hayete Gallot, vicepresidenta ejecutiva de seguridad de Microsoft, en el blog oficial de la compañía.
Gallot aclaró que esto no se debe a que los modelos sean maliciosos, sino a que buscan cumplir objetivos sin seguir las normas o el criterio de una organización, lo que los vuelve impredecibles. Según ella, los agentes pueden adaptarse a los cambios de contexto, actuar de forma distinta a la esperada e incluso coordinarse entre sí para lograr un objetivo, sin necesidad de haber sido hackeados.
Microsoft llamó a estos sistemas “agentes internos”, en alusión al concepto de amenaza interna que usa la industria de la seguridad informática para describir a un empleado que representa un riesgo desde adentro de la organización. La compañía advirtió que muchos de esos agentes tienen permisos excesivos y acceso a datos, herramientas y procesos críticos de las empresas que los contratan.
Guardian Agents vigila a otros agentes de Microsoft
Guardian Agents forma parte de Project Perception, la plataforma de ciberseguridad que Microsoft presentó en julio y que originalmente organizaba tres tipos de agentes: uno que simulaba ataques de hackers, otro que detectaba esos ataques y evaluaba las vulnerabilidades, y un tercero encargado de corregirlas.
Ese sistema fue pensado para enfrentar amenazas externas. Ahora Microsoft lo extiende hacia adentro: los nuevos Guardian Agents reúnen señales de identidad, datos, redes, dispositivos y la nube para calcular en tiempo real el riesgo de cada agente y ajustar sus permisos de forma automática, incluida la posibilidad de bloquear una acción o aislar por completo a un agente si el riesgo lo justifica.
La compañía también añadió a su producto de seguridad Defender una función capaz de detectar hasta 60 tipos de agentes que los empleados llevan a sus trabajos sin autorización, entre ellos Claude Code de Anthropic, Codex de OpenAI y OpenClaw.
Una advertencia que incomoda a los propios socios de Microsoft
El movimiento resulta llamativo porque Microsoft es inversora de OpenAI y Anthropic, es uno de los mayores clientes de la nube de OpenAI y además desarrolla sus propios modelos de inteligencia artificial. Al advertir que ningún modelo es confiable “sin importar su origen”, la compañía siembra dudas sobre productos de los que depende comercialmente.
El director ejecutivo de Microsoft, Satya Nadella, había anticipado este giro semanas antes en su blog personal, donde escribió que las empresas no pueden delegar en los proveedores de IA la responsabilidad de controlar lo que sus agentes hacen. “Las garantías de un proveedor de modelos no nos liberan de esa responsabilidad (...) necesitamos separar quién provee la inteligencia de quién tiene la autoridad sobre ella”, afirmó.
Nadella resumió esa idea con una frase que Microsoft usó para presentar Guardian Agents: “El sistema de agentes más confiable no será el que use el modelo en el que más confiamos. Será el que esté diseñado para permitirnos confiar menos en el modelo”.
El enfoque también tiene un componente comercial evidente: Microsoft busca que las empresas compren sus herramientas de vigilancia de agentes en lugar de depender de los controles que ofrecen OpenAI y Anthropic junto con sus propios productos.
La idea se expande al resto de la industria de IA
La desconfianza hacia los agentes de IA ya se extendió a otras compañías. Microsoft figura entre los miembros fundadores de la nueva plataforma de seguridad de Nvidia para agentes, respaldada por más de 100 empresas de tecnología, que aísla a los agentes en entornos controlados y puede detener su funcionamiento a través del propio hardware, de forma similar a un interruptor de emergencia.

articles.title: Japan launches mission to bring home a piece of the Martian moon Phobos
articles.text:
Japan launched a $578 million mission Monday on a five-year expedition to land on the largest moon of Mars and retrieve samples for return to Earth, a daring international project that could yield new insights into the formation of the Solar System.
The robotic Martian Moons eXploration mission, known as MMX, lifted off at 3:41 pm EDT Monday (4:41 am Japan Standard Time Tuesday) from Tanegashima Space Center in southern Japan.
The MMX spacecraft rode into orbit atop a 207-foot-tall (63-meter) H3 rocket, Japan’s flagship launch vehicle. The rocket assigned to MMX debuted a new souped-up configuration with four strap-on solid rocket boosters, full-throttle main engines, and an extended payload shroud to accommodate the demands of Japan’s heaviest and most ambitious interplanetary mission to date.
The rocket’s upper stage accelerated the MMX spacecraft to a top speed of more than 24,000 mph, fast enough to break free of Earth’s gravitational pull for the 10-month voyage to Mars. The nearly 9,900-pound (4.5-metric ton) spacecraft—two-thirds of its mass comprised of propellant—separated from the H3 rocket about 71 minutes after liftoff.
Hiroshi Yamakawa, president of the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), declared the launch a success. “A long journey of five years has just started,” Yamakawa said.
MMX established contact with ground controllers, unfurled its solar panels, and was in a “very stable condition” soon after separating from the H3 rocket, according to Yasuhiro Kawakatsu, the mission’s project manager at JAXA. “So far, so good.”
“The MMX [mission] we launched today is a challenging mission aiming for the world’s first sample return from the Martian moons,” said Yoshihiro Seki, Japan’s science minister. “We hope that the results obtained through this mission will contribute to the development of our nation’s space science and exploration technology.”
Building on a legacy
The mission to the Martian moons builds on Japan’s success in leading the Hayabusa and Hayabusa 2 missions, the world’s first two spacecraft to bring back pristine specimens from asteroids. Scientists believe Phobos could itself be an asteroid that was captured into orbit around Mars billions of years ago. One of MMX’s science goals is finding out if that theory is correct.

articles.title: Microsoft's Bing Wallpaper App Hijacks Desktop Clicks to Promote Bing.com
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
Microsoft's Bing Wallpaper App Hijacks Desktop Clicks to Promote Bing.com
Microsoft's popular wallpaper application, Bing Wallpaper, has now been transformed into adware, according to a new report by Windows Latest. When a user clicks on an empty area of the desktop—not on any icon or menu—the application redirects them to Bing.com, Microsoft's search engine. Normally, this behavior would not be acceptable and would likely trigger a strong reaction from the community. However, Microsoft has limited this issue to occur only once every 24 hours. Repeated clicks after the initial activation do not open another browser window. Testing has confirmed that this behavior persists after the waiting period, even when Google Chrome is set as the default browser.
Interestingly, Microsoft tested a similar feature in 2025, which included a clearly labeled setting in Bing Wallpaper that allowed a desktop click to open Bing. At that time, the feature could be turned off, but this option is not available in the latest version of the application. Microsoft has removed the ability to disable this feature, meaning that every 24 hours, a desktop click will redirect to Bing.com. This change leaves users with less control over an action that is unrelated to managing wallpaper. The application has also reportedly displayed prompts encouraging users to make Bing their default search engine across installed browsers, even when the default browser is Google Chrome or another non-Microsoft browser.The only way to avoid this random redirect behavior is by choosing a different application to manage desktop wallpapers. For those who still want rotating Bing imagery due to its wide selection of images from around the world, Windows Spotlight is an option to consider. However, a third-party application might be the best choice, as it may only be a matter of time before Microsoft implements something similar in Windows Spotlight as well.

articles.title: US restarts three shut-down nuclear reactors to feed AI data centers — 2.25 GW coming online with backing from Microsoft and Google
articles.text:
US restarts three shut-down nuclear reactors to feed AI data centers — 2.25 GW coming online with backing from Microsoft and Google
Doc Brown would be abuzz and alight with joy.
The current and expected power draw of AI data centers has been the subject of strong discussion, but today, there appears to be some good news. Three U.S. nuclear reactors are being restarted after many years offline, expected to bring 2.25 GW total to the grid. According to a report, the Palisades Nuclear Plant in Michigan, the Crane Clean Energy Center on Three Mile Island (Pennsylvania), and the Duane Arnold Energy Center in Iowa are getting a fresh set of proverbial tires to get rolling again.
The Palisades plant was under active decommissioning, apparently marking this event as the first time a nuclear reactor is being put back to work after dismantling had begun. Despite what sounds like a tough starting point, this plant is the one that's furthest along, as it was loading fuel in August 2026 and is expected to generate 800 MW around March 2027.
Much like the other projects mentioned here, the Holtec Palisades firm running the reactor took a loan from the U.S. Department of Energy. Palisades borrowed from the DoE under the Biden administration's 2024 investment in nuclear energy, while the others were issued under the purview of the Trump administration's 2025 push.
The second reactor is the Crane Clean Energy Center on Pennsylvania's Three Mile Island, repurposing the facility's Unit 1. The project started in 2024, with Constellation Energy saying it would spend $1.6 billion total for the reactor. The firm then took a $1 billion loan from the Department of Energy in 2025. Microsoft is set to be the main customer, with a 20-year contract. This facility is projected to bring 835 MW online sometime in 2027.
This facility was famous in 1979 for the partial meltdown of its Unit 2, although mercifully the event had relatively tame environmental consequences. Constellation's ongoing project is restoring and refurbishing Unit 1, which didn't show significant issues until its 2019 decommissioning and has undergone a safety inspection from the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. This entity still needs to grant its blessing before the reactor starts loading fuel.
The Duane Arnold Energy Center in Iowa is the third unit being brought back to the grid, in a collaboration between NextEra Energy and Google. The predicted output is 615 MW, with the juice expected to start flowing in 2029. Next Energy CEO John Ketchum stated that the firm was happy with its cooperation contract with Google, as it meant that "none of the costs are being paid by residential customers in Iowa."
All three facilities had previously been shut down at various points as they were deemed too expensive to run, as labor and maintenance costs made nuclear-generated watts pricier than alternative means of production.

But the financial landscape for power has shifted, plus with such overwhelming demand and grid connections being a primary blocker for data center buildouts, their operators are likely willing to pay for premium power as long as they get it now instead of in a few decades.
Some quick browsing indicates that Michigan is going to need somewhere between 1.2 and 2.3 GW for data centers alone around 2030. Pennsylvania's forecast has a wide range of 0.8 to 3.4 GW, while Iowa's range is 1.55 to 2.8 GW. These figures are loose, as they include planned capacity for data center projects that may or may not end up being built, and whose timetables may slip due to economic conditions, hardware availability, and public resistance against expansive buildouts.

articles.title: World, de Sam Altman, veut protéger les réunions Zoom grâce au scan de l’iris
articles.text:
World, la société cofondée par Sam Altman, lance World ID for Zoom. L'outil affiche un badge sur la vignette d'un participant dont l'"humanité" a été vérifiée (oui, on en est là). Il est proposé aux clients professionnels de Zoom via la Zoom Marketplace.
Nous sommes arrivés à un stade où voir un visage en visioconférence ne garantit plus que la personne est celle qu'elle prétend être. Selon une enquête Gartner de septembre 2025, 62% des responsables cybersécurité interrogés avaient vu leur organisation subir une attaque par deepfake (une vidéo ou une voix truquée par IA) l'année précédente.
Trois images à faire concorder pour décrocher le badge
Nous rapportions en octobre 2024 que World, anciennement Worldcoin, dévoilait son Orb 2.0 et un service baptisé World ID Deep Faces contre les deepfakes en ligne. Deux ans plus tard, elle s'attaque aux réunions Zoom. Bain Capital, OpenExchange, Outtake, Pantera Capital et VanEck Funds font partie des premiers partenaires.
Tout part de l'Orb, l'appareil de World qui scanne l'iris. Chacun peut y obtenir une "Proof of Human", une preuve d'humanité. Il peut être installé au bureau ou apporté à domicile. Son image est signée cryptographiquement, un peu comme un sceau numérique, ce qui empêche de la modifier, affirme World. Le participant relie ensuite son World ID à son compte Zoom. Pendant une réunion, une notification arrive sur son téléphone et il prend un selfie dans l'application. Ce contrôle permet donc qu'une personne bien vivante est devant l'appareil. Trois images sont alors comparées : celle de l'Orb, le selfie et le flux vidéo que voient les autres invités. Si elles concordent, le badge s'affiche pour tous.
World insiste sur la différence avec la détection classique. Celle-ci analyse les images pour deviner si elles sont truquées. Résultat, une course entre faussaires et détecteurs, où un seul faux non repéré peut coûter cher. Ici, on compare à une référence signée. L'intégration repose sur les Realtime Media Streams de Zoom, une interface donnant accès au flux vidéo en direct. Elle tourne sur AWS et n'analyse que la vidéo, pas l'audio ni les transcriptions. la validité du badge est fixée par les organisateurs. Par la suite, la vérification s'effectuera au sein d'une salle d'attente virtuelle.
Reste la vie privée. Selon heise, World affirme chiffrer l'identité des personnes scannées, si bien que l'entreprise ne peut pas la lire. Tiago Sada, directeur produit, explique que le protocole de World ID repose sur du code open source. Les concurrents peuvent donc le reprendre à leur compte. Pour décentraliser et chiffrer les données, il s’appuie sur la blockchain, un registre numérique partagé. Plusieurs banques et prestataires financiers déploient aussi l'outil, sans passer systématiquement par l'iris. L'application propose trois niveaux. Le premier vérifie un document officiel, le deuxième demande un selfie, le troisième, la Proof of Human, passe par l'Orb. C'est donc celui qu'utilise Zoom.

articles.title: ChatGPT's Chrome extension can now control tabs, download files, and fill out forms
articles.text:
In a nutshell: OpenAI has released a major update to its ChatGPT browser extension, bringing deeper integration with Google Chrome. The extension can now access content from open webpages, analyze information, and complete tasks directly in the browser. The update also introduces new voice features and support for several additional languages.
ChatGPT's Chrome extension gained the ability to access content from open tabs last July. The latest update introduces two distinct AI modes, Chat and Work, allowing ChatGPT to interact with browser tabs and perform a wide range of tasks, including filling out online forms using information from documents stored on the device.
In Chat mode, the AI can read content from open tabs to analyze information and answer questions based on the active page context. For example, users can compare prices, delivery times, return policies, and other factors for products listed across different shopping sites.
In Work mode, ChatGPT can control the browser to send messages, download files, and group open tabs by topic. It can also fill out forms using information gathered online or extracted from files stored on the computer. Once a form is completed, users can review it manually before submitting it.
 – ChatGPT (@ChatGPT) October 15, 2026
Users can also tag ChatGPT with "@Chrome" directly in the ChatGPT app or on the website to perform browser tasks without opening the extension's side panel. Additionally, ChatGPT can now be restricted to specific tabs, preventing it from accessing other open pages.
Another new feature is a dedicated ChatGPT tab in Chrome that contains the user's ChatGPT history. Users can ask questions in Chat mode or perform tasks in Work mode from this tab. When accessing chat history or visiting new websites, ChatGPT will ask for permission, allowing users to choose between "allow once," "allow for this site," "allow for all sites," and "decline."
The new features are available for free in several Chromium-based browsers, including Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera, and Vivaldi. However, they will not be immediately available in Firefox or Safari. The updated extension can be downloaded from the Chrome Web Store.
OpenAI originally integrated ChatGPT into Chrome last July, allowing users to access several AI features through the extension's Side Chat panel. The update enabled ChatGPT to summarize articles, explain complicated content in simple English, answer questions about YouTube videos, and translate text from a wide range of supported languages.
While OpenAI continues to improve ChatGPT's support for third-party browsers, its own Atlas browser, which debuted last year with ChatGPT integration, was retired in August after failing to capture a substantial share of the browser market from established competitors such as Chrome, Safari, Edge, and Firefox.

articles.title: Streaming guide JustWatch becomes a streamer itself | TechCrunch
articles.text:
JustWatch, a company offering a search engine and guide for streaming movies and TV shows, is now moving directly into the streaming business itself. On Tuesday, the company behind the popular guide that’s used by 50 million people is launching JustWatch TV. The new streaming service will feature content from 30 partners and will offer both free and paid tiers, as well as a movie rental store.
The media and entertainment company behind the streaming guide, the JustWatch Group, initially announced its plans to venture into streaming last month. At the time, it said partners like Paramount, New Regency, Fremantle, Bleecker Street, and Vortex Media were on board. The company has since announced other content partners, including Cineverse in the U.S., LEONINE Studios in Germany, SND in France, and Altitude in the U.K.
The 12-year-old company has long been known for its online guide to movies and TV. Essentially, it’s a “TV Guide” for the streaming era, helping users navigate a landscape where movies and shows move from one service to another, making it harder to keep up with what’s streaming where.
Available in 140 markets globally, the guide provides streaming options for more than 500,000 movies and shows across more than 1,500 service providers worldwide. This “where to watch” information and streaming chart data are also used to power some 1,400 partner websites and apps and are valuable to studios, distributors, streamers, and agencies that use the data to target their campaigns across social media platforms like Meta, YouTube, TikTok, and others.
Now the company believes there’s an even bigger opportunity to grow its audience data and insights by running its own service.
“At a time where there is so much choice, yet with so many people constantly searching for a place to find their favourite film, the series they just heard about, or something exciting that fits them, it is a great moment to be a hub for all things entertainment,” said Quentin Carbonell, JustWatch SVP of Global Content Acquisitions and Strategy, in an email shared with TechCrunch. “By having our own service with titles to watch directly on JustWatch TV, we can grow our already massive audience, while continuing to direct them to all our streaming partners. This is a natural continuation of our mission to contribute to the entire ecosystem, from the big screen to the small one.”
The new streaming service will be available within JustWatch’s existing apps and website across 12 markets, including the U.S., Canada, the U.K., Ireland, Germany, Austria, France, Italy, Spain, Switzerland, Australia, and New Zealand.
Its free tier will offer a selection of ad-supported titles, while the ad-free version, JustWatch TV Plus, will offer more than 300 ad-free titles in the U.S., as well as other exclusive features, like advanced filters and the option to hide previously seen or disliked titles in the guide.
A movie rental store will also initially be available in the U.S., U.K., Ireland, Australia, and New Zealand, with more markets to follow in time.
While the ad-supported tier competes with free streamers like Tubi and Plex, the Plus tier will compete with low-cost streamers like Roku’s $2.99 per month ad-free service, Howdy. It will be similarly priced at $3.99 per month or $49.99 for a lifetime subscription. (The latter is an interesting way to price streaming, given the evolving content costs, but JustWatch believes there will be additional value in the data collected.) Paid subscribers will also be able to take 10% off on hundreds of rentals in the JustWatch TV Store, the company noted.
Like most low-cost services, JustWatch’s content lineup focuses on older movies and shows, as well as more indie content.
Another unique feature is that users will be able to influence the service’s content to some extent. JustWatch says users will be able to request titles they want to see to help shape what comes to the service.

articles.title: Air Canada now charges you $30 fee for phone bookings
articles.text:
Air Canada has started charging customers a $30 fee for booking flights over the phone.
As spotted by CP24, the change went into effect on Oct. 15, per Air Canada’s website. On the page, the airline notes that this $30 (plus applicable taxes) charge will apply to each passenger on new bookings made by phone. It adds that the booking fee will continue to apply for Aeroplan flight reward bookings.
Fliers will still be able to call Air Canada for support with existing reservations, travel disruptions and other inquiries without paying any fees.
In an FAQ on its site, Air Canada says the reason it has introduced this fee is to push its self-serve digital tools.
“Air Canada’s website and mobile app make it easy to book and manage your travel,” writes the airline. “Using these digital tools for everyday travel needs helps reduce wait times and allows our Contact Centre agents to focus their expertise on situations that require personalized support. ”
It should be noted that other Canadian airlines WestJet and Flair already charge for phone bookings, although their prices are $25 each.
While most people likely book their flights online anyway, it’s always annoying to see more fees added onto services, especially when, in this case, it’s literally for the purposes of giving money to Air Canada. If nothing else, charging people for speaking to an agent isn’t as bad as Cineplex, which for the past couple of years has charged a $1.50 booking fee for online purchases where it saves money because it’s a self-serve process where you don’t even deal with any actual humans.

articles.title: Netflix : nouveau séisme sur la plateforme avec un changement majeur en interne
articles.text:
Netflix n’a même pas attendu de présenter ses résultats trimestriels aux analystes de Wall Street, prévus ce mardi 20 octobre. Face à une action en baisse de plus de 20 % depuis janvier et à un temps de visionnage qui n’a progressé que de 2 % au premier semestre, le co-CEO de Netflix, Ted Sarandos, a sorti le couperet. Vingt-quatre heures après l’éviction brutale de sa directrice des contenus Bela Bajaria, c’est Dan Lin (qui s’occupait du cinéma) que Ted Sarandos a appelé vendredi pour lui annoncer son renvoi, officialisé ce lundi 19 octobre.
La fin de l’ère de l’austérité pour Netflix : Dan Lin et le piège du « zéro chèque en blanc »
L’aventure aura duré deux ans et demi, soit la moitié de son contrat de cinq ans, pour celui qui avait été nommé en février 2024 pour succéder à Scott Stuber. À son arrivée, Lin incarnait la rupture : fini la distribution de billets verts à l’aveugle, fini le gavage des stars hollywoodiennes et la promesse intenable d’un film inédit par semaine.
En juin, dans le New York Times, Dan Lin affirmait que Netflix avait « accepté » de ne plus travailler avec les cinéastes qui tiennent à une sortie en salles. Mais à Hollywood, la rigueur budgétaire se paie cash dès que les chiffres de visionnage ne suivent plus. Malgré la réorganisation des équipes par genre et quelques sorties en salles à titre d’essai, Lin n’a pas trouvé l’équilibre entre films taillés pour le streaming et sorties au cinéma, principal motif de son renvoi selon les sources du média américain.
Clashs avec Greta Gerwig et Ben Affleck : quand le patron agace les superstars
En coulisses, la méthode cassante de Dan Lin chez Netflix a fini par créer un climat délétère avec l’élite hollywoodienne. Selon Variety, une réunion Zoom consacrée à Narnia (qui s’est fait détruire son premier trailer par les fans), la superproduction au budget de 250 millions de dollars (environ 215 millions d’euros), a mal tourné plus tôt dans l’année. Dan Lin se serait montré « dédaigneux » envers Greta Gerwig, la réalisatrice de Barbie, plus gros succès mondial au box-office de 2023.
L’incident a pris une telle ampleur que l’agent surpuissant de la cinéaste, Bryan Lourd, est intervenu directement auprès de Ted Sarandos. Dan Lin s’est ensuite effacé du projet au profit de son bras droit, Doug Belgrad, lui-même licencié la semaine dernière. Dan Lin se serait aussi opposé à Ben Affleck sur l’usage, pour son film Animals, d’InterPositive, la start-up d’IA cofondée par l’acteur et rachetée par Netflix en juillet, comme le détaillait nos amis de chez Frandroid. Les représentants de Ben Affleck contestent toute dégradation de ses relations avec la plateforme.
Que se passe-t-il vraiment chez le géant du streaming ?
Cette purge au sommet en dit long sur le virage chaotique que traverse Netflix. En confiant l’ensemble de ses contenus (séries, films, programmes en direct) à Peter Rice, ancien dirigeant de Disney et de Fox, la plateforme admet à demi-mot l’échec de sa ligne d’austérité.
Pour rassurer Wall Street, Netflix tente désespérément de retisser des liens avec les réseaux de salles de cinéma traditionnels (un comble pour le pionnier qui méprisait la projection en salle) tout en cherchant sa nouvelle recette magique. Peter Rice prendra ses fonctions le lundi 26 octobre et devra désigner le successeur de Dan Lin. D’après Variety, Mike De Luca et Pam Abdy, anciens patrons du cinéma chez Warner Bros., discuteraient déjà avec Netflix.
