articles.title: En Colombia, 7 de cada 10 personas guardan archivos de trabajo o académicos en internet y no en su PC o celular
articles.text:
El almacenamiento en la nube dejó de ser un espacio reservado para fotografías y recuerdos personales en Colombia. Un estudio de Kaspersky determinó que el 69% de los colombianos guarda allí archivos relacionados con el trabajo, la universidad o el colegio, y que el 31% reconoce conservar información relevante o confidencial en estos servicios.
A esto se suma que el 78% mantiene en la nube contenidos de su teléfono, como fotografías, contactos y conversaciones. Esta concentración de datos personales, académicos y laborales en un mismo lugar obliga a prestar mayor atención a la seguridad de las cuentas, ya que un acceso no autorizado podría exponer información que no solo pertenece al usuario, sino también a empresas, instituciones educativas u otras personas.
Por qué la seguridad de la nube ya no es un asunto solo personal
La nube se convirtió en un repositorio que mezcla archivos personales con documentos sensibles vinculados a entornos laborales y educativos. Esa mezcla cambia el nivel de riesgo que implica una cuenta vulnerada, porque ya no está en juego únicamente la privacidad individual.
Carolina Mojica, gerente de Productos al Consumidor para NOLA y SOLA en Kaspersky, explica el fenómeno: “La nube facilita enormemente nuestra vida digital, pero también está concentrando cada vez más información que antes permanecía distribuida entre distintos dispositivos”.
La ejecutiva agrega que esta centralización modifica la naturaleza del problema. “Cuando guardamos allí documentos laborales, académicos o confidenciales, proteger la cuenta deja de ser únicamente un asunto personal, porque esos archivos también pueden contener información de empresas, compañeros, clientes o familiares”, señala.
Por esa razón, desde Kaspersky insisten en la necesidad de revisar periódicamente qué se almacena, limitar el acceso a los archivos sensibles y reforzar la seguridad de las cuentas utilizadas para conservarlos, según indica Mojica.
En términos prácticos, la nube es un servicio de almacenamiento remoto donde conviven fotos, contactos, chats y documentos de trabajo o estudio. Cuando esa cuenta se ve comprometida, el riesgo ya no se limita al usuario: puede afectar a empresas, instituciones educativas o terceros cuyos datos también quedaron guardados allí.
Qué medidas recomiendan los expertos para proteger los archivos guardados en la nube
Frente a este escenario, los especialistas de Kaspersky plantean un conjunto de recomendaciones orientadas a reducir la exposición de datos sensibles y fortalecer el control sobre las cuentas en la nube.
La primera medida consiste en revisar de forma constante qué información se guarda. Esto implica evitar la conservación de documentos confidenciales o archivos sensibles que ya no se necesiten y eliminar periódicamente contenido innecesario.
La protección de la cuenta ocupa un lugar central en estas recomendaciones. Los expertos aconsejan utilizar una contraseña única y activar la autenticación de dos factores, de manera que una contraseña comprometida no habilite automáticamente el acceso a otros servicios asociados.
Otra sugerencia apunta a separar, cuando sea posible, los archivos personales de los laborales. Esto supone utilizar las herramientas y cuentas autorizadas por la organización para almacenar documentos de trabajo, en lugar de trasladarlos a servicios personales sin autorización previa.
La empresa de seguridad informática también recomienda mantener copias adicionales de la información considerada importante, bajo la premisa de que la nube no debería ser el único sitio donde se conserven archivos que el usuario no pueda permitirse perder.
Finalmente, se sugiere recurrir a una solución de seguridad confiable. Este tipo de herramientas contribuye a detectar páginas de phishing, enlaces maliciosos y otras amenazas orientadas a robar credenciales de acceso, lo que reduce el riesgo de que terceros ingresen a la información almacenada en la nube.

articles.title: Companies are spending nearly a third of IT budgets on software upgrades
articles.text:
Companies are spending nearly a third of IT budgets on software upgrades
'Software tax' is a major ongoing cost
- Enterprises are being forced into software upgrades that they can't really get out of, report finds
- 91% have upgraded hardware in the past three years just to maintain software
- Enterprise protection legislation and software support obligations could be the answer
Legacy tech has become something of a hot topic in recent years with AI, but while hardware and data foundations have been core to the discussion around artificial intelligence, a new Origina report has revealed that around one-third of enterprise IT budgets are being earmarked for software upgrades.
The report found that 28% of large enterprise IT budgets are being spent on vendor-driven changes that they would not have otherwise chosen in a trend the company's calling a 'software tax'.
But more than just consuming budgets, software changes are also impacting worker time and leading to potentially lost productivity as a result.
Software upgrades cost more than you might think
"That's not a one-off cost, it's a recurring drag on capacity, and every year it repeats is a year those people aren't working on the initiatives that actually differentiate the business," former Liberty Mutual CIO James McGlennon and Origina board member James McGlennon explained.
More than four in five (84%) report that senior engineering staff always or often spend time dealing with vendor-driven software changes, taking them away from more meaningful work that they're employed to do. A similar number (80%) also reported that leaving a major software vendor could lead to widespread disruption within their business, ultimately forcing them to stay with that software vendor and enforcing vendor lock-in – with exit costs and migration technicalities to blame.
More than three-quarters now agree their software vendor dictates the timing and terms of changes, not them (78%), and that they have very little negotiating power (76%).
In many instances, enterprise customers don't even feel that an upgrade was totally necessary. Nearly all (91%) had retired fully functional hardware within the past three years just to comply with software vendor support deadlines. While Origina doesn't specifically state it, Windows 10's end of support is likely a large factor in this statistic.

articles.title: WhatsApp s'attaque à Safari avec un navigateur intégré sur iOS
articles.text:
Une version de test de WhatsApp pour iPhone, repérée le 19 octobre, embarque un navigateur intégré capable d’ouvrir tous les liens partagés dans les discussions. La fonction existe depuis l’an dernier pour certains liens d’entreprises ; elle s’étendrait désormais à l’ensemble des conversations. De quoi éviter le détour par Safari ou le navigateur par défaut de votre iPhone.
Tous les liens, sans quitter la discussion
Le chantier se cache dans la bêta 26.41.10.72, distribuée via TestFlight. Un réglage dédié apparaît dans les paramètres des discussions, pour activer ou couper le navigateur intégré à tout moment. À la première utilisation, un écran détaille le fonctionnement de l’outil. Les pages s’ouvrent ensuite directement dans WhatsApp, sans bascule vers une autre application. L’approche rappelle celle d’Instagram ou de X, qui gardent déjà les liens entre leurs murs.
Depuis iOS 14, chacun peut remplacer Safari par Chrome ou Firefox comme navigateur par défaut de son iPhone. Les applications gardent toutefois la main sur leurs propres liens, une latitude dont les réseaux sociaux usent massivement.
La navigation s’effectue dans une session isolée du reste de la messagerie, assortie d’une commande pour effacer cookies, cache et données en un geste. Un menu permet aussi de renvoyer la page vers le navigateur habituel. L’application, chiffrée de bout en bout, assure ne voir ni les liens partagés dans les conversations, ni ceux que vous ouvrez.
Aucune date de déploiement n’accompagne la découverte, et la fonction reste pour l’heure inaccessible, même aux testeurs. Elle prolonge un premier essai lancé en mai 2025 avec la bêta 25.14.10.72, limité aux liens de comptes professionnels et aux adresses sécurisées en HTTPS.
Le précédent Instagram pèse encore
En août 2022, le développeur Felix Krause démontrait qu’Instagram et Facebook sur iOS injectaient du code JavaScript dans les pages consultées via leur navigateur intégré. De quoi suivre, en théorie, chaque pression sur l’écran et chaque texte saisi, coordonnées bancaires comprises. Son outil en ligne, inappbrowser.com, permettait à chacun de mesurer l’ampleur du dispositif. La démonstration prouvait une capacité de collecte, sans établir qu’elle était exploitée. Meta avait alors justifié ce script maison par le respect du dispositif anti-pistage d’Apple.
L’affaire a durablement entamé la confiance dans les navigateurs intégrés, conçus d’abord pour retenir l’utilisateur dans l’application. Chaque minute gagnée en vaut une de plus pour la publicité, premier revenu de Meta. Les garde-fous mis en avant par WhatsApp répondent point par point à cet épisode : session cloisonnée là où Instagram injectait son code, effacement des traces là où rien n’était prévu. La promesse de ne rien voir devra toutefois se vérifier une fois l’outil entre toutes les mains : le script de 2022 était lui aussi passé inaperçu, jusqu’au regard d’un développeur extérieur.

articles.title: AI-assisted vibe coding brings Thunderbolt 4 support to Windows 98 SE
articles.text:
The takeaway: Vibe coding is viewed negatively by many, but when dedicating resources to a specific project isn't feasible, few alternatives exist. Microsoft, for example, doesn't have the time or resources to create modern drivers for operating systems they've long moved on from… but AI has no problem crafting code for legacy versions of Windows.
A developer by the name of Yeo Kheng Meng recently commissioned AI to create a driver that enables generic USB 3.x, USB4, and Thunderbolt 3/4 host controllers to work on ancient operating systems including Window 98 SE, ME, 2000, XP, Vista, and 7.
Dated versions of Windows barely make a blip on the OS market share radar, so why should anyone even care about something like this? Well, despite the low percentage of overall users, there are still lots of retro computing enthusiasts out there actively using older computers running legacy hardware and software. Being able to take advantage of modern connectivity is just icing on the cake for them.
Even if you aren't interested in this particular driver, there's a lot to take away from a story like this. Vibe coding gets trashed in the mainstream as a lazy way to approach a coding problem but as mentioned, not everyone has the time or resources to devote human programmers to every project. Tasks are often tackled based on priority, and making a driver for retro computing fans likely isn't going to rank high on that list.
One can also argue that vibe coding is a great way to explore ideas without having to be an expert in the field of programming. Every day, people come up with new and creative ideas that could help others but don't have the technical skills to turn them into a practical application. If vibe coding can get them a step closer and teach them something about the process along the way, I'm all for it.
Those interested in learning more about the vibe-coded driver for Win98 are encouraged to check out Meng's deep dive over on his blog.

articles.title: Galaxy Watch Ultra cai 62% para quem busca relógio para aventuras • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Galaxy Watch Ultra cai 62% para quem busca relógio para aventuras
Galaxy Watch Ultra tem corpo de titânio e monitora diversos esportes; smartwatch da Samsung sai por menos da metade do preço original, no Pix com cupom no Mercado Livre
O Galaxy Watch Ultra LTE de 47 mm está saindo por R$ 1.884 no Pix com cupom OFFSOHJ no Mercado Livre. O smartwatch da Samsung lançado em 2025, que possui corpo de titânio e sensores que suportam diversos esportes, recebe desconto de 62% sobre o preço original de R$ 4.999.
O Galaxy Watch Ultra é um dos melhores smartwatches da Samsung, equipado com o mesmo kit de sensores do novo Ultra 2. Ele oferece suporte a diversas modalidades esportivas, como corrida e ciclismo, e traz funções de qualidade de vida, como eletrocardiograma (ECG), monitores do sono e da oxigenação do sangue.
Seu corpo em titânio de 47 mm resiste a até 10 atmosferas de pressão (10 ATM) e traz certificações IP68 e militar MIL-STD-810H, podendo assim ser usado em esportes aquáticos em águas rasas, enquanto resiste a altas temperaturas.
Graças à conectividade 4G/LTE, este wearable pode salvar a vida do usuário em uma situação de risco. No caso de uma emergência médica, ele pode disparar alertas para contatos pré-programados e ligar para números como 190 (polícia) e 192 (bombeiros), sem depender de um celular.
A tela Super AMOLED de 1,5″ com brilho de até 3.000 nits do Watch Ultra pode reproduzir imagens nítidas com cores vibrantes e oferece visibilidade garantida em qualquer lugar. O vidro Cristal de Safira protege o display contra arranhões, pancadas e quedas.
O gadget traz o chip Exynos W1000, 2 GB de RAM e 64 GB de espaço interno, um kit interno que o permite instalar e rodar apps localmente. Sua bateria de 590 mAh resiste até 100 horas de uso no modo economia de energia, segundo a fabricante, podendo ser usado por um dia inteiro sem descarregar.
O Galaxy Watch Ultra de 47 mm (R$ 1.884 no Pix com cupom OFFSOHJ) suporta redes Wi-Fi 5, Bluetooth 5.3, o já mencionado 4G/LTE e GPS multibanda, que determina a posição do usuário em tempo real, recurso essencial para a prática de esportes e outras aventuras.
Aviso de ética: ao clicar em um link de afiliado, o preço não muda para você e recebemos uma comissão.

articles.title: Exclusive: Plants can speak using electricity, so this startup built an AI model to decipher their language | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Justin Mast’s life was changed by a cyborg plant.
A few years ago, Mast was reading through some scientific literature when he stumbled upon research about a houseplant wired to a motorized stand. When the plant wanted more light, electrical signals flowed through the living tissues. A control board sensed the current and wheeled the plant closer to the light source.
“I’m like, what the heck?” Mast told TechCrunch. “That was the entry to the rabbit hole for me.”
Mast wound up partnering with Lee von Kraus, a neuroscientist who has worked with DARPA, to found Electric Plant, which has been spending the past three years collecting data to build a large language model, Bombadil, capable of interpreting the subtle electrical signals coursing through a plant’s stem and relaying details about the plant’s needs to growers.
The founders believe their model could one day lead to a tool that would let people “speak” to plants. “We’re listening more than we’re speaking, but listening’s the first step,” said Mast, co-founder and CEO of Electric Plant.
To bring its sensors and Bombadil to market, Electric Plant recently raised an $11.2 million seed round led by Onto Ventures and Climactic, with participation from Ponderosa, Endeavor Catalyst, Ludlow, Michigan Rise, The Fund, Schox VC, and Dug Song.
Even in the most controlled greenhouses, farmers and growers don’t have full visibility of what their plants require, Mast said. Traditionally, farmers, growers, and foresters have relied on coarse tools that react to plants’ demands for water, nutrients, or light. And tools like soil probes, handheld spectroscopes, and satellite imagery work well enough, but they leave much to be desired, Mast said.
“That technology is sophisticated, but its ability to get at the inside of the plant isn’t very sophisticated. Most of that stuff still lags quite a bit behind the real-time needs of the plant,” he said.
Electric Plant had to start somewhere, though, so it used those devices to train its Bombadil model, which is capable of interpreting electrical signals in about 125 different species. “We know the model will surpass a lot of that equipment,” Mast said.
The startup’s sensors are also significantly cheaper than existing tools, which generally cost thousands of dollars. “This is tens of dollars,” he said.
The sensors, about the size of a regular iPhone folded lengthwise, are attached to a plant using stainless steel screws. The screws must penetrate the cambium — the layer of living tissue just under the bark — to connect to the microvolt changes occurring within the plant. Data collected from these sensors is sent to a base station via a low-power wireless network.
Electric Plant only needs a couple sensors per acre for accurate results, Mast said. The data gets interpreted by Bombadil in the cloud, and the results are sent back to the customer, who can use it to, for example, adjust their watering or fertilizer schedules. Mast claims such a system can boost yields while reducing water use by 20% or more.
Mast wouldn’t disclose who Electric Plant’s initial customers are, but it’s easy to imagine applications in agriculture and forestry.
Bombadil’s first hundred-plus species runs the gamut of plant forms, from ferns, redwoods, and tomatoes to dahlias, Mast said.
“This is the most diverse model ever created on biological electrical signals,” he said. “No one’s ever done anything equivalent to this in the animal world.”

articles.title: Bell boosts wireless in Toronto with another new wireless site
articles.text:
Bell has upgraded its wireless service in another part of Toronto as part of the company’s ongoing network densification program.
In an email to MobileSyrup, Bell said it completed construction of and put into service a new wireless site that will “help enhance network capacity and performance in the Earlscourt, Carleton Village and Stockyards communities” in Toronto.
Bell says the upgrade will support the connectivity needs of residents, businesses, and visitors in these neighbourhoods.
“As wireless usage continues to increase, Bell is making targeted investments to add capacity and improve network performance in areas where demand is growing.”
The upgrade is part of a larger wireless network expansion and densification program that aims to strengthen Bell’s wireless network across Canada.
Previously, as part of this program, Bell added a new wireless site in Roncesvalles Village in Toronto and shared images of other upgrades in Ontario and Quebec.
The program started in 2024 and, as of May of this year, has seen Bell add 167 new wireless sites in 76 communities across the country, as well as enhance 349 existing sites in 50 communities. Bell says its workers have spent a combined 600,000 labour hours planning and installing upgrades and towers.
We also recently reported on Bell’s effort to bring better service to Orilla, Ont., which included partnering with a local church to use its land for a new wireless tower. Elsewhere, Bell brought fibre internet to remote island communities in Nova Scotia.

articles.title: Oblivion gamer uses Claude AI to boost average FPS gains up to 48%, stutters slashed by 90% — performance mod doesn't change game assets or alter visuals
articles.text:
Oblivion gamer uses Claude AI to boost average FPS gains up to 48%, stutters slashed by 90% — performance mod doesn't change game assets or alter visuals
Yes, this mod is just about 100% vibe-coded.
The revelation that there was a ton of performance lying on the table in the remastered The Elder Scrolls Part IV: Oblivion won't be a surprise to people who have played the game, which is notorious for its hitching and stuttering. The reason primarily lies in its poor utilization of hardware, and that's a big part of what LTSharpe and Claude have addressed in the new Oblivion Remastered Performance Fix that changes nothing about the game's visuals yet increases performance by as much as 68% in the worst case. (h/t to ComputerBase)
Yes, this mod is just about 100% vibe-coded, and yet, rather than hacking Minecraft into GTA V on iPhone, or hacking CoD Black Ops 2 maps into Minecraft, this mod is a binary code modification for Oblivion Remastered that seeks to improve performance and stability considerably, and according to numerous jubilant and thankful posts on NexusMods, it seems to do exactly that, with one user proclaiming that the performance increase was "dramatic" and that the overworld stuttering that plagues the game is "completely gone."
The story goes like this: gamer and mod creator LTSharpe has a slightly older system with a Ryzen 7 5800X CPU. Not the newest chip on the block to be sure, but Zen 3 isn't so old that it should be crumpling under the weight of games just yet. Frustrated with the verifiably awful performance of the remaster of The Elder Scrolls Part IV: Oblivion, he paid for a subscription to Anthropic's Claude AI agent and started working with the assistant to diagnose and fix the performance problems.
"Diagnose" is a critical keyword here, because it isn't like Claude was hallucinating an engine.ini tweak somebody else published for the original game 20 years ago. The partners, with Claude doing the hard work and LTSharpe directing, reverse-engineered the game to the point that they were able to build a repeatable benchmarking framework. That allowed them to systematically diagnose the causes of the performance problems and then test fixes against the real behavior of the game with modified machine code.
That's the thing; this was done without source code. Neither TES4 Oblivion nor the remaster's Unreal Engine is open-source software. The sheer magnitude of the task would be incredibly daunting to a team of human engineers, much less a single person. According to LTSharpe, over the course of two weeks Claude successfully diagnosed and fixed bugs in not only the Remaster's Unreal Engine code, but also in the underlying Gamebryo original engine, in AMD's frame generation code, and even in the Unreal Engine itself, improving performance and avoiding crashes.
The developer—or perhaps we should say, coordinator?—is careful to acknowledge that the performance tweaks were created with his system specifically in mind and that they may not work well for others. Indeed, he has a Radeon graphics card, which puts him within a surprisingly small minority of PC gamers, and some portion of his fixes were aimed at making sure AMD's FSR upscaling and frame generation remain in effect despite a long-standing game bug that disables them when you task-switch (Alt+Tab) out of the game. The good lieutenant invites other gamers to try out the fix and report back, and he's even helping out with support requests on NexusMods, too. Head over there if you're keen to grab the fix and try it for yourself.
Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Zak is a freelance contributor to Tom's Hardware with decades of PC benchmarking experience who has also written for HotHardware and The Tech Report. A modern-day Renaissance man, he may not be an expert on anything, but he knows just a little about nearly everything.

articles.title: Après les violents pillages, pourquoi l’état d’urgence ne permettrait pas de bloquer les réseaux sociaux
articles.text:
Après les pillages du 17 octobre, certains, comme Bruno Retailleau, réclame l’état d’urgence et le gouvernement le garde en réserve. Ce régime d’exception issu d’une loi de 1955 permettrait surtout des mesures individuelles, mais pas de couper librement les réseaux sociaux.
Depuis les pillages qui ont suivi les manifestations du 17 octobre, l'état d'urgence s'est invité dans de nombreuses conversations, des plateaux télé aux fils d'actualité, aussi bien c'est ceux qui réclament son instauration que ceux qui le vilipendent. Le gouvernement de Sébastien Lecornu a préféré miser lundi soir des couvre-feux localisés à Paris, Lyon ou Lille, tout en gardant le régime d'exception sous le coude « si c'est nécessaire ». Entre la loi de 1955, la jurisprudence du Conseil d’État sur TikTok et le règlement européen DSA sur le services numériques, les marges de manœuvre de l’exécutif sont pourtant plus étroites qu’il n’y paraît.
L'état d’urgence, un pouvoir d’exception, pas un chèque en blanc
Cette fameuse loi de 1955, justement, mérite qu'on s'y arrête. Votée le 3 avril 1955, en pleine guerre d'Algérie, elle a donné naissance à un régime d'exception que la Constitution ne mentionne même pas, et qui ne peut être déclenché qu'en cas de péril imminent lié à des atteintes graves à l'ordre public. Le président le décrète en conseil des ministres, pour douze jours maximum. Au-delà, seul le Parlement peut le prolonger par une loi, qui devient caduque quinze jours après une démission du gouvernement ou une dissolution de l'Assemblée. Dimanche soir, dans son allocution, Emmanuel Macron s'est bien gardé de franchir le pas, pour le moment.
Les couvre-feux instaurés lundi soir, eux, s'en passent très bien. À Paris, la place de la République et une partie des Halles étaient concernées de 23 heures à 6 heures. Un hélicoptère rodait d'ailleurs dans le ciel de la Capitale. À Lyon, c'était une partie de la Presqu'île dès 21 heures. Dans le Nord, l'arrêté préfectoral vise les mineurs non accompagnés, même si Denain a étendu la mesure aux adultes. Les préfets et maires disposent déjà de ce levier, à condition qu'il reste limité dans le temps et l'espace. Pour Antoine Fouret, avocat associé au cabinet Nausica Avocats, l'apport de l'état d'urgence se joue ailleurs, à savoir dans les mesures qui visent des personnes précises. Il s'agit de l'assignation à résidence, de l'interdiction de séjour dans un périmètre et, si le décret ou la loi le prévoit, des perquisitions administratives sans feu vert préalable d'un juge. Le changement est bien réel, car en temps normal, le droit commun ne prévoit même pas d'interdiction administrative de manifester visant un individu.
Les sanctions, elles aussi, changent d'échelle. Braver un couvre-feu décrété sous état d'urgence peut coûter jusqu'à six mois de prison et 7 500 euros d'amende, contre une simple contravention en temps normal. Il permet en outre de dissoudre des groupements impliqués dans les violences, et ces dissolutions survivent à la fin du dispositif. Chaque décision reste toutefois contestable devant le juge administratif, souvent en 48 heures. Elle doit reposer sur le comportement de la personne visée, pas sur ses convictions. La France a d'ailleurs été condamnée en 2024 par la Cour européenne des droits de l'homme pour une assignation à résidence prononcée en 2015. « Régime d'exception, l'état d'urgence n'en demeure pas moins un régime de droit », rappelle maître Antoine Fouret. Mais qu'en est-il des réseaux sociaux ?
Le précédent calédonien plane sur le blocage des réseaux sociaux
Couper ou brider les réseaux sociaux est presque un vieux serpent de mer de notre ère moderne, comme la remise en cause du chiffrement des communications d'ailleurs. Sur la radio RTL, Gabriel Attal, candidat Renaissance à la présidentielle, a plaidé pour un blocage « temporaire, ciblé » des réseaux sociaux, limité aux territoires touchés par les émeutes, comme nous le racontions ce matin. Il reproche à ces plateformes de rassembler les casseurs et d'entretenir un effet de meute. L'ancien Premier ministre connaît le sujet, puisque c'est lui qui avait fait couper TikTok en Nouvelle-Calédonie en 2024. Mais l'état d'urgence ne lui offrirait pas ce pouvoir, souligne Antoine Fouret. La loi de 1955 autorise bien le ministre de l'Intérieur à suspendre un site ou un réseau social, mais dans un seul cas : lorsqu'il pousse à commettre des actes terroristes ou en fait l'apologie. Un appel au pillage, aussi choquant soit-il, ne relève pas du terrorisme et n'entre donc a priori pas dans cette case.
Il y a toutefois le cas des circonstances exceptionnelles. Le Conseil d'État l'a balisée en avril 2025, en jugeant le blocage de TikTok décidé en Nouvelle-Calédonie en mai 2024. Une coupure n'est admise que si elle est indispensable face à des événements d'une particulière gravité, sans alternative technique moins intrusive, et pour une durée limitée. Décidée sans échéance, celle de l'archipel a été jugée illégale. La plupart des géants visés relèvent en outre du règlement européen DSA, dont l'application revient à la Commission européenne. Le gouvernement prévoit, lui, une visioconférence avec les plateformes, invitées à modérer les contenus.
Juridiquement, rien n'interdit de dégainer l'état d'urgence face à des violences urbaines. La France l'a fait en 2005, puis en Nouvelle-Calédonie en 2024, mais pas pendant les Gilets jaunes. Encore faut-il démontrer un risque sérieux que les violences se répètent, insiste l'avocat. Bruno Retailleau, lui, réclame « l'état d'urgence maintenant, sans attendre le couvre-feu ».
En attendant, la traque des pilleurs se poursuit surtout devant des écrans. Les enquêteurs épluchent les images de vidéosurveillance, mais aussi les vidéos publiées sur les réseaux sociaux, où certains se sont eux-mêmes filmés en plein pillage, comme nous l'expliquions. L'autre dossier, c'est celui des objets volés ont été remis en vente sur Vinted ou Leboncoin dans les heures qui ont suivi. Le gouvernement a réuni ces plateformes, qui viennent de s'engager à « transmettre régulièrement aux autorités un bilan chiffré des actions de retrait des annonces problématiques, des mesures mises en œuvre, ainsi que des signalements transmis aux autorités, avec un premier retour attendu sous 48 heures », comme l'a déclaré le gouvernement ce mardi 20 octobre.

articles.title: Super Mario 64 : une énigme vieille de 30 ans enfin déchiffrée met fin à une légende urbaine
articles.text:
Parmi les légendes urbaines les plus populaires du jeu vidéo, celle de Super Mario 64 figure en bonne place. Les ingrédients ? Un message indéchiffrable gravé sur une plaque, un L majuscule vaguement lisible et une théorie sur la présence de Luigi dans le jeu. Depuis 30 ans, cette rumeur fait parler d’elle sur Internet. Le 15 octobre 2026, un fan a publié sur Reddit ce qu’il présente comme la lecture la plus probable de l’inscription.
Tout commence dans la cour du château de Peach, où se trouve une statue en forme d’étoile ornée d’une minuscule inscription. Une bouillie de pixels, avec des lettres de 3 à 5 pixels de haut, impossible à déchiffrer, sur laquelle les fans s’écharpent depuis près de trente ans. La théorie la plus célèbre veut que l’inscription indique « L is real 2401 », autrement dit « Luigi est réel », et que le nombre 2401 serait un indice pour le débloquer. Le magazine Nintendo Power l’a reprise dans un poisson d’avril de son numéro d’avril 1998, et elle s’est installée durablement dans la culture Internet.
Cette légende reposait sur un élément réel : Luigi avait bien été envisagé durant le développement de Super Mario 64, avant d’être écarté de la version finale.
Un fan de Mario, connu sous le pseudonyme supermochi64, affirme avoir trouvé une autre interprétation de l’inscription avec l’aide de deux IA, Claude et Grok. Plutôt que de demander à une IA d’agrandir l’image, comme beaucoup l’ont fait sans succès, il a reconstitué la méthode de travail d’un graphiste des années 1990. « Les upscalers IA n’ont pas réussi à résoudre le mystère. Ils inventent simplement de nouvelles lettres à chaque tentative. Alors, avec Claude (Opus 5.5), j’ai essayé quelque chose de différent », explique supermochi64.
« Nous avons reconstitué le texte exactement comme un artiste chargé des textures aurait pu le faire en 1996. Une police, une petite toile, une réduction à 32 × 32 pixels, un léger flou, puis l’application du résultat sur de la pierre. Ensuite, un GPU a testé des millions de polices, de réglages et de phrases jusqu’à trouver une combinaison reproduisant les véritables pixels du jeu. »
Une réponse se démarque nettement des autres : « Eternal Star / We Hope So », soit « Étoile éternelle / Nous l’espérons ».
Le mystère de Super Mario 64 est-il vraiment résolu ?
D’après les résultats publiés par supermochi64, son outil a passé au crible plus de 1,2 million de mots. « Eternal Star / We Hope So » obtient le meilleur score, avec un écart de 1 129 par rapport à la texture du jeu (plus le score est bas, plus les pixels se ressemblent). La fameuse lecture « L is Real 2401 » affiche un écart de 2 031 sur la seule première ligne.
« Étoile éternelle / Nous l’espérons » est une jolie conclusion à un mystère qui traîne depuis près de 30 ans. Mario pourrait bien être cette étoile éternelle, tandis que le « nous l’espérons » serait un message des développeurs de l’époque, loin d’imaginer que le plombier serait toujours aussi populaire en 2026. C’est d’ailleurs la lecture qu’en fait supermochi64 lui-même dans son message publié sur X.
Sous la publication sur Reddit, des internautes pointent toutefois plusieurs limites à ce déchiffrage. Certains internautes rappellent que l’expression « Eternal Star » avait déjà été proposée bien avant cette analyse, tandis que d’autres contestent la lecture de la seconde ligne.
Pour obtenir une réponse définitive, il faudrait idéalement retrouver les documents de développement de l’époque, ou recueillir le témoignage de l’artiste qui a créé cette texture et son message indéchiffrable.

articles.title: Une mission révolutionnaire : mais que va faire le rover français IDEFIX sur la lune de Mars, au juste ?
articles.text:
Le Japon vient de lancer MMX, une mission inédite pour ramener sur Terre des morceaux de Phobos, l’une des deux lunes de Mars. À son bord, le petit rover franco-allemand, IDEFIX, jouera un rôle crucial.
Mars n’est pas seule : notre voisine est accompagnée de deux petites lunes, Phobos et Deimos. Découvertes en 1877 par l’astronome américain Asaph Hall, elles ressemblent à deux gros cailloux difformes, souvent comparés à des pommes de terre.
Phobos, la plus grande, mesure environ 22 kilomètres de large. Et elle se rapproche inexorablement de Mars et finira, dans 50 millions d’années, par s’écraser sur la planète ou se disloquer en anneau. Deimos, elle, atteint 15 kilomètres seulement. Leur origine reste, à ce jour, un mystère : sont-elles les débris d’un impact géant sur Mars, ou des astéroïdes capturés par sa gravité ?
IDEFIX, un éclaireur sur Phobos
C’est justement la question à laquelle va tenter de répondre la mission MMX de la JAXA, l’agence spatiale japonaise. Elle a décollé ce 19 octobre à bord d’une fusée H3, depuis le centre spatial de Tanegashima, dans le sud-ouest de l’archipel.
La sonde va voyager environ dix mois dans l’espace pour rejoindre la planète rouge, où elle doit arriver en août 2027. Elle se placera ensuite autour de Phobos et y restera près de trois ans. C’est à ce moment-là qu’IDEFIX entrera en scène. Ce petit rover a été conçu par l’agence spatiale allemande (DLR) et le CNES. De la taille d’une caisse de boissons, il pèse 25 kilos sur Terre. Mais sur Phobos, où la gravité est infime, il ne fera plus que 15 grammes.
Largué fin 2028 ou début 2029, il tombera de 40 à 100 mètres, rebondira tout doucement, puis se redressera tout seul. Pendant 100 jours, il parcourra le sol pour repérer les deux sites où la sonde pourra se poser. Un éclaireur, en somme.
Comprendre l’origine de Phobos
Une fois que les sites seront choisis par IDEFIX, MMX viendra se poser à deux reprises sur Phobos, sur la face tournée vers Mars, puis sur celle qui y est opposée. Deux outils lui permettront de prélever de la matière : un carottier pour creuser sous la surface, puis un échantillonneur pneumatique, qui va soulever la poussière grâce à un jet de gaz. L’objectif est de récupérer plus de 10 grammes de roche.
La sonde embarque également l’instrument MEGANE de la NASA, un spectromètre à rayons gamma et neutrons qui doit repérer la présence d’éléments légers comme l’hydrogène. Ce point est crucial, et doit nous éclairer sur les origines de Phobos. En effet, ces éléments s’évaporent facilement quand la température monte.
Si la lune est née d’un impact géant, les débris projetés dans l’espace auraient été portés à très haute température, ils auraient donc presque tous disparu. À l’inverse, un astéroïde venu des confins du Système solaire en contiendrait beaucoup plus. Cette mesure devrait donc nous éclairer sur les origines de la lune
Une première mondiale
Le retour de MMX vers la Terre est prévu en novembre 2030, et la capsule doit atterrir en Australie en 2031. Ce sera une première : jamais un échantillon d’une lune martienne n’aura été ramené. Il pourrait même contenir des fragments de Mars, projetés dans l’espace puis tombés sur Phobos. De quoi mieux comprendre l’histoire de la planète rouge et, peut-être, l’origine de son eau.
Une course effrénée : la mission Tianwen-3 de la Chine, prévue pour 2028, doit rapporter des roches directement depuis la surface de Mars en 2031.

articles.title: Spotify : cette nouvelle vérification va faire une hécatombe sur les partages de compte
articles.text:
Le partage de compte et les règles des plateformes de streaming : une histoire qui semble ne jamais finir. Justement, Spotify a décidé de sévir concernant son abonnement Premium Famille, qui permet de partager un compte Premium avec les membres de sa famille qui « vivent sous le même toit ». La plateforme de streaming musical semble estimer que trop de personnes partagent un compte Famille Premium, sans vivre sous le même toit. Elle a donc décidé de mettre en place un nouveau système de vérification.
Un QR code dynamique à scanner
Spotify a décidé de s’attaquer aux personnes qui partagent un abonnement Premium Famille, sans vivre sous le même toit. Comme le rapporte Android Authority, des utilisateurs de Reddit signalent une demande de vérification de la part de la plateforme de streaming musical. Pour être plus précis, ceux qui bénéficient d’un abonnement Premium Famille doivent scanner un QR code avec le propriétaire du compte Premium.
Point important : il s’agit d’un QR code dynamique, autrement dit, il est renouvelé toutes les quelques secondes, ce qui complique sensiblement la réalisation d’une capture d’écran pour ensuite le scanner. De ce fait, ce système de vérification par scan de QR code dynamique permet de vérifier que les deux personnes se situent à proximité l’une de l’autre, et donc vivent bel et bien sous le même toit.
Ceux qui ne scannent pas le QR code seront banni de l’abonnement Famille Premium
D’après la documentation d’assistance de Spotify, les personnes qui reçoivent cette notification de vérification disposent de 7 jours pour scanner le QR code. Ceux qui ne s’y soumettent pas seront bannis automatiquement de l’abonnement Premium Famille en cours, tandis que leur compte basculera sur l’offre gratuite financée par la publicité. Mais cela n’est pas tout puisqu’ils ne pourront plus rejoindre un autre abonnement Premium Famille (ou un abonnement Premium Duo) pendant une période de 12 mois. À noter toutefois que certains utilisateurs parviendraient à contourner ce système de vérification en partageant leur écran pour scanner le QR code.

articles.title: Google suspende una inversión de miles de millones en centros de datos en España a la espera del decreto del Gobierno
articles.text:
En el mapa europeo de centros de datos de Google, el norte, con Finlandia al frente como "la Texas de Europa", está lleno de chinchetas. Sin embargo, el sur de Europa sigue casi en blanco. España parecía la candidata ideal para rellenar ese hueco pero algunos proyectos se están poniendo en pausa ante la incertidumbre regulatoria de un Gobierno que ha anunciado medidas más estrictas en un próximo Real Decreto.
Hasta que se conozcan los detalles de la nueva normativa española, Google ha suspendido su apuesta por un gran campus tecnológico en España, según adelantaba El Mundo.
El nodo Sol en pausa. La incertidumbre regulatoria ha hecho que Google y otras empresas tecnológicas hayan puesto en pausa sus proyectos en España a la espera del contenido del próximo Real Decreto que prepara el Gobierno para regular las condiciones ambientales y de sostenibilidad energéticas de los centros de datos.
De acuerdo a lo publicado por El Mundo, Google habría pausado sus proyectos de ampliación de su capacidad de cómputo en España y su correspondiente inversión de miles de millones de dólares. Google ya contaba con un centro de datos en Madrid con servidores alojados en centros de terceros, pero el proyecto más afectado es el que contemplaba la construcción de la estación para el cable submarino Sol que unirá Santander con Florida en una parcela de casi 6.000 m2 en Cantabria. Amazon, por su parte, tiene comprometidos 33.700 millones en Aragón hasta 2035.
Hambre de capacidad de cómputo. Alphabet ha elevado su previsión de gasto para este año hasta una horquilla de 195.000 a 205.000 millones de dólares. Además, admite que la demanda de IA supera su actual capacidad de cómputo.
Mientras tanto, otros países se postulan como competencia para llevarse esos proyectos que ya estaban sobre la mesa. En septiembre, la compañía anunció la inversión de 13.000 millones de euros en Finlandia, la mayor inversión de su historia en Europa. Allí también se aseguró el suministro de energía incluyendo una central nuclear.
Unas reglas más estrictas con la sostenibilidad. El borrador del Gobierno obliga a los centros de datos a cubrir el 80% de su consumo con nuevas fuentes de energía renovable. Y ese porcentaje debe cumplirse hora a hora, no como media anual. La patronal SpainDC, de la que Google es asociada, avisa de que algunos proyectos serían mucho más caros o inviables.
UN VISTAZO A...
El Ejecutivo quiere evitar que la factura de la luz se dispare. Los números le dan argumentos. La CNMC cifra en unos 12 GW los permisos de acceso ya concedidos. La Estrategia de IA preveía como máximo 4 GW para 2030.
Lobby en Madrid. Google no se ha quedado quieta y, junto a otras tecnológicas ha enviado a sus mejores negociadores a Europa. Tal y como publicaba El Confidencial, Kent Walker, jefe global de asuntos públicos de Google, se reunió el 8 de octubre con el presidente de la CNMC. El regulador asegura que hablaron de competencia y no del decreto.
Poco después se conoció el informe de la CNMC, que pide flexibilizar varias exigencias del borrador del Real Decreto. Con el texto actual, peligra entre el 80% y el 90% de la nueva inversión. Begoña Villacís, directora ejecutiva de Spain DC se muestra contundente con estas nuevas medidas: "Se construirá en otro lugar y será allí desde donde presten los servicios digitales a empresas y ciudadanos españoles".
Gobierno a contrarreloj. El Gobierno quiere aprobar el decreto antes de las elecciones del 29 de noviembre, pero no lo tiene fácil. Hay más de 600 alegaciones sobre la mesa y el texto aún debe superar el examen del Consejo de Estado. Eso deja margen para aplicar cambios.
Según adelantó El País, responsables del Ejecutivo se abrieron a suavizar algunas exigencias incluidas en el borrador del Real Decreto si los centros de datos no contribuyen a encarecen el precio de la luz. Google, de momento, espera con la cartera guardada.

articles.title: Jeder Fünfte ist von zu vielen Chats überfordert – warum eine Antwort auch mal dauern darf
articles.text:
Jeder Fünfte ist von zu vielen Chats überfordert – warum eine schnelle Antwort gar nicht immer sein muss
Familienchat, Freundesgruppe, Sprachnachrichten: Viele Menschen in Deutschland fühlen sich einer Befragung zufolge von der Menge an Nachrichten in Messenger-Apps überfordert. 72 Prozent der Nutzerinnen und Nutzer kennen das Gefühl, 20 Prozent geht es sogar häufig so, wie aus einer repräsentativen Umfrage des Unternehmens Bitkom Research im Auftrag des Digitalverbands Bitkom hervorgeht.
69 Prozent lassen Nachrichten gelegentlich unbeantwortet
Ältere fühlen sich demnach häufiger überfordert als Jüngere. Bei den Nutzern ab 65 Jahren kennen 78 Prozent das Gefühl, 28 Prozent häufig. Bei den 16- bis 29-Jährigen sind es 68 Prozent, häufig überfordert sind 16 Prozent. Für die Erhebung wurden den Angaben zufolge 1.006 Menschen ab 16 Jahren zwischen Juli und August telefonisch befragt, darunter 875 Messenger-Nutzer.
    „Viele setzen sich selbst stärker unter Antwortdruck, als sie es von anderen erwarten.“
Insgesamt nutzen demnach 87 Prozent der Menschen ab 16 Jahren privat zumindest gelegentlich Messenger wie Whatsapp, Signal, Telegram oder Threema. 69 Prozent lassen Nachrichten zumindest gelegentlich länger unbeantwortet, weil es ihnen zu viel wird. Zwölf Prozent machen das öfter. 73 Prozent haben dann zumindest gelegentlich ein schlechtes Gewissen, 75 Prozent entschuldigen sich für späte Antworten.
„Viele setzen sich selbst stärker unter Antwortdruck, als sie es von anderen erwarten“, sagte Bitkom-Experte Sebastian Klöß. 87 Prozent haben zumindest gelegentlich Verständnis, wenn andere nicht sofort antworten. Die Geduld hat aber Grenzen: Für 69 Prozent ist es zumindest gelegentlich ein Grund, einen Kontakt auslaufen zu lassen oder abzubrechen, wenn Freunde sehr lange zum Antworten brauchen. Häufig ist das allerdings nur bei neun Prozent der Fall.
Auch eine Umfrage der IU Internationalen Hochschule hatte im Mai Hinweise auf digitalen Stress gefunden. Dort hatten 56,2 Prozent das Gefühl, ihr Umfeld erwarte zeitnahe Antworten. 44,3 Prozent fühlten sich von der Menge an digitalen Informationen überfordert.

articles.title: Hackers vulneraron OpenCode: hicieron compras de hasta USD 1.700 en cuentas de OpenAI, Anthropic y Google
articles.text:
Un ataque informático contra OpenCode, una herramienta de programación con inteligencia artificial de código abierto, dejó expuestas las claves de acceso de un grupo de usuarios y les generó cargos no autorizados de hasta USD 1.700 en sus cuentas de OpenAI, Anthropic y Google.
La compañía confirmó en la red social X que un atacante entró a un sistema antiguo que estaba en proceso de dar de baja y accedió a las claves que el 1,4% de los usuarios de OpenCode Console, su plataforma paga, habían guardado para conectar modelos de otros proveedores.
Esas claves funcionan como una contraseña digital: permiten que una aplicación use los servicios de IA de una empresa en nombre del usuario y le cobre a su cuenta. Según The Hacker News, la primera exposición posible ocurrió la madrugada del 17 de octubre de 2026.
OpenCode, que compite con herramientas como Claude Code y Cursor entre desarrolladores, notificó por correo a los afectados esa misma mañana y aclaró que quienes no recibieron el aviso no fueron alcanzados por la brecha.
Facturas que llegaron antes que el aviso de OpenCode
Varios desarrolladores se enteraron del problema por sus propias facturas antes del comunicado oficial. En Reddit y en X, usuarios publicaron alertas de gasto y cargos que no habían generado.
Uno de ellos, identificado como Colin Parsons, escribió que le cobraron USD 281 en su cuenta de OpenAI y USD 168 en la de Anthropic. Otro usuario, Preston Zeller, calculó sus pérdidas en USD 1.700, mientras que un tercero reportó más de USD 700 en consumo de OpenAI antes de desconectar su clave.
Anthropic revocó las claves de Claude que consideró comprometidas, OpenAI dijo que trabajó con OpenCode para restablecer el acceso de los usuarios y reembolsar los créditos consumidos durante el ataque y Google, suspendió proyectos que detectó con actividad de uso indebido.
Dax Raad, cofundador de OpenCode, aclaró que la brecha afectó únicamente a Console, el servicio alojado en los servidores de la empresa y no a la aplicación de código abierto que se instala en la computadora del usuario: “esas claves nunca nos llegan a nosotros”, escribió.
La compañía vinculó el episodio con un “ataque de destilación a gran escala”: una técnica que consiste en usar las respuestas de un modelo de IA costoso para entrenar, sin autorización, un modelo propio más barato. Algunos especialistas en seguridad cuestionaron esa explicación y plantearon que podría tratarse de una brecha común cuyo destino final todavía no está probado.
Los propios filtros de seguridad frenaron la respuesta
Raad relató que, mientras su equipo investigaba el ataque, los modelos de IA que usaban para analizar el código malicioso se negaban a procesarlo porque activaba sus propios filtros de seguridad. “Fue bastante frustrante”, escribió en X.
El problema se resolvió cuando OpenCode obtuvo acceso al programa Daybreak Blue de OpenAI, que habilita modelos menos restrictivos para tareas defensivas de ciberseguridad a usuarios verificados.
David Sacks, copresidente del Consejo de Asesores en Ciencia y Tecnología del presidente de Estados Unidos, comentó el caso en X: “OpenCode, como antes Hugging Face, chocó con el mismo muro en medio de un ataque: los modelos de IA más avanzados se negaron a analizar los mismos códigos maliciosos que hacían falta para defenderse porque activaban los filtros de seguridad”.
En julio pasado, la plataforma Hugging Face había enfrentado una situación similar cuando los modelos comerciales de IA se negaron a analizar los registros de una intrusión que, luego reveló OpenAI, habían ejecutado sus propios modelos durante una prueba con medidas de seguridad reducidas.
Raad dijo que los atacantes intentaron ingresar a los sistemas de OpenCode de forma ininterrumpida durante 48 horas, lo que obligó al equipo a mantener agentes de IA defensivos activos todo el tiempo. La compañía aún no reveló cómo lograron el acceso inicial ni la extensión total del robo de datos, y pidió a los usuarios afectados revocar y reemplazar sus claves directamente en cada proveedor.

articles.title: Europe's four largest carriers want to build a Starlink rival, but they don't have satellites
articles.text:
In brief: In another sign of Europe's continuing push away from reliance on US tech, four of the continent's biggest mobile operators are considering joining forces to create a Starlink competitor. The proposed service would connect phones directly to satellites, helping fill coverage gaps while giving European carriers an alternative to Elon Musk's network.
Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Telefónica, and Vodafone have signed a letter of intent to explore a joint bid for Mobile Satellite Services spectrum in Europe. The agreement, announced on Monday, is an early step toward offering direct-to-device connectivity through their existing mobile networks.
The aim is to reach areas where conventional mobile infrastructure falls short. Starlink already offers similar coverage through partnerships with carriers including T-Mobile in the US and O2 in the UK.
There is, however, a fairly significant piece of the plan missing: the satellites. The four operators don't intend to invest directly in a constellation themselves. Instead, they would build ground infrastructure and establish coordination and monitoring operations in Europe, with a satellite partner providing the orbiting hardware. That partner has yet to be selected.
The companies say other mobile operators would also be able to access the service on equal terms. They want the project to improve coverage in underserved areas, protect critical communications, and make public networks more resilient. Existing satellite partnerships would remain in place.
The European Commission has proposed reserving some of the 2 GHz satellite spectrum for European operators.
Earlier this month, SpaceX secured FCC approval for 15,000 Starlink Mobile satellites. A separate waiver allows it to offer satellite wireless services without leasing spectrum from a terrestrial carrier, opening a way to competing directly with established operators. The planned mobile upgrade also goes beyond emergency messages and basic data, with support for native calls, streaming, browsing, and more demanding apps. It means Starlink could become both a useful partner and a serious rival for traditional carriers.
Europe's effort to reduce its dependence on American technology have been gaining pace in recent times. France plans to move government systems from Windows to Linux, alongside a broader shift toward European software and services. Control over essential infrastructure is becoming a recurring theme.
There was also a German state's plans to replace Windows and Microsoft Office with Linux and LibreOffice for 30,000 government employees. More recently, Switzerland launched an $11 million pilot to move 3,000 federal workstations to openDesk, an open-source alternative to Microsoft's productivity tools.
The Netherlands is trying to break from Microsoft with its DAWO project, an independent IT environment built around NixOS that would offer public institutions alternatives to US desktop software, office applications, and cloud services.

articles.title: GPUs avaliadas em R$ 2,5 milhões somem do aeroporto de Guarulhos • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
GPUs avaliadas em R$ 2,5 milhões somem do aeroporto de Guarulhos
Cada placa com RTX 5090, da Nvidia, pode custar R$ 35 mil no mercado brasileiro.
Resumo
- Duas cargas de placas de vídeo GeForce RTX 5090 da marca Zotac, avaliadas em R$ 2,5 milhões, sumiram no Aeroporto de Guarulhos.
- As placas, modelo premium da Nvidia, foram trazidas ao Brasil pelo Grupo Oderço e tinham valor aproximado de R$ 35 mil cada no mercado brasileiro.
- A GRU Airport afirmou que trabalha para solucionar o caso e que o Grupo Oderço foi orientado a pedir indenização, mas ainda não há informações sobre a resolução do caso.
Duas cargas de placas de vídeo GeForce RTX 5090 trazidas ao Brasil sumiram neste final de semana no Aeroporto de Guarulhos (GRU), em São Paulo. O caso foi denunciado pelo perfil oficial do Grupo Oderço, responsável pela importação das GPUs. Segundo o post da distribuidora, os dois pallets perdidos representam um prejuízo de R$ 2,5 milhões, o que deve representar centenas de chips gráficos.
A publicação também aponta que não há registros em vídeo do momento em que os componentes foram abduzidos. A empresa cobra um retorno da gestora GRU Airport, responsável pelas operações no aeroporto internacional de São Paulo. Os modelos que sumiram são da marca Zotac. A versão pode ser encontrada a partir de R$ 35 mil no e-commerce nacional.
Em resposta ao G1, a GRU Airport garantiu que “vem empenhando todos os esforços” para solucionar o caso, e que o sumiço das placas de vídeo já foi “reportado às autoridades competentes”. Segundo a concessionária, o Grupo Oderço já recebeu orientações para pedir indenização pela situação.
Placas de vídeo são carga preciosa
As placas RTX 5090 são artigo de luxo para quem deseja montar um PC gamer ou mesmo um computador capaz de rodar softwares de edição e trabalhos mais pesados, por exemplo. Cada unidade abduzida tem valor aproximado de R$ 35 mil no mercado brasileiro, e a Oderço fala em prejuízo de R$ 2,5 milhões considerando o preço de custo.
Modelos do tipo vêm sofrendo uma valorização no mercado por conta da crise dos chips de memória RAM. Cada Zotac RTX 5090 conta com pelo menos 32 GB de RAM GDDR7, padrão mais atual do mercado. A versão também conta com três ventoinhas para resfriamento do sistema, luzes RGB, entre outras características que vão além do componente padrão da Nvidia.
O que acontece agora?
Segundo a concessionária GRU Airport, o sumiço se deu na última quinta-feira (14/10), quando o Grupo Oderço já foi orientado sobre o procedimento para receber uma indenização pelo sumiço dos pallets.
Em nota, a administradora do aeroporto afirmou ainda que a distribuidora precisa apresentar a documentação solicitada para finalizar o processo. Vale ressaltar que a denúncia da empresa aconteceu no sábado (16/10) cobrando esclarecimentos e a localização da carga. Até o momento, não há informações sobre a resolução do caso.

articles.title: GitHub Actions Runner Controller 0.15.0 Targets Reliability at Scale
articles.text:
GitHub has released Actions Runner Controller (ARC) 0.15.0, introducing reliability, scalability, and observability improvements for organisations running self-hosted GitHub Actions runners on Kubernetes. The October 1 release focuses on reducing unnecessary Kubernetes API requests, improving controller throughput and making upgrades and shutdowns more predictable, particularly for environments managing large numbers of runner scale sets.
ARC is a Kubernetes operator that automatically scales self-hosted runners in response to workflow demand. It allows organisations to run their own execution infrastructure while creating and removing runner instances as jobs arrive and finish. This is particularly useful for enterprises that need control over build environments, network access, compute resources, or workload isolation without maintaining a permanently provisioned pool of runners.
One of the main themes in version 0.15.0 is reducing the work the controller performs to keep runner resources in sync. Controller updates now use Kubernetes patch requests instead of full update requests, reducing the size of API payloads. Runner status aggregation has also moved to metrics for EphemeralRunnerSet and AutoscalingRunnerSet, reducing the number of status updates sent to the Kubernetes API.
The controllers now filter incoming events to avoid unnecessary reconciliation, while listener API client rate limits can be configured through queries-per-second and burst settings. Teams can also configure reconciliation concurrency globally or for individual controllers using max-concurrent-reconciles flags. Together, these changes give platform teams more control over how ARC behaves under load and should help reduce avoidable processing and API traffic in larger deployments.
The release also addresses lifecycle management. Patch-version upgrades now update resources in place, maintaining a one-to-one mapping between autoscaling runner sets and ephemeral runner sets and reducing disruption during upgrades.
Controller shutdown behaviour has also been improved. The terminationGracePeriodSeconds setting is now configurable and aligned with the controller manager's graceful-shutdown timeout, allowing operators to better control how the controller exits during restarts or upgrades.
ARC can also re-register a runner scale set when its recorded counterpart no longer exists in the GitHub Actions service. This helps the controller recover from a mismatch between its local Kubernetes state and the scale-set state maintained by GitHub.
Finally, ephemeral runners can be deleted faster when their runner pods exit successfully because ARC skips an additional server-side check for runner removal. While individually small, these changes address the operational details that become increasingly important when runner environments are created and destroyed continuously.
Moving runner status aggregation into metrics is particularly relevant to teams operating ARC as shared CI infrastructure. Large runner fleets generate frequent lifecycle events as jobs are queued, runners are provisioned, workloads execute, and ephemeral environments are removed. Reducing status patches can ease pressure on the Kubernetes API, while metrics provide a more suitable basis for monitoring aggregate controller and runner behaviour.
Configurable reconciliation concurrency and listener rate limits also help operators tune the balance between throughput and API pressure. However, these settings are not simply performance switches: increasing concurrency can increase the rate at which the controller interacts with Kubernetes and GitHub services. Teams should therefore validate changes against their workload patterns and cluster capacity rather than assuming higher concurrency is always better.
ARC is part of a broader move towards dynamically managed CI execution infrastructure. CircleCI's Machine Runner Orchestrator, for example, focuses on scaling machine-based runners and supports different resource classes, including CPU, GPU, and ARM workloads. ARC instead integrates directly with Kubernetes to manage GitHub Actions runner scale sets, commonly using ephemeral runner environments. The two approaches address the same broad challenge, matching execution capacity to CI demand, but differ in their platform integration and runner execution models
For organisations already standardised on GitHub Actions and Kubernetes, ARC provides a native way to manage runner capacity alongside other cluster resources. Its trade-off is that platform teams must also operate the controller, manage Kubernetes capacity and understand how runner scaling interacts with cluster scheduling, API limits and workflow demand.
ARC 0.15.0 is an incremental release, but its emphasis reflects a significant engineering concern: once CI infrastructure serves many repositories and teams, controller efficiency and lifecycle reliability become delivery concerns in their own right.

articles.title: TikTok staff raised child safety concerns, but executives reportedly failed to act | TechCrunch
articles.text:
TikTok was repeatedly warned by employees about the risks the social media platform posed to children, according to court records obtained by NPR. The documents say employees were frustrated with how executives responded to their concerns about risks to children, including sexual exploitation and exposure to suicide-related content.
Depositions of employees filed in March 2026 are shedding new light on TikTok’s child safety practices.
According to NPR, TikTok employees warned that minors were appearing in sexual content that was available for purchase on TikTok, raising concerns that the company could profit from potentially illegal activity. They also flagged that minors were exploiting loopholes to access age-restricted content and hide their activity from parents.
Additionally, the court documents show that TikTok didn’t conduct surveys to determine the age of its users out of concern that it would have to share the results with the Federal Trade Commission.
“These citations and claims are clearly cherry-picked at the behest of trial lawyers and used to inaccurately rewrite our history and mislead the public about our commitment to youth safety and how our platform works,” a TikTok spokesperson said in an emailed statement to TechCrunch. “It’s unfortunate that NPR has chosen to ignore the numerous documents and resources we have provided that demonstrate how these claims mischaracterize our record and platform features.”
The statement continues, “We have invested billions of dollars in Trust & Safety and rolled out more than 50 preset safety, privacy, and security settings for teens, including Family Pairing, which helps parents and guardians customize the experience for their teens. We remain steadfast in our commitment to the well-being of our community.”
TikTok, in addition to Meta, Google, and Snap, faces hundreds of lawsuits consolidated in federal court. The lawsuits allege that these companies’ platforms harm minors and that they failed to disclose known risks to young users.
TikTok has reached settlements in several of these cases before they went to trial, including one in Los Angeles where a jury found that Meta and YouTube had designed their platforms to be addictive to young users.
Update 10/20/2026 10:00 a.m. PT: The article was updated to include a statement from TikTok.

articles.title: Final Fantasy Resonance is comfort food at its most delicious
articles.text:
Final Fantasy Resonance feels like a long-lost SNES Final Fantasy game in the best way. Smartly, it takes the grand sense of adventure and purposeful structure of those 16-bit era JRPGs and introduces some welcome modernizations. It might not do anything wholly new, but when it’s all so slickly crafted, you can’t help but love it all the same.
The savviest thing Square Enix did with its first proper turn-based FF in years, ironically enough, was to look to none other than mobile gaming. Indeed, Resonance is an extensive remake of Brave Exvius, a now-discontinued FF Android and iOS title. Similar to how last year’s Octopath Traveler 0 adapted Champions of the Continent, Resonance takes Exvius‘ core story and world and dramatically expands it with significantly more narrative material, overhauled gameplay mechanics and other additional content.
What’s more, Resonance is the first-ever HD-2D Final Fantasy, meaning it benefits from the arrestingly beautiful blend of retro-inspired pixel art and sprites with 3D environments and modern rendering effects like dynamic lighting that was introduced with Octopath Traveler. Given that the 2018 JRPG was itself so inspired by Final Fantasy, it’s so wonderfully fitting for Final Fantasy to at long last be given the same treatment. And boy, is it something.
A fondly familiar fantasy
Beyond the aesthetic, Resonance feels like a proper SNES-era FF through and through. For one, the premise is an unabashed throwback to the FFs of old, focusing on a plucky band of warriors, mages, and mechanics who set out on a journey to stop a villainous cohort from destroying the Crystals that serve as the world’s life force. It’s a very basic FF plot, but that’s a feature, not a bug. It allows Resonance to play the hits, paying tribute to everything from legendary composer Nobuo Uematsu’s original iconic melodies to the Rebel Army from FFII, Golbez from FFIV, the Steampunk world of FFVI and, of course, people named Cid.
The narrative itself, meanwhile, is admittedly fairly standard. None of the cast has all that much depth, with main character Rain, in particular, being an archetypal “pure-hearted knight” who doesn’t ever really change. Meanwhile, big twists revealing the secret identities of certain villains can be seen a mile away. But in keeping with the loving homage to FF history, Resonance on the whole has an endearing playfulness and sense of humour that, when paired with exceptional voice acting, keeps it consistently enjoyable. In fact, it reminded me a lot of FFV, a very whimsical and humorous romp that was sandwiched between two decidedly darker SNES numbered entries. This lightheartedness is honestly refreshing, especially after Final Fantasy XVI went for a Game of Thrones-inspired dourness.
Resonance also harkens back to FF‘s roots with its fully turn-based combat system. Not Active Time Battle where metres slowly fill, not some action-menu hybrid like the FFVII Remake series — pure “nothing-happens-until-you-act” battles. It’s glorious, and it’s something that has sorely been missing from FF pretty much this entire millennium. In these four-character skirmishes, you select from your regular attacks, character-specific skills, magic abilities and other commands like you would in the FFs of old. You’ll use these moves to exploit enemy weaknesses and, eventually, fill a Stagger bar to make them significantly more susceptible to damage for a brief period.
But Resonance‘s unique gimmick, which is also lovingly rooted in nostalgia, is the Vision system. As you explore the world of Lapis, you’ll come across caves containing Visions, which are spirits of characters from all 16 FF mainline games, plus some folks who were created for Brave Exvius/Resonance. Each of these encounters are accompanied by short cutscenes featuring music and montages from their original game, which is a sweet bit of fan service. From there, they’ll join you as a sort of equippable gear that imbues your party members with special abilities and attributes.
It’s a brilliant mechanic, allowing you to combine predefined character archetypes with the unique strengths of fan-favourite heroes. On his own, Rain only has Fire-based sword moves, but with FFVII‘s Cloud, he gets powerful Lightning and Water attacks to bolster his offensive prowess. Conversely, Fina the mage is better served as a healer and buffer, so FFXIV‘s Y’shtola provides some welcome boosts on that front. But of course, you can mix-and-match for wilder combinations that play against type but might still help chip away at elemental weaknesses and more quickly Stagger enemies.
Turn orders, which you can see in the top left, are also essential to maximizing effectiveness. Upon Staggering every enemy, you’ll enter a period in which the party can launch a series of attacks that culminates in a special Resonance move of your choice from one of your Visions. These flashy pre-rendered cinematics unleash devastating assaults that can also sometimes have bonus effects like Regen, so it’s always immensely satisfying to successfully execute them after Staggering an enemy to deal extra damage.
Resonance‘s gameplay as a whole is so pleasant outside of combat, too, thanks to how tight it all feels. Dungeons never overstay their welcome due to little navigational gimmicks, multiple save points and the ability to return to the entrance before the boss. Fast travel is available throughout the entire world. You can change the party at any time. Altogether, it’s a splendid line-up improvements from some classic FF games where you could sometimes soft-lock yourself in a particularly tough dungeon.
But perhaps best of all are the sidequests. This collection of short stories actually fleshes out the characters in ways that the main quest often doesn’t, especially once the world opens up via airship. Take Rain’s Knight companion Lasswell, a similarly morally virtuous man and pretty standard “best friend” archetype. One sidequest has him dealing with a Robin Hood-type figure in his past, revealing shades of grey we hadn’t previously seen. Another sidequest, meanwhile, sees Nichol, the stoic strategist of a city of monks, having to grapple with his people’s prosperity has come at the cost of another tribue. In keeping with the FFV comparisons, though, my favourite sidequest chain by far is one I won’t dare say much about but can tease that it involves Gilgamesh, everyone’s lovably goofy multi-armed antihero from that very same 1992 SNES classic.
My only gripe with the otherwise ample quality side content is that some of it can drag. On the whole, Resonance is a fairly easy game on Normal difficulty, but some of these endgame challenges feel exponentially harder and even artificially padded due to enemies’ extremely large health bars coupled with a maddening tendency to heal themselves. (Also: not necessarily a flaw, per se, but the game features a mechanic that lets you see when your next random encounter will occur. It’s novel in concept, but because it always happens after a set period and there’s no way to prevent it, the strategic value here is pretty much non-existent.)
A crystalline comeback
Final Fantasy Resonance is a game that doesn’t reinvent the wheel at all, but that’s absolutely not a bad thing. If anything, it serves as the perfect celebration of Final Fantasy, right on time for the series’ 40th anniversary next year. With its excellent mix of stunning aesthetics, fanciful charm, satisfying combat system that makes classic FF characters an actual part of character progression and numerous quality-of-life features, Resonance is a thoroughly enjoyable ride that rarely lulls.
As I reflect on my time with Resonance, I’m reminded of one of the standout songs from FFV, “Home, Sweet Home.” It’s sweet, tender melody that, as the name suggests, brings to mind many nostalgic memories of childhood — of simpler, more comforting times. That’s Final Fantasy Resonance in a nutshell, and really, what’s more resonant than that?
Final Fantasy Resonance launches on PS5, Xbox Series X/S, Nintendo Switch 2, Nintendo Switch and PC on Oct. 20.
Image credit: Square Enix

articles.title: NordVPN patches "clumsy" Windows bug that let attackers disable system services
articles.text:
NordVPN patches "clumsy" Windows bug that let attackers disable system services
The vulnerability allowed low-privileged local attackers to disable unprotected Windows services, but critical antivirus defenses remained completely safe.
- A vulnerability in NordVPN's Windows app allowed local attackers to stop unprotected system services.
- The flaw, officially tracked as CVE-2026-106030, does not affect NordVPN version 8.12.0.0 or later
- Experts label the bug "clumsy," but the actual impact on users is minimal, requiring a device to already be compromised by malware.
Nord Security has rolled out an important security update for its Windows application to address a vulnerability that could allow a hacker to stop unprotected Windows services.
The flaw allowed a local, low-privileged attacker to act as a trusted process. From there, they could potentially stop unprotected Windows services or change their startup types to manual, leading to a denial of service for those specific applications.
When a top-tier provider, frequently ranked as the best VPN on the market, flags a security patch of this nature, it naturally turns heads. However, cybersecurity experts stress that while the coding error shouldn't have happened, the real-world danger to users is incredibly low.
The issue, officially tracked as CVE-2026-106030, was responsibly reported to CERT Polska by IT Security Expert Marcin Ressel. NordVPN appears to have fixed the vulnerability in version 8.12.0.0, and users are simply advised to ensure their app is fully up to date.
How the vulnerability works
To understand the bug, you have to look at how Windows applications talk to each other using a feature called "named pipes."
According to an intelligence brief published by Mallory, the vulnerability allowed an attacker to connect to a specific NordVPN named pipe and invoke methods to stop services or change their start types without proper authorization.
Mike Williams, Technical Editor at TechRadar, explains the core of the issue: "Named pipes are a common means for Windows processes to communicate with each other. One process might send a message to another asking it to carry out some task."
Because this communication channel is incredibly powerful, it is a frequent target for threat actors. "Because named pipes are so sensitive, hackers often try to abuse them, to run these tasks without permission," Williams notes. "That means it's important to secure them, and make sure that only messages from legitimate processes are accepted. Any good developer knows this: it's a fundamental aspect of using named pipes."
Unfortunately, the NordVPN Windows app, specifically versions earlier than 8.12, fell short of this standard. "NordVPN has failed to do that, which makes this a clumsy bug. It should never have happened," Williams adds.
Why the real-world impact is minimal
While the technical details of the flaw, which carries a CVSS v4 base severity score of 6.8, sound alarming, the practical implications for the average user are far less dramatic.
In a LinkedIn post, the researcher who discovered the flaw, Marcin Ressel, described it as "a local privilege escalation with limited impact" that he found while "playing around with NordVPN for Windows."
Crucially, this exploit can't shut down critical, system-protected security services. Built-in defenses like Windows Defender and processes guarded by Windows Tamper Protection are entirely immune to this specific attack.
"But the impact of the bug is very small," Williams clarifies. "All an attacker can do is change the status of non-critical Windows services. That is, it can't turn off Windows Defender, but maybe it could disable something related to media playback. But even if it did that, it's only flipped a Windows setting, and once you understood the cause, you could just flip it back."
Furthermore, this vulnerability cannot be triggered remotely over the internet. An attacker would already need to have a local foothold on your machine to exploit it. There has also been no active exploitation of this flaw reported in the wild.
"In other words, there's no impact on the VPN itself, and you would have to have malware running on your PC to even cause the issue," Williams concludes. "(And if there's malware running on your device then you've much bigger problems than this.)"
If you are running NordVPN on Windows, your best defense is simple: open the app and confirm you are running version 8.12.0.0 or later.
