articles.title: NCC device verification questions Nigeria's phone imports
articles.text:
Nigeria’s telecom regulator launched a device verification tool that lets buyers check whether a phone is approved for use on local mobile networks. But enforcing compliance across an import-dependent market could test the agency’s technical reach.
With 99% of smartphones imported into Nigeria and an estimated 63 million mobile devices sold annually, the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) faces a market structured around multi-layered supply chains, informal distribution networks, and varied entry routes.
Launched on October 7, 2026, the NCC’s Device Checker requires consumers to dial *315# to verify whether a phone meets Type Approval requirements—the NCC’s mandatory regulation that all communication equipment must meet before connecting to local networks.
The regulator says the tool is part of a broader effort to enforce its Device Management System (DMS) under Section 132(2) of the Nigerian Communications Act 2003.
The checker uses a phone’s International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI), a unique 15-digit identifier, to verify its status against the NCC’s approved equipment records. By linking device records to import declarations, the regulator says it can investigate whether a phone was properly declared to the Nigeria Customs Service and trace the business responsible for importing it.
However, the stakes are substantial in a market that imports an estimated ₦50 billion ($30 million) worth of mobile devices every month. Its near-total reliance on imports creates a complex supply chain that could hamper enforcement.
As a result, a consumer whose phone gets flagged risks navigating an informal multi-tier supply chain with no clear recourse, no standard refund procedure, and no guarantee of compensation.
How device verification works across categories
Consumers can check a mobile device’s status by dialling *315#. Selecting “Check this device” on the menu displays whether the handset is NCC Type Approved and verified for use. Alternatively, buyers can retrieve the 15-digit IMEI code by dialling *#06# and entering it on the NCC’s online portal.
These verification methods enable buyers to detect non-compliant devices before completing a transaction rather than discovering issues after payment.
For personally imported devices, the workflow differs. Individuals bringing phones into the country for use with local SIM cards must contact the NCC via its 315 helpline for guidance on individual verification.
Foreign visitors roaming on international SIM cards do not need to register their devices. Devices connected to a local network before October 7 are automatically allowed. However, new, unverified handsets imported by visitors are subject to a cumulative 30-day grace period per year before registration becomes mandatory.
Commercial entities importing SIM-enabled hardware—including smartphones, tablets, connected laptops, smart meters, and point-of-sale (POS) terminals—must verify compliance with type approval before distribution.
Regulatory responsibility lies upstream: original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), commercial importers, and primary distributors are legally required to obtain Type Approval before offering hardware for sale.
The distinction between consumer verification and enterprise registration is critical: consumers verify network eligibility, whereas supply-chain entities bear the burden of regulatory compliance.
Through the DMS portal, the regulator states it can track SIM-enabled devices back to primary importers, log total import volume, and initiate sanctions against non-compliant entities.
However, backend traceability does not guarantee immediate redress for consumers when an unapproved device is flagged post-purchase.
Enforcement challenges in a fragmented market
Sellers in Abuja’s GSM Village support the regulator’s initiative, yet there are concerns that structural complexities within Nigeria’s device distribution networks could impede implementation. Elsewhere at Banex Plaza in Abuja, TechCabal‘s findings from sellers were not different.
Nigeria records an estimated 63 million mobile device sales annually. Trade data from Volza shows mobile phone imports totalled 4,886 shipments between July 2024 and June 2025, involving 11 international exporters and 12 registered major buyers in Nigeria.
While import metrics do not quantify grey-market volume, the NCC’s enforcement partnership with the Nigeria Customs Service highlights lingering vulnerabilities around grey-market imports and border smuggling.
In 2024, the Nigeria Customs Service reported 3,555 contraband seizures. Although specific device counts were omitted, persistent illicit inflows indicate that unapproved hardware continues to enter retail channels, creating post-purchase compliance risks for consumers.
Regularising upstream accountability
The NCC states that approximately 231 million active devices registered before October 7, 2026, have been automatically onboarded into the DMS database without requiring subscriber intervention. However, the commission did not disclose the number of devices flagged or pending clearance.
Merchants holding inventory imported before that date can regularise their stock by registering their business documentation and uploading batch IMEI records to the NCC enterprise portal. Support is available via the 315 desk.
This transition window aims to protect compliant trade vendors from regulatory penalties on legacy stock.
Traders contend that regulatory enforcement must target primary importers rather than downstream micro-retailers who lack the technical means to evaluate upstream Type Approval status.
Secondary retailers rarely receive customs documentation or Type Approval certificates from distributors. While this does not absolve vendors knowingly trading in illicit goods, it creates operational friction when stock is acquired in good faith.
The NCC’s digital ledger could help trace undeclared devices to sellers and suppliers. But as Ogoh suggests, having “empirical data” is only the first step; turning that evidence into accountability and consumer refunds remains the bigger test.
The commission indicates that these audit trails help regulators distinguish between deliberate contraband trading and inadvertent distribution by secondary vendors.
However, audit trails alone do not determine financial liability or resolve refund disputes once non-compliant hardware has passed through multiple intermediaries to reach end users.
Enforcement and consumer protection
Consumer protection underpins the rationale for the Device Checker. Yet the tool’s impact will depend on whether enforcement mechanisms can penetrate multi-tiered supply chains to guarantee consumer indemnification.
Although the regulator maintains that automated verification prevents erroneous network blocking, dispute resolution remains complex. Nigeria’s Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act 2018 grants rights to repair, replacement, or refund for non-compliant goods, but practical enforcement across informal markets remains difficult.
The Device Checker’s ultimate success hinges on converting technical detection into actionable consumer safeguards. Identifying unverified IMEIs offers little relief to buyers left holding deactivated hardware without a clear, enforced refund path in informal trade hubs.
To scale sustainably, the NCC must strengthen inter-agency coordination with the Nigeria Customs Service to stop unapproved hardware at entry ports rather than at retail points of sale. Without stringent primary-importer enforcement and structured consumer indemnities, digital verification risks transferring systemic supply-chain failures onto consumers.

articles.title: La última sensación viral de la IA es eliminar anuncios y bloatware de las Smart TV: he "tontificado" mi Chromecast y es maravilloso
articles.text:
El domingo por la tarde, como quien no quiere la cosa, veo un tuit curioso de Monos Estocásticos. En él citaban otro tuit de un usuario llamado @gathint con un descubrimiento llamativo. Ese usuario (o usuaria) había "vibecodeado" la TV de sus padres para quitar los anuncios y transformar la interfaz intrusiva de Android TV en una mucho más minimalista similar a la de Apple TV.
Sin anuncios, sin bloatware, y solo con las apps que él necesitaba.
Tontifica tu tele. El tuit se ha convertido en la última sensación viral de la IA. Hace un mes parecía que la sensación era conectar ChatGPT con GPT-6 Astra a Unreal Engine o Blender, y hace una descubrimos el proyecto REA capaz de clonar casi cualquier software, pero ese mensaje de Gathint ha sido todo un fenómeno, porque en apenas unos días ha obtenido 6,4 millones de visualizaciones y ha generado una nueva fiebre de la IA: la de tontificar tu tele.
Dicho y hecho. Tras echar un vistazo al repositorio, decidí probar a hacerlo en mi dongle HDMI, un Onn 4K Plus. El proceso es realmente sencillo en un Mac (y análogo en un PC) si tienes Git instalado:
- Abres una terminal
- git clone https://github.com/Gathin23/cleanyourtv
- cd cleanyourtv
- claude (o el agente de IA de programación que uses)
- Usar como prompt "Revisa el proyecto y guíame paso a paso para hacer esto que dice que se puede hacer en mi TV/Chromecast"
El repositorio de Github de este usuario explica que el proceso es compatible con numerosas televisiones con Android TV y Google TV, aunque antes hay que activar las opciones de depuración USB desde el menú de configuración (es muy sencillo, le puedes decir a Claude "cómo activo las opciones de depuración USB en mi tele"). Con la tele y el portátil en la misma Wi-Fi, lo tienes hecho todo en apenas cinco minutos.
Ya puestos, a dejarlo a mi gusto. El resultado me pareció simpático, pero quería tener al alcance varias aplicaciones en esa primera fila, así que le pedí a Claude que hiciera los iconos más pequeños y que no usase esos grandes textos encima de los iconos en la fila superior. Además hice otro cambio más personal: le pedí que como fondo de la interfaz usase la carpeta de fotos favoritas de mi instalación de Immich, así que ahora cada 10 segundos se muestra una de esas fotos de forma aleatoria. Es curioso: me he dado cuenta de repente de que me quedo esperando a la siguiente foto en lugar de usar cualquier app de las que tengo en protada. Es la excusa perfecta para revisitar esos momentos.
UN VISTAZO A...
Adiós bloatware, adiós anuncios. En su proceso inicial, Gathint usó Claude Code para pedirle que la tele Xiaomi de sus padres dejase de mostrar publicidad antes incluso de entrar en Netflix. Tras darle el modelo y pedirle al agente que hiciese el trabajo, desactivó 25 paquetes de Xiaomi y creó un launcher mucho más limpio.
De experimento a proyecto. Poco después de completar este pequeño proyecto con éxito, Gathin publicó también el prompt y las herramientas que había usado en GitHub. Llamó al repositorio tv-vibehack para acabar rebautizándolo el 19 de octubre como cleanyourtv. Su funcionamiento es relativamente sencillo: aprovecha ADB, el sistema de depuración de Android, para conectarse a la TV (o dongle HDMI) por la red local, detectar los paquetes instalados y desactivar los relacionados con telemetría, publicidad, recomendaciones y aplicaciones preinstaladas que necesitamos.
Puedes volver atrás. Después instala un pequeño launcher inspirado en el de los Apple TV. No necesita acceso de superusuario (root), y además los paquetes se desactivan en lugar de desinstalarse. Eso quiere decir que el proceso se puede revertir: si algo no te convence y quieres volver a la interfaz por defecto de tu Smart TV o dispositivo tipo Chromecast, puedes hacerlo.
Un proyecto contagioso (también para Fire TV). Poco después las redes sociales, sobre todo Twitter (X) se comenzaron a llenar de proyectos que eran una variación del que había publicado Gathint. Entre los más tracción ganaron está dumbtv, creado por Muzzammil Yasin Sabuwala con ayuda de DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Claude Opus 5.5 y Claude Sonnet 5.5. Su filosofía era aún más contundente: que el televisor se limite a mostrar nuestras aplicaciones y las entradas HDMI, sin anuncios ni telemetría.
Forks a gogó, pero antes de probar, revisa. El proyecto funciona mediante ADB en FireTV y Android TV/Google TV, aunque para plataformas más cerradas como Samsung, LG o Roku el acceso puede complicarse. Lo mejor es pedirle al agente de IA que verifique que tu modelo de TV/dispositivo es compatible con el proceso. Hay decenas de proyectos similares en GitHub, algunos de ellos tan llamativos como Free My TV, aunque como siempre conviene pedirle al agente de IA que antes de ejecutar nada o guiarnos revise si el código puede resultar malicioso o tener puertas traseras.
Esto lleva años siedo posible. Cambiar el lanzador de Android TV, usar ADB para deshabilitar paquetes o instalar alternativas como Projectivy Launcher y FLauncher no es ninguna revolución. Lo realmente interesante está en que ahora no necesitamos ser expertos en ADB ni averiguar a qué corresponde el paquete com.google.android.tvlauncher, porque todo ese trabajo lo hace la IA. Es ella la que toca configuracioes y genera scripts que automatizan el proyecto mientras nosotros solo tenemos que pedir cosas con lenguaje natural.
La IA nos devuelve el control de nuestros dispositivos. Es probable que buena parte del éxito de este proyecto y sus variantes resida en el hecho de que durante años los fabricantes de tecnología están quitándonos el control de los dispositivos que compramos. Productos como las Smart TV, los Chromecast o los Fire TV se han convertido de la mañana a la noche en nuevas plataformas publicitarias por sorpresa y sin que pudiéramos protestar. Ahora podemos: basta con decirle a la IA que tontifique esos dispositivos y los convierta justo en lo que nosotros queremos. Y eso es maravilloso.

articles.title: Can a Simple App Really Fix PC Game Stutters?
articles.text:
Shader compilation stutter has plagued PC gaming for years, and a new application called Shader Compilation Stutter Killer, or SCSKiller for short, promises to do something about it. The idea is simple enough: compile shaders before launching a game rather than waiting for them to be compiled during gameplay. But does it actually work?
That's what we set out to find out, testing the application across several notoriously stutter-prone games. Along the way, we also discovered something rather interesting about shader compilation on Radeon GPUs. Something that could be a pretty big deal, and that we hadn't heard about before.
What's SCSKiller?
SCSKiller is a free and open-source application, so if you're interested, we recommend downloading it and giving it a shot for yourself. For those unfamiliar with shader compilation stutter, it's a common issue in modern PC gaming where a game briefly freezes or hitches the first time a new visual effect appears.
Some games attempt to address this by precompiling shaders before gameplay begins. The Last of Us Part I, for example, is famous for its lengthy shader compilation process.
Unfortunately, even games that precompile shaders can still suffer from horrific shader compilation stutter, while others don't bother precompiling much of anything, which can also lead to a poor experience.
Rather than relying on a game to compile shaders, either beforehand or on the fly, SCSKiller attempts to do the work before you launch it. The application scans game files, extracts the necessary shader code, and compiles as many shader pipelines as possible into the GPU driver's cache. The idea is that when you launch the game, those shaders are already compiled, so the driver doesn't have to interrupt gameplay to process new visual effects.
SCSKiller doesn't rely on a whitelist of specific games. Instead, it works at the engine level, with support for games built using Unreal Engine 4 and 5, Unity, RE Engine, and FromSoftware's engines, alongside a more generic approach for other DirectX 12 titles. It also supports DirectX 11 games on Nvidia GPUs.
For games where shader pipelines can't easily be extracted from the game files, SCSKiller includes an optional recorder. This allows you to play for a few minutes with recording enabled, after which the application can use the collected data to compile additional shaders.
It's important to understand that SCSKiller doesn't solve all forms of stuttering, because not every stutter you encounter is related to shader compilation. One of the biggest issues, particularly with Unreal Engine 5 games, has been traversal stutter, and SCSKiller can't address that.
In our opinion, traversal stuttering is generally more disruptive, as it can result in longer pauses when new environmental assets are loaded from local storage. This typically happens as you cross an invisible boundary within the game world, triggering the loading of additional assets. Perhaps we'll get a Shader Traversal Stutter Killer, or STSKiller, in the future. Fingers crossed.
The Drawbacks: Compilation Time, Storage, and Memory
There are some drawbacks to SCSKiller, though they're largely unavoidable consequences of how the application works. For starters, brute-forcing thousands of shader pipelines can take considerable time, depending on how many shaders need compiling and the performance of your CPU.
Of course, the advantage is that you can run the compilation process when you're not actively using your PC. Just be aware that it can pin CPU usage at 100% for extended periods, though with a properly configured system, that shouldn't be an issue.
SCSKiller also consumes additional storage space, and with SSDs at a premium right now, that's something worth considering. Compiling thousands of shaders increases the size of the GPU driver's shader cache. As a result, you may need to increase the cache size to prevent older compiled shaders from being removed.
Nvidia users can adjust this through the driver settings. The standard limit is typically 10 GB, but you can increase it to 100 GB or even set it to unlimited, preventing older shaders from being deleted as new ones are added.
Unfortunately, things are more restrictive for Radeon users. According to SCSKiller, AMD's driver has a fixed shader cache limit of 16 GB. We haven't independently confirmed that limit with AMD, but if accurate, it means Radeon owners can't simply increase the cache size. Once the cache reaches its limit, older entries are removed to make room for new ones. SCSKiller will then identify previously optimized games as needing to be compiled again.
This potentially limits the usefulness of SCSKiller on Radeon GPUs, particularly if you're trying to optimize a large library of games. That said, there's no need to panic. As we discovered during testing, AMD has some pretty interesting shader compilation behavior of its own, and we'll explore that shortly.
Test System and Methodology
For all of this initial testing, we used our Ryzen 7 9800X3D test system with 32 GB of RAM, initially paired with the GeForce RTX 5090. Later, we also tested the Radeon RX 9070 XT and GeForce RTX 5070 to investigate some interesting differences in shader compilation behavior.
We may explore additional hardware configurations in the future, particularly slower CPUs. For now, though, the goal was simply to determine whether SCSKiller actually works. As it turns out, we were able to demonstrate that quite clearly using the 9800X3D. So, let's get into the results.
Test System Specs
| CPU | AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D | 
| Motherboard | MSI MPG X870E Carbon WiFi [BIOS 7E49v1AA7] | 
| Memory | G.Skill Trident Z5 RGB DDR5-6000 32GB CL30 [CL30-38-38-96] | 
| Graphics Card | GeForce RTX 5090, GeForce RTX 5070, Radeon RX 9070 XT | 
| ATX Case | MSI Prospect 700R | 
| Power Supply | Kolink Regulator Gold ATX 3.0 1200W | 
| Storage | TeamGroup T-Force Cardea A440 M.2 PCIe Gen4 NVMe SSD 4TB | 
| Operating System | Windows 11 25H2 | 
| Display Driver | AMD Radeon Adrenalin 26.9.2 Nvidia GeForce Game Ready Driver 617.42 | 
Gaming Benchmarks
Star Wars Jedi: Survivor
We'll start with Star Wars Jedi: Survivor, a game famous for its numerous stuttering issues. Jedi: Survivor precompiles shaders when loading for the first time. For this initial test, both configurations were running the game for the first time immediately after completing that initial shader compilation process.
There are quite a few interesting things to note here. First, performance was substantially better with SCSKiller enabled, boosting the average frame rate by 25%, with a similar improvement to the 1% lows. However, you might have also noticed that the standard configuration was consuming around 60% more GPU power, at least at the beginning of the test. That difference gradually decreased to just under 40% by the end of our run.
Despite the game precompiling shaders when initially loading, there appears to be considerable additional shader compilation work taking place during gameplay, particularly in the early stages. This can reduce frame rates and increase the processing overhead associated with rendering new effects.
Something else worth noting is that SCSKiller increased system memory usage. We're looking at around 7% more RAM consumption in this example, apparently due to the additional precompiled shader data being buffered into system memory.
For our second Jedi: Survivor test, we loaded an earlier section of the game immediately after completing the first run. By this point, the game had already been running for quite some time. In terms of performance, the SCSKiller configuration was around 14% faster, though neither configuration suffered from what we'd consider shader compilation stutter.
Interestingly, SCSKiller was now consuming around 30% more system memory, representing almost 7 GB of additional RAM usage. That wasn't a problem for our 32 GB configuration, but it's certainly something to consider if you have less than 32 GB of system memory.
GPU power consumption also increased with SCSKiller this time, which makes sense given that we were rendering more frames. It also suggests the RTX 5090 was spending less time dealing with shader compilation work during gameplay. Although SCSKiller wasn't solving any noticeable shader compilation stutter in this particular example, since the standard configuration wasn't stuttering to begin with, it still managed to improve performance substantially.
It's possible that slower hardware would have exhibited more obvious stuttering with the standard configuration, but that's something we'll need to explore in future testing. It's also worth noting that despite consuming more system memory, SCSKiller didn't always improve frame rates. In another section of the game, performance was much the same between the two configurations. And as we mentioned earlier, SCSKiller can't fix traversal stutter, which remained clearly visible at several points throughout our testing.
Grounded 2
Another game reportedly affected by shader compilation stutter is Grounded 2, so we decided to take a look. However, with the hardware configuration we were testing, we didn't encounter any significant stuttering issues, at least in the sections of the game we examined.
Despite SCSKiller increasing system memory usage by around 5 to 6 GB, there were no measurable performance improvements. In this case, the application simply didn't provide any meaningful benefit.
Hogwarts Legacy
Another game we were particularly keen to investigate was Hogwarts Legacy, especially since the developer of SCSKiller specifically highlights performance improvements in this title. Unfortunately, we couldn't reproduce those improvements in our testing. Initially, we tested using the Ultra quality preset at 4K with Performance upscaling and ray tracing enabled.
Performance remained pretty poor even after running SCSKiller, particularly the 1% lows, and we couldn't identify any meaningful improvements to frame times. What we did see, however, was a substantial increase in system memory usage of over 20%, effectively maxing out our 32 GB capacity.
Concerned that the additional memory consumption might be preventing SCSKiller from delivering an improvement, we decided to retest with ray tracing disabled, which reduced overall memory usage. Unfortunately, that didn't change much. Performance was virtually identical between the two configurations. If anything, the standard configuration was slightly faster, while SCSKiller was now consuming over 50% more system memory without providing any measurable advantage.
Frame pacing was also largely unchanged. In a final attempt to reduce system memory usage, we dropped to the Medium quality preset, again with ray tracing disabled. But once again, frame rates and frame pacing were essentially identical between the two configurations. This time, SCSKiller increased system memory usage by around 25%, still without delivering any meaningful improvement.
So, what's going on here?
It's possible that our hardware configuration was influencing the results, though the SCSKiller developer also reported improvements using an RTX 5090. Alternatively, it could simply be that the section of the game we tested wasn't particularly affected by shader compilation stutter. Either way, we weren't able to reproduce the improvements claimed by the developer, despite testing several graphics configurations.
The Blood of Dawnwalker
The Blood of Dawnwalker is another game we've heard suffers from shader compilation stutter, though in our testing, the issue didn't seem particularly problematic. That said, SCSKiller did manage to deliver a reasonable performance improvement, presumably by making additional compiled shader data available in system memory.
By the end of our test, the 1% lows had improved by 15%, accompanied by a 6% increase in the average frame rate. That's a pretty decent improvement considering the application is free, assuming you have enough storage space and system memory available.
In this example, system memory usage increased by 33%, with SCSKiller consuming approximately 5 GB of additional RAM.
Silent Hill: Townfall
Another relatively new game we decided to examine was Silent Hill: Townfall. Unfortunately, performance was much the same between the two configurations, and SCSKiller wasn't able to eliminate the stuttering we encountered.
In fact, we observed more stuttering with SCSKiller enabled, though it's important to note that this was based on a single pass through the game. That's one limitation of this type of side-by-side testing, as stuttering behavior can vary between runs, so we wouldn't read too much into that particular result. Still, there was no evidence of a meaningful improvement in the section we tested.
Tiny Tina's Wonderlands: A Dramatic Improvement
Now, here's a game we know stutters like absolute buggery. Tiny Tina's Wonderlands is an Unreal Engine 4 title with so much shader compilation stutter that it's almost unplayable at times. And keep in mind, we're testing with a Ryzen 7 9800X3D and GeForce RTX 5090 here. The average frame rate looks pretty impressive, but the 1% lows tell a very different story. They're absolutely horrid.
The game does precompile shaders before you start playing, and while things improve as you spend more time in the same area, moving somewhere new often means it's Stutter City all over again. For example, we left our initial test area for a few minutes before returning. Despite having already explored that section of the game, it didn't take long for the shader compilation stutters to return.
Admittedly, they weren't quite as severe as before, but they remained pretty annoying, especially considering the hardware we were using. This is where SCSKiller really comes into its own. It transformed Tiny Tina's Wonderlands from a stuttery mess into an exceptionally smooth experience, eliminating the constant hitching we had been experiencing.
By the end of our test, the 1% lows had improved from just 45 fps to an incredible 147 fps. More importantly, the constant stuttering and hitching were completely gone in the section we tested. This was one of the most impressive results we'd seen so far, demonstrating SCSKiller can be effective when shader compilation is responsible for poor performance.
However, what happened next was arguably even more interesting.
AMD's Background Shader Compilation: An Unexpected Discovery
Having seen how dramatically SCSKiller improved performance on the RTX 5090 in Tiny Tina's Wonderlands, we decided to swap out the GeForce GPU for a Radeon RX 9070 XT. And we're glad we did, because the results were rather puzzling, but in a good way. What we observed was the first few seconds of gameplay after freshly installing the RX 9070 XT along with AMD's latest display driver. SCSKiller hadn't been used at all.
We simply allowed the game to perform its usual shader precompilation process before loading our save file. Yet, despite everything we'd just seen with the RTX 5090, the game ran perfectly smoothly. There was no noticeable stuttering whatsoever. We couldn't quite believe what we were seeing, especially after spending so much time testing the GeForce GPU, where the experience had been a complete mess.
We continued playing, exploring several new areas, but at no point did the game exhibit the same stuttering problems. This left us looking for answers. That's when we came across an extremely brief article on AMD's website titled AMD Software: Adrenalin Edition 26.9.2 Background Shader Compilation. This was the exact driver we were using for our testing. The article explains that AMD has expanded its DirectX 12 background shader processing support to Unreal Engine 5 games.
According to AMD, the functionality was already enabled for Unreal Engine 4 titles, along with several specifically named games, including Borderlands 3, Dirt 5, Cyberpunk 2077, Guardians of the Galaxy, Halo Infinite, and Tiny Tina's Wonderlands. AMD also notes that background shader compilation can reduce initial game loading times, though performance may be temporarily reduced while compilation is taking place. Because shader compilation is CPU-intensive, the time required to complete the process depends on the processor and overall system load.
For benchmarking purposes, AMD recommends allowing approximately 15 minutes of gameplay for background compilation to finish before recording performance measurements. The company also recommends excluding the first run of each new session when using an in-game benchmark. Based on that explanation, AMD appears to be saying that background shader compilation has already been supported in Unreal Engine 4 titles for some time, with Unreal Engine 5 support arriving more recently.
So the bigger news for Radeon owners is that AMD has been working on background shader compilation at the driver level, and its latest update expands that functionality to Unreal Engine 5 games. This was news to us. Admittedly, shader compilation performance isn't something we've investigated in detail for quite some time. There didn't appear to be much progress on the issue, so it had become one of those unfortunate realities of PC gaming that we'd more or less accepted.
But based on what we're seeing in Tiny Tina's Wonderlands, AMD appears to have effectively solved shader compilation stutter in this particular game. And what's particularly impressive is how quickly it happens. After a brief shader preparation process, we could simply load into the game and start playing without encountering any noticeable stutters. Meanwhile, the same game remained a complete mess on our GeForce GPUs without SCSKiller.
Tiny Tina's Wonderlands: Radeon vs. GeForce
Despite Tiny Tina's Wonderlands already running perfectly smoothly on the RX 9070 XT, we still wanted to see what would happen if we used SCSKiller. This was also when we discovered the apparent 16 GB shader cache limitation on Radeon GPUs. After precompiling the game's shaders using SCSKiller, we ran the test again and found virtually identical performance. SCSKiller increased system memory usage by approximately 2 GB, but this had no measurable effect on frame rates or frame pacing. In other words, AMD's standard driver configuration was already doing everything we needed.
For a better representation of image quality comparisons, check out the HUB video below:
For comparison, we also tested the GeForce RTX 5070 under identical conditions, both with the standard driver configuration and after using SCSKiller. As expected, the RTX 5070 suffered from severe shader compilation stutter when running the game normally. However, after using SCSKiller, those issues were completely eliminated in our test. The application also increased VRAM usage by around 4 GB, bringing it roughly in line with what we observed on the Radeon RX 9070 XT.
Comparing the two GPUs with their standard driver configurations reveals how significant AMD's advantage was in this particular game. Although average frame rates were similar, the 1% and 0.1% lows were substantially better on the Radeon GPU, with AMD's background shader compilation apparently doing an excellent job of preventing the constant interruptions we encountered on GeForce.
For a better representation of image quality comparisons, check out the HUB video below:
Now, compare the standard RX 9070 XT configuration against the RTX 5070 after using SCSKiller. Both GPUs delivered exceptionally smooth performance at roughly the same frame rates, with the GeForce GPU actually coming out ever so slightly ahead. That's a good result for SCSKiller, but it's also a demonstration of what AMD's driver is already doing.
What makes this particularly interesting is the amount of preparation required. For the RX 9070 XT, we literally installed the driver, restarted the system, loaded into Windows, and immediately launched Tiny Tina's Wonderlands. After the game's brief initial shader preparation process, we were playing without any issues.
For the RTX 5070 to deliver the same kind of smooth performance, we first had to install SCSKiller and then spend around 30 minutes precompiling shaders. Only after completing that process were we able to achieve the results shown here. So, at least in Tiny Tina's Wonderlands, AMD's driver implementation appears considerably more efficient at preparing shaders and avoiding compilation stutter. Very impressive stuff.
Final Fantasy VII Rebirth: Another Stutter-Filled Experience
Finally, we wanted to compare the RTX 5070 and RX 9070 XT in Final Fantasy VII Rebirth, another game we've heard suffers from severe shader compilation stutter. And unfortunately, those reports appear to be accurate. Starting with the RX 9070 XT, we compared the standard driver configuration against SCSKiller. Neither configuration was flawless.
It's worth noting that Final Fantasy VII Rebirth has a hard 120 fps frame rate cap, which is a little annoying for this type of testing. However, we're primarily interested in the 1% and 0.1% lows anyway, so the cap isn't a major concern. With the standard Radeon driver configuration, 1% lows remained above 60 fps, but there were still noticeable stutters, reflected in the 0.1% low results. SCSKiller certainly helped, though it wasn't able to eliminate every stuttering issue in this particular title.
While the RX 9070 XT wasn't perfect, its performance was considerably better than what we observed with the RTX 5070. In fact, the situation was remarkably similar to Tiny Tina's Wonderlands. With the standard GeForce driver configuration, Final Fantasy VII Rebirth was a stuttery mess. Whereas the Radeon GPU managed to keep its 1% lows above 60 fps, the RTX 5070 suffered from severe performance drops, with its 1% lows falling into single digits. Average frame rates were very similar between the two GPUs, but the 1% and 0.1% lows on the GeForce GPU were terrible.
Then we enabled SCSKiller. After precompiling shaders, the RTX 5070's performance problems were essentially eliminated. The jarring stutters disappeared, 1% lows remained well above 60 fps throughout our testing, and even the 0.1% lows were very good. Frame pacing was excellent, resulting in a completely transformed gaming experience.
We initially captured several minutes of gameplay, but continued playing beyond that and didn't encounter any further issues in the areas we explored. Comparing the RX 9070 XT and RTX 5070 with SCSKiller enabled on both GPUs produced very similar results. Interestingly, SCSKiller consumed more system memory with the RTX 5070 than with the RX 9070 XT. It's possible that this relates to the Radeon driver's more restrictive on-disk shader cache capacity.
Overall, SCSKiller helped improve performance on both GPUs, though the most dramatic improvement was clearly seen on the GeForce side.
Conclusion: Does SCSKiller Actually Work?
SCSKiller certainly took us down a rabbit hole we weren't expecting. At some point, we might conduct a more extensive investigation comparing Radeon and GeForce GPUs across a broader range of hardware configurations and games. For now, though, we can conclude that SCSKiller is genuinely useful and it can improve performance in games affected by shader compilation stutter.
That doesn't mean it's a universal solution. It doesn't address traversal stutter, and even in games where shader compilation is an issue, the benefits can vary significantly depending on the hardware and the sections being tested. In some titles, such as Hogwarts Legacy, we couldn't reproduce the developer's claimed improvements at all. In others, such as Star Wars Jedi: Survivor and The Blood of Dawnwalker, we observed respectable performance gains, even when the standard configuration wasn't exhibiting particularly severe stuttering.
Then there are games like Tiny Tina's Wonderlands and Final Fantasy VII Rebirth, where SCSKiller completely transformed the experience on our GeForce GPUs.
Of course, there are some practical considerations. Compiling shaders can take considerable time, particularly when dealing with thousands of pipelines. You may also need to repeat the process after driver or game updates, and the resulting shader cache can consume a substantial amount of local storage. SCSKiller can also increase system memory consumption considerably, which may or may not be a problem depending on your PC's configuration.
But the good news is that the application itself is free, and there's little downside to trying it in a game you're already having trouble with, provided you're mindful of storage requirements and anti-cheat compatibility. It's straightforward to download and use, and based on our results, certainly worth experimenting with if you're experiencing shader-related stutters.
The Radeon results, however, are a different story, and potentially the more interesting discovery to come out of this testing. Initially, the inability to increase AMD's on-disk shader cache size seemed like a bit of a Radeon fail. And while we'd still like to see AMD provide more control over that limit, if the company continues improving background shader compilation, perhaps it won't be such a significant limitation after all.
We actually spoke with AMD about this, and the company said that while it appreciates third-party applications such as SCSKiller, it also considers itself an industry leader in supporting DirectX 12 Advanced Shader Delivery, which aims to address the same underlying problems through an officially supported approach.
Advanced Shader Delivery is a separate technology developed by Microsoft for Windows 11 and DirectX 12. It allows supported games to download precompiled shaders, reducing the need for compilation on the player's PC and helping prevent stuttering. AMD has been an early supporter of this technology, though its benefits depend on game and platform support.
In any case, there's clearly more testing to be done. We're particularly interested in seeing how AMD's background shader compilation performs across more games, different CPU configurations, and older Radeon hardware. Likewise, SCSKiller deserves a closer look with slower processors, where shader compilation stutter may be even more disruptive. For now, though, we've learned two things: SCSKiller really can work, and AMD's shader compilation improvements might be a bigger deal than we initially realized.

articles.title: AI Platform Cairn Abused to Hack Over 100 Organizations
articles.text:
Threat actors have been abusing open source AI platform Cairn to automate malicious operations against hundreds of websites worldwide, AI security firm Norforge reports.
Cairn is a general-purpose problem-solving engine that can coordinate AI agents towards a set goal and can be used as an autonomous penetration testing engine.
Each task in Cairn is considered a project, with an origin and a predefined goal, and agents work step by step from origin to goal, posting their intents and findings to a shared blackboard.
Following a recent Gambit Security report on hackers using three AI harnesses to automate attacks against hundreds of online retailers, Norforge decided to investigate further and discovered that some threat actors left their panels open.
On Cairn, the cybersecurity firm identified three clusters of activity that appear to be malicious, focused on persistent access and financial theft.
The largest of the clusters uses Chinese language and comprises over 1,100 attack projects across 14 dashboards. It has targeted e-commerce/payment infrastructure in the US, Japan, and Australia.
According to Norforge, the threat actor’s goal appears to be persistent access to large platforms via webshells, likely to be monetized later. Automated validation was also included, and targets were ranked by traffic and tested using Microsoft’s browser automation framework Playwright before being fed to Cairn.
While Norforge has not named any of the victims, Reuters reports that this threat actor breached over 100 companies, including US-based equipment maker John Deere and home appliance firm SharkNinja.
The second cluster of activity exposed 10 panels. The group uses English and focuses on credit card and cryptocurrency theft, mainly from merchant payment services, gray-market payment sites, and pharmaceutical platforms.
Some of the cluster’s targets are African commerce sites, and Norforge believes the threat actor has a base on that continent.
The third cluster exposed a panel with 59 projects targeting all types of e-commerce sites, including very large US-based commercial platforms. The group is focused on shell access, as well as admin panel and database access.
According to the cybersecurity firm, the threat actors were successful in roughly 10% of their attempts. Hundreds of secrets were found in the exposed panel data, 11% of which were verified as valid.

articles.title: Electronics hobbyist converts $120 DDR5 SODIMM kit into ‘$1000’ desktop kit to fight RAM crisis — ICs from SK hynix DDR5-5600 16GB modules used to create DDR5-7800 desktop sticks
articles.text:
Electronics hobbyist converts $120 DDR5 SODIMM kit into ‘$1000’ desktop kit to fight RAM crisis — ICs from SK hynix DDR5-5600 16GB modules used to create DDR5-7800 desktop sticks
You have to be lucky to find such cheap DDR5 SODIMMs, and specialist equipment and skills are required for success.
What if you could buy a cheap used DDR5 SODIMM (laptop memory) kit and transform it into a super-fast DDR5 desktop kit? That’s what electronics hobbyist Blighted Agent recently did when they succeeded in converting a SK hynix 2x 16GB DDR5-5600 SODIMM kit they got from Facebook Marketplace for $120 into a 2x 16GB DDR5-7800 desktop kit, claimed to be worth around $1,000. They also had to buy some blank DDR5 desktop memory PCBs from AliExpress for around $16 each, and a set of heatsinks for around $18.
In the above video, our hero says they bought the donor laptop 2x 16GB DDR5-5600 sticks for just $120, which is a bargain. With extra bits and pieces from AliExpress (desktop DDR5 PCBs, etc.), the total bill of materials came to $175. Blighted Agent comments that the SODIMMs used what he believed to be SK hynix A-die modules, which are the same as the ICs used in expensive desktop DDR5 modules like the G.Skill Trident Royal line.
The process began with taking the memory ICs from the donor modules using a hot air station. Then they were cleaned and had 0.45mm leaded solder balls added, using a DDR5 stencil, reballing jig, and hot air. Next, the blank desktop DDR5 PCBs were prepared. A little solder was added to the plethora of BGA connectors to be ready for the memory chips to connect to.
The old DDR5 ICs and the new desktop modules could now be mated, using flux, the preheater, hot air, and watching and prodding carefully with a dental pick. Blighted Agent’s experience lets him know when the BGA chips have successfully mated with the PCB. You can eyeball when they pop precisely into place due to surface tension, and offer up a modicum of resistance to pick prodding.
Finally, the enthusiast added the SPD chip and BIOS chip from the SODIMMs to the new desktop DIMMs. These new desktop DIMMs were quickly tested in a PC before they were finished off with carefully applied thermal pads and the fancy-looking heatsinks.
Blighted Agent felt lucky that there were no issues with the newly created desktop modules. There’s a lot of intricate things that can go wrong during such a process. The initial boot verification showed them recognized in his Asus ROG Maximus Z790 Apex Encore motherboard as two “SK hynix 16,384MB 5600MHz” modules, which was correct. Some tuning resulted in rock-steady performance at DDR5-7800 CL38 and 1.40V. This was verified by stress testing for 90 minutes, which the enthusiast reckons was ample for a gaming PC. It is very likely a better result than using those mechanical SODIMM-to-DIMM converters you can buy, which can be problematic.
Blighted Agent seems to specialize in BGA soldering work, and has also successfully upgraded several graphics cards with double the VRAM. Though videos like this are edited to be brief, and they make the process look easy, the TechTuber admits there is a lot that can go wrong during this kind of rework. Moreover, with RAM modules, they lack the testing equipment to locate an issue with any particular IC on the PCB. So, if this module didn’t work, they might have ended up in a world of pain, not knowing which memory chip had an issue due to either an internal fault or a BGA soldering glitch.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Looking around at used DDR5 SODIMMs, it looks like Blighted Agent was very lucky to get a used working 32GB kit for $120. I just checked eBay U.S., and the best deal there was $320. Meanwhile, the best price for a new 32GB DDR5-6000 kit seems to be $449 at the time of writing.
We reported on Russian enthusiast VIK-on succeeding in a similar project earlier this year, but all their costing was in Rubles, and they went the extra mile in flashing custom firmware so the remade modules would be auto-detected with 6400 MT/s XMP support on most motherboards. In late 2026, DDR5 RAM continues to be too expensive.
Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
Mark Tyson is a news editor at Tom's Hardware. He enjoys covering the full breadth of PC tech; from business and semiconductor design to products approaching the edge of reason.

articles.title: Infomaniak met à jour son client kDrive sur Windows
articles.text:
Infomaniak a mis à jour l'application de bureau de kDrive sur Windows. Au programme, une interface redessinée, censée préparer des changements techniques plus importants.
La fenêtre de kDrive propose trois entrées, accueil, activité et stockage. Des raccourcis mènent aussi aux favoris, aux partages, à la corbeille et à la version web.
Des composants natifs, une synchronisation à la demande
Infomaniak avait présenté en juillet une nouvelle application, re-développée avec des composants natifs. Concrètement, elle utilise les éléments d'affichage fournis par Windows. Selon l'éditeur, le rendu est plus net sur les écrans haute définition. Les notifications sont plus discrètes et la gestion des conflits plus claire lorsqu'un même fichier est modifié à deux endroits avant d'être synchronisé
En bêta depuis des années, Lite Sync est de la partie. Rappelons qu'il s'agit de placeholders. Les fichiers apparaissent donc dans l'Explorateur de Windows mais ne se téléchargent qu'à l'ouverture, histoire de ménager l'espace disque. Selon le guide d'assistance de la version 4, la fenêtre se redimensionne librement et un même identifiant peut relier plusieurs kDrive. Un réglage permet aussi d'envoyer à la corbeille de Windows les fichiers supprimés depuis le web ou le mobile. Après cette version pour Windows, macOS, et Linux auront également le droit à une mise à jour.
Nous rapportions que kDrive revendiquait plus d'un million d'utilisateurs. L'éditeur a aussi relevé la taille maximale d'un fichier, de 50 Go à 1 To. L'import depuis Google Drive doit arriver d'ici la fin de l'année, une fonctionnalité que proton vient d'ailleurs tout juste d'annoncer pour son propre Drive. Dropbox, OneDrive, Nextcloud et WebDAV sont déjà pris en charge.
Côté kSuite, Infomaniak a détaillé en juillet une trentaine de nouveautés. L'assistant IA de la messagerie s'appuie sur un nouveau modèle présenté comme souverain, pour rédiger, résumer ou traduire un échange. L'import de fichiers MBox permet de rapatrier des boîtes de 50 Go. SwissTransfer accepte un logo et un nom de domaine personnalisés. Les applications de kSuite Pro proposent des serveurs MCP, lesquels permettent à un agent d'IA de se connecter aux données d'un service. L'offre gratuite my kSuite reste à 15 Go pour kDrive et 20 Go pour la messagerie.
- mood15 Go d'espace gratuit
- uploadPas de limite d'envoi
- home_pinServeurs en Suisse
Infomaniak kDrive regroupe le stockage cloud, la synchronisation, le partage et l’édition collaborative dans un service accessible sur ordinateur, mobile et navigateur. Il convient aussi bien à un utilisateur individuel qu’à une équipe qui échange régulièrement des documents. La répartition des fonctions entre de nombreuses offres demande cependant de vérifier précisément la formule choisie. Le service ne doit pas non plus être confondu avec une sauvegarde indépendante, malgré son historique de versions et sa corbeille.

articles.title: Germany’s NEURA Robotics shows no signs of slowing down as it teams up with Austria’s NXAI for physical AI | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Following last week’s announcement that Germany’s NEURA Robotics would be launching its multimodal foundation for physical AI, today the company confirmed that it would be working with Austria’s NXAI on a building block for the memory of cognitive robots.
To this end, the partners are combining NEURA’s Physical AI stack with xLSTM, a recurrent architecture from NXAI that can efficiently maintain and update state over long sequences. Furthermore, NXAI plans to make its own model, based on the xLSTM architecture, available on the Neuraverse platform.
It is set to be available alongside NEURA’s own foundation model, Neuron AI, in future.
“A robot that truly helps in everyday life and in industry must be able to remember,” says David Reger, founder and CEO of NEURA Robotics. “With Neuron AI, we have the foundation. With Neuraverse, we are creating the platform on which other powerful AI approaches can also find their way into robots. Together with Sepp Hochreiter and NXAI, we are expanding this memory capability. Two European strengths, one goal: Physical AI from Europe, together for the world.”
This follows a period of sustained growth for the Metzingen-based robotics unicorn.
As previously reported by EU-Startups, NEURA secured €15 million from InterAlpen Partners in 2023, following a €52 million round earlier that year. By September 2024, the company had reportedly raised €148.67 million in total, before securing a further €120 million Series B in January 2025. At the time, NEURA reported having doubled its workforce to more than 300 employees and increased its revenue tenfold over the preceding year.
This was followed by the announcement of a Series C of up to €1.2 billion in June 2026, and subsequently by acquisitions involving mobile logistics and autonomous cleaning robotics compamy Adlatus Robotics, extending its capabilities and the potential applications of its Neuraverse ecosystem.
“Memory and experience are essential for robots to reliably solve tasks involving many steps,” says Prof. Dr Sepp Hochreiter, founder of NXAI. “xLSTM is built for this; it is fast, memory-efficient and can maintain its state over long sequences. Together with NEURA, we are bringing this strength to Physical AI – from Europe for the world.”
Today’s news brings two companies that already share many touch-points even closer together.
Founded in 2019, Neura develops the technologies that enable intelligent machines to learn, adapt and work side by side with humans in the real world. The company develops cognitive robots that can see, hear, feel and learn, as well as the software, AI and data infrastructure required for their large-scale deployment.
Founded in 2023, NXAI is an Austrian DeepTech company based in Linz that develops solutions for industrial applications. The company’s mission is to translate its own AI research into market-ready products and to bridge the gap between research and industry. Its research focuses on xLSTM models in the fields of time series and robotics.
The planned integration between the two is intended to enable companies to tailor the NXAI model to their own tasks using the Neuraverse toolchain, test it in the NEURA Gyms and deploy it on suitable robots. This will allow customers to utilise different model approaches within the same training and application environment.
Neuron AI remains NEURA’s own multimodal foundation model and will continue to be developed independently. The partnership brings an additional model option to the platform and includes joint research. Companies retain control over their process knowledge and decide for themselves whether to share data and capabilities.
NEURA contributes the Physical AI Stack: its own multimodal foundation models, robotics, sensor technology, real-world training data from the NEURA Gyms, and the platform for industrial deployment. NXAI brings decades of AI research and a fundamentally different approach to recurrent intelligence and memory. Together, the two aim to make capabilities available more quickly.
In the long term, the aim is for robots not only to perform individual tasks, but to build on their experience over time. This aligns with the vision of the Neuraverse and the Robot Skill Economy: skills that robots learn from interacting with the real world, improve upon, and transfer to other machines and environments.
Editor’s Note: Albert Ortig, CEO of NXAI, will be speaking at the MeOut Summit (November 25-26) – co-organised by EU-Startups.

articles.title: Ce clone de l'Apple Watch Ultra chute sous les 50 € jusqu’à ce soir sur Amazon — Frandroid
articles.text:
Sur Amazon, la Realme Watch 5 se place parmi les montres connectées les plus abordables du moment puisqu’elle est actuellement disponible pour moins de 50 euros grâce à une réduction de 17 %. Avec ce prix attractif, la montre devient intéressante pour la vie quotidienne, mais elle ne l’est toujours que très peu pour un usage sportif.
Les points forts de la Realme Watch 5 :
- Une autonomie confortable d’une semaine
- Un design réussi
- La possibilité de répondre à des appels et des messages
Habituellement, la Realme Watch 5 est déjà attractive puisqu’elle est vendue pour 59,99 euros, mais Amazon renforce son attractivité en baissant son prix à 49,98 euros.
Si, par la suite, l’offre mentionnée dans cet article n’est plus disponible, merci de jeter un coup d’œil ci-dessous afin de dénicher d’autres offres concernant la Realme Watch 5. Le tableau s’actualise automatiquement.
Des inspirations prononcées
Un rapide coup d’œil au design de cette Realme Watch 5 devrait vous permettre de voir que cette montre s’inspire grandement de l’Apple Watch Ultra 3. Sans surprise donc, son design est réussi avec ce bouton unique en forme de couronne rotative et ce cadran aux angles arrondis. Seule différence, la présence du plastique pour cette Realme Watch 5.
Pour l’écran, Realme a opté pour une dalle AMOLED de 1,97 pouce avec une densité de 302 pixels par pouce. C’est suffisant pour distinguer les différents éléments, mais si vous vous approchez trop de la montre, vous pourrez voir les différents pixels. Cet écran montre ses limites en plein été puisque sa luminosité de 600 cd/m² ne permet pas une lecture optimale lorsque le soleil est à son zénith.
Parmi les autres points forts de cette Realme Watch 5, il y a l’autonomie. La marque annonce 20 jours en mode économie d’énergie ou 16 jours sans.
Un prix suffisant pour effacer les défauts ?
Pour 50 euros, il n’est pas surprenant de constater que la Realme Watch 5 souffre de quelques défauts et le plus contraignant est certainement la partie logicielle. S’il est possible de répondre aux appels et d’envoyer des messages, il est impossible d’installer des applications tierces. Pire encore, il est impossible d’exporter vos données d’entraînement vers Strava.
Pour rester sur le sport, la montre dispose d’un GPS qui s’avère fiable contrairement au capteur de la fréquence cardiaque qui commet souvent des erreurs. Néanmoins, il est difficile de croire que cette montre se destine au sport à cause de cette impossibilité d’exporter les données vers les applications d’entraînement.
Concrètement, cette Realme Watch 5 coche beaucoup de cases surtout pour ce prix-là. Le design est réussi, l’écran est lisible et le suivi GPS est au rendez-vous. Si ce sont vos principales attentes alors la montre sera intéressante, mais si vous comptez l’utiliser pour un usage sportif, les nombreux manquements vont ternir l’expérience.
Grâce à notre test, vous pourrez avoir un aperçu plus détaillé de cette Realme Watch 5.

articles.title: TikTok é alvo de denúncias sobre exploração de menores em lives
articles.text:
Funcionários do TikTok alertaram repetidamente a liderança sobre riscos a crianças e adolescentes, incluindo exploração sexual em transmissões ao vivo e exposição a conteúdos nocivos. Os relatos constam de documentos judiciais analisados pela NPR (National Public Radio).
Os depoimentos também apontam falhas em mecanismos de proteção e questionamentos internos sobre a monetização de transmissões irregulares. As alegações fazem parte de processos nos Estados Unidos que ainda não foram julgados por um júri.
Investigação identificou menores em vídeos ao vivo
Uma investigação interna citada nos documentos identificou crianças de 13 a 15 anos em 112 mil vídeos do TikTok Live apenas em janeiro de 2022. Segundo os depoimentos, o levantamento apontou riscos de aliciamento por predadores e produção de material de abuso sexual infantil. Também registrou receita significativa com presentes virtuais enviados a transmissões que violavam as regras da plataforma.
Reagen Maher, que ocupou cargos seniores nas áreas de segurança e investigações entre 2021 e 2024, afirmou ter tentado resolver o problema durante meses. Em uma conversa interna, escreveu: “Tenho brigado para consertar isso há meses com pessoas que não achavam que os danos eram graves o suficiente”.
A preocupação não se limitava ao conteúdo transmitido. Para Silvija Krupena, diretora da Unidade de Inteligência Financeira da RedCompass Labs, os pagamentos feitos durante essas lives precisam ser considerados no contexto da exploração sexual de menores.
“Tire a linguagem de presentes, moedas e diamantes, e a acusação fica clara. Um adulto pagou. Uma criança foi explorada. A plataforma ficou com uma parte”, afirmou à NPR.
Falhas nos controles e nas recomendações
Os depoimentos também descrevem problemas em recursos destinados a limitar o acesso de menores e permitir a supervisão dos responsáveis. Entre os pontos relatados estão:
- Acesso à versão adulta: segundo Maher, havia uma maneira de chegar à versão 18+ do aplicativo usando contas vinculadas ao Google, Facebook ou Instagram.
- Supervisão familiar: um link oculto permitia que adolescentes desfizessem o pareamento com as contas dos responsáveis pelo recurso family pairing.
- Conteúdo recomendado: funcionários discutiram o risco de o algoritmo conduzir usuários repetidamente a vídeos sobre suicídio e automutilação.
- Estimativa de idade: mensagens internas registraram receio de que autoridades solicitassem os resultados de pesquisas sobre a idade dos usuários.
Sobre o controle parental, Jordon Furlong, gerente de produto de bem-estar digital, escreveu em um chat de 2021 que a possibilidade de desfazer o pareamento “torna a função meio inútil”.
As discussões sobre recomendações também chegaram a conteúdos relacionados ao suicídio. Eric Han, chefe de segurança do TikTok entre 2019 e 2023, citou um relatório interno de 2020 que apontava: “Há um efeito real de contágio. Ideação e comportamento suicida, e a forma como isso é falado na plataforma”.
Processos questionam a proteção de menores
Os relatos integram uma ação coletiva iniciada em 2022, que reúne centenas de processos contra TikTok, Meta, Google e Snap. As ações alegam que as plataformas foram projetadas de forma prejudicial a usuários menores de 18 anos e que as empresas conheciam riscos que não teriam sido devidamente informados.
Outro ponto envolve a COPPA, lei norte-americana que protege a privacidade de crianças menores de 13 anos. Adam Wang, então responsável pelo TikTok Live, escreveu que incluir a opção “ensino fundamental” em uma pesquisa “definitivamente viola a COPPA”. Em outra mensagem, demonstrou receio de que a Comissão Federal de Comércio dos Estados Unidos (FTC) solicitasse os resultados: “Se a FTC souber dessa pesquisa, talvez queira que a gente envie os resultados, e eu não tenho certeza se é um bom resultado”.
A NPR também citou um acordo de US$ 8 milhões (cerca de R$ 39,8 milhões) firmado em maio de 2026, em uma ação sobre saúde mental e vício movida por um distrito escolar do Kentucky.
Os processos mencionados ainda não foram julgados por um júri. Procurado pela NPR, o TikTok não comentou diretamente as alegações e direcionou a emissora às políticas publicadas em seu site.
Valdir Antonelli é jornalista com especialização em marketing digital e consumo.

articles.title: Tesla Roadster moins cher : la marque annonce un 4e bolide plus « abordable »
articles.text:
Le 15 octobre dernier, Elon Musk a dévoilé le Tesla Roadster. Pour rappel, le modèle est décliné en trois versions : le Roadster Performance (une version routière classique, deux places, avec aérodynamique active et système d’aspiration sous la voiture), le Roadster Thrust (une version deux places ajoutant des propulseurs à gaz froid à l’arrière pour améliorer l’accélération) et le Roadster Rocket (une version monoplace, avec des propulseurs répartis autour du véhicule et des capacités de décollage). La présentation du 15 octobre était centrée sur ce dernier modèle, particulièrement impressionnant, il faut le dire. Ces trois modèles sont présents sur le site de Tesla, et une quatrième version pourrait prochainement les rejoindre.
Une Tesla Roadster standard
Franz von Holzhausen, designer en chef de Tesla, a confirmé l’information auprès du magazine MotorTrend : un quatrième modèle de Tesla Roadster rejoindra prochainement les trois autres. Concrètement, il est question d’une version standard, placée juste en dessous de la Roadster Performance, et donc moins performante, mais aussi plus « abordable ».
Selon Top Gear, ce modèle Standard atteindrait 1 090 ch, contre 1 360 ch pour la Performance. Il serait dépourvu du système d’aspiration multimode et pourrait également faire l’impasse sur l’aérodynamique active. Le véhicule pourrait donc être moins performant sur les accélérations, tout en offrant une meilleure autonomie. Les matériaux haut de gamme au sein de l’habitacle et le revêtement doré sur les vitres teintées pourraient aussi être remplacés par d’autres matériaux afin de faire baisser le prix. En revanche, ce modèle standard devrait bel et bien intégrer une propulsion, avec deux moteurs installés à l’arrière.
Quel prix pour ce modèle standard ?
Pour l’instant, Tesla ne présente pas ce modèle standard sur son site. Étant donné que nous ne disposons pas de fiches techniques, toutes ces informations devront être confirmées. En revanche, l’existence de ce modèle « plus accessible » semble actée. À ce titre, il reste aussi à connaître son prix. Ce modèle standard devrait afficher un prix plus bas que celui de la Roadster Performance, mais il devrait tout de même coûter un bras.
Pour rappel, Tesla demande un acompte de 50 000 € pour la Roadster Performance. En ce qui concerne le modèle Roadster Thrust, l’acompte s’élève à 250 000 €. Les prix de ces deux modèles sont toujours inconnus à l’heure où nous écrivons ces lignes, et il n’y a aucune garantie de livraison.

articles.title: Oubliez PowerPoint : voici ChatGPT Slides
articles.text:
Le mois dernier, OpenAI officialisait l’arrivée de ChatGPT Space avec son lot d’outils bureautiques intégrant des pages et des feuilles de calcul, tout en précisant que les présentations arriveraient plus tard. C’est désormais chose faite avec le lancement de ChatGPT Slides. L’entreprise détaille les nouvelles possibilités offertes à ses abonnés pour générer rapidement des supports visuels directement à partir de documents existants ou de modèles prédéfinis. PowerPoint et Google Slides n’ont qu’à bien se tenir.
Collaboration en direct et options d’exportation
Une fois le diaporama généré par l’intelligence artificielle, il est possible de le partager avec des collaborateurs pour travailler simultanément sur le projet. Les membres invités peuvent donc apporter des modifications et laisser des commentaires en direct. De son côté, ChatGPT peut même appliquer automatiquement des changements en fonction des retours des membres de l’équipe.
Lorsque le résultat final vous convient, l’outil permet d’ouvrir directement le fichier dans des logiciels tiers comme PowerPoint ou Google Slides. Vous pourrez évidemment télécharger le document au format PDF ou l’exporter directement sous forme de fichier PowerPoint pour l’utiliser hors ligne.
Qui peut profiter de ChatGPT Slides ?
ChatGPT Slides est disponible dès maintenant pour les personnes abonnées aux formules Pro, Business et Enterprise d’OpenAI. Pour en profiter, il suffit de demander directement à l’IA de créer des diapositives à partir d’un fichier texte ou d’une conversation en cours.
À lire : Avec Atlas enterré, ChatGPT s’installe dans vos onglets Google Chrome
En revanche, les utilisateurs payants de la formule Plus ne peuvent malheureusement pas en profiter. On peut l’expliquer par le fait que ChatGPT Slides est intégré à l’écosystème ChatGPT Space, lequel est déjà réservé aux abonnements supérieurs. Une distinction qui n’est pas sans rappeler le retrait par Google de ses meilleurs modèles sur son abonnement payant Google AI Plus.

articles.title: OVHcloud CLI releases backdoored on GitHub to steal developer secrets
articles.text:
French cloud and hosting provider OVHcloud is warning users that attackers compromised its open-source command-line interface (CLI) tool to distribute information-stealing malware.
The attacker hijacked a developer’s GitHub account to gain access to the OVHcloud CLI repository and modify versions 0.11.0 through 0.15.0 of the tool.
OVHcloud offers the CLI tool as an alternative for system administrators and developers to manage cloud and hosting services directly from a terminal, including for automating tasks.
OVHcloud CEO Octave Klaba disclosed that the company’s CLI repository on GitHub had been compromised, urging users who downloaded the latest version yesterday to update or remove the tool.
Klaba said that the compromised release appeared at 14:47 on October 19 and was detected and blocked at 16:21 after a customer reported it.
"The compromised versions are v0.11.0 v0.12.0 v0.13.0 v0.14.0 v0.15.0," the CEO said, adding that older version 0.10.0 and the latest release 0.16.0 were clean.
Despite the poor quality of the malware, its purpose was to "retrieve secrets from the disk," Klaba explained.
In a later update, Klaba shared that GitHub’s release immutability setting was disabled, allowing a sufficiently privileged account to modify existing releases without passing CI/CD checks.
"The entire set of CI/CD pipelines with unit tests, functional tests, CVE detection, etc., were not impacted."
OVHcloud has enabled GitHub’s release immutability feature and considers the incident resolved.
However, Klaba urges users who downloaded a compromised CLI package to perform a system cleanup and revoke all secrets.
"The quality of the binary is poor but it can go all the way. If you are affected, please change all the secrets on your disk."
GlassWorm connection
According to OpenSourceMalware, a community-driven threat intelligence platform, the attack was likely part of a new GlassWorm operation, known for campaigns since late 2025 that impacted the VSCode, OpenVSX, GitHub, and npm software development ecosystems.
The researchers confirmed that the attacker did not tamper with the CI/CD pipelines and uploaded malware-infected packages built locally.
The researchers note that the GitHub account used in the attack had been compromised for more than half a year.
"Its public repositories show a scripted history rewrite on 5 March 2026 and a hidden preinstall.js loader that decodes to a second stage using a Solana memo dead drop," OpenSourceMalware researchers found.
Although the associated wallet is a known GlassWorm indicator, the researchers did not analyze the malicious payload delivered through a trojanized version of the OVHcloud CLI.
According to OpenSourceMalware's report, affected platforms are macOS (Intel and ARM), Linux (x86_64 and ARM64), and Windows x86-64. Source builds and Docker images remained unaffected.
Anyone who ran an affected binary should treat all secrets on the machine as compromised.
Once attackers have valid credentials, only 37% of their actions are blocked
Overall prevention scores can hide what happens after initial access. Once attackers are using valid credentials, prevention drops sharply.

articles.title: Wisst ihr noch? Als Tester versehentlich das erste Samsung Galaxy Fold zerstörten
articles.text:
Folie abgezogen, Display tot: Als Tester versehentlich das erste Samsung Galaxy Fold zerstörten
Am 23. Oktober kommt das iPhone Duo in den Handel. Zwar ist es Apples erstes Foldable, ein Pionier ist das Unternehmen damit aber nicht. Samsung stellte sein erstes faltbares Smartphone, das Samsung Galaxy Fold, bereits Anfang 2019 vor. Schon damals war die Technik nicht günstig. 2.000 Euro sollte das Telefon kosten. Dass das Unternehmen damit dennoch groß auftrumpfen wollte, war klar. Vor dem Markstart produzierte das Unternehmen einen Werbefilm mit bekannten Größen wie dem Fußballstar Mario Götze oder dem Youtube-Influencer Casey Neistat.
Schon längst ist dieses Video auf Samsungs eigenen Kanälen aber nicht mehr auffindbar. Denn das Gerät hatte gleich mehrere Probleme mit der Stabilität, wie unter anderem The Verge 2019 berichtete. Dieter Bohn, damals Redakteur bei dem Medium, bemerkte nach einem Tag der Nutzung, dass etwas unterhalb der Displayfalte gegen den Bildschirm drückte. „Meine Vermutung ist, dass es sich um einen Fremdkörper handelt, auf jeden Fall um etwas, das härter ist als Flusen“, schrieb er damals. Kurze Zeit später habe das Display nicht mehr funktioniert. Auch CNBC berichtete zeitgleich von einem ausgefallenen Bildschirm.
Displayschicht wird zur Falle für Tester
Weitere Stimmen, die über Probleme mit dem Bildschirm klagten, waren daran zumindest nicht ganz unschuldig. Youtuber Marques Brownlee entfernte eine Schutzfolie vom Bildschirm, die er besser an Ort und Stelle gelassen hatte. Wie Samsung später in einem Statement mitteilte, war diese Folie „Teil der Bildschirmstruktur“. Sie sollte das Display vor Kratzern schützen, durfte aber nicht entfernt werden.
Brownlee war damit nicht allein. Auch der vor allem für seine Apple-Berichterstattung bekannte Mark Gurman von Bloomberg entfernte den wichtigen Film vom Bildschirm. Beide hielten das Cover für einen normalen Schutzfilm, wie er üblicherweise aufs Smartphone angebracht ist und nach dem Auspacken entfernt wird. In beiden Fällen trug das Display allerdings Schäden davon.
Zum Verhängnis wurde den Testern, dass die Bildschirmschicht so aufgebracht war, dass sie den Anschein erweckte, man könnte sie leicht abziehen. Brownlee bemängelte in einem Video, dass entsprechende Hinweise nicht auf das Verpackungsmaterial gedruckt waren. Joanna Stern, damals noch beim Wall Street Journal, begann ebenfalls, die Displayfolie abzuziehen, ließ dann aber doch auf dem Gerät. Samsung tauschte es nach ihren Angaben, wie auch bei den anderen Testern, aus.
Nur bei Einheiten, die Mobilfunkprovidern vorlagen, war offenbar schon vorab eine Warnung aufgedruckt, wie Des Smith, damals Senior Product Manager bei T-Mobile US, auf X postete. Smith betrieb naher einen Youtube-Kanal und war und ist auch in anderen sozialen Netzwerken aktiv. Erst mit dem Statement erklärte Samsung: „Wir werden sicherstellen, dass wir unseren Kunden diese Information deutlich vermitteln.“
Start verschoben, Smartphone verbessert
Trotz der negativen Berichte der Tester wollte Samsung zum nächsten am geplanten Starttermin (dem 26. April 2019 in den USA und dem 3. Mai in Europa) festhalten, entschloss sich kurzfristig aber doch um und kündigte an, den Verkaufsstart zu verschieben. „Erste Ergebnisse aus den Auswertungen der gemeldeten Display-Probleme zeigen, dass die Ursache am Scharnier liegen kann. Es gab auch einen Fall, in dem Stoffe, die sich im Inneren des Geräts befanden, die Display Leistung beeinträchtigten“, verkündete das Unternehmen in einem weiteren Statement.
Der Start folgte dann im September 2019. Diesmal stellte Samsung sicher, dass Nutzer die Schutzfolie nicht mehr entfernen konnten. Neue Abdeckungen sorgten zudem dafür, dass sich keine Fremdkörper mehr unters Display verirren konnten.
Längst bereiten die Samsung-Geräte Testern keine Probleme mehr. Im Jahr 2025 war Samsung mit 40 Prozent Marktanteil laut Counterpoint Research sogar Marktführer bei den Foldables. Ob das Unternehmen die Poleposition auch 2026 behält, bleibt abzuwarten. Da kommt ja schließlich noch was von Apple.

articles.title: Orange éteint définitivement sa 2G : 1,7 million de SIM concernées, SFR et Bouygues suivront en décembre
articles.text:
Trente-quatre ans après le lancement d’Itinéris par France Télécom, Orange a éteint ce mardi 20 octobre son réseau 2G dans l’Hexagone, là où il fonctionnait encore. Quarante-trois départements de l’Hexagone étaient concernés, de la Normandie à la Gironde.
Cette coupure, annoncée dans un communiqué, boucle presque l’extinction de la 2G d’Orange, déjà terminée à La Réunion en octobre 2025. La fin de cette génération de téléphonie mobile s’était ensuite faite par vagues en métropole depuis le 31 mars, de Bayonne, Anglet et Biarritz jusqu’à 44 départements d’un coup le 6 octobre.
Un téléphone qui ne capte que la 2G ne peut plus appeler ni envoyer de SMS sur le réseau d’Orange. C’est aussi le cas chez Free Mobile, qui passe par ce réseau.
Pour Orange, la 2G, déployée dans les années 1990, « ne répond plus aux exigences actuelles en matière de connectivité ». Les fréquences occupées par cette norme vont être recyclées pour servir aux nouvelles générations que sont la 4G et la 5G. Orange avance aussi un argument énergétique en citant la Fédération française des télécoms : un gigaoctet transmis en 2G consomme jusqu’à 500 fois plus d’énergie qu’en 5G.
Quelques endroits garderont la 2G d’Orange un peu plus longtemps. À Mayotte, l’opérateur la coupera le 31 décembre. Quant aux zones blanches réglementaires, ces communes rurales où les opérateurs partagent les mêmes antennes, elles la perdront entre le 1er et le 15 décembre.
Plus d’un million de téléphones 2G encore actifs cet été
Fin juin 2026, 1,06 million de cartes SIM tournaient encore dans des téléphones et des tablettes qui ne fonctionnent qu’en 2G. Le chiffre vient de l’observatoire publié le 24 septembre par l’Arcep, le régulateur des télécoms. S’y ajoutaient 620 000 cartes glissées dans des alarmes, des téléassistances ou des systèmes de télésurveillance, soit près de 1,7 million au total.
Le régulateur pressait depuis des mois les opérateurs d’accélérer la migration de leurs abonnés vers la 4G. De son côté, le gouvernement avait prévenu les derniers utilisateurs dès mai 2025.
Chez SFR, la 2G s’arrête le 15 novembre 2026. Bouygues Telecom la coupe le même jour à Brest, Guipavas, Nancy et Vandœuvre-lès-Nancy, puis partout ailleurs entre le 1er et le 15 décembre. D’ici là, vérifiez que le vieux mobile ou la téléalarme que vous utilisez fonctionne bien en 4G.
